## Cross-reference — what the 4 new files would corroborate (if content confirms the filenames)

These map straight onto the de novo findings already built for the substantive appeal
(see the hearing-strategy thread) and onto the pressed Notice items. **For the
substantive hearing / evidence-in-chief — NOT the 64G** (the 64G stays argument-free).

- **#1, #2 (pay) → Factor 3 + the "timeliness is the duty" point.** The Reviewing
  Officer excused the pay failures as "blemished but resolved." Contemporaneous
  correspondence showing the manager/Director ignoring or sitting on payroll goes to the
  *delay itself* being the breach (the duty is timely correct payment), not cured by the
  eventual fix. Corroborates the admitted 25-day AVAC delay (Form 24 ¶¶40–41).
- **#3 (roster / "does not know about the FRMS in place") → Factor 4 + the FRMS breach.**
  Lines up with MSH's own Item 5 admission in the 5 June letter that fatigue risk
  management at the Switchboard was **implemented only "after 30 June 2024."** If the
  manager was building rosters without knowledge of (or before) any FRMS, that is direct
  support for "no fatigue risk assessment existed at 17–18 March 2024."
- **#5 (redaction direction; disparate standard vs Chloe's office-hours request) →
  Item 10(d) + Form 24 ¶21/¶22.** Para 21 (retraction directed) is **admitted**; Para 22
  (the comparator email) is **denied** — this is the disparate-treatment fact Item 10
  targets. A document showing the manager directing redaction of one email while applying
  a different standard to the office-hours request is precisely the comparator.

## High-value finding from the now-authoritative MSH letter (item 6)

Having the full text confirms an **internal contradiction in MSH's own 5 June letter** —
already trapped by the filing's Schedule C Item 3(c):

- **Item 3(c):** "there have been **no 'consequential' changes** to operating procedures
  over the period requested."
- **Item 5:** fatigue-risk-management implementation at the Switchboard "occurred after
  30 June 2024 **in connection with an organisational change related to the reporting
  lines for Switchboard.**"

MSH asserts "no consequential changes" while, two items later, describing exactly such a
change (a Switchboard reporting-line reorganisation). Draft Order Schedule C Item 3(c)
already requires MSH to address the reporting-line reorganisation **and** reconcile its
answer with the "no consequential changes" statement — so the letter walks into the trap.

# Evidence Index — WC/2024/227

Searchable, curated index of the matter's evidence held across the cloud
(OneDrive / SharePoint, via the Microsoft 365 connector) and the repo. Built for
the `wc227-matter` skill's **evidence** sub-skill so the evidence-processor can
reason over the whole matter without the source binaries living in git.

## Curation rules (mirror `skill/SKILL.md` discipline — non-negotiable)

1. **WC/2024/227 only.** The QPS / DV / Alexia Negro criminal matter, any
   third-party criminal or health data, and unrelated matters (Sibley, etc.) are
   **EXCLUDED**, not indexed. The user's cloud co-mingles them; this index does not.
2. **Quarantine (discipline rule 2).** The ESU / PID **complaint form** and any
   "fraud" / collateral-purpose material (e.g. the 11 July 2024 email) are listed
   by **existence / location only** in a "parallel-track" section if encountered —
   their content is **never** pulled onto the WC track.
3. **Verified vs working (the cardinal habit).** A descriptive filename is the
   **user's characterisation = working / asserted**, NOT a verified fact, until the
   document's content is read against source. Files with **no extractable text**
   (image / screenshot PDFs) are marked `content-unverified`.

## Status legend

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[repo]` | already in the repo (`documents/…`) — content ingested |
| `[new-text]` | new to the project; text extracted and mirrored under `sources-text/` |
| `[new-image]` | new; **image-only** PDF — content NOT extractable via the connector (needs OCR or the original file) |
| `[dup]` | duplicate of another listed item |

  `01 FINISHED APPEAL` folder.

  (the binaries stay in the cloud / `documents/`).

## Cadence & the signal

- **Matheson / Regulator — diligent, never silent, model-litigant posture.** Same-day or next-day replies; a listing-attendance confirmation before *every* mention (24 Feb, 10 Mar, 31 Mar, 20 May). Flatly rejected Calderbank #1 and committed to "defending the appeal" (18 Feb) — **yet disclosed MSH-adverse documents on 11 June** under the ongoing-disclosure duty. That combination (defend hard / disclose anyway) is the seam the case theory relies on: the Regulator's overriding duty to the Commission overrides alignment with MSH.
- **MSH — minimal, reluctant, appearance-averse.** Surfaces only at formal triggers (extension application 30 Apr; objection 5 Jun). **Did not attend the 22 May mention** (the Commissioner expressly noted it). Now **compelled** to attend 7 August. MSH is doing the minimum a non-party can and avoiding the room — consistent with a party that does not want its records tested in person.
- **Registry — prompt but format-strict.** Bounced the application **twice** on format (A4 scaling Feb; "incorrect format" 14 Jun). Procedural, not substantive — but it cost ~11 days in June.
- **Reply-rate summary:** Cory is the high-volume sender (filings + covering emails, often in urgent multi-part bursts); Matheson responds reliably and briefly; MSH responds only through set-piece correspondence; Registry responds procedurally. The one party that goes quiet / absents itself is MSH.

# DECISION TABLE — 2 July to 28 July 2026
## Every decision point since the ECC was required: what was done vs what could have been done

> Source-anchored to the filed correspondence (Chloe Taylor 2 Jul; the minute-stamped 3 Jul thread;
> Forrest 7 Jul; Harrison 13 Jul (fund) and 15 Jul; leave coding). "Could have done" = the option
> available under the instruments MSH is bound by (EB12; Directive 12/24; QH-IMP-401-5; QH-POL-210;
> Psychosocial Code 2022; WHS Act ss 47-49). For the union brief and hearing use. NOT for
> correspondence.

| # | Date / time | Decision or event | What they DID | What they COULD have done (instrument) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 Jul | Return conditional on medical | Taylor: cannot "facilitate" return until a completed ECC; shifts processed as sick leave / sick leave no pay | Set the condition **and** state what would follow once met — timeframe, decision-maker, and pay treatment in the interim (QH-IMP-401-5; Directive 12/24) |
| 2 | 3 Jul 14:32 | ECC provided — GP certifies **fit with restrictions**, having read the AO3 role description | Received | Treat the condition as satisfied and commence the certified arrangement (QH-IMP-401-5; QH-POL-210 temporary adjustment) |
| 3 | 3 Jul 14:49 | Leave-type decision | Taylor: "sick leave / sick leave no pay" | Identify the correct characterisation for an employer-directed absence — special leave under EB12 cl 9.12 + Directive 12/24, or ordinary pay |
| 4 | 3 Jul 15:18 | Cory: certified fit, ready, asks annual leave for the past period, asks to attend | **Never answered** (25+ days) | Answer. Leave applications require a decision; silence is not one |
| 5 | 3 Jul 15:30 | **The exclusion decision — 58 minutes after the ECC arrived** | Held out "pending review"; shifts "paid out of your available sick leave" | Conduct a task-by-task match of the ECC to the role description before deciding; consult the worker (WHS Act ss 47–49); identify the power relied on |
| 6 | 3 Jul onward | Basis for the direction | No stand-down, suspension or other power ever identified | Identify the instrument and the delegate for the direction, and record reasons |
| 7 | 3 Jul onward | Risk assessment | None conducted, before or since | Conduct a psychosocial risk assessment of the **work system** using the Code (EB12 cl 7.2; Code of Practice 2022) |
| 8 | 7 Jul | Forrest letter | Four demands; states restrictions "already accommodated"; "not aware of any concerns" | Reconcile "already accommodated" with the exclusion; provide feedback on the WHS matters raised (EB12 cl 7.1.11) |
| 9 | 7–13 Jul | Interim/alternative duties | Refused pending "further medical clarification" | Identify alternative duties or re-training in another area (EB12 cl 7.1.5(f)–(h); QH-IMP-401-5; QH-POL-210) — or state which duty is incompatible and why |
| 10 | 13 Jul 16:20 | Communication to the super fund | Told ART "unable to facilitate Cory's return" — **before** the medical clarification said to be needed was sought | Seek the clarification first, then decide; or tell the fund a decision was pending |

| 15 | 15 Jul | Duties | Refused "in any capacity" | Blanket refusal requires justification duty-by-duty; consider adjustment (QH-POL-210) |
| 16 | 15 Jul | Legal characterisation | WCRA rehab limited to accepted claims → "remains at the discretion of the Employer"; refers to "Health Management processes" | Apply QH-IMP-401-5 (rehab available without an accepted claim where operationally reasonable) and QH-POL-210 (applies to all HHS employees); identify any process actually being applied, and its instrument |

| 20 | Throughout | Decision-makers | None identified for any decision | Record who decided what, under what power, and when |

## THE PATTERN THE TABLE SHOWS
1. **Every condition met produced a new condition.** ECC required → provided → excluded → further medical required → not sent.
2. **Conclusions preceded the evidence said to justify them** (item 10 is the clearest).
3. **No decision has an identified maker or power** (items 6, 11, 20).
4. **No process the instruments require was performed**: no task match, no risk assessment, no consultation, no feedback (items 5, 7, 9, 17).
5. **The financial consequence ran continuously** while none of the above occurred (items 3, 11, 12).

institutional-response material for the Krishnaiah report. **Not** for correspondence with MSH — the
28 July letter already asks the questions this table answers.

I refer to the Form 29 – Notice of non-party disclosure (the Notice) regarding the above matter. Mr
Shepherd is a current employee of Metro South Hospital and Health Service (Metro South Health) as
Switchboard Operator at Logan Hospital.

The Notice compels Metro South Health to produce various documents that Mr Shepherd claims to
require for his Workers' Compensation Appeal. Metro South Health has complied with some of the Items
requested in the Notice as outlined below. In accordance with Rule 64E(4) of the Industrial Relations
(Tribunals) Rules 2011, our objections to production/compliance with the Notice are also outlined below.

At the outset, it should be noted that Metro South Health is not in receipt of the Applicant's Amended
Statement of Facts and Contentions (Form 9A). Throughout the Notice, the Applicant has expressed
various opinions and views about the relevance of the documents to the allegations and stressors the
subject of the appeal. While Metro South Health's substantiative grounds of objection to compliance with
the Notice are outlined below, our ability to determine whether the requested documents are 'relevant' to
the proceeding (and therefore give rise to an objection under Rule 64E4(b)) has, to some extent been
limited. We submit this ought to be taken into consideration by the Commissioner.

Items 1 and 2 - SPOK emergency paging export and Aggregate SPOK activation counts
Metro South Health cannot comply with the request for Items 1 and 2. The requested records do not exist.
The system was upgraded in SPOK, and records predating that upgrade were not retained. However, a
spreadsheet of recorded MET calls is available for the period 17-18 March 2024.

Item 3(a) - Complaints received - server side exchange filter
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 3(a). The reason for this objection is the expense and
inconvenience that Metro South Health will incur (Rule 64E(4)(a)). All employee complaints relating to
Logan Hospital Switchboard operational errors are made directly to the Line Manager of Switch Board and
managed solely via email or verbally with the complainant. Metro South Health's core function is to provide
health services to the public. Compliance with a request of this date range would require approval from the
Health Service Chief Executive to engage external resources and assistance from eHealth Queensland at
the Department of Health to review and search individual staff member email accounts. This would have a
significant administrative and operational burden. Particularly as the date range requested is so broad
(between the period 1 December 2023 to 30 June 2024). In circumstances where the Matter in Issue as
pleaded in the Notice relates to "consecutive shifts of 17 to 18 March 2024", Metro South Health submits a
search of the requested range and breadth will take an unreasonable amount of time and resourcing and
detract from our core functions of providing health care to the community.

Item 3(b) - Management discussion of complaints
Metro South Health relies on the same grounds for objection as for Item 3(a) above.

Item 3(c) - Consequential changes to operating procedures
Metro South Health cannot comply with the request for Item 3(c) because there have been no
'consequential' changes to operating procedures over the period requested.

Item 4 - FRMS risk assessment record
Metro South Health cannot comply with the Notice in relation to Item 4. This is because the requested
documents do not exist. Mandatory Fatigue Risk Management System training only applies to health
practitioners and clinical assistants. The Logan Hospital Switchboard staff are non-clinical staff, and
therefore there is no mandatory requirement for them to complete Fatigue Risk Management System training.

Item 5 - FRMS training and competency records
Metro South Health cannot comply with the request in relation to Item 5. The implementation of fatigue risk
management assessment at Switchboard Logan Hospital occurred after 30 June 2024 in connection with an
organisational change related to the reporting lines for Switchboard.

Item 6 – FRMS delegation and governance record
Metro South Health encloses the attached Role Description for Manager of Switchboard Services.

Item 7 - FRMS register entries and switchboard roster expectations
Metro South Health cannot comply with the Notice in relation to Item 7. This is because the requested
documents do not exist. Mandatory Fatigue Risk Management System training only applies to health
practitioners and clinical assistants.

Item 8 – Management System Log in records
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 8. The reason for this objection is the expense and
inconvenience that Metro South Health will incur (Rule 64E(4)(a)). Compliance with a request of this date
range would require approval from the Health Service Chief Executive to engage external resources and
assistance from eHealth Queensland at the Department of Health to review and search individual staff
member email accounts. This would have a significant administrative and operational burden, particularly as
the date range requested is so broad (between the period 1 December 2023 to 30 June 2024) and a search
of the requested range and breadth will take an unreasonable amount of time and resourcing and detract
from our core functions of providing health care to the community. In circumstances where the Matter in
Issue as pleaded in the Notice relates to "consecutive shifts of 17 to 18 March 2024", Metro South Health
submits this date range is a reasonable range to search. Further, the reference to "Management system
login records - Active Directory / Entra ID / Citrix. Native electronic 2024 export of Windows Active
Directory, Entra ID and Citrix session-login audit records" is unreasonably broad (lacking particularity).
Metro South Health uses various application platforms and it is not clear which system is being referred to.

Item 9 - Management building access
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 9 on the basis that the request lacks relevance,
particularity and could affect a person (Rule 64E(4)(b)(c) and (f). The Switchboard office is collocated in an
office area where there are other staff from various departments going through the office area. The
switchboard office does not have its own access-swipe access. The Applicant is a current employee and
reports directly to the line manager. The request is unreasonably broad (lacks particularity) and production
could have an effect on the line manager.

Item 10 - various
Metro South Health objects to the production of the documents requested in Item 10. The reason for this
objection is the expense and inconvenience that Metro South Health will incur (Rule 64E(4)(a)). Compliance
with a request of this date range would require approval from the Health Service Chief Executive to engage
external resources and assistance from eHealth Queensland at the Department of Health to review and
search individual staff member email accounts. This would have a significant administrative and operational
burden. Particularly as the date range requested is so broad (between the period 1 December 2023 to 30
June 2024). In circumstances where the Matter in Issue as pleaded in the Notice relates to "consecutive
shifts of 17 to 18 March 2024", Metro South Health submits a search of the requested range and breadth
will take an unreasonable expenditure of time and resourcing, and detract from our core functions of
providing health care to the community.

Item 11 - Appellant's MyHR audit trail - COVID Special Pandemic Leave (Process Reference 15480560)
Metro South Health encloses the following documents in compliance with the request for Item 11:
- MyHR report leave submission for period 1 February 2024 to 31 May 2024;
- Leave form evidence of pandemic leave for period 20 to 27 February 2024;
- Leave form for period 20 to 27 February 2024;
- AVAC history for pandemic leave for the period 20 to 27 February 2024.

Item 12 – Comparator MyHR audit trails
In compliance with the request for Item 12, Metro South Health encloses a complete audit trail of the
requested pandemic leave for the period requested for Logan Hospital Switchboard. Metro South Health
otherwise objects to the production of other documents as outlined in Item 12. This request would require
accessing the relevant staff members' supporting evidence of their Special Pandemic Leave requests
during the period 1 January 2024 – 30 June 2024. Examples of supporting evidence could be a photograph
of a positive COVID test, medical certificate, lab results confirming COVID diagnosis, or letter from their
child's school in the event of school closure. This request is unreasonable in circumstances where the effect
of production would have on the other staff members (i.e. breach of their right to their privacy and reputation)
and that the proof of COVID test contains confidential and sensitive personal health information of the
relevant staff members.

Item 13 – Line Manager authority framework – COVID Special Pandemic Leave processing
In compliance with the request for Item 13, we enclose:
- HR Delegation COVID-19 Pandemic Event – Paid Special Pandemic Leave signed 23 November 2022;
- Pandemic Directive 01/20 – Employment Arrangements in the event of a Health Pandemic
  Implementation Guideline – Directive 01/20 dated 14 April 2020.

Item 14 - Text message and electronic communication corpus - Appellant and Line Manager concerning COVID Special Pandemic Leave
The requested information in Item 14 is not in control or possession of Metro South Health. The line
manager was not issued with a Queensland Health mobile device, and as such the SMS messages
exchanged between the Applicant and the Line manager relating to the pandemic leave request was made
using the line manager's personal mobile device. The Queensland Health retention policy does not apply to
employee's personal mobile. The Switchboard line manager was issued with Queensland Health mobile
device in or around the third quarter of 2024.

Item 15 - Leave ledger - 19 March 2024
In compliance with the request for Item 15, we enclose: Leave takings report for the Applicant 19 March 2024.

Item 16 - AVAC payroll export - Appellant (PRN 15397775 and PRN 15605601).
In compliance with the request for Item 16, we enclose:
- Daily Staffing variance form for the period 5 to 18 February 2024.
- Daily Staffing variance form for the period 19 February 2024 to 3 March 2024.

Item 17 – Comparator payroll export
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 17 on the basis of Rule 64E(4)(e). Disclosing the
requested information would infringe upon the human rights to privacy and reputation of the team members
within the switchboard team, because: the staff members' identity can be easily re-identified even if
redacted; the Logan Hospital Switchboard team is comprised of a small team; given that the Applicant is a
current employee within the same team, re-identification of the other team member would create a real risk
of harm to their reputation.

Item 18 - Communication Book and 15 November 2023 Business Case minutes
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 18 on the grounds of irrelevance (Rule 64E(4)(b)). The
Notice indicates that the destruction of the record had already been pleaded at Form 9A, Part B, para 2
Stressor l(b) (Form 24, Para 14). In those circumstances, it is difficult to identify the relevance of the
present request, given that the issue appears to have already been conceded.

Item 19 - Union delegate correspondence - server-side Exchange server
Metro South Health objects to the production of Item 19 on the basis of Rule 64E(4)(a) and (f). Metro South
Health employed approximately 20,006 MOHRI occupied headcount during the period of the dates of the
Notice. The requested documents require searching through these staff's email messages received from
Together Queensland. Compliance with a request of this date range and email recipients would require
approval to engage external resources and assistance from eHealth Queensland at the Department of
Health, resulting in a significant administrative and operational burden. We consider that the date range
ought to be narrowed to 17-18 March 2024, limited to emails received from Together Queensland by the
Switchboard line manager and their Director, or by members of the Logan Hospital Human Resources team
who were employed by and remained with Metro South Health. Further, any disclosure of correspondence
involving Together Queensland would also require consultation with or issuing a production notice to them
(as an affected party), if they were included in the email communication.

Item 20 - Operational HR reaction to PID 24-ESU-1130
The information requested in item 20 does not exist, as the reference cited in the Notice being
"PID24-ESU-1130" commenced in November 2024, which falls outside the specified search period of
13 May 2024 to 31 May 2024.

[Closing] In the event you have any questions or concerns about this correspondence, I have arranged for a
Principal Lawyer from the Metro South Health Legal team to be available to assist. Yours sincerely,
Ms Noelle Cridland, Chief Executive, Metro South Hospital and Health Service.

PART A: Appellant Cory Lea Shepherd; Employer State of Qld (Qld Health) — Logan Hospital Switchboard;
Role Administration Officer (OO3); INJURY: "Major Depressive Disorder with Anxious Distress (DSM-5 296.23)";
Date of onset 18 June 2024.

PART B — MATERIAL FACTS
1. Clean baseline:
 1.1 Switchboard, coordinating life-safety codes (Code Blue, MET).
 1.2 Clean psychiatric baseline; 16 Nov 2023 clinical record "No psychological illness such as
     depression/psychosis" (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 34).
 1.3 18 June 2024 onset; diagnosed by Dr Ravikumar Krishnaiah as MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER
     (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 38); Krishnaiah warned premature workplace exposure would likely
     cause clinical deterioration (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 39).
 1.4 Treating GP Dr Hawes recorded mechanism: "ongoing breaking of workplace rules by bosses,
     victimizing him" (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 36).

2. Causative stressors (composite course ~June 2023–June 2024):
 Stressor 1 — Hostile course / reprisal / suppression:
  (a) Dereliction of clinical governance: Taylor's erratic presence + unassessed unilateral directives;
      bottlenecked emergency workflows; delayed urgent pathology results.
  (b) Destruction of WHS records: 6 June 2023 comm-book entry removed by Taylor; admitted "I took it out
      last week" (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 14).
  (c) Refusal to investigate WHS/fatigue: 7 Aug 2023 grievance dismissed same day by Reese
      (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 5).
  (d) COVID leave obstruction: 20 Feb–1 March 2024; upload timestamp 11:41:27am 20 Feb; declined twice
      then approved on identical evidence.
  (e) PID: 13 May 2024 corrupt-conduct complaint; ESU determined it a PID (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 20).
  (f) Immediate reprisal: within 48hrs of the PID, Reese directed retraction of a routine email; a
      comparable Taylor email attracted none (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 21).
  (g) Suppression of representation: April 2023 union-delegate interest (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 18);
      contra QH-POL-248 (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 17); suppressed 13 months.
 Stressor 2 — Remuneration:
  (a) Persistent payroll failures Feb–April 2024; "42% pay disparity."
  (b) 3 May 2024 payroll directed Taylor to correct "IMMEDIATELY" (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 40);
      not actioned until 28 May — admitted 25-day delay (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 41).
 Stressor 3 — Fatigue (KEYSTONE):
  (a) 17-18 March 2024 consecutive shifts, 7-hour break (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 1); ~4 hours sleep.
  (b) "The Award and the FRMS mandate a minimum 10-hour rest break (Admitted Fact: Form 24, Para 3)."
      [NOTE: Form 24 Resp ¶3 admits 10h OR 8h-by-agreement; Resp ¶4 DENIES no-agreement / asserts a signed
      June 2020 8-hr agreement. The "10-hour minimum" is OVERSTATED here — the live minimum is contested

  (c) Misapplied a "superseded 2020 casual agreement" to deny paid fatigue leave; forced use of personal

1. Compensable injury (s 32(1)).

HEADER: To the Workers' Compensation Regulator c/- OIR (Appeals), Attn Matheson, Appeals@oir.qld.gov.au.
From Cory Shepherd. Date 1 July 2026. WPSATC; Calderbank v Calderbank [1976] Fam 93.

1. PURPOSE — offer to resolve the appeal "and all related matters" on the Part 6 terms; may be
   produced only on costs; invites the Regulator to get its own advice; model-litigant framing.

2. INJURY & CAUSE ESTABLISHED — MDD w/ anxious distress, diagnosed by Dr Krishnaiah (psychiatrist);
   Regulator admits the report states that diagnosis (Form 24 Para 38); 16 Nov 2023 "no psychological
   illness" record admitted listed (Para 34). Employment a significant contributing factor (s 32(1)).
   Hawes mechanism (disregard of workplace rules to his detriment) admitted as to contents; corroborated
   by the 31 Aug 2023 contemporaneous record (Exhibit CS-3) pre-dating any injury/claim. Krishnaiah:
   referred by Hawes Sept 2024, diagnosed 24 Oct 2024, WRITTEN REPORT (Exhibit A4) dated 13 Feb 2025 —
   independent clinical pathway, not a litigation reconstruction.

3. ONLY ISSUE = s 32(5)(a); appeal succeeds whoever bears the onus (either not "management action" -> nothing
   to exclude; or it is, but can't be shown reasonable on the admitted facts).

4. EXCLUSION NOT ENGAGED — a COURSE OF INACTION (omissions measured against positive duties: WHS Act 2011,
   fatigue framework, consultation, union rep, grievance/PID). s 32(5)(a) is a defence to positive management
   ACTION, a confined concept (Read v WCR [2017] QIRC 72; Allwood v WCR [2017] QIRC 88). Unifying pattern:
   inaction, and where management acted, MISDIAGNOSIS blaming the switchboard/appellant (CS-1 misrouting).

5. IN ANY EVENT NOT DISCHARGEABLE:
   5.2 The Regulator's OWN REVIEW found the 17-18 Mar fatigue failure "amounted to unreasonable management
       action" + employment a significant contributing factor; contents admitted (Form 24 Para 37); can't
       now press "reasonable in all respects."
   5.3 MSH's own 5 June letter: no FRMS applied (Item 4); implemented only "after 30 June 2024" (Item 5);
       no consequential change (3(c)); paging records not retained (Items 1-2) — confirmations of inaction.
   5.4 Comm-book page removed 6 June 2023 (removal admitted, Form 24 Para 6); management texts off-system
       (Item 14) outside retention.
   5.5 NEW: Reese misrepresented the appellant's FTE cyclic-roster proposal to HR (10 May 2024: "not fair and
       equitable," "Cory's roster will not be considered," "Cory is not yet aware") and omitted his proportionate
       offer; on his payslip loadings the proportionate method pays part/full-time the same effective rate.
   5.6 NEW: Ultra vires — the COVID leave declined 3x by an AO4 who held NO delegation (CE Instrument of
       Sub-Delegation eff. 5 Dec 2022, confined to a Band-9 delegate, no sub-delegation; produced at Item 13,
       described signed 23 Nov 2022) -> decisions BEYOND POWER, not valid/"reasonable" management action; same
       want of authority attended the pay delay ("escalate for delegate approval").
   5.7 Single unreasonable stressor suffices (Q-COMP v Hochen, adopted Mahaffey [2016] ICQ 10 [51],[54]-[57]);
       not arithmetical, exclusion not restored by outnumbering (Adams [2015] ICQ 1 [23]); pleaded stressors
       define the enquiry (Adams [19]-[20]); global evaluation (Delaney; Carr [2022] QIRC 59).

6. THE OFFER
 6.1 CORE: (a) Regulator consents to appeal allowed + claim accepted (or set aside/remit to a different
     decision-maker); (b) Regulator PAYS the Appellant's costs of the appeal (counsel, expert, solicitor),

 6.2 ADDITIONAL (SEVERABLE, not conditions of 6.1): (c) on acceptance, Appellant DISCONTINUES the r 64G

    emailed 6.23pm; email "ultimately removed from the server"); "reasonable in all respects."
17. 1(g) union delegate — DOES NOT ADMIT; says the 5.03pm text "just putting his hand up" was not a formal
    notification; DENIES policy breach/active suppression; says no assistance requested; delegate info provided;
    no deliberate inaction; "reasonable in all respects."

STRESSOR 2 (pay):
18. 2(a) — DOES NOT ADMIT ("no particulars").
19. payroll/2(a) — DOES NOT ADMIT; Easter 8-9 April 2023; "rostered in an equitable way... would not have
    earned 42% less"; "reasonable in all respects."
20. Further: pay issues raised over 2023-2024 "all investigated in a timely manner"; "discrepancies/errors
    remedied in a timely manner"; not entitled to 'Public Holiday not Worked'; "no outstanding underpayments";
    "reasonable and taken in a reasonable way."
21. 2(b) AVAC delay — DOES NOT ADMIT; 3 May payroll email to submit AVAC; 21 May Taylor awaiting confirmation;
    "Taylor submitted the AVAC on 28 May 2024"; "reasonable in all respects."

STRESSOR 3 (fatigue — THE KEYSTONE):
22. 3(a) — DOES NOT ADMIT; (a) "the shift was separated by only a 7-hour break (RATHER THAN AN 8-HOUR BREAK)...
    a result of HUMAN ERROR and NOT intentional or repeated"; (b) "the appellant could refuse shifts at anytime";
    (c) "took leave on 19 March 2024 but says this was PAID leave"; (d) leave-fatigue policy + the Award define
    the operative circumstances; (e) "in June 2020, the Appellant SIGNED AN AGREEMENT allowing an 8-HOUR break
    between shifts"; (f) "this issue was NOT CAUSATIVE of the appellant's injury."
23. 3(b) — DOES NOT ADMIT; "no breach of any mandate"; repeats 3(a).
24. 3(c) — DOES NOT ADMIT; repeats 3(a); (a) 19 March leave was paid; (b) "pursuant to CLAUSE 18.10 of the Award,
    the appellant is NOT ENTITLED to fatigue leave, because he was not performing overtime."

25. Subsequent conduct 3(a)-(c) — "occurred AFTER the WC application (1 July 2024) and POST-DATE any injury...
    NOT RELEVANT."

26. Admits the appellant is a worker (s 11 WCRA).
27. Contends any management action causative of any injury was reasonable management action taken reasonably (s 32(5)).

DECISION SOUGHT: (1) appeal DISMISSED; (2) the 24 Oct 2024 decision CONFIRMED; (3) "The appellant PAY THE
RESPONDENT'S COSTS of the hearing."

----- 2026-03-20T04:14:36Z | FROM coryshepherd1@hotmail.com | TO qirc.registry@qirc.qld.gov.au, renee.matheson@oir.qld.gov.au
SUBJ: WC/2024/227 – Appellant’s Update Pursuant to s552A Conference on 13 March 2026 
Dear recipients,

I refer to the conference held before Commissioner Dwyer on 13 March 2026 and the Commissioner’s
 direction that I provide an update on the progression of this matter.

1. Interlocutory Application (Form 4)

I have carefully considered the Commissioner’s guidance regarding the jurisdictional scope
 of the Commission in an appeal under s 549 of the Workers’ Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2003 (WCRA) and the requirement for the proportionate conduct of this matter.

Noting the Commissioner’s indication on the record that the Medical Exhibit will be sealed
 if it comes on the record, the primary prejudice to my case regarding privacy has been addressed. Accordingly, to focus the Commission’s resources entirely on the substantive merits of the appeal, I formally advise that:

I withdraw the portions of my Form 4 Application (filed 11 February 2026) and Supplementary Form 4 Application (filed 23 February 2026) seeking orders for findings of statutory reprisal, referrals to external agencies, or personal/indemnity costs against the
 Respondent’s representatives.

I accept the Commissioner’s indication that Exhibit A5 will be sealed on the Commission’s file to protect my privacy pursuant to
s 580 of the Industrial Relations Act 2016. On this basis, I do not require a formal hearing on the exclusion of this evidence.

I no longer press for orders regarding representative removal or the strike-out of the Respondent’s defence.

For the avoidance of doubt, this withdrawal does not constitute an abandonment of the factual
 matters set out in those applications. Those matters remain part of the evidentiary record and may be relied upon at the substantive hearing to the extent they are relevant to the s 32(5)(a) assessment.

2. Progression to Substantive Hearing

The matter is ready to proceed to a hearing on the substantive issue of whether the Appellant’s
 psychological injury arose out of reasonable management action carried out in a reasonable way within the meaning of s 32(5)(a) of the WCRA.

3. Proposed Timetable

I respectfully propose the following timetable to progress the matter:

27 March 2026: Appellant to serve Notice to Produce Documents (Form 29) on the Respondent.

10 April 2026: Respondent to comply with Notice to Produce (14-day compliance period).

1 May 2026: Appellant to file and serve List of Witnesses, Outlines of Evidence, and Expert/Medical Reports.

29 May 2026: Respondent to file and serve List of Witnesses, Outlines of Evidence, and Expert/Medical Reports.

12 June 2026: Parties to confer and file Agreed Trial Plan.

At the Commission’s convenience: Matter to be listed for further s 552A conference, orders or hearing dates regarding the matter.

4. Summary

By this correspondence, I have withdrawn interlocutory elements falling outside the Commission’s
 substantive jurisdiction, accepted the sealing of the medical Exhibit, and provided a clear path to trial.

I remain ready to cooperate with the Commission and the Respondent to ensure the efficient
 disposition of this appeal on its merits.

Yours faithfully,

Cory Lea Shepherd

> STATUS: DRAFT for Cory's review. OPEN correspondence (not without prejudice — this letter is
> MEANT to be on the record). SEND CHECKLIST AT FOOT — do not send before it is done.
> DESIGN: corrects the factual frame ("return to work" → working employee held out); states the
> governing frameworks neutrally; makes numbered requests with a response date. It contains NO

**To:** Michelle Harrison, Injury Management Consultant, LBHS HR Team 1
(LBH_InjuryManagement@health.qld.gov.au)
**Cc:** [ORGANISER NAME], Together Queensland ([organiser email]); [Cory's own records address]
**Subject:** RE: Cory Shepherd (MSH-INJ-5795) — correction of record; reinstatement to roster; pay
and leave; request for particulars

Good afternoon Michelle,

Thank you for your letter of 15 July 2026. Before responding to its substance, I need to correct
the basis on which my situation is being described and managed, because several of the letter's
conclusions rest on that description. I have copied my union, Together Queensland, into this
correspondence, and they will be assisting me from this point.

**1. Correction of the record — I am not "returning to work"**

1.1 Your correspondence describes me as an employee "proposing" or "requesting" a return to work,
and describes my situation to others as "a QSuper Claimant request[ing] to return to duties." That
is not my situation, and I ask that the Health Service's records be corrected.

1.2 The facts are: I have been continuously employed and **working my rostered shifts for the past
year**, up to and including early July 2026. Across that period I adjusted my hours within my
certified capacity, and my income protection benefits ceased **at my own request in March 2026
because I was working**. There was no absence from which to "return."

1.3 On **3 July 2026 at approximately 2:32pm**, I provided the Employee Capability Checklist
completed by my treating practitioner, Dr Ma, certifying me **fit to work with identified
restrictions**. I provided it as a serving employee updating my medical information, in connection
with finalising my superannuation income-protection matters — not as an application for permission
to work. I was rostered to work at that time.

1.4 By **approximately 3:30pm the same day** — less than one hour later — I was advised I would be
held out of the workplace pending a review, with my rostered shifts to be "paid out of [my]
available sick leave." I have been held out of work since, while certified fit, for now twelve
days, with no timeframe.

1.5 Accurately described, then: I am a working employee who has been **directed not to attend work
by my employer**, while holding a current fitness-for-duty certification. Any process applied to me
should proceed on that footing.

**2. Pay and leave**

2.1 I am, and at all times since 3 July have been, **ready, willing and able** to work my rostered
shifts. The decision that I not attend is the Health Service's, not mine.

2.2 No stand-down, suspension, or other power authorising an unpaid direction not to attend has
been identified to me. Unless and until one is identified, I do not accept that my rostered shifts
during this employer-directed period can be treated as unpaid or debited against my accrued leave.

2.3 I note in particular that **sick leave compensates incapacity for work**. I am certified fit.
Debiting sick leave — leave I have already substantially exhausted through the period of my
illness — to cover shifts I was ready to work, and was directed not to attend, is not a purpose
for which that leave exists.

2.4 **Request:** that all leave debited for rostered shifts from 3 July 2026 onward be re-credited,
and that those shifts, and any future rostered shifts during this employer-directed period, be
treated as paid time. If the Health Service's position is otherwise, please identify in writing the
specific power or instrument relied upon.

2.5 For completeness on your letter's final point: my QSuper income protection claim is closed, and
in any event an insurance benefit is not wages. My remuneration for rostered shifts is a matter
between me and my employer under my contract, the Award, and the certified agreement. I will
provide the fund's written confirmation of closure when I receive it, as you have requested.

**3. The applicable framework**

3.1 Your letter states that, absent an accepted workers' compensation claim, my situation "remains
at the discretion of the Employer." I do not understand that to be a complete statement of the
position, and I draw the following to your attention:

(a) **Queensland Health's Workplace Rehabilitation Standard (QH-IMP-401-5)** provides that
workplace rehabilitation, including suitable duties and temporary adjustments, may be provided to
employees **without** a current accepted workers' compensation claim where operationally
reasonable, and that managers are responsible for identifying such duties;

(b) **Queensland Health's Reasonable Adjustment policy (QH-POL-210)** applies to my circumstances;

(c) the **Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld)**, including the positive duty in force since
1 July 2025, and the **Human Rights Act 2019 (Qld) s 58**, apply to decisions the Health Service
makes about my employment;

(d) the **Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld), ss 47–49**, requires consultation with me about
matters affecting my health and safety — including decisions to exclude me from the workplace and
any assessment said to concern psychosocial risk. To date there has been no consultation: the
decision of 3 July was made and communicated within the hour, and I have not been consulted since.

3.2 Against that framework, the current position — no duties in any capacity, no pay, no
consultation, and no timeframe, for a worker certified fit with restrictions — does not appear to
me to reflect the exercise of discretion those instruments contemplate. My offer to perform
suitable duties within my certified capacity (including drawing on my prior Metro South Health
experience in finance and scanning/records, and my substantive Switchboard role) remains open.

**4. "Health Management processes" — request for particulars**

4.1 Your letter refers to employees "being managed through Health Management processes." So that I
can understand my position and obtain advice, please confirm in writing:

(a) whether I am presently being managed under any such process and, if so, **which** process,
under **what policy or statutory instrument**, commenced **when**, by **whom** as decision-maker;

(b) if reliance is placed on chapter 3, part 8 of the *Public Sector Act 2022*, the basis on which
its preconditions are said to be met, noting that I was working until directed not to attend and
hold a current fitness-for-duty certification;

(c) if I am **not** being managed under any such process, confirmation of that fact.

**5. The Request for Medical Information to Dr Ma**

5.1 I repeat my request that the Request for Medical Information be issued promptly, and that I be
provided a copy when it is sent. I ask that it be confined to my **capacity, restrictions, and
their operational application** — the matters your letter identifies as requiring clarification —
and I confirm my consent extends to information of that kind.

5.2 I again ask that you advise the timeframe within which a decision about my rostered shifts
will be made once Dr Ma's response is received. My restrictions are certified **now**; 28 August
2026 is a review date, not a start date.

**6. Response**

6.1 Given that I remain without work or income while certified fit, I ask for a written response to
the requests at 2.4, 4.1 and 5 by **[DATE — 7 days]**. My union may be in contact separately.

I remain certified fit, ready, and available to work my rostered shifts.

Kind regards,
**Cory Lea Shepherd**

**To:** Heath Moran (heath.moran@together.org.au)
**Subject:** FW: The current HR position in writing — 15 July letter (for Friday's review)

Good afternoon Heath,

As promised, the final piece for your review — the full email chain ending with HR's letter of
15 July 2026 (below), which sets out their position in writing. I've held off responding pending
your review and the industrial team's advice. To make Friday easier, here is the chain in short,
and the issues as I understand them.

**What the chain shows**

- **13 July:** HR (Michelle Harrison, Injury Management) phoned and then wrote to my QSuper case
  manager advising the Health Service is "unable to facilitate" my return — before the further
  medical information they say they need had been requested from my GP.
- **13 July (me):** I asked four things — what was disclosed to the fund and on what authority;
  that the Request for Medical Information to my GP go out within 3 business days with a copy to
  me, and the decision timeframe once his response arrives; that my rostered shifts while held out
  be paid and not taken from my leave; and a response to my standing offer of interim duties.
- **15 July (their letter):** the request to my GP has **no timeframe** ("unable to commit"); pay is
  **refused** on the basis that I "hold a current QSuper Income Protection Claim" (I don't — it is
  closed, and I've asked the fund for written confirmation); interim duties are **refused "in any
  capacity"** pending the un-timetabled GP request; and my situation "**remains at the discretion
  of the Employer**" because I don't have an accepted workers' compensation claim, with reference
  to employees "being managed through **Health Management processes**."

**Issue 1 — the situation is being mischaracterised as a "return to work."** I have been
continuously employed and working my shifts for the past year, on hours I adjusted within my
certified capacity. Throughout that period I kept the fund side correct myself: while the appeal
was ongoing I asked QSuper to assess my payslips and adjust my benefit to partial payments
reflecting the hours I was actually working, and ultimately my income protection payments stopped
at my own request, to prevent overpayment, because I was working. On 3 July at about 2:32pm I provided the Employee Capability
Checklist my GP completed certifying me **fit to work with identified restrictions** — as a serving
employee updating my medical information while finalising my super matters, not as an application
for permission to work. By about 3:30pm the same day — under an hour — I was held out of the
workplace "pending review," with my rostered shifts "paid out of [my] available sick leave." I have
been out since, thirteen days now, with no timeframe. Accurately described, I'm a working employee
**directed not to attend by my employer while certified fit** — not an absent employee requesting
to return. Their letters (including to my super fund) describe me as "a QSuper Claimant request[ing]
to return to duties," which is wrong on both counts.

**Issue 2 — pay and leave.** I am and have been ready, willing and able to work my rostered shifts;
the decision that I not attend is theirs. No stand-down, suspension or other power has been
identified to me, yet the shifts are being debited against my own **sick leave** — leave that exists
to cover incapacity, which on their own file I don't have, and which I have already substantially
exhausted through my illness. Their stated basis for refusing pay — that the fund is responsible —
rests on a claim that is closed, and in any event an insurance benefit isn't wages.

**Issue 3 — the policies and frameworks I believe are being misapplied or ignored.** Their letter
treats the absence of an accepted workers' compensation claim as leaving everything to "the
discretion of the Employer." As I understand it, that is not complete:
(a) **QH's Workplace Rehabilitation Standard (QH-IMP-401-5)** — rehabilitation, suitable duties and
temporary adjustments may be provided to employees **without** an accepted claim where operationally
reasonable, and managers are responsible for identifying such duties;
(b) **QH's Reasonable Adjustment policy (QH-POL-210)**;
(c) the **Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld)** (including the positive duty in force since
1 July 2025) and **Human Rights Act 2019 s 58**;
(d) **WHS Act 2011 ss 47–49** — consultation. There has been none: the 3 July decision was made and
communicated within the hour, and I haven't been consulted since, even though their letter now
frames the assessment in psychosocial-risk terms.

**Issue 4 — "Health Management processes."** Their letter says the rehabilitation obligations don't
extend to employees "being managed through Health Management processes" — but no one has told me
whether I am in such a process, which one, under what instrument, or who the decision-maker is. If
this is the *Public Sector Act 2022* ch 3 pt 8 pathway, I don't understand how its preconditions
could be met — I was working until directed not to attend, and I hold a current fitness-for-duty
certification.

**Issue 5 — the request to my GP.** No timeframe to send it, no timeframe to decide once answered,
and their letter describes its subject as "the nature of the matters identified by Dr Ma" — which
reads wider than the restrictions themselves. I want any request to my GP copied to me and confined
to my capacity, restrictions and their operational application, and I've said so.

**Issue 6 — the two-year reversal on "psychosocial risk."** The psychosocial concerns in this
workplace were raised **by me**, beginning more than two years ago: fatigue and rest-break breaches
(including the March 2024 rostering that left me a 7-hour break between shifts), unresolved pay
failures, and switchboard workload and communication-flow issues — including in a written grievance
on 7 August 2023 that was dismissed the same day it was lodged, and later in the disclosure I
mentioned in my first email. To my knowledge, no psychosocial risk assessment of the switchboard
was ever undertaken in response to any of it, and I managed my own exposure over the past year by
adjusting my hours within my certified capacity. The first time the Health Service has applied
psychosocial-risk language to this workplace in writing is the 15 July letter — and its subject is
not the hazards I raised, but **me**: whether the "matters identified by Dr Ma" (that is, my
medical condition) "present any psychosocial hazards or risks." Two years on, the hazards remain
unassessed, and the worker who raised them — and was injured — has become the subject of the
assessment. Given you mentioned switchboard hazards are a recurring theme from members, I'd
particularly value the industrial team's view on that sequence.

I had prepared a full response to HR raising all of this (with the policy citations) — I'm holding

Happy to talk any time after your Friday review. Thanks again for moving quickly on this.

Subject: Clarification of my email of 28 July 2026 — special leave and pay treatment (MSH-INJ-5795) — response date unchanged

Dear Michelle / Injury Management / HR,

One clarification to my email of 28 July 2026. It concerns item 5 only, and it does not extend the response date sought in that email.

THE CORRECTION

I wrote that special leave under Directive 12/24 "must be applied." I should state my meaning precisely. I do not contend that the Directive compels a particular outcome — clause 6 confers a discretion, and I acknowledge that. What I contend is that the instrument must be applied: identified as the governing instrument, considered, and a decision made under it.

THE DIFFICULTY IS NOT THAT THE QUESTION WENT UNANSWERED

Your email of 15 July 2026 determined the pay question by reference to a QSuper Income Protection claim. That is an insurance arrangement which is not a source of wages and to which the Health Service is not a party. Payments ceased at my request in March 2026 when I returned to work, and the fund placed the claim on hold from 1 June 2026 pending reassessment. No benefit is payable in respect of the shifts I was rostered to work and directed not to attend.

The instruments that govern the treatment of an employer-directed absence — EB12 clause 9.12 and Directive 12/24 — were not applied.

So the position is twofold: a matter that does not bear on the question was treated as determinative, and the instruments that do bear on it were not engaged.

WHY THOSE INSTRUMENTS ARE ENGAGED HERE

The absence is employer-directed. I remain certified fit for modified duties and have been ready, willing and available throughout. Ongoing financial detriment is being produced, including the depletion of my own accrued leave.

In those circumstances the decision-maker is required to consider whether paid special leave, or ordinary pay treatment of the directed absence, is the appropriate characterisation, having regard to the matters at clause 6.5 — the reason, the duration, and the impact on me if it is not approved.

The consideration is not discretionary. The outcome is.

REQUEST

Please confirm whether Directive 12/24 and EB12 clause 9.12 have been considered in relation to my absence from 3 July 2026 — as distinct from the QSuper claim — and if so, by whom and with what result. If they have not been considered, I ask that they now be considered, and that I be advised of the outcome and the delegate who determined it.

If it would assist, I am willing to meet at short notice to work through the Employee Capability Checklist and a suitable duties plan. I would ask that any meeting occur alongside, rather than in place of, a written response to the matters raised.

This clarification is to be read with my email of 28 July 2026.

RESPONSE TO CORRESPONDENCE OF 29 JULY 2026 - REQUEST FOR FURTHER MEDICAL INFORMATION
Employee Capability Checklist dated 3 July 2026 (MSH-INJ-5795)

Dear Michelle,

Thank you for your email of 29 July 2026.

1. MY ELECTION

1.1 I will take the request to my treating practitioner myself. I would rather progress this quickly than add a further step, and I will arrange an appointment as soon as I have the request.

1.2 As I will provide the request to Dr Ma directly, I do not propose to complete the Employee Authority Form. It is broader than the present request - it extends to disclosures to and from WorkCover Queensland and income protection insurers, and it is open-ended in duration. If a written authority is needed for Dr Ma to respond to a specific request, I am happy to provide one confined to that purpose.

2. WHAT I NEED IN ORDER TO DO THAT

2.1 To put a request to Dr Ma, I need the request. Your email states that "further clarification is required regarding your functional capacity and the medical restrictions identified", but does not identify what is unclear. Dr Ma cannot respond to a request in those terms.

2.2 Could you please provide, in writing:

(a) the specific questions the Health Service asks Dr Ma to answer, set out as questions;

(b) for each question, the duty or task to which it relates, identified by reference to the Administration Officer, Switchboard Services (AO3) role description, which Dr Ma reviewed before completing the checklist;

(c) what in the 3 July Employee Capability Checklist is said to be insufficient - which entry requires clarification, and why the existing entry does not enable the assessment; and

(d) who will consider Dr Ma's response, and the timeframe within which the decision about my duties will then be made.

3. WHY THAT SPECIFICITY IS NEEDED

3.1 Your email states the request is made under the Health Service's obligation to assess the medical information "alongside the inherent requirements of the role". I accept that the Health Service has its own obligations. Five things follow.

(a) The assessment is task-based, so the questions should be. QH-POL-210 directs adjustments to enabling an employee to safely perform the genuine occupational requirements of the role, tailored to their circumstances, and reflects the obligation under the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld) to make reasonable adjustments for an employee with an impairment unless doing so would impose unjustifiable hardship. QH-IMP-401-5 makes managers responsible for identifying suitable duties, guided by medical information. Each operates at the level of identified duties. A refusal of all duties, without identifying which duty cannot be performed or adjusted, does not engage that assessment - and a question not tied to a duty cannot produce information that either instrument can use.

(b) Assessing a risk requires identifying the risk. EB12 clause 7.2 and the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 proceed by identifying a hazard, assessing the risk it presents, and considering controls. I am not presently able to identify what risk is said to arise, or from which duty - and without that I cannot meaningfully participate in the assessment, as consultation under sections 47 to 49 of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (Qld) contemplates.

(c) The checklist is the Health Service's own instrument. It was required by the Health Service and completed by Dr Ma after he reviewed the AO3 role description. If it is now insufficient, the entry said to be insufficient should be identifiable, together with what the form did not capture.

(d) The arrangement is not new. I worked in the role on reduced hours within my certified capacity for approximately twelve months before 3 July 2026, and the Health Service's correspondence of 7 July 2026 records that my restrictions were already being accommodated. Could the request please also identify what has changed - that is, which duty is now said to be affected in a way it was not during that period.

(e) The framework identifies hazards in the work, not in the worker. The Code of Practice identifies psychosocial hazards by reference to features of work and its management - job demands, job control, support, role clarity, change management, workplace relationships and organisational justice. EB12 clause 7.2 correspondingly provides for risk assessments of workplaces, conducted using the Code and in consultation with workers and health and safety representatives. I therefore ask that any assessment framed in psychosocial terms be directed to the work and the work system, and that questions to Dr Ma be confined to my capacity to perform identified duties.

4. THE RESTRICTIONS AND THE DUTIES

4.1 Since your email refers to the inherent requirements of the role, I have compared the restrictions certified on 3 July with the responsibilities set out in the AO3 role description.

4.2 The role description lists the position's key responsibilities as: attending to telephone enquiries and maintaining call queues; collating information and maintaining the Omnivista database and SharePoint; supporting the allocation, coordination and fault repair of pager units; participating in the emergency response process in accordance with emergency code procedures; establishing and maintaining networks and records; exercising discretion and judgement to resolve problems within the scope of the role; interacting appropriately with the public and service providers; multitasking and operating under pressure; contributing to the team; working with limited supervision; treating patients and staff fairly; and following safety policies and procedures.

4.3 First, the restriction on complaint-handling does not correspond to any responsibility listed in the role description. If the Health Service considers complaint-handling to be an inherent requirement of the position, could you please identify where it appears in the role description, or on what other basis it is said to be an inherent requirement.

4.4 Second, the remaining restrictions - the limits on peak weekday day and afternoon shifts, predictable rostering, and a minimum ten-hour break between shifts - go to when I work, not to which duties I perform. They do not remove any of the responsibilities listed above.

4.5 I note the role description records that the position is a continuous shift working role. I worked that role, on reduced hours and within my certified restrictions, for approximately twelve months prior to 3 July 2026, and the correspondence of 7 July 2026 records that those restrictions were already being accommodated. If the rostering restrictions are now said to be incompatible with the role, could you please identify what has changed since that period.

4.6 Third, a reduction in ordinary hours is an arrangement the industrial instruments expressly contemplate. Clause 8.2 of the Hospital and Health Service General Employees (Queensland Health) Award - State 2015 provides for part-time employment on a regular number of ordinary hours, pro rata to full-time conditions, with a minimum of eight ordinary hours per fortnight. EB12 clause 10.3 provides that an employee may request a change in the way they work, including their ordinary hours, that such a request may be refused only on reasonable grounds, and that the employer must give written notice of its decision, with reasons, within 21 days.

4.7 A reduction in hours does not of itself remove any duty from the role, and where such an arrangement is made for reasons unrelated to health it does not ordinarily require medical clarification or absence from the workplace while it is considered. Could the Health Service please identify why the reduced hours certified on 3 July 2026 are treated differently - that is, what it is about those hours, as distinct from the reasons for them, that prevents the duties of the position from being performed.

4.8 Accordingly, could the request to Dr Ma please identify which of the responsibilities listed at paragraph 4.2 the Health Service says I cannot perform, and which restriction is said to prevent it.

5. THE CHARACTERISATION OF RISK

5.1 Across your correspondence of 13, 15 and 29 July 2026, the Health Service has stated that it must assess whether my return can be "safely and operationally supported", whether "the matters identified by Dr Ma ... present any psychosocial hazards or risks", whether duties "can be safely facilitated", and has referred to its obligation to ensure the health and safety of workers "and others in the workplace".

5.2 I appreciate that the last of these reflects the language of the primary duty, and I do not suggest the Health Service should not satisfy itself as to safety.

5.3 However, in the twenty-seven days since 3 July, no incident, complaint, hazard or particular of any kind has been identified to me. Nor was any raised at any point during the approximately twelve months I worked in the role on reduced hours, or in the correspondence of 7 July 2026 recording that my restrictions were already being accommodated. There has been no finding of any kind made in relation to my performance of this role.

5.4 A concern about safety expressed only in general terms is not something I am able to answer, and it is not something Dr Ma can answer either. Could you please therefore confirm:

(a) whether it is asserted that my performing the duties of my position, within the restrictions certified on 3 July 2026, would present a risk to my own health and safety or to that of any other person; and

(b) if so, the basis for that view - the duty concerned, the risk identified, and the material relied upon.

5.5 If no such assertion is intended, I would be grateful if you would confirm that in writing, so that the questions to Dr Ma can be confined to my capacity and restrictions, and so that the position is clear on my record.

6. DECISION-MAKING

6.1 The Code of Conduct for the Queensland Public Service, made under the Public Sector Ethics Act 1994, provides at clause 4.1 that we will "treat all people equitably and consistently, and demonstrate the principles of procedural fairness and natural justice when making decisions", and will "exercise our lawful powers and authority with care and for the purpose for which these were granted". Clause 4.4 provides that official information is to be treated with care and used "only for the purpose for which it was collected or authorised".

6.2 I raise this only to explain the basis of the requests above. I ask that the decisions concerning my attendance, my duties and my pay since 3 July 2026 be made and recorded consistently with those standards - that is, that the decision-maker and the power relied upon be identified, that reasons be given, that I be treated consistently with the arrangement that operated for the preceding twelve months, and that medical information be sought and used only for the purpose for which it is collected.

7. SCOPE

7.1 I will provide Dr Ma with the questions and the role description. My consent extends to information concerning my capacity, my restrictions, and their operational application to the duties of my position, and I ask that the questions be limited to what is necessary for that purpose. PROPOSED METHODOLOGY — PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK ASSESSMENT, SWITCHBOARD SERVICES

Cory Lea Shepherd
AO3, Switchboard Services, Logan Hospital, Metro South Health
August 2026 — a worker's proposal for how the clause 7.2 assessment be conducted, offered in
consultation under sections 47 to 49 of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011. Companion to the
Psychosocial Hazard Mapping and the Proposals for Consultation. Nothing in this document is a
demand or an allegation; the method proposed is drawn from the Code of Practice 2022,
ISO 45003, and recognised practice in emergency communications settings.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 — THE EIGHT PHASES PROPOSED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.  GOVERNANCE. An assessor independent of the functions being assessed; published terms of
    reference; a small steering group including an operator representative, any Health and
    Safety Representative, and the union. The Code of Practice 2022 and ISO 45003 stated as
    the methods frame.

2.  THE RECORDED DATA (work as recorded). Call volumes by hour and day; emergency-code
    activity; the rosters audited against the fatigue rules; the team's leave usage mapped
    against the rosters and the demand data; turnover, vacancy and backfill data; the
    complaints correspondence; EAP usage; incident history; overtime.

3.  THE SURVEY (work as experienced). The "People at Work" instrument — the validated,
    benchmarked psychosocial risk survey developed with the Queensland regulator, available
    without cost — offered to all operators with anonymity protected.

4.  OBSERVATION (work as done). The assessor attends the room across shift types, including
    night and weekend shifts, and observes the work as it is actually performed — the
    concurrency, the interruptions, the emergency activations.

5.  INTERVIEWS. An interview offered to every operator; structured prompts; and exit
    interviews sought from operators who have recently left the area.

6.  CONVERGENCE AND RISK RATING. The data, survey, observation and interview findings
    triangulated; each hazard rated by duration, frequency and severity as the Code
    provides; the resulting risk register shared with the operators.

7.  CONTROL SELECTION IN CONSULTATION. A controls workshop with the operators; controls
    considered in the order the Regulation requires; each adopted control given an owner
    and an implementation date. The Proposals for Consultation are offered as a starting
    set.

8.  REVIEW. Implemented controls carry review dates; a small set of indicators is tracked
    (fatigue-rule compliance, complaint response times, leave-against-demand correlation);
    the survey repeated at twelve months.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 — MATTERS PROPOSED FOR INCLUSION IN SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(a)  A critical-incident debrief and peer-support step following defined trigger events
     (emergency codes, deaths, abusive or distressing calls), as is standard in comparable
     emergency communications settings.

(b)  Post-call recovery arrangements — a short off-queue recovery after distressing calls —
     and a defined surge protocol for periods when demand exceeds capacity.

(c)  The physical work environment of the room: headset acoustic protection, noise,
     console ergonomics, screen-based work breaks, and lighting.

(d)  A quality-assurance framework including call-recording review, introduced in
     consultation and framed as protective — an objective record that resolves complaints
     and accusations without them resting on the operator.

(e)  An evidence-based occupancy standard, so that sustained utilisation remains within
     recognised bounds for call-handling work.

(f)  Service standards on departments for the supply of roster and contact-detail updates
     to the Switchboard, addressing the recurring cause of misdirected calls at its source.

(g)  A documented training and competency framework for the room's functions, including
     any shift-supervision function.

(h)  A standing, anonymous route for operators to raise hazards, with feedback guaranteed,
     measured at the twelve-month review.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 — CONSULTATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I offer this methodology as an input to the scoping of the assessment, and ask that the
scoping discussion address each phase and each proposed scope item, with the outcome
recorded. I will attend any discussion at any time, with a support person and my union
representative present.

Cory Lea Shepherd
AO3, Switchboard Services, Logan Hospital
0417 400 227 · coryshepherd1@hotmail.com

WHY THIS WORKS
- ⭐ THE REQUEST COMES FROM THE UNION (organiser-signed, delegate named) = institutional
  correspondence a CE must answer, not an employee letter HR can absorb; engages cl 3.1.5;
  immune to any leverage characterisation; survives his settlement.
- His account annexed = personal testimony carried inside an institutional ask, which is
  where it is strongest.
- Union first = the request gets an owner who survives his settlement; delegate status is

  the HSR election get a proper home.
- CE letter asks for NOTHING personal — no pay, no return, no dispute — so it cannot be

0417 400 227 · coryshepherd1@hotmail.com

WHY THIS IS THE HARDEST-HITTING REMAINING MOVE
- The fork has no safe exit: an authorisation EXISTS (the CE personally authorised the
  conflicted line to keep deciding — she now owns every subsequent act, incl. the leave
  push and the insurer communication) or it DOESN'T (officers acted in a disclosed-conflict
  matter with CE knowledge documented from 12:45 on day one).
- It ties the ART revelation to the conflict question in one sentence, at the only level
  with power over both.
- It is the s 101 produce-or-concede structure, applied one level up.
- It keeps HIS record perfect: no allegation, no names, a request for the ordinary
  separation of functions — the same ask as 3 Aug, now with a dated event showing why.
- Whatever answer comes (or doesn't) feeds: Stage 2 (independent decision-maker ask),
  the s 32(5) manner case, and any later adverse-action defence (knowledge + persistence).
