PART 4 — QUESTIONS FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

These four questions ask a doctor to answer matters which the Health Service's own policy and
the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 place with the Health Service. I ask that the Health
Service answer them, after which the properly medical component of each can be put to my
practitioners.

4.1  QUESTION 2 — is there a performance or conduct process?

The question asks whether I can "follow a reasonable and lawful direction issued by [my]
supervisor" and "participate in discussions in relation to [my] workplace performance and/or
conduct."

These are not questions about capacity to perform the genuine occupational requirements of my
role. They concern readiness for a management process. Either such a process is on foot
concerning me — in which case I am entitled to be told of it, given particulars, and afforded
procedural fairness — or there is not, in which case the questions do not serve the stated
purpose of this inquiry.

  → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: please confirm whether any performance or conduct process
    concerning me is on foot or contemplated, and if so provide particulars.

  → THEN, IF APPROPRIATE, FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Does the employee have capacity to participate
    in ordinary workplace meetings and supervision, and are any supports required?"

The premise of Question 2 is separately incorrect and is addressed at Part 5.

4.2  QUESTION 3 — is the workplace safe?

The question asks whether I am "medically fit to return to their substantive role under the
existing reporting arrangements, including working with and reporting to their current line
manager." That asks a treating doctor to certify that a workplace arrangement is safe. Under
section 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 that duty rests with the Health Service; under
the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 a psychosocial
hazard is a feature of the work, identified and controlled by the PCBU; and G03 clause 1
requires proper consideration of that Code. A doctor can advise on me; a doctor cannot assess
the Health Service's reporting arrangements.

The letter of 7 July 2026 records that the Health Service "does not have sufficient information
to understand the nature of these matters or assess whether they present any psychosocial
hazards or risks". That gap is real, and it is closed by the Health Service consulting and
assessing — sections 47 to 49 require consultation with workers directly affected, and none has
occurred since 26 June 2026. For completeness, the matters concern how work in the unit is
organised and decided: how patient safety concerns raised at the switchboard are escalated; how
changes to work and roster have been introduced; fatigue and recovery between shifts; and staff
input into decisions affecting the work. They are workplace matters, which is why the assessment
belongs with the Health Service.

  → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: a risk assessment of the Switchboard work environment addressing
    the psychosocial hazards identified. Clause 7.2.1 of the certified agreement provides the
    mechanism.

  → THEN FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Are any adjustments recommended in relation to supervision
    arrangements, and if so, what are they in functional terms?"

4.3  QUESTION 6 — what are the genuine occupational requirements?

The question asks whether I can "fulfill the full inherent requirements of [my] Role ...
without restrictions or modifications to duties."

This applies the wrong test. G03 states its purpose as assisting employees "to meet the genuine
occupational requirements of their role by applying principles of reasonable adjustment," and
at clause 3 provides that adjustments "should support the employee to undertake the genuine
occupational requirements of their role, without risk to their own health and safety or that of
others in the workplace." Section 34 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 is to the same effect.
Neither asks whether an employee can perform a role without adjustment.

A clinician also cannot determine which duties are genuine occupational requirements. That is
the employer's determination. The Health Service has itself already made part of it: its letter
states that "established process for client complaints received by Switchboard employees is for
immediate escalation and management by the Health Service Client Liaison Officer and/or
Manager, Switchboard Services," and the Role Description at Attachment 2 contains no
complaint-handling responsibility.

  → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: identify which duties of the role it says are genuine occupational
    requirements, having regard to the Role Description at Attachment 2.

  → THEN FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Can the employee perform the genuine occupational requirements
    of the role with the adjustments you have recommended?"

4.4  QUESTION 9 — can the adjustments be accommodated?

The question asks: "If we are not able to accommodate the restrictions you have recommended, is
Mr Shepherd able to safely return to the workplace?"

This presupposes an inability to accommodate before any accommodation has been assessed. G03
clause 2 provides that unjustifiable hardship "is tested against the whole organisation, not a
division or unit within the organisation," and that "the onus is on Queensland Health, as the
employer, to prove an adjustment is unreasonable, not on the person to prove that it is
reasonable."

The question therefore asks my doctor to answer the final step first, on a hypothetical the
Health Service has constructed and not yet tested, and on which the onus is not mine.

  → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: assess the recommended adjustments against the whole organisation.
    If it considers any cannot be accommodated, identify which and its reasons.

  → THEN, IF NECESSARY, the question can be put to my practitioner properly.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 — THE QUESTION I ASK BE WITHDRAWN, AND A CORRECTION OF FACT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1  WITHDRAWAL REQUESTED

Q1(b)  "What is the clinical basis for identifying these specific workplace stressors as
       contributing to the exacerbation of Mr Shepherd's condition."
       This is not a question a general practitioner can properly answer. The clinical basis
       for a psychiatric causal formulation is a matter for a psychiatrist.
       It is also a question I ask be withdrawn. For the purpose of identifying controls, what
       matters is that the stressors exacerbate my condition and what controls address them —
       both of which are obtained by Questions 1(d) and 8. The clinical reasoning as to
       causation goes to a matter in issue in WC/2024/227 and is not necessary for the stated
       purpose of this inquiry.

I record that section 124(1) of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 provides that a person "must
not ask another person, either orally or in writing, to supply information on which unlawful
discrimination might be based," and that under section 124(3) the defence requires the
respondent to prove "that the information was reasonably required for a purpose that did not
involve discrimination." Impairment is a protected attribute. I raise this not as a complaint
but so that the Health Service can satisfy itself that each question it presses meets that
standard.

5.2  CORRECTION OF FACT

Question 2 is premised on the statement that "the Health Service is not aware of any concerns
being raised for appropriate management."

That statement is incorrect. Concerns have been raised in writing on multiple occasions,
including a public interest disclosure (PID 24-ESU-1130); a written patient safety report;
correspondence to Human Resources over a period exceeding two years concerning fatigue,
rostering and the management of directory information; a written complaint to the A/Director,
Human Resources Business Partnering dated 3 October 2025; and the matters in WC/2024/227, in which the Health Service filed an objection dated 5 June 2026
under the signature of the Health Service Chief Executive.

I do not ask the Health Service to agree with any of those concerns. I ask only that my
treating practitioner not be asked to answer a question which assumes they were never made. I
request that the correction be provided to Dr Ma in writing before he is asked to answer any
question resting on that premise.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 — DELEGATION AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This is not a personal complaint about any individual. I make no allegation and I ask for no
finding about anyone. My concern is with how the process is being run — who is deciding, on what
material, and under what instrument — and with the support and adjustment that ordinarily apply
when an employee is certified fit with restrictions. G03 clause 1.1 provides for temporary
adjustments so an employee may "continue work during their recovery"; the Workplace
rehabilitation standard requires suitable duties to be actively sought and the worker's
connection with the workplace maintained, for "either a work or non-work-related
injury/illness". I obtained the checklist the Health Service required for that purpose. It
certified me fit with restrictions. What followed was exclusion rather than adjustment.

Due process is the other half: being told what power is being used and who decides; a fair
opportunity to respond before a serious employment consequence; consultation on the matters in
issue; deadlines that are not one-sided; and decisions made by an officer independent of the
matters they concern — what the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of
Practice 2022 calls organisational justice. I do not say any tribunal has found a denial of fair
process; I say that process has not been applied, and I ask that it be.

I asked on 28 July 2026 who is making decisions about me and whether any conflict of interest
has been identified. I have not received a response. Both letters of 31 July 2026 are written in
the first person of the decision-maker and signed by Mr Hughes, Director, Corporate Services;
question 3 asks my doctor about the reporting arrangements within that same directorate, and the
Manager who gave the advice of 2 July 2026 reports within it. The officer determining my return
therefore sits within the arrangements in issue. I ask the Health Service to confirm: (a) the
source and instrument of the delegation; (b) whether any conflict has been identified, declared
and managed, and how; and (c) whether the decisions of 2 and 3 July 2026 were made with the
knowledge or approval of the officer now determining my return.

6.1  A PROPOSED MANAGEMENT OF THE CONFLICT

I propose the ordinary separation of functions: the clinical material held exclusively by the
Injury Management team on a medical-in-confidence basis — which is what the Checklist itself
recommends at Additional Comments 4(c); any decision concerning my capacity or return made by an
officer outside Corporate Services; and implementation — rostering, and putting the adjustments
in place — retained within Corporate Services. The officer steps out of the decision, not out of
the workplace. I record, because it bears on the assessment, that on 3 October 2025 I made a
formal written request for review to the A/Director, HR Business Partnering concerning a process
initiated by the officer who has signed the letters of 31 July 2026; I do not reopen it here.
Code of Conduct clause 1.2 provides that a conflict is not wrongdoing in itself — failing to
disclose and manage one is likely to be.

I have written separately to the Chief Executive today about the conflict and the handling of my
personal information, because section 89 of the Public Sector Act 2022 makes the chief executive
the person to whom a conflict is disclosed. That letter deals with the matter in full.

*** SUPERSEDED — DO NOT SEND ***

To: lbh_InjuryManagement@health.qld.gov.au
Cc: LBH.HRTeam1@health.qld.gov.au
Subject: Response — Request for Medical Information, MSH-INJ-5795 [CLM-317073] — scope of the request, delegation, and continuation of exclusion

Dear Ms Harrison,

I refer to your email of Friday 31 July 2026 timed at 11:43am, and to the two letters of the
same date signed by Mr Scott Hughes, Director, Corporate Services.

I confirm at the outset that I am engaging with this process. I have asked the Health Service
for some weeks to apply its reasonable adjustment framework, and I welcome that it has now
been identified. I will obtain and provide the information sought, within a scope that is
proper and settled.

This letter deals with the framework the Health Service has invoked, the continuation of my
exclusion, time, delegation, a correction of fact, disclosure, and costs, and closes with a
proposal for my return to work. Schedule A responds to each of the nine questions
individually and identifies those I will answer.

1. THE FRAMEWORK THE HEALTH SERVICE HAS INVOKED

The letters cite Human Resources Policy G03 (QH-POL-210) Reasonable adjustment, and sections
17 and 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011. I accept both as the applicable framework.
It is worth recording what that framework provides, because it answers much of what is in
issue.

G03 states its purpose as "to assist employees requiring support to meet the genuine
occupational requirements of their role by applying principles of reasonable adjustment." At
clause 1.1 it provides that temporary reasonable adjustments exist so that employees "continue
work during their recovery." At clause 1.1.1 it confirms that workplace rehabilitation support
is available to employees "who have an injury/illness impacting their current ability to
perform their role, with no claim or entitlement to compensation (health management case)."
At clause 1 it provides that "Managers are responsible for ensuring work environments and
work, do not unreasonably prevent employment for people."

The policy therefore contemplates that an employee in my position remains at work, with
adjustments, while the assessment is undertaken. It does not contemplate exclusion pending
assessment, and I have not been directed to any provision which does.

G03 also provides, at clause 1: "When applying this policy, proper consideration must be given
to the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022, to ensure the
process of providing reasonable adjustments in the workplace, identifies and manages
psychosocial hazards and risks."

That obligation attaches to the process itself, and I ask that it be given effect.

2. THE CONTINUATION OF MY EXCLUSION

I have been held out of the workplace since 3 July 2026 — five weeks — without wages, with my
accrued leave debited, and self-funding the medical costs of the process.

The letter to Dr Ma identifies complaint handling as the restriction in issue. On the same
page, the Health Service states its own position: "established process for client complaints
received by Switchboard employees is for immediate escalation and management by the Health
Service Client Liaison Officer and/or Manager, Switchboard Services." The Role Description at
Attachment 2 contains no complaint-handling responsibility.

The Health Service has therefore confirmed, in writing, that the duty in question is not a
duty of my role. There is accordingly no identified restriction preventing my performance of
the genuine occupational requirements of my position, and no basis for my exclusion to
continue while further information is obtained.

I ask that I be returned to my roster immediately. If the Health Service maintains the
exclusion, I ask that it identify the instrument under which it does so. Sections 17 and 19 of
the Work Health and Safety Act impose duties on the Health Service; they do not confer a power
to exclude a worker who has been certified fit to work with restrictions. If the exclusion is
maintained, I ask that the period be treated as paid special leave and that the debits against
my accrued entitlements from 3 July 2026 be reversed.

I also record that no consultation occurred before the decision of 3 July 2026, or since.
Section 47 of the Work Health and Safety Act requires consultation with workers "who are, or
are likely to be, directly affected by a matter relating to work health or safety." Section 48
requires that I be given a reasonable opportunity "to contribute to the decision-making
process relating to the matter." Section 49 requires consultation when identifying hazards and
assessing risks, when making decisions about ways to eliminate or minimise those risks, when
proposing changes that may affect the health or safety of workers, and when making decisions
about the procedures for monitoring the health of workers. The present request is a procedure
for monitoring my health. I was not consulted on it.

3. TIME

Your letter allows seven calendar days from receipt, expiring 7 August 2026, and expressly
contemplates a reasonable extension. I request one.

The letter was received at 11:43am on Friday 31 July, approximately two hours before a
consultation with Dr Ma of which the Health Service had been notified on 30 July. Nine
questions cannot be put to a practitioner on two hours' notice, and because the scope of the
questions is in issue I cancelled that consultation rather than incur a cost that both the
Health Service and I would have wasted. I will rebook it once the question set is settled.

I propose the response be provided in two parts:

  (a) the questions within Dr Ma's scope — 21 days from the date the Health Service confirms
      the final question set; and
  (b) any question requiring specialist input — on a timeframe set once the Health Service
      confirms which questions it presses and that it will meet the cost. A psychiatric review
      cannot be arranged within seven days, and in the ordinary course will take considerably
      longer.

I do not seek delay; the exclusion is costing me my income. But I ask the Health Service to
note the consequence of its own question set. Several questions can only be answered by a
specialist. If the Health Service presses them it necessarily extends the inquiry, and it
cannot be reasonable to maintain an unpaid exclusion for a period created by the Health
Service's own requirements. That is a further reason why my return to duty, or at minimum my
return to pay, should not await the completion of this process.

4. DELEGATION AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST

I have previously raised by email the question of who is making decisions about me and whether
any conflict of interest has been identified. I have not received an answer. I ask again, and
ask that it be answered in writing on this occasion.

Both letters are written in the first person of the Injury Management Consultant — "I am
seeking further clarification", "I require further information", "I will make a decision
regarding your ability to perform your role" — and are signed by Mr Hughes. Please confirm:

  (a) who is the delegate for any decision concerning my capacity or my return to duty;
  (b) the source and instrument of that delegation; and
  (c) whether any conflict of interest has been identified, declared and managed in relation
      to that decision-maker, and if so, how.

I raise (c) because Question 3 asks my general practitioner to advise whether I am fit to
return "under the existing reporting arrangements, including working with and reporting to
[my] current line manager." Those reporting arrangements sit within Corporate Services, and
the line manager reports to the signatory.

I make no allegation against any individual. I ask that the position be confirmed, consistent
with clause 1.2 of the Code of Conduct for the Queensland Public Service, which provides that
a conflict of interest is not wrongdoing in itself, but that failing to disclose and manage
one is likely to be wrongdoing. I note that the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at
work Code of Practice 2022 identifies poor organisational justice — including a lack of
procedural fairness — as a psychosocial hazard in its own right, and that G03 requires proper
consideration to be given to that Code in applying this very process.

5. A CORRECTION OF FACT

Question 2 is premised on the statement that "the Health Service is not aware of any concerns
being raised for appropriate management."

That statement is incorrect. Concerns have been raised in writing on multiple occasions,
including:

  - a public interest disclosure (PID 24-ESU-1130);
  - a written patient safety report;
  - correspondence to Human Resources over a period exceeding two years concerning fatigue,
    rostering and the management of directory information;
  - a formal complaint in February 2026; and
  - the matters in WC/2024/227, presently before the Queensland Industrial Relations
    Commission, in which the Health Service filed an objection dated 5 June 2026 under the
    signature of the Health Service Chief Executive.

I do not ask the Health Service to agree with any of those concerns. I ask only that my
treating practitioner not be asked to answer a question which assumes they were never made. I
request that the correction be provided to Dr Ma in writing before he is asked to answer any
question resting on that premise.

6. DISCLOSURE — OPTION 1

I adopt option 1. I will obtain the information from my practitioners and provide it. I do not
consent to option 2, and I do not provide an authority for the Health Service to obtain
information directly from my treating practitioners.

G03 clause 3 provides: "Queensland Health acknowledges the right of the person with
disability, condition, cultural considerations or neurodivergence to choose how disclosure of
information occurs." It further provides that "it may only be necessary to share information
when the ability to meet genuine occupational requirements and or individual safety is at risk
and reasonable adjustment is required." My election is the exercise of a right the policy
expressly recognises, and it is not an obstruction of the process.

7. COSTS

I note and accept the confirmation that "MSH will meet your reasonable costs of preparing this
report." For completeness:

  (a) the consultation of 3 July 2026 which produced the Employee Capabilities Checklist was
      invoiced at $150.00 and paid by me on 10 July 2026 (receipt N471065713633). I ask that
      it be reimbursed;
  (b) the rebooked consultation with Dr Ma, and any further consultation required to answer

  (c) if specialist input is required, please confirm the Health Service will meet that cost
      on the same basis.

8. RECORDS

Your email is copied to notes@solv.com.au and refers to a transition to "Solv, a new Injury
Management Case System." Please confirm what personal and health information concerning me is
held in or transmitted to that system, the basis on which it is held, and the arrangements
governing its use and disclosure.

9. PROPOSAL

So that this is not simply a set of objections, I set out what I propose. Each item is within
the Health Service's existing processes and, so far as I can see, requires no material
expenditure and no restructuring.

  (a) Return to duty. That I return to my rostered shifts now, on the restrictions already
      certified in the Employee Capabilities Checklist of 3 July 2026, while the balance of
      this inquiry is completed. This is what G03 clause 1.1 contemplates — adjustments which
      allow an employee to "continue work during their recovery."

  (b) Complaint handling. That the Health Service confirm in writing that complaints received
      by Switchboard staff are escalated in accordance with the process it has itself
      described — immediate escalation to the Client Liaison Officer and/or the Manager,
      Switchboard Services. This is the Health Service's own stated process and requires no
      change to anything.

  (c) Roster predictability. That my roster be published in accordance with the certified
      agreement and not altered without my agreement other than in an emergency.
      Unpredictable rostering is one of the identified stressors, and predictability is the
      adjustment most likely to address it.

  (d) Ordinary procedural fairness. That any concern about my performance or conduct be raised
      with me in writing, with particulars, in accordance with the applicable directive, and
      that I be afforded a support person. I ask for nothing beyond what the Health Service's
      own processes already require.

  (e) A separate contact point. That leave, injury management and human resources matters
      concerning me be handled by an officer outside Switchboard Services rather than by my
      line manager, who wrote to me on 2 July 2026 concerning leave types and my return to
      duty. This does not alter day-to-day supervision and involves no change to reporting
      lines.

  (f) Workplace risk assessment. That the Health Service conduct a risk assessment of the
      Switchboard work environment addressing the psychosocial hazards identified. This is
      required by section 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act and by G03's direction that
      proper consideration be given to the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work
      Code of Practice 2022. Clause 7.2.1 of the Queensland Public Health Sector Certified
      Agreement provides the mechanism. It is also the proper vehicle for the subject matter
      of Question 3.

  (g) Review. That the arrangements be reviewed at six weeks, or earlier if either of us
      considers it necessary.

  (h) Graduated return. If the Health Service prefers, I am willing to return on a graduated
      basis by agreement. I am not seeking to avoid any part of my role.

If any part of this proposal cannot be accommodated, I ask that the Health Service identify
which part and its reasons. I note that under G03 clause 2, unjustifiable hardship "is tested
against the whole organisation, not a division or unit within the organisation," and that "the

I remain willing to return to work, and to do so on terms which are safe for me and workable
for the Health Service. I would be glad to meet to progress that, with a support person

SCHEDULE A — RESPONSE TO THE QUESTIONS OF 31 JULY 2026

THE TEST I HAVE APPLIED

The letter to Dr Ma states the purpose of the request: "to identify and implement any
appropriate workplace controls or reasonable adjustments to support a safe and sustainable
return to his substantive position."

G03 clause 3 sets the same limit: "Reasonable adjustment may need to be supported by medical
or rehabilitation information, where necessary, to either identify required workplace
adjustments and/or assess the suitability of proposed adjustments."

I have therefore asked of each question: is this information necessary to identify required
adjustments, or to assess the suitability of proposed adjustments? Where it is, I will answer
it. Where it is not, I ask that it be withdrawn or reframed, and I have proposed an
alternative in each case.

I record that section 124(1) of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 provides that a person "must
not ask another person, either orally or in writing, to supply information on which unlawful
discrimination might be based," and that under section 124(3) the defence requires the
respondent to prove "that the information was reasonably required for a purpose that did not
involve discrimination." Impairment is a protected attribute. I raise this not as a complaint
but so the Health Service can satisfy itself that each question it presses meets that
standard.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CATEGORY 1 — QUESTIONS I WILL ANSWER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Q1(d)  Whether exposure to the identified stressors presents a foreseeable risk to health or
       safety on return, and what specific workplace controls or adjustments are medically
       necessary to manage that risk.
       → Necessary to identify required adjustments. WILL BE ANSWERED.

Q4     If not able to return under the existing arrangements, the restrictions or adjustments
       recommended, the clinical basis in functional terms, and the anticipated duration and
       review date.
       → Necessary to identify required adjustments. WILL BE ANSWERED.

Q5     What specific activities are encompassed within "complaint handling."
       → Necessary to assess the suitability of a proposed adjustment. WILL BE ANSWERED.
         I note the Health Service's own statement in the same letter that complaints received
         by Switchboard employees are escalated to the Client Liaison Officer and/or Manager,
         Switchboard Services, and that the Role Description at Attachment 2 contains no
         complaint-handling responsibility.

Q8     Specific tasks, situations or environments which may exacerbate the condition.
       → Necessary to identify required adjustments. WILL BE ANSWERED.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CATEGORY 2 — PROPER IN SUBSTANCE, BUT BEYOND A GENERAL PRACTITIONER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Q7     What "working memory is affected under stress" means in functional terms, including how
       it may affect capacity under normal workplace demands and the circumstances likely to
       cause difficulty.
       → This is a legitimate adjustment question. Dr Ma can address it in general terms only;
         a functional cognitive opinion is properly a treating psychiatrist's.

SPECIALIST INPUT — WHAT I PROPOSE

I am willing to obtain a treating psychiatrist's opinion. So that it can be arranged, please
confirm:

  (a) that the Health Service presses Question 7, and identify any part of Questions 1(d), 4
      or 8 on which it requires a specialist rather than a general practitioner's opinion;
  (b) that it will meet the cost, consistent with its confirmation that it will meet my
      reasonable costs; and
  (c) that it accepts the timeframe consequences set out at paragraph 3 of my letter.

Consistent with option 1 and with G03 clause 3, I will obtain that opinion and provide it. I
will settle its scope by reference to the question set the Health Service confirms.

The specialist opinion will address current capacity, functional restrictions and recommended
adjustments. It will not address the aetiology of my condition, which is a matter in issue in
WC/2024/227 and is not necessary for the stated purpose of this inquiry.

I note for completeness that a request to my own treating practitioners rests on a different
footing from an independent medical examination, which is governed by chapter 3 part 8
division 5 of the Public Sector Act 2022 and Directive 04/24, and which has not been invoked.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CATEGORY 3 — QUESTIONS I ASK BE WITHDRAWN OR REFRAMED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am not declining to provide information. I am asking that the questions be directed to the
decision the Health Service says it is making.

Q1(a)  "When was Mr Shepherd first diagnosed with MDD?"
       → The date of a historical diagnosis cannot identify a required adjustment, nor assess
         the suitability of a proposed one. It does not meet the limit in G03 clause 3, and it
         is information on which discrimination might be based within the meaning of section
         124 of the Anti-Discrimination Act. I ask that it be withdrawn.
         PROPOSED INSTEAD: "What is the employee's current condition and prognosis, and over
         what period are the recommended adjustments expected to be required?"

Q1(b)  "What is the clinical basis for identifying these specific workplace stressors as
       contributing to the exacerbation of Mr Shepherd's condition."
       → For the purpose of identifying controls, what matters is that the stressors
         exacerbate my condition and what controls address them — both of which are obtained
         by Questions 1(d) and 8. The clinical reasoning as to causation is not necessary for
         that purpose, and is a matter in issue in WC/2024/227. I ask that it be withdrawn.

Q1(c)  Whether the stressors are based "solely on Mr Shepherd's self-report, your own clinical
       assessment, or other medical information/reports available to you."
       → This goes to the reliability of the causal history rather than to any adjustment, and
         does not meet the limit in G03 clause 3. I ask that it be withdrawn. To the extent
         the question seeks to identify other medical reports concerning me held by third
         parties, I do not consent to that inquiry.

Q2     Whether I am "able to follow a reasonable and lawful direction issued by [my]
       supervisor" and can "participate in discussions in relation to [my] workplace
       performance and/or conduct."
       → These are not questions about capacity to perform the genuine occupational
         requirements of my role. They concern readiness for a management process. Either
         there is a performance or conduct process on foot concerning me — in which case I am
         entitled to be told of it and given particulars, and to procedural fairness — or
         there is not, in which case the questions do not serve the stated purpose. Please
         confirm which is the case. The premise of the question is separately incorrect and is
         addressed at paragraph 5 of my letter.
         PROPOSED INSTEAD: "Does the employee have capacity to participate in ordinary
         workplace meetings and supervision, and are any supports required?"

Q3     Whether I am "medically fit to return to their substantive role under the existing
       reporting arrangements, including working with and reporting to their current line
       manager."
       → This asks a treating doctor to certify that a workplace arrangement is safe. Under
         section 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act that duty rests with the Health Service,
         and under the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022
         a psychosocial hazard is a feature of the work, to be identified and controlled by
         the person conducting the business or undertaking. G03 requires proper consideration
         of that Code in applying this process. The assessment sought is a workplace risk
         assessment, not a medical opinion.
         PROPOSED INSTEAD: "Are any adjustments recommended in relation to supervision
         arrangements, and if so, what are they in functional terms?" — together with a
         workplace risk assessment conducted by the Health Service, as proposed at paragraph
         9(f) of my letter.

Q6     Whether I am "able to fulfill the full inherent requirements of [my] Role ... without
       restrictions or modifications to duties."
       → This applies the wrong test. G03 states its purpose as assisting employees "to meet
         the genuine occupational requirements of their role by applying principles of
         reasonable adjustment," and at clause 3 provides that adjustments "should support the
         employee to undertake the genuine occupational requirements of their role, without
         risk to their own health and safety or that of others in the workplace." Section 34
         of the Anti-Discrimination Act is to the same effect. Neither asks whether an
         employee can perform the role without adjustment.
         PROPOSED INSTEAD: "Can the employee perform the genuine occupational requirements of
         the role with the adjustments you have recommended?"

Q9     "If we are not able to accommodate the restrictions you have recommended, is Mr
       Shepherd able to safely return to the workplace?"
       → This presupposes an inability to accommodate before any accommodation has been
         assessed. G03 clause 2 provides that unjustifiable hardship "is tested against the
         whole organisation, not a division or unit within the organisation," and that "the
         onus is on Queensland Health, as the employer, to prove an adjustment is
         unreasonable, not on the person to prove that it is reasonable." The question asks my
         doctor to answer the final step first, on a hypothetical the Health Service has
         constructed and not yet tested, and on which the onus is not mine. I ask that it be
         withdrawn as premature.
         PROPOSED INSTEAD: once the Health Service has assessed the recommended adjustments
         against the whole organisation, if it considers any cannot be accommodated, I ask
         that it identify which and its reasons, so that the question can then be put
         properly.

def esc(t):
    t = t.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;")
    return re.sub(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", r"<b>\1</b>", t)

def alloc_table():
    data = [[Paragraph("Q", S["cellB"]), Paragraph("SUBJECT", S["cellB"]),
             Paragraph("PROPOSED RESPONDENT", S["cellB"])]]
    for q, subj, who in ALLOC:
        data.append([Paragraph(esc(q), S["cellB"]),
                     Paragraph(esc(subj), S["cellL"]),
                     Paragraph(esc(who), S["cellL"])])
    t = Table(data, colWidths=[14*mm, 74*mm, 74*mm], repeatRows=1)
    st = [("VALIGN", (0,0), (-1,-1), "TOP"),
          ("BACKGROUND", (0,0), (-1,0), BAND),
          ("LINEBELOW", (0,0), (-1,0), 0.6, RULE),
          ("LINEBELOW", (0,1), (-1,-2), 0.25, colors.HexColor("#DDDDDD")),
          ("BOX", (0,0), (-1,-1), 0.6, RULE),
          ("TOPPADDING", (0,0), (-1,-1), 3.5),
          ("BOTTOMPADDING", (0,0), (-1,-1), 3.5),
          ("LEFTPADDING", (0,0), (-1,-1), 5),
          ("RIGHTPADDING", (0,0), (-1,-1), 5)]
    for i, (q, _, who) in enumerate(ALLOC, start=1):
        if who.startswith("Health Service"):
            st.append(("BACKGROUND", (0, i), (-1, i), colors.HexColor("#F6F6F6")))
    t.setStyle(TableStyle(st))
    return t

def flush():
    global buf, mode
    if not buf:
        return
    txt = " ".join(x.strip() for x in buf).strip()
    buf = []
    if not txt:
        return
    flow.append(Paragraph(esc(txt), S[mode]))
    mode = "body"

while i < len(lines):
    ln = lines[i]
    s = ln.strip()
    i += 1

    if ln.startswith("------"):
        flush(); continue

    if not s:
        flush(); continue

    if s == "IN SUMMARY" or re.match(r"^PART \d+", s):
        flush()
        flow.append(Paragraph(esc(s), S["h1"]))
        continue

    if re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\s+[A-Z]", s):
        flush()
        flow.append(Paragraph(esc(s), S["h2"]))
        continue

    # the ASCII allocation table -> real table
    if s.startswith("Q") and "SUBJECT" in s and "RESPONDENT" in s:
        flush()
        flow.append(Spacer(1, 2))
        flow.append(alloc_table())
        flow.append(Spacer(1, 6))
        # consume the ASCII rows: skip to the paragraph after the table block
        while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith("Of the nine questions"):
            i += 1
        continue

    if s.startswith("→") or s.startswith("→"):
        flush()
        mode = "arrow"
        buf = [s]
        # continuation lines
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(
                r"^\s*(→|→|\(|PART|\d+\.\d+)", lines[i]) and lines[i].startswith("    "):
            buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
        flush()
        continue

    if re.match(r"^\([a-z0-9]+\)\s", s) or re.match(r"^[0-9]+\.\s", s):
        flush()
        mode = "item"
        buf = [s]
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and not re.match(
                r"^\s*(\(|→|→|PART|\d+\.\d+|Q\d)", lines[i].strip()) and lines[i].startswith("    "):
            buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
        flush()
        continue

    if re.match(r"^Q\d\(?[a-d]?\)?\s{2,}", s):
        flush()
        mode = "qref"
        buf = [s]
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and lines[i].startswith("       "):
            buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
        flush()
        continue

    if ln.startswith("    “") or ln.startswith('    "'):
        flush()
        mode = "quote"
        buf = [s]
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and lines[i].startswith("    "):
            buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
        flush()
        continue

    buf.append(s)

flush()

def alloc_table():
    data = [[Paragraph(h, S["cellb"]) for h in HDR]]
    for q, ques, who, basis in ROWS:
        data.append([Paragraph("<b>%s</b>" % q, S["cell"]),
                     Paragraph(ques, S["cellq"]),
                     Paragraph(who, S["cell"]),
                     Paragraph(basis, S["cell"])])
    t = Table(data, colWidths=[13*mm, 54*mm, 40*mm, 63*mm], repeatRows=1)
    st = [("GRID",(0,0),(-1,-1),0.4,RULE),
          ("BACKGROUND",(0,0),(-1,0),BAND),
          ("VALIGN",(0,0),(-1,-1),"TOP"),
          ("LEFTPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4),("RIGHTPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4),
          ("TOPPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4),("BOTTOMPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4)]
    for i in range(1, len(data)):
        if i % 2 == 0: st.append(("BACKGROUND",(0,i),(-1,i),LITE))
    t.setStyle(TableStyle(st))
    return t

import subprocess
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm
from reportlab.lib import colors
from reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle
from reportlab.lib.enums import TA_JUSTIFY
from reportlab.platypus import (BaseDocTemplate, Frame, PageTemplate, Paragraph,
                                Spacer, Table, TableStyle, HRFlowable)

INK  = colors.HexColor("#111111"); MUTE = colors.HexColor("#555555")
RULE = colors.HexColor("#9a9a9a"); BAND = colors.HexColor("#ECECEC")
BOX  = colors.HexColor("#BBBBBB")

def P(n, **kw):
    b = dict(fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=9.2, leading=12.8, textColor=INK); b.update(kw)
    return ParagraphStyle(n, **b)
S = {
 "title": P("t", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=12.5, leading=15.5, spaceAfter=1),
 "sub":   P("s", fontSize=9.4, leading=12.4, textColor=MUTE, spaceAfter=8),
 "meta":  P("m", fontSize=8.7, leading=12),
 "h1":    P("h1", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=10, leading=13, spaceBefore=12, spaceAfter=5),
 "body":  P("b", alignment=TA_JUSTIFY, spaceAfter=6),
 "q":     P("q", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=9.2, leading=12.6,
            leftIndent=15, firstLineIndent=-15, spaceBefore=8, spaceAfter=4),
 "qs":    P("qs", fontSize=9.0, leading=12.4, leftIndent=15, spaceAfter=4),
 "note":  P("n", fontSize=8.4, leading=11.5, textColor=MUTE, spaceAfter=5),
 "cell":  P("c", fontSize=8.6, leading=11.6),
}
def para(t, s="body"): return Paragraph(t, S[s])
def rule(): return HRFlowable(width="100%", thickness=0.6, color=RULE, spaceBefore=4, spaceAfter=7)

def answerbox(h=26*mm):
    t = Table([[""]], colWidths=[170*mm], rowHeights=[h])
    t.setStyle(TableStyle([("BOX",(0,0),(-1,-1),0.5,BOX),
                           ("BACKGROUND",(0,0),(-1,-1),colors.white)]))
    return t

def signblock():
    rows = [[Paragraph("<b>Practitioner name</b>", S["cell"]), "",
             Paragraph("<b>Provider no.</b>", S["cell"]), ""],
            [Paragraph("<b>Signature</b>", S["cell"]), "",
             Paragraph("<b>Date</b>", S["cell"]), ""],
            [Paragraph("<b>Practice details / stamp</b>", S["cell"]), "", "", ""]]
    t = Table(rows, colWidths=[34*mm, 60*mm, 22*mm, 54*mm],
              rowHeights=[11*mm, 11*mm, 24*mm])
    t.setStyle(TableStyle([("GRID",(0,0),(-1,-1),0.5,BOX),
                           ("SPAN",(1,2),(3,2)),
                           ("VALIGN",(0,0),(-1,-1),"TOP"),
                           ("LEFTPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4),
                           ("TOPPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),4)]))
    return t

def header(F, who, addr, formref):
    F.append(para("REQUEST FOR MEDICAL INFORMATION — %s" % formref, "title"))
    F.append(para("Questions arising from the correspondence of Metro South Health dated 31 July 2026 "
                  "&nbsp;·&nbsp; Ref MSH-INJ-5795 &nbsp;·&nbsp; CLM-317073", "sub"))
    F.append(Table([[Paragraph("<b>Patient:</b> Mr Cory Shepherd &nbsp; <b>DOB:</b> 11 January 1991<br/>"
                               "<b>Employer:</b> Metro South Health — Logan and Beaudesert Health Service<br/>"
                               "<b>Role:</b> Administration Officer (AO3), Switchboard Services, Logan Hospital "
                               "(permanent full-time, 76 hours per fortnight)", S["meta"]),
                     Paragraph("<b>To:</b> %s<br/>%s<br/><br/><b>Date:</b> 31 July 2026" % (who, addr), S["meta"])]],
                   colWidths=[100*mm, 70*mm],
                   style=TableStyle([("VALIGN",(0,0),(-1,-1),"TOP"),
                                     ("LEFTPADDING",(0,0),(-1,-1),0)])))
    F.append(rule())
    F.append(para("<b>This form is provided by the patient, Mr Cory Shepherd. It is not a document of "
                  "Metro South Health.</b> The Health Service issued nine questions on 31 July 2026. Four "
                  "of those are not medical questions and have been returned to the Health Service. The "
                  "questions below are those properly within your field. They are reproduced as the Health "
                  "Service put them.", "note"))
    F.append(para("Metro South Health has advised in writing that it \"will meet your reasonable costs of "
                  "preparing this report\". Invoices are to be sent to Ms Michelle Harrison, Injury "
                  "Management Consultant, Human Resources, Logan and Beaudesert Health Service, "
                  "lbh_InjuryManagement@health.qld.gov.au.", "note"))

def build(path, who, addr, formref, intro, questions, closing, extra_intro=None):
    F = []
    header(F, who, addr, formref)
    F.append(para(intro, "h1"))
    if extra_intro: F.append(para(extra_intro, "body"))
    for label, text, hint, h in questions:
        F.append(para("%s&nbsp;&nbsp;%s" % (label, text), "q"))
        if hint: F.append(para(hint, "qs"))
        F.append(answerbox(h)); F.append(Spacer(1, 5))
    F.append(para(closing, "note"))
    F.append(Spacer(1, 6))
    F.append(signblock())
    def deco(c, d):
        c.saveState(); c.setFont("Helvetica", 7.6); c.setFillColor(MUTE)
        c.drawString(20*mm, 12*mm, "Provided by Cory Shepherd  ·  MSH-INJ-5795  ·  %s" % formref)
        c.drawRightString(190*mm, 12*mm, "Page %d" % d.page); c.restoreState()
    raw = "/tmp/_form_%s.pdf" % formref.replace(" ","_")
    doc = BaseDocTemplate(raw, pagesize=A4, leftMargin=20*mm, rightMargin=20*mm,
                          topMargin=18*mm, bottomMargin=20*mm, title=formref)
    doc.addPageTemplates([PageTemplate(id="n",
        frames=[Frame(20*mm, 20*mm, 170*mm, 259*mm, id="f")], onPage=deco)])
    doc.build(F)
    subprocess.run(["qpdf","--linearize","--",raw,path], check=False)
    subprocess.run(["exiftool","-overwrite_original","-all=","-Title=%s" % formref, path],
                   check=False, capture_output=True)
    print("built:", path)

>>> drafts/SEND_31JUL/build_email_pdfs.py :: text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Render the five 3 Aug 2026 email bodies as individual PDFs, then stitch the six
outgoing documents into one combined attachments PDF. Metadata scrubbed like build_letters."""
import os, re, subprocess
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "out")

def read(p):
    with open(os.path.join(HERE, p)) as f:
        return f.read()

def block(paste, start, end):
    t = read("EMAILS_TO_PASTE_3AUG.txt")
    i = t.index(start); j = t.index(end, i)
    seg = t[i:j]
    m = re.search(r"^-{40,}\n(.*?)\n-{40,}", seg, re.S | re.M)
    return m.group(1)

EMAILS = [
    ("EMAIL_1_Response_HR_3Aug2026.pdf", "Email 1 — Response (RFMI) — to Human Resources", read("RFMI_RESPONSE_EMAIL.txt")),
    ("EMAIL_2_Request_HR_3Aug2026.pdf", "Email 2 — Request under clause 10.3.2 — to Human Resources",
     "TO: LBH.HRTeam1@health.qld.gov.au\nCC: Emily Petering; Heath Moran\nSUBJECT: Request under clause 10.3.2 — change in the way I work — C Shepherd, MSH-INJ-5795\n\n" + block(None, "EMAIL 2", "EMAIL 3")),
    ("EMAIL_3_Dispute_Taylor_HR_3Aug2026.pdf", "Email 3 — Notice of dispute — to C Taylor and Human Resources",
     "TO: chloe.taylor3@health.qld.gov.au; LBH.HRTeam1@health.qld.gov.au\nCC: Emily Petering; Heath Moran\nSUBJECT: Notice of dispute — clause 1.11 — attendance, roster, leave and pay from 26 June 2026\n\n" + block(None, "EMAIL 3", "EMAIL 4")),
    ("EMAIL_4_CE_3Aug2026.pdf", "Email 4 — The Chief Executive, Metro South Health",
     "TO: MetroSouthCorro@health.qld.gov.au (Office of the Chief Executive) — no Cc\nSUBJECT: Attention Ms Noelle Cridland, Chief Executive — Conflict of interest and information handling — C Shepherd, MSH-INJ-5795\n\n" + block(None, "EMAIL 4", "BEFORE YOU SEND")),
]

def render(fname, title, body):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, fname)
    c = canvas.Canvas(path, pagesize=A4)
    w, h = A4
    margin = 22 * mm
    y = h - margin
    c.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 11)
    c.drawString(margin, y, title)
    y -= 6 * mm
    c.setFont("Helvetica", 8.5)
    c.drawString(margin, y, "Sent Monday 3 August 2026 — record copy of the email body as sent")
    y -= 8 * mm
    c.setFont("Courier", 8.6)
    for raw in body.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        while True:
            if y < margin:
                c.showPage(); y = h - margin; c.setFont("Courier", 8.6)
            if len(line) <= 100:
                c.drawString(margin, y, line); y -= 4.1 * mm; break
            cut = line.rfind(" ", 0, 100)
            cut = cut if cut > 0 else 100
            c.drawString(margin, y, line[:cut]); y -= 4.1 * mm
            line = "  " + line[cut:].lstrip()
    c.setTitle(title); c.setAuthor(""); c.setSubject(""); c.setCreator(""); c.setProducer("")
    c.save()
    print("built", path)
    return path

built = [render(*e) for e in EMAILS]

DOCS = ["RFMI_Response_and_Allocation_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
        "PROPOSAL_Return_to_Work_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
        "NOTICE_Appointments_and_Costs_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
        "REQUEST_Change_in_the_way_I_work_cl10.3_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
        "NOTICE_OF_DISPUTE_cl1.11_Stage1.pdf",
        "LETTER_Conflict_and_Information_Handling_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf"]
stitched = os.path.join(OUT, "Shepherd_Documents_MSH-INJ-5795_3Aug2026.pdf")
subprocess.run(["qpdf", "--empty", "--pages"] + [os.path.join(OUT, d) for d in DOCS] + ["--", stitched], check=True)

import pikepdf
for p in built + [stitched]:
    pdf = pikepdf.open(p, allow_overwriting_input=True)
    with pdf:
        try:
            del pdf.Root.Metadata
        except (AttributeError, KeyError):
            pass
        try:
            del pdf.docinfo
        except (AttributeError, KeyError):
            pass
        pdf.trailer["/Info"] = pdf.make_indirect(pikepdf.Dictionary())
        pdf.save(p)
print("stitched", stitched)

"""Builds the two standalone letters that force a response under a power:

  1. FWA_REQUEST_cl10.3.txt          -> clause 10.3.2 flexible working request (21-day clock)
  2. DISPUTE_NOTICE_cl1.11_STAGE1.txt -> clause 1.11.2(a) Stage 1 dispute notice

Same house style as build_alloc_pdf.py. Metadata scrubbed on the way out.
"""
import re, subprocess, sys
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm
from reportlab.lib import colors
from reportlab.lib.styles import ParagraphStyle
from reportlab.lib.enums import TA_JUSTIFY
from reportlab.platypus import (BaseDocTemplate, Frame, PageTemplate, Paragraph,
                                Spacer, HRFlowable)

BASE = "/home/user/Personalproject/wc2024227/drafts/SEND_31JUL"
OUTD = "/home/user/Personalproject/wc2024227/drafts/out"

INK = colors.HexColor("#111111")
MUTE = colors.HexColor("#555555")
RULE = colors.HexColor("#999999")

S = {
 "title": ParagraphStyle("title", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=13.5, leading=17,
                         textColor=INK, spaceAfter=2),
 "sub":   ParagraphStyle("sub", fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=10, leading=13,
                         textColor=MUTE, spaceAfter=8),
 "meta":  ParagraphStyle("meta", fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=8.8, leading=12.5,
                         textColor=INK),
 "h1":    ParagraphStyle("h1", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=10.2, leading=13,
                         textColor=INK, spaceBefore=13, spaceAfter=5),
 "h2":    ParagraphStyle("h2", fontName="Helvetica-Bold", fontSize=9.2, leading=12,
                         textColor=INK, spaceBefore=9, spaceAfter=3),
 "body":  ParagraphStyle("body", fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=9.1, leading=12.8,
                         textColor=INK, alignment=TA_JUSTIFY, spaceAfter=6),
 "quote": ParagraphStyle("quote", fontName="Helvetica-Oblique", fontSize=8.9, leading=12.4,
                         textColor=INK, leftIndent=14, rightIndent=10, spaceAfter=6),
 "item":  ParagraphStyle("item", fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=9.1, leading=12.8,
                         textColor=INK, leftIndent=16, firstLineIndent=-11,
                         alignment=TA_JUSTIFY, spaceAfter=5),
 "sig":   ParagraphStyle("sig", fontName="Helvetica", fontSize=9.1, leading=12.8,
                         textColor=INK, spaceAfter=2),
}

DOCS = [
 dict(src="FWA_REQUEST_cl10.3.txt",
      out="REQUEST_Change_in_the_way_I_work_cl10.3_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
      title="Request for a change in the way I work",
      sub="Clause 10.3.2, Certified Agreement (No. 12) 2025 &#183; s 27, Industrial Relations Act 2016 (Qld)",
      foot="Cory Lea Shepherd · MSH-INJ-5795 · Request under clause 10.3.2 — decision due within 21 days (cl 10.3.6)"),

      sub="Clause 1.11.2(a), Certified Agreement (No. 12) 2025",
      foot="Cory Lea Shepherd · Notice of dispute under clause 1.11 — Stage 1"),

      foot="Cory Lea Shepherd · MSH-INJ-5795 · Conflict of interest, delegation and information handling"),
 dict(src="PROPOSAL_RETURN_TO_WORK.txt",
      out="PROPOSAL_Return_to_Work_MSH-INJ-5795.pdf",
      title="Proposal for Return to Work",
      sub="Accompanying the Response to the Request for Medical Information &#183; MSH-INJ-5795",
      foot="Cory Lea Shepherd · MSH-INJ-5795 · Proposal for Return to Work"),
]


def esc(t):
    t = t.replace("&", "&amp;").replace("<", "&lt;").replace(">", "&gt;")
    return re.sub(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", r"<b>\1</b>", t)


def build(spec):
    lines = open("%s/%s" % (BASE, spec["src"]), encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
    flow = [Paragraph(spec["title"], S["title"]),
            Paragraph(spec["sub"], S["sub"])]

    # the To/Cc/Date/Subject block is everything before the first rule
    i = 0
    head = []
    while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].startswith("------"):
        if lines[i].strip():
            head.append(lines[i].rstrip())
        i += 1
    # drop the title lines already rendered above
    head = [h for h in head if not h.startswith(("REQUEST FOR", "NOTICE OF DISPUTE",
                                                 "NOTICE OF MEDICAL", "ARRANGEMENTS FOR", "Request for Medical",
                                                 "CONFLICT OF INTEREST", "Section 89,",
                                                 "PROPOSAL FOR RETURN", "Accompanying the Response",
                                                 "Clause 10.3.2,", "Section 27,",
                                                 "Clause 1.11.2(a),"))]
    if head:
        flow.append(Paragraph("<br/>".join(esc(h).replace("  ", "&nbsp;&nbsp;") for h in head),
                              S["meta"]))
        flow.append(Spacer(1, 5))
    flow.append(HRFlowable(width="100%", thickness=0.8, color=RULE, spaceAfter=2))

    buf, mode = [], "body"

    def flush():
        nonlocal buf, mode
        if not buf:
            return
        txt = " ".join(x.strip() for x in buf).strip()
        buf = []
        if txt:
            flow.append(Paragraph(esc(txt), S[mode]))
        mode = "body"

    while i < len(lines):
        ln = lines[i]
        s = ln.strip()
        i += 1

        if ln.startswith("------"):
            flush(); continue
        if not s:
            flush(); continue

        if re.match(r"^\d+\.\s+[A-Z]", s):
            flush(); flow.append(Paragraph(esc(s), S["h1"])); continue
        if re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\s+[A-Z]", s):
            flush(); flow.append(Paragraph(esc(s), S["h2"])); continue

        if re.match(r"^\([a-z0-9]+\)\s", s):
            flush(); mode = "item"; buf = [s]
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and \
                    not re.match(r"^\(", lines[i].strip()) and lines[i].startswith("    "):
                buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
            flush(); continue

        if ln.startswith('     "') or ln.startswith("     “"):
            flush(); mode = "quote"; buf = [s]
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].strip() and lines[i].startswith("     "):
                buf.append(lines[i]); i += 1
            flush(); continue

        if s in ("Yours sincerely,",) or s.startswith("Cory Lea Shepherd") or \
           s.startswith("AO3, Switchboard") or "coryshepherd1@hotmail.com" in s:
            flush(); flow.append(Paragraph(esc(s), S["sig"])); continue

        buf.append(s)

    flush()

    def deco(canv, doc):
        canv.saveState()
        canv.setFont("Helvetica", 7.2)
        canv.setFillColor(MUTE)
        canv.drawString(18*mm, 12*mm, spec["foot"])
        canv.drawRightString(192*mm, 12*mm, "Page %d" % doc.page)
        canv.setStrokeColor(RULE); canv.setLineWidth(0.4)
        canv.line(18*mm, 15*mm, 192*mm, 15*mm)
        canv.restoreState()

    raw = "/tmp/_letter_raw.pdf"
    out = "%s/%s" % (OUTD, spec["out"])
    doc = BaseDocTemplate(raw, pagesize=A4,
                          leftMargin=18*mm, rightMargin=18*mm,
                          topMargin=16*mm, bottomMargin=20*mm,
                          title=spec["title"], author="", subject="", creator="", producer="")
    frame = Frame(doc.leftMargin, doc.bottomMargin, doc.width, doc.height, id="f")
    doc.addPageTemplates([PageTemplate(id="p", frames=[frame], onPage=deco)])
    doc.build(flow)

    subprocess.run(["qpdf", "--empty", "--pages", raw, "1-z", "--", out], check=True)
    import pikepdf
    with pikepdf.open(out, allow_overwriting_input=True) as p:
        p.trailer.get("/Info") and p.trailer.__delitem__("/Info")
        if "/Metadata" in p.Root:
            del p.Root["/Metadata"]
        p.save(out)
    print("built", out)


for spec in DOCS:
    build(spec)

!! SUPERSEDED - DO NOT SEND.  Marked 1 August 2026.

Good afternoon Michelle,

Thank you for your email of 29 July 2026.

This email is sent on Thursday 30 July 2026. My appointment with Dr Ma is Friday 31 July 2026 at 2:00 pm. The Health Service's questions and completed forms (or the same information by email) are required before that time.

THE SEQUENCE

I was working my rostered shifts. Following my request to temporarily reduce my ordinary hours from 0.6 to 0.5 FTE for two weeks, I was told I could not work until I completed an Employee Capability Checklist. I obtained and provided that checklist on 3 July 2026. I was then told I still could not work, pending a review. The requirement has since changed again - to further medical clarification, for which no timeframe has been given.

I was not absent and I was not seeking to recommence. I had been performing the role on reduced hours within my certified restrictions for approximately twelve months. I mention this because the questions to Dr Ma should be directed to that situation.

I have elected to take the request to Dr Ma myself, and I have booked an appointment for 2:00 pm on Friday 31 July 2026.

WHAT I NEED BEFORE 2:00 PM FRIDAY 31 JULY 2026

1. The Health Service's questions for Dr Ma, or completed Attachment 1.
2. Completed Attachment 2, or the same information by email.
3. Confirmation of who will be responding before the appointment.
4. Reimbursement of the $150.00 I have already paid, and the name and address to which the practice should direct the invoice for Friday's consultation.

If the forms are not convenient, the same information in an email is equally welcome - before 2:00 pm Friday.

If the questions are not received in time, I will attend the appointment regardless and ask Dr Ma to address my capacity and restrictions against the duties in the role description (attached). I will forward his response to you. I would prefer to put the Health Service's own questions to him, which is why I ask now.

ABOUT THE ATTACHMENTS

To make this as straightforward as possible, I have attached two one-page forms.

Attachment 1 - Duty / Restriction Mapping - sets out the twelve key responsibilities listed in the AO3 role description (also attached). If the Health Service indicates which duty or duties it says I cannot perform, and which restriction is said to prevent it, that identifies precisely what Dr Ma needs to address.

Attachment 2 - Psychosocial Hazard Identification - follows the structure of the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022: hazard, source in the work, risk, assessment, controls, consultation. The form also provides for the Health Service to confirm the position if no hazard is identified.

Completing and returning either or both would give me what I need to put to Dr Ma for this step.

1. MY ELECTION

1.1 I will take the request to Dr Ma myself rather than add a further step.

1.2 I do not propose to complete the Employee Authority Form. It is broader than the present request - it extends to disclosures to and from WorkCover Queensland and income protection insurers, and it is open-ended in duration. If a written authority is needed for Dr Ma to respond to a specific request, I am happy to provide one confined to that purpose.

2. COST OF THE CONSULTATIONS

2.1 The consultation of 3 July 2026 was invoiced to me personally - My Doctors Clinic Surfers, invoice 574370, dated 3 July 2026, $150.00 (item WCO002, case conference). I paid that invoice in full on 10 July 2026 (receipt N471065713633, reference 574370 C Shepherd). The invoice and payment receipt are attached.

2.2 A further consultation is booked for 2:00 pm on Friday 31 July 2026 and is expected to attract the same fee.

2.3 Both consultations are required by the Health Service for its own assessment; neither is material I have volunteered. Consistently with the approach taken elsewhere in the public sector, where the entity that requires medical information meets the reasonable costs of obtaining it, I ask:

(a) that the $150.00 I have paid be reimbursed to me; and

(b) that the Health Service provide the name and address to which the practice should direct Friday's invoice, so that the cost of the Health Service's own request is not again met from my funds.

2.4 If the Health Service does not intend to meet these costs, could you please confirm that in writing, together with the basis for that position.

3. THE QUESTIONS I NEED

3.1 Your email states that "further clarification is required regarding your functional capacity and the medical restrictions identified", but does not identify what is unclear. Dr Ma cannot respond to a request in those terms.

3.2 Could you please provide, in writing, before 2:00 pm Friday:

(a) the specific questions the Health Service asks Dr Ma to answer, set out as questions;

(b) for each question, the duty or task to which it relates - Attachment 1 is provided for this purpose;

(c) what in the 3 July Employee Capability Checklist is said to be insufficient - which entry, and why it does not enable the assessment; and

(d) who will consider Dr Ma's response, and the timeframe within which the decision about my duties will then be made.

4. THE ORIGIN OF THE REQUIREMENT

4.1 Could you please confirm the date on which, and the basis on which, the Health Service required me to complete an Employee Capability Checklist. My understanding is that the requirement was raised in response to my request to temporarily reduce my hours. I am not aware of any incident, complaint or performance concern preceding it.

4.2 Could you also please confirm the outcome of that request to reduce my hours, and if no decision has been made, when one will be made and by whom. EB12 clause 10.3 provides that an employee may ask for a change in the way they work, including their ordinary hours of work; that the request may be refused only on reasonable grounds; and that the employer must give written notice of its decision, with reasons, within 21 days.

5. THE RESTRICTIONS AND THE DUTIES (Attachment 1)

5.1 Since your email refers to the inherent requirements of the role, I have compared the restrictions certified on 3 July with the responsibilities set out in the AO3 role description, which Dr Ma reviewed before completing the checklist. Attachment 1 lists those twelve responsibilities as they appear in that document.

5.2 First, the restriction on complaint-handling does not correspond to any responsibility listed in the role description. If the Health Service considers complaint-handling to be an inherent requirement of the position, could you please identify where it appears, or on what other basis it is said to be one.

5.3 Second, the remaining restrictions - the limits on peak weekday day and afternoon shifts, predictable rostering, and a minimum ten-hour break between shifts - go to when I work, not to which duties I perform. They remove none of the responsibilities listed in Attachment 1.

5.4 I note the role description records the position as continuous shift work. I performed that role, on reduced hours and within my certified restrictions, for approximately twelve months, and the Health Service's correspondence of 7 July 2026 records that my restrictions were already being accommodated. If the rostering restrictions are now said to be incompatible with the role, when they were not during that period, could you please identify what has changed.

5.5 Third, reduced ordinary hours are expressly contemplated by the industrial instruments. Clause 8.2 of the Hospital and Health Service General Employees (Queensland Health) Award - State 2015 provides for part-time employment on a regular number of ordinary hours, pro rata to full-time conditions, with a minimum of eight ordinary hours per fortnight. A reduction in hours does not of itself remove any duty from the role. Could you please identify why the reduced hours certified on 3 July are treated differently - that is, what it is about those hours, as distinct from the reasons for them, that prevents the duties of the position from being performed.

5.6 QH-POL-210 applies to all Queensland Health and Hospital and Health Service employees and directs adjustments - including temporary adjustment for rehabilitation and return to work, and for capacity restriction - to enabling an employee to safely perform the genuine occupational requirements of the role. It reflects the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 (Qld), which contemplates reasonable terms and special conditions where job capacity is restricted by impairment (s 34) and permits departure only where unjustifiable hardship is established (ss 5, 35). QH-IMP-401-5 makes managers responsible for identifying suitable duties, guided by medical information, and its application is not limited to accepted workers' compensation claims. Each operates at the level of identified duties, which is what Attachment 1 is directed to.

6. THE CHARACTERISATION OF RISK (Attachment 2)

6.1 Your correspondence of 13, 15 and 29 July 2026 refers to whether my return can be "safely" facilitated, whether the matters identified by Dr Ma "present any psychosocial hazards or risks", and to the health and safety of workers "and others in the workplace". I do not suggest the Health Service should not satisfy itself as to safety.

6.2 However, in the twenty-seven days since 3 July, no incident, complaint or hazard has been identified to me. None was raised during the twelve months I performed the role on reduced hours. No finding of any kind has been made in relation to my performance of this role.

6.3 EB12 clause 7.2 and the Code of Practice proceed by identifying a hazard, assessing the risk, and considering controls, in consultation with workers and health and safety representatives - and they identify psychosocial hazards by reference to features of work and its management. Attachment 2 follows that structure.

6.4 Could you please confirm whether it is asserted that my performing my duties within the certified restrictions would present a risk to me or to any other person and, if so, whether the hazard is said to arise from the work and work system or from me, together with the material relied upon. Attachment 2 provides for both. If no such assertion is intended, could you please confirm that in writing.

6.5 For clarity, my cooperation with the medical request does not suspend the other matters: the restoration of my roster, the treatment of my pay and leave, and the workplace psychosocial assessment remain live in parallel.

7. CONFLICT OF INTEREST

7.1 I raise one further matter, without alleging wrongdoing.

7.2 The requirement that I complete an Employee Capability Checklist was raised by my line manager, Ms Taylor. Ms Taylor is the subject of a complaint which the Ethical Standards Unit determined to be a public interest disclosure, and her conduct is a matter in issue in proceedings before the Queensland Industrial Relations Commission in which she may give evidence.

7.3 The Code of Conduct for the Queensland Public Service provides at clause 1.2 that having a conflict of interest is not unusual and is not wrongdoing in itself, but that failing to disclose and manage it appropriately is likely to be wrongdoing, and that employees will disclose any personal interest that could be seen as influencing the performance of their duties.

7.4 Could you please confirm what involvement Ms Taylor has had in the decisions concerning my attendance, duties and pay since 2 July 2026; whether any conflict of interest has been disclosed and managed, and how; and that decisions concerning my attendance, duties and pay will be made by a person without involvement in those proceedings.

8. SCOPE AND MEETING

8.1 I will provide Dr Ma with the questions and the role description. My consent extends to information concerning my capacity, my restrictions, and their operational application to the duties of my position, and I ask that the questions be limited to what is necessary for that purpose.

8.2 If it would assist, I am willing to meet at short notice - including before Friday - to work through Attachment 1 duty by duty. I would ask that any meeting occur alongside, rather than in place of, a written response.

9. OTHER MATTERS

10. WHAT I ASK

I am conscious that time and cost are accumulating for both of us, and I would prefer to resolve this now, collaboratively, rather than through further process.

11.2 A direction to an employee not to attend work is an exercise of authority. I have asked on more than one occasion for the source of that authority to be identified, and it has not been. Nor have I been told the process under which I am being managed, or the person who made the decision.

11.3 I raise this not as a complaint, but because without it I am unable to understand or respond to the basis on which I am being kept from my substantive position.
