>>> analysis/README.md :: text
# MONTE CARLO — STRATEGY, FRAMING, AND THE TRAPS
> Run 31 July 2026. `montecarlo_strategy.py` · 200,000 trials · results in `MONTECARLO_RESULTS.txt`
> ⚠️ **Priors are judgement calibrated to the documentary record in this repo — not measured
> frequencies.** The value is the *relative* ordering of choices and the tornado, not the absolute
> percentages. Re-run after any material change to the record.

## THE MODEL
**Five substantive blocks**, each given a blue(high)/red(low) range and moved by a **shared
decision-maker disposition** so correlated issues move together:
| Block | Blue | Red | Why the range |
|---|---|---|---|
| No authority for the exclusion | 0.88 | 0.55 | Nothing identified in five weeks; ss 17/19 are duties; G03 says the opposite; PS Act s 104 never used **vs** implied power to direct + a coherent theory Forrest articulated on 7 July |
| Direction unreasonable | 0.85 | 0.45 | No risk assessment, no consultation, certificate of fitness, unanswered question **vs** the 5 May request was legitimate and TC Alfred is real |
| Leave debiting unlawful | 0.80 | 0.38 | s 105 never invoked; the absence is MSH's own act **vs** he was not attending and QSuper IP is his own claim |
| No psychosocial assessment exists | 0.85 | 0.35 | Five weeks, mandatory under s 55C, and they say they *cannot assess* **vs** a large HHS may produce something generic |
| Consultation breach (s 47/48) | 0.82 | 0.50 | 26 emails, none about the work; no HSR identified **vs** consultation obligations are "so far as reasonably practicable" |

⭐ **The central mediating variable is CREDIBILITY.** Substantive strength is multiplied by
`0.45 + 0.55 × credibility`. **The traps do not lose the argument. They lose the audience — and the
audience is what converts the argument into an outcome.**

## THE RESULT
| Strategy | Credibility | Back at work ≤8wk | Pay restored | Settlement improves | **Adverse event** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⭐ **DISCIPLINED** | **0.79** | **62.4%** | **33.2%** | **57.6%** | **17.4%** |
| MINIMAL | 0.73 | 50.1% | 32.3% | 55.0% | 19.4% |
| LATE (after 7 Aug) | 0.60 | 56.7% | 27.7% | 48.4% | 42.0% |
| AGGRESSIVE | 0.23 | 45.3% | 21.9% | 12.4% | 42.9% |
| ⛔ **SILENT** | 0.26 | **12.4%** | 5.4% | 31.9% | **76.0%** |

## THE TORNADO — one choice flipped, from DISCIPLINED
| Choice | Back@work | Pay | Settle | **ADVERSE** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ⛔ **Do not respond at all** | **−45.7** | −27.4 | −24.0 | **+47.1** |
| Respond after 7 August | −4.6 | −3.2 | −7.4 | +13.4 |
| Use the word "bullying" | −5.0 | −3.6 | −7.9 | +11.7 |
| Seek no extension | −1.0 | −2.3 | −1.7 | +11.5 |
| ⚠️ **Raise motive theories** | −8.3 | −5.9 | **−22.5** | +9.8 |
| ⚠️ **Raise employment at the mention** | −8.1 | −5.8 | **−25.9** | +9.2 |
| Raise the metadata timings | −3.1 | −2.2 | −5.0 | +3.7 |
| Omit the psychosocial request | **−8.5** | −0.9 | −2.5 | +1.8 |
| ⚠️ **Report A covers causation** | 0.0 | 0.0 | **−16.3** | +0.1 |
| Ask costs before booking | −3.4 | +0.2 | 0.0 | −0.1 |
| Omit the named delegate | −4.6 | +0.1 | 0.0 | −0.2 |

## WHAT THE MODEL SAYS
1. ⛔ **Silence is catastrophic and it is not close.** Adverse risk **17% → 76%**; return **62% → 12%**.
   It is four times worse than the worst affirmative mistake.
2. ⭐ **Three traps cost more than they appear to.** Motive theories, conflating the tracks at the
   mention, and a loose Report A each strip **16–26 points off the settlement position** — the single
   most valuable asset — while barely moving the employment outcome. **They are expensive in the
   currency that matters most.**
3. **The psychosocial assessment request is the biggest *upside* lever** (−8.5 pts if omitted) and is
   nearly free on adverse risk (+1.8). **Highest ratio in the model.**
4. **Timing is cheap to get right and expensive to get wrong** — responding late costs +13.4 pts of
   adverse risk for nothing gained.
5. **AGGRESSIVE is worse than MINIMAL on every measure.** Adding the traps to a strong case makes it
   weaker than saying almost nothing.
6. **Book-first vs ask-costs-first barely registers** (−3.4 back@work, −0.1 adverse). ⇒ **Cory's
   judgement to book first is sound and the disagreement was not worth having.**

## BIMODALITY
Credibility 80% interval under DISCIPLINED is **0.57 – 0.98** — wide. The distribution is
**gated on whether the psychosocial assessment exists.** If MSH produces a real one the case
narrows sharply to the reasonableness limb; if it cannot, `B4` and `B5` fire together and the
outcome distribution shifts hard to the good tail. **That single answer is the fork.**

## WHAT WOULD MOVE IT — ranked by leverage
1. **The answer to "when was the last assessment with worker input"** — the fork above
2. **Whether the position is being worked by another employee** (Part 11) — converts Q9
3. **The Magistrates Court chronology** — currently suspends two recorded findings
4. **MSH's employer responses of 16 Aug and 6 Sep 2024** — never held
5. **eHealth backups of the wiped mailbox** — restores the destroyed record

## ⚠️ WHAT THE MODEL CANNOT DO
It cannot tell you whether a Commissioner will believe him, whether MSH will settle, or what the
court file says. It ranks **controllable choices** against a record that is already documented.
**Every prior is contestable and is stated so it can be argued with.**

>>> analysis/montecarlo_strategy.py :: text
"""
WC/2024/227 employment track — Monte Carlo over strategy choices.
Priors are JUDGEMENT calibrated to the documentary record in this repo, not measured
frequencies. Ranges are blue(high)/red(low) per the full-picture method.
"""
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260731)
N = 200_000

def beta_from_range(lo, hi, n, disp):
    """Draw in [lo,hi] shaped by a shared decision-maker disposition (0=hostile,1=receptive)."""
    span = hi - lo
    # disposition shifts within the range; noise adds independent uncertainty
    base = lo + span * (0.30 + 0.55 * disp)
    noise = rng.normal(0, span * 0.16, n)
    return np.clip(base + noise, 0.01, 0.99)

# ---- shared disposition of the decision-maker (correlates all blocks) ----
disp = rng.beta(5, 5, N)

# ---- SUBSTANTIVE BLOCKS: blue(high) / red(low) ----
BLOCKS = {
 # name                          blue   red    what it is
 "B1_no_authority_exclusion":  (0.88, 0.55),  # nothing authorised keeping him out
 "B2_direction_unreasonable":  (0.85, 0.45),  # reasonableness limb fails
 "B3_leave_unlawful":          (0.80, 0.38),  # accrued/sick-no-pay/IP debiting
 "B4_no_psychosocial_assmt":   (0.85, 0.35),  # the assessment does not exist
 "B5_consultation_breach":     (0.82, 0.50),  # WHS s47/48 not complied with
}
B = {k: beta_from_range(lo, hi, N, disp) for k, (hi, lo) in
     ((k, (v[0], v[1])) for k, v in BLOCKS.items())}

# ---- STRATEGY VECTOR ----
# Each decision returns (credibility_delta, direct_effect_multipliers)
STRATS = {
 "DISCIPLINED": dict(respond="early", psychosocial=True, scope_consent=True,
                     name_delegate=True, motive=False, metadata=False,
                     bullying=False, reportA="tight", mention_clean=True,
                     book_first=True, extension=True),
 "AGGRESSIVE":  dict(respond="early", psychosocial=True, scope_consent=True,
                     name_delegate=True, motive=True,  metadata=True,
                     bullying=True,  reportA="loose", mention_clean=False,
                     book_first=True, extension=True),
 "MINIMAL":     dict(respond="early", psychosocial=False, scope_consent=False,
                     name_delegate=False, motive=False, metadata=False,
                     bullying=False, reportA="tight", mention_clean=True,
                     book_first=True, extension=True),
 "SILENT":      dict(respond="none", psychosocial=False, scope_consent=False,
                     name_delegate=False, motive=False, metadata=False,
                     bullying=False, reportA="tight", mention_clean=True,
                     book_first=False, extension=False),
 "LATE":        dict(respond="late", psychosocial=True, scope_consent=True,
                     name_delegate=True, motive=False, metadata=False,
                     bullying=False, reportA="tight", mention_clean=True,
                     book_first=True, extension=False),
}

def credibility(s):
    """Credibility index 0-1. The central mediating variable."""
    c = rng.beta(7, 3, N)               # baseline: strong documentary position
    if s["respond"] == "none": c *= rng.uniform(0.30, 0.45, N)
    if s["respond"] == "late": c *= rng.uniform(0.72, 0.88, N)
    if s["motive"]:            c *= rng.uniform(0.55, 0.75, N)   # unprovable allegations
    if s["metadata"]:          c *= rng.uniform(0.80, 0.93, N)   # reads as gotcha + burns capability
    if s["bullying"]:          c *= rng.uniform(0.70, 0.88, N)   # invites RMA defence, shifts register
    if not s["mention_clean"]: c *= rng.uniform(0.55, 0.78, N)   # conflating tracks before Dwyer
    if s["psychosocial"]:      c *= rng.uniform(1.03, 1.12, N)   # asks them to do a mandatory thing
    if s["extension"]:         c *= rng.uniform(1.02, 1.08, N)   # engaged, reasonable
    return np.clip(c, 0.02, 1.0)

def simulate(s):
    c = credibility(s)
    # substantive blocks are only as persuasive as the person advancing them
    eff = {k: v * (0.45 + 0.55 * c) for k, v in B.items()}

    # ---- O1: back at work within 8 weeks ----
    p_ret = 0.10 + 0.42*eff["B2_direction_unreasonable"] + 0.20*eff["B1_no_authority_exclusion"]
    if s["respond"] == "none": p_ret *= 0.35
    if s["psychosocial"]:      p_ret *= rng.uniform(1.05, 1.20, N)   # forces the assessment question
    if s["name_delegate"]:     p_ret *= rng.uniform(1.03, 1.14, N)   # removes the conflicted blocker
    if s["book_first"]:        p_ret *= rng.uniform(1.02, 1.10, N)   # no delay vector
    ret = rng.random(N) < np.clip(p_ret, 0, 0.97)

    # ---- O2: pay / leave restored (incl. backpay) ----
    p_pay = 0.06 + 0.55*eff["B3_leave_unlawful"] * (0.55 + 0.45*eff["B1_no_authority_exclusion"])
    if s["respond"] == "none": p_pay *= 0.25
    if s["extension"]:         p_pay *= rng.uniform(1.02, 1.09, N)
    pay = rng.random(N) < np.clip(p_pay, 0, 0.95)

    # ---- O3: settlement position in WC/2024/227 improves ----
    p_set = 0.12 + 0.40*c + 0.25*eff["B4_no_psychosocial_assmt"]
    if s["reportA"] == "loose": p_set *= rng.uniform(0.62, 0.82, N)  # causation opinion to the Regulator
    if not s["mention_clean"]:  p_set *= rng.uniform(0.60, 0.82, N)
    if s["motive"]:             p_set *= rng.uniform(0.70, 0.88, N)
    setl = rng.random(N) < np.clip(p_set, 0, 0.96)

    # ---- O4: adverse event (decision made against him / disciplinary escalation) ----
    p_adv = 0.10 + 0.35*(1-c)
    if s["respond"] == "none":  p_adv += 0.30
    if s["respond"] == "late":  p_adv += 0.08
    if not s["extension"]:      p_adv += 0.10
    if s["bullying"]:           p_adv += 0.06
    adv = rng.random(N) < np.clip(p_adv, 0, 0.95)

    return dict(cred=c.mean(), ret=ret.mean(), pay=pay.mean(),
                setl=setl.mean(), adv=adv.mean(),
                cred_lo=np.percentile(c,10), cred_hi=np.percentile(c,90))

print("="*94)
print(f"{'STRATEGY':<14}{'Credibility':>13}{'Back@work':>12}{'Pay restored':>14}"
      f"{'Settle+':>10}{'ADVERSE':>10}")
print("="*94)
res = {}
for name, s in STRATS.items():
    r = simulate(s); res[name] = r
    print(f"{name:<14}{r['cred']:>12.2f} {r['ret']:>11.1%} {r['pay']:>13.1%}"
          f" {r['setl']:>9.1%} {r['adv']:>9.1%}")
print("="*94)

# ---- TORNADO: single-variable deviations from DISCIPLINED ----
print("\nTORNADO — flipping ONE choice away from DISCIPLINED (Δ percentage points)")
print("-"*94)
base = res["DISCIPLINED"]
flips = [("do not respond at all", dict(respond="none")),
         ("respond after 7 Aug", dict(respond="late")),
         ("no extension sought", dict(extension=False)),
         ("raise motive theories", dict(motive=True)),
         ("raise employment at the mention", dict(mention_clean=False)),
         ("use the word bullying", dict(bullying=True)),
         ("Report A covers causation", dict(reportA="loose")),
         ("raise metadata timings", dict(metadata=True)),
         ("omit psychosocial request", dict(psychosocial=False)),
         ("omit named delegate", dict(name_delegate=False)),
         ("ask costs before booking", dict(book_first=False))]
rows = []
for label, ch in flips:
    s = dict(STRATS["DISCIPLINED"]); s.update(ch)
    r = simulate(s)
    rows.append((label, (r['ret']-base['ret'])*100, (r['pay']-base['pay'])*100,
                 (r['setl']-base['setl'])*100, (r['adv']-base['adv'])*100))
rows.sort(key=lambda x: x[4], reverse=True)
print(f"{'CHOICE':<36}{'Back@work':>11}{'Pay':>9}{'Settle':>9}{'ADVERSE':>10}")
for l, a, b_, c_, d in rows:
    print(f"{l:<36}{a:>+10.1f} {b_:>+8.1f} {c_:>+8.1f} {d:>+9.1f}")
print("-"*94)
print(f"\nDISCIPLINED credibility 80% interval: {base['cred_lo']:.2f} – {base['cred_hi']:.2f}")
print(f"N = {N:,} trials.  Priors are judgement calibrated to the record, not frequencies.")

| analysing the disclosure dispute — objection grounds, metadata, provenance, who-reads-it | `sub-skills/disclosure-mechanics.md` |
| weighing settlement, Calderbank, the deed, release scope | `sub-skills/settlement.md` |
| touching PID/reprisal, QHRC, CCC, QCAT, or any non-WC track | `sub-skills/parallel-tracks.md` |
| framing or wording an argument — how to structure submissions, persuade, sentence craft, Bar-table technique, the established voice | `sub-skills/advocacy-and-persuasion.md` |

When in doubt, load the parent + confirmed-record and ask which task. Several sub-skills may apply to one request — load all that fit.

## Discipline rules (govern every sub-skill — non-negotiable)

1. **Conspiracy/reprisal framing never reaches paper or the bar table.** Coordination between MSH and the Regulator is real and lawful (joint defence). Use the *asymmetry* (same documents, same custodians, two postures by requester), held in reserve, deployed only on trigger — never the collusion narrative.
2. **The word "fraud" never appears in the WC track.** Cory's PID alleged timesheet fraud against a named manager — the collateral-purpose grenade. It belongs to the PID/reprisal track and evidence-in-chief only. The PID *complaint form* stays out of the 64G; only the clean *response/routing* documents go in.
3. **Items 8–9 (manager's attendance records) anchor ONLY to pleaded Stressor 1(a)** (erratic presence — a contested live fact the records measure) and the "roster was equitable" denial (Form 24 ¶39). NEVER to the reprisal (admitted, so the records prove nothing about it) or the fraud allegation (the collateral purpose).
4. **File first, ask second.** The 64G compels; the index email requests. Never lead with the request when holding the compeller. Communications to the Regulator wait until after filing + service, in writing only — never by phone.
5. **Tone is neutral, procedural, proportionate.** Dwyer (close reader, ran the failed conference) must discover MSH's problems himself. A discovered pattern is evidence; a stated pattern is discounted argument. Strip adjectives.
6. **Restraint as posture.** Concede what's honestly available; withdraw what the record doesn't need — the concessions certify that what remains is necessary and make it grantable.
7. **Severity = the whole course of conduct** (cumulative institutional response to raising concerns), never a single event. Lives in evidence-in-chief, the medical case, closing — not the 64G.
8. **Parallel tracks stay sequenced BEHIND the WC settlement.** Maximum accountability risks the WC matter; restraint manufactures the accountability later.
9. **At settlement, release the compensation claim ONLY.** Any deed reaching MSH, the reprisal tort, or "all claims arising from employment" buys their liability-shield immunity with Cory's compensation money. The whole strategy is tested here.

## The cardinal habit: verified vs. working

Keep **confirmed-against-source** strictly separate from **working-theory**. A memory reconstruction is a lead to verify, not authority. (Proven necessary: the Form 24 schedule carried across sessions was wrong on the medical-records Form 29 — only reading the document caught it.) Before any pinpoint, date, or quote enters a filing, open the source.

# ASSESSMENT — the 31 July 2026 documents: every error, matched to the instrument, and the rush

> The two letters signed by Mr Scott Hughes, Director Corporate Services, sent 11:43 AEST
> 31 July 2026. Every error quoted from source. Every substantive error matched to the provision it
> contradicts. All timings from PDF metadata and recovered revisions.
> **Purpose: to establish that these documents were not reviewed before they were sent.**

---

## PART A — THE RUSH, ESTABLISHED

### A1. The production sequence

| Time (AEST, Fri 31 Jul 2026) | Event | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **11:10:27** | GP letter (5 pp, 9 questions) exported from Word | `xmp:CreateDate` |
| **11:11:02** | Employee letter (2 pp) exported from Word | `xmp:CreateDate` |
| **11:11:27** | Employee letter signed — **25 sec after creation** | recovered revision 3 |
| **11:11:42** | GP letter signed — **75 sec after creation** | recovered revision 3 |
| **11:43** | Both transmitted | covering email |

**Both letters exported 35 seconds apart. Both signed within 75 seconds. Sent 32 minutes later.**

### A2. The signature was applied without the document being read

Revision recovery (truncation at each of the 3 `%%EOF` markers) establishes:
- **rev1 → rev2** = +185 bytes, adds `/StructTreeRoot`, **text identical**. Standard Word output —
  the unsigned Role Description does exactly the same.
- **rev2 → rev3** = **+99,121 bytes** (employee) / **+101,021** (GP); adds `/OCProperties` and
  **`/ADBE_FillSignInfo`** (Adobe Fill & Sign); **text identical**.
- What rev3 added: a **1000 × 398 px JPEG at 624 dpi** with transparency mask — **1.60 in × 0.64 in**
  — placed on the signature page. **Identical dimensions and byte size in both files: the same
  stored signature image.**

⇒ **You cannot read a five-page letter putting nine questions to a doctor in 75 seconds. You cannot
read a two-page letter in 25 seconds.** The signature was applied to documents that were not read at
the point of signing.

### A3. And nothing was corrected afterwards
Text identical across all three revisions of both letters. Nothing was amended between creation,
signing and transmission. **The errors below were in the version signed and in the version sent.**

### A4. What the metadata does NOT establish
A Word→PDF export timestamp fixes **finalisation**, not drafting. The Word document may have existed
earlier. ⇒ **The rush established is a rush to finalise and send. The errors below independently
establish that no proofread occurred at any stage.**

## PART C — THE SUBSTANTIVE ERRORS, MATCHED TO THE INSTRUMENT

### C1. Q6 applies a test that does not exist under the policy the same letter cites
> **Their question:** *"In your medical opinion is Mr Shepherd able to fulfill the full inherent
> requirements of his Role… **without restrictions or modifications to duties**?"*

| Instrument | What it actually requires |
|---|---|
| **G03, purpose** | "to assist employees… to meet the **genuine occupational requirements** of their role **by applying principles of reasonable adjustment**" |
| **G03 cl 3** | adjustments "should support the employee to undertake the **genuine occupational requirements** of their role" |
| **AD Act s 34** | reasonable terms where capacity is restricted — with adjustment, subject to unjustifiable hardship (ss 5, 35) |
| **IME Guideline** | information on capacity "to carry out the **genuine occupational requirements** of their role" |

⇒ **Four instruments, one test — and it is not the test asked.** "Without restrictions or
modifications" is the incapacity formulation. **They cited G03 in the same document and asked the
opposite of what G03 asks.**

### C2. Q9 reverses the onus their own policy places on them
> **Their question:** *"**If we are not able to accommodate** the restrictions you have
> recommended, is Mr Shepherd able to safely return to the workplace?"*

> **G03 cl 2:** unjustifiable hardship "is tested against **the whole organisation, not a division or
> unit within the organisation**… **the onus is on Queensland Health, as the employer, to prove an
> adjustment is unreasonable, not on the person to prove that it is reasonable.**"

⇒ Three errors in one question: it presupposes an inability never assessed; it asks the doctor to
discharge **MSH's** onus; and it is framed at unit rather than organisation level.

### C3. Q3 asks a clinician to discharge MSH's statutory duty
> **Their question:** *"whether Mr Shepherd is medically fit to return to their substantive role
> **under the existing reporting arrangements**"*

| Instrument | Where the duty sits |
|---|---|
| **WHS s 19(1)–(2)** | The **PCBU** must ensure health and safety of workers **and of other persons** |
| **Psychosocial Code 2022** | Psychosocial hazards are **features of the work**, identified and controlled by the PCBU |
| **G03 cl 1** | "proper consideration **must** be given to the [Code]… to ensure the **process**… identifies and manages psychosocial hazards and risks" |
| **EB12 cl 7.2.1** | supplies the risk-assessment mechanism |

⇒ A workplace risk assessment was asked of a general practitioner.

### C4. Q2 rests on a statement that is false on MSH's own record
> **Their premise:** *"As the Health Service **is not aware of any concerns being raised** for
> appropriate management"*

> **MSH's own objection, 5 June 2026, signed by the Chief Executive, Item 20:** *"the reference
> cited in the Notice being '**PID24-ESU-1130**' commenced in November 2024…"*

⇒ **Eight weeks earlier the Health Service addressed his public interest disclosure by reference
number, over the Chief Executive's signature.** Also on the record: the patient safety report; the
complaint of 4 October 2025 to the A/Director HR Business Partnering; two years of correspondence;
and WC/2024/227 itself.

### C5. "Primarily" — an undisclosed secondary purpose, against a statutory prohibition
> *"This information will **primarily** be used for the purposes of better understanding your
> condition and to support the implementation for appropriate controls"*

> **IP Act 2009, QPP 3.3** (sch 3; current 1 July 2026): "An agency **must not collect sensitive
> information** about an individual unless— (a) the individual **consents** and the information is
> **reasonably necessary for, or directly related to**, 1 or more of the agency's functions or
> activities…"
> **sch 5:** sensitive information includes "**health information**"; health information includes
> "the individual's **health at any time**" and "**a disability** of the individual at any time".

⇒ Collection of sensitive information must be tied to a stated function. **"Primarily" concedes
uses that are not stated.**

### C6. No power was ever identified
G03 is a **policy**. WHS ss 17 and 19 are **duties on MSH**. Neither confers a power to exclude a
worker, compel information, or debit leave.
**PS Act 2022 s 104** — the only statutory power to require a medical examination — **was never
cited**, and its **s 103** gateway requires absence or unsatisfactory performance: no performance
issue has ever been put, and **the absence is MSH's own act**. **s 105**, the only statutory link in
that division to leave, operates solely where an s 104(b) requirement is not complied with —
never invoked.

## PART D — THE CONCLUSION

**Fourteen identified errors across seven pages**, including two errors in a single five-word phrase,
a wrong policy number, an internal inconsistency on the same page, and pronoun drift between adjacent
questions.

**Five substantive failures**, each contradicting an instrument the letters themselves cite or are
governed by: the wrong test under G03, the reversed onus under G03 cl 2, a statutory duty put to a
GP, a false premise contradicted by their own Chief Executive's objection, and an undisclosed
secondary purpose against QPP 3.3.

**And the physical evidence:** exported at 11:10:27 and 11:11:02, signed with a stored image 25 and
75 seconds later, transmitted at 11:43, with the text unchanged throughout.

⇒ **These documents were not reviewed before they were sent.** The errors prove no proofread at any
stage; the timings prove the signature was applied to an unread document; and the substantive
failures prove that nobody checked the letters against the instruments they cite.

⚠️ **USE.** Errors 1–14 are for the union brief and the reserved tracks — raising typographical
errors in correspondence reads as petty and forfeits the register currently working. **Only C1, C2,
C3, C4 and C6 are deployed in the response, and each is argued on the instrument, never as a
mistake.** C5 is raised only as a neutral question about the handling of health information.

>>> skill/references/9C-contradiction-matrix.md :: text
# The Regulator's Form 9C (SOFC, 13 May 2026, v4.4) — contradiction matrix

> The Regulator's operative defence pleading, signed Matheson. Read against: the earlier Form 24
> admissions, the Regulator's own admitted Review Decision (24 Oct 2024), MSH's 5 June 2026 letter,
> and the 11 June 2026 disclosure. TIERS: T1 = contradiction on the face of the record (provable
> NOW). T2 = contradiction the MSH disclosure exposes (provable now). T3 = contradiction the 64G
> disclosure will TEST (working — pending production). Discipline: T3 stays working-theory; never
> asserted as fact; verify against source before any filing. NOT for the 64G text (case-law-free);
> this feeds hearing submissions, settlement/Calderbank, and the reception model.
> Note: "v4.4" = the defence has been redrafted repeatedly — a moving position, not a settled one.

## TIER 1 — contradictions on the face of the record (no disclosure needed)

**T1-A — "Not causative" + "reasonable in all respects" vs the Regulator's OWN admitted Review Decision.**
9C ¶22(f): the 7-hour-break issue "was NOT CAUSATIVE of the appellant's injury"; ¶22 "reasonable in
all respects." BUT the Review Decision (24 Oct 2024) found the 7-hour break "amounted to unreasonable
management action" AND that "employment was a significant contributing factor" — and the Regulator
ADMITS the contents of that decision, both findings (Form 24 Para 37). Worse: the 9C's Decision
Sought ¶2 asks the Commission to CONFIRM the 24 Oct 2024 decision. The Regulator is pleading two
positions (not causative; reasonable) that contradict findings inside the very decision it admits
and asks to confirm. THE central contradiction: their own review body already found for Cory on
UMA and significant-contribution.

**T1-B — the 7-hour breach is CONCEDED on their own pleading.**
9C ¶22(a): the shifts were "separated by only a 7-hour break (RATHER THAN AN 8-HOUR BREAK)"; ¶22(e):
"in June 2020 the Appellant SIGNED AN AGREEMENT allowing an 8-HOUR break." Put together, the
Regulator's own pleading concedes the operative minimum was 8 hours and the actual break was 7 —
i.e. a breach of the applicable minimum is admitted. (This also disposes of the 9A's "10-hour"
overstatement: even on the Regulator's own 8-hour figure, 7 < 8. Argue the CONCEDED 8-hour minimum,
never the 10.)

**T1-C — "human error" is the antithesis of "reasonable management action taken reasonably."**
9C ¶22(a): the 7-hour break was "a result of HUMAN ERROR." ¶14 (COVID): the decline was "human error
by Ms Taylor." The s 32(5)(a) exclusion protects considered management ACTION taken reasonably (Read;
Allwood). An error is the absence of a considered decision. By pleading "human error," the Regulator
concedes these were not reasoned management actions — so there is either nothing for the exclusion to
protect, or the "reasonable in all respects" characterisation of the same events is internally
inconsistent. They cannot be both errors and reasonable management actions.

**T1-D — the COVID decline reason is conceded to be factually wrong.**
9C ¶14: Taylor declined the COVID leave because (on her assessment) the stat dec "was not attached";
"a review indicates the attachments WERE present." Self-defeating: the stated ground for the
twice-decline is conceded to be mistaken. And the excuse offered — "a background of high work
demands" — corroborates the appellant's stressor of an overloaded/under-resourced environment.

**T1-E — "remedied in a timely manner" vs the admitted 25-day AVAC delay.**
9C ¶20: pay "discrepancies/errors remedied in a timely manner"; "reasonable and taken in a reasonable
way." BUT Form 24 Para 40-41 ADMITS payroll directed the correction "IMMEDIATELY" on 3 May 2024 and
the AVAC was not submitted until 28 May — a 25-day delay. "Immediately" ignored for 25 days is not
"timely." Admission contradicts contention.

**T1-F — cherry-picked medical records (baseline vs diagnosis).**
9C ¶8: does not admit the clean baseline "because medical records identify a PAST MEDICAL HISTORY OF
ANXIETY" — relying on the medical records as authoritative. ¶9: does not admit the MDD/Krishnaiah
diagnosis — "matters for determination." They treat the same body of records as proof when it helps
(prior anxiety) and as unproven when it hurts (the diagnosis). And the 16 Nov 2023 record ("no
psychological illness such as depression/psychosis") is ADMITTED as listed (Form 24 Para 34) — a
clean contemporaneous baseline they've admitted, against the "past history of anxiety" they assert.

## TIER 2 — contradiction the MSH disclosure exposes (provable now)

**T2-G — "reasonable management action" on fatigue vs NO fatigue system existing.**
9C pleads the fatigue handling "reasonable in all respects." MSH's 5 June letter confirms: NO FRMS
applied to the Switchboard (Item 4); FRMS implemented only "after 30 June 2024" (Item 5) — after the
injury; "no consequential changes to operating procedures" (Item 3(c)). One cannot take "reasonable
management action" under a fatigue-risk framework that did not exist. The absence of any FRMS is the
concrete refutation of "reasonable in all respects" on the keystone stressor. (Frame as: the
Regulator's contention is contradicted by the non-party's own factual confirmation — NOT as collusion.)

## TIER 3 — contradictions the 64G disclosure will TEST (working — pending production)

**T3-H — "Ms Reese was unaware of the PID" (¶16) — the reprisal linchpin.**
The retraction direction (15 May) fell within 48 hrs of the PID (13 May). The 9C defends by asserting
Reese was UNAWARE of the PID. The 11 June disclosure (CS-4) is the 15-16 May correspondence
concerning "the complaint and the operational and HR response to it." What Reese knew, and when, is
exactly what the Item 20 material (13-31 May window) and the custodian correspondence would show. IF
production shows Reese engaged with "the complaint" in that window, the "unaware" defence is in
jeopardy. WORKING — the disclosure tests it; do not assert.

**T3-I — "rostered in an equitable way... would not have earned 42% less" (¶19).**
Denies the pay-disparity stressor by asserting equitable rostering. The security-access/attendance
records (Items 8-9) and the roster records go directly to whether the rostering was in fact
equitable. Disclosure tests the assertion. WORKING.

**T3-J — the grievance narrative proves the problem persisted (¶13).**
The 9C denies the 7 Aug grievance was "dismissed" by narrating an ongoing process: 10 Aug meeting,
29 Aug + 8 Sept emails, "Taylor emailed 14 Nov re shift/break compliance," 15 Nov meeting. That
timeline is double-edged FOR CORY: an unresolved shift/break-compliance issue running Aug-Nov 2023
corroborates that the rostering/fatigue concern was real, live, and unresolved for months — and the
"14 Nov re shift/break compliance" email concedes a compliance issue existed. The disclosure of that
correspondence supports the appellant. WORKING/mixed.

## THE UNIFYING READ (for submissions / settlement, not the 64G)
The 9C defends by (i) contradicting the Regulator's own admitted Review findings (T1-A), (ii)
conceding the operative breach while relabelling it "human error" (T1-B/C), (iii) asserting
"reasonable in all respects" over conduct its own admissions and MSH's disclosure show was error,
delay, or ungoverned (T1-D/E, T2-G), and (iv) resting key denials on factual assertions the
compelled records will test (T3-H/I/J). A defence redrafted to v4.4 that still contradicts its
author's own review decision is not a settled position — it is the reason the produce-or-swear
application matters and the reason the costs exposure on the Calderbank is real.

>>> skill/references/ASSESSMENT-DESIGN-gold-standard.md :: text
# HOW A COMPREHENSIVE PSYCHOSOCIAL + WHS ASSESSMENT WOULD ACTUALLY BE RUN HERE
> ⛔ Strategy layer / ready position. The gold-standard methodology to hold against whatever
> MSH eventually proposes — and the additional improvements a real assessment would surface
> beyond the current proposals. Use at scoping consultation. Banked 4 Aug 2026.

## THE EIGHT-PHASE METHODOLOGY
1. GOVERNANCE. Independent assessor (outside Corporate Services; conflict-screened);
   published terms of reference; steering group incl. operator representative + HSR + union;
   Code + ISO 45003 as the stated methods frame.
2. DATA (work-as-recorded). Demand curves (call volumes by hour/day; code activations);
   rosters audited against FRMS rules (count the sub-10h breaks); ⭐ leave × demand
   correlation (the team-wide leave-as-fatigue-control test); turnover/vacancy/agency fill;
   complaint corpus analysis (the recurring vocabulary IS a dataset); EAP usage; incident +
   workers' comp history; overtime; SPOK error/paging-failure data.
3. SURVEY (work-as-experienced). ⭐ "People at Work" — Queensland's own free, validated
   psychosocial risk survey (WorkSafe QLD co-developed, benchmarked). MSH cannot refuse its
   own regulator's instrument. All operators, anonymity protected.
4. OBSERVATION (work-as-done). Assessor sits in the room across shift types INCLUDING nights
   and weekends; structured task-concurrency observation. (The assessment itself applying
   the integrated-presence principle.)
5. INTERVIEWS. All operators offered, structured prompts; EXIT interviews of recent leavers
   — turnover carries the story the survey misses.
6. CONVERGENCE + RISK RATING. Triangulate 2–4–5; rate per Code (duration × frequency ×
   severity); publish the risk register to the room.
7. CONTROLS CO-DESIGN. Workshop WITH the room (the consult principle); hierarchy-ordered;
   owners + dates per control; the existing Proposals P1–P8 tabled as the starting set.
8. REVIEW LOOP. Leading-indicator dashboard (FRMS breach count → zero; complaint response
   times; leave-on-peak correlation trending down; survey re-run at 12 months).

## IMPROVEMENTS A REAL ASSESSMENT WOULD SURFACE BEYOND P1–P8
A. CRITICAL-INCIDENT DEBRIEF PROTOCOL. Operators handle codes, deaths, abusive and
   distressing calls with NO defusing/peer-support step. A brief structured debrief +
   opt-in peer support after defined trigger events. (Standard in QAS/000 rooms; absent here.)
B. POST-CALL RECOVERY MICRO-BREAKS + SURGE PROTOCOL. Defined short off-queue recovery after
   distressing calls; a surge protocol for when the queue exceeds capacity, instead of
   silent endurance.
C. ACOUSTIC + ERGONOMIC WHS (the physical assessment). Headset acoustic-shock limits, room
   noise, console ergonomics, screen/DSE breaks, lighting — the recognised physical hazard
   set for call rooms, never assessed here.
D. QA FRAMEWORK WITH CALL-RECORDING REVIEW (per the APCO/NENA QA standard). Protective for
   operators: the recording resolves accusations — directly answers the blame-absorption
   baseline (¶23). Framed as protection, introduced in consultation.
E. OCCUPANCY CAP. Call-centre science: sustained occupancy above ~80% predicts burnout;
   staffing set so occupancy stays within evidence-based bounds (feeds P7).
F. UPSTREAM DATA SLAs. The wrong-number/stale-roster problem ORIGINATES in departments not
   feeding updates. Service standards on DEPARTMENTS for roster/contact updates into the
   Switchboard — fixes the cause, not the symptom (pairs with P1).
G. TRAINING + COMPETENCY MATRIX. Documented competencies per function (incl. the supervisor
   pathway's training layer) — role clarity made structural.
H. PSYCHOLOGICAL SAFETY MEASURE. A standing, anonymous route for operators to raise hazards
   with feedback guaranteed (cl 7.1.11 made systematic) — measured in the 12-month re-survey.

## THE SCOPING-MEETING POSTURE
Table the mapping + proposals as inputs; ask for the eight phases by name; nominate People
at Work as the survey instrument (their regulator's own tool); ask that observation include
nights/weekends; ask for the leave × demand correlation explicitly; and ask which of A–H
the assessment will scope in — every "no" is recorded in a consultation minute.

# THE CHRONOLOGY SHIELD — IF THE RESPONDENT REACHES FOR THE 2024–25 PERSONAL EVENTS
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Never volunteered. Deploy ONLY if the Regulator puts personal/police
> material into the appeal (submissions, expert opinion, cross). Banked 3 Aug 2026.
> Companion: taylor-DFV-disclosure-to-Matheson.md §4A/4B (the over-supply answer).

## 1. THE THREE DATES THAT END EVERY VERSION OF THE ARGUMENT
| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| **Injury (claimed)** | **18 June 2024** |
| **Diagnosis recorded, medication escalated** (MDD w/ anxious distress, treating psychiatrist) | **24 October 2024** |
| **First personal/police event of the story** (dog removed; PPN next day) | **1–2 December 2024** |

**The injury was diagnosed and medicated BEFORE the first minute of the personal story.**
Every event the Respondent could reach for — the orders (Dec 2024), the arrest (24 Feb 2025),
the charge, the homelessness, the seizures, the family displacement (Apr 2025) — post-dates
the injury by 5–10 months and the DIAGNOSIS by 1–6 months. On a s 550(4) liability appeal,
the question is whether employment was A significant contributing factor TO THE
INJURY (s 32(1), verified ATT26 — the 2013 "major" test was repealed in 2019). Events after onset cannot cause the onset. The dilution argument is chronologically
impossible, from the Regulator's own file (their SOFC pleads the diagnosis history).

## 2. THE "UNDATED CONTEXT" TRICK — AND ITS ONE-LINE ANSWER
Expect the material blurred: "a period of significant personal turmoil, including police
matters and relationship breakdown." The answer, every single time, in every forum:
**"Put a date on it."** Then the table above. Never argue the events; date them.
- In cross of any expert: "Doctor, the diagnosis is recorded 24 October 2024. The first
  event you rely on is 1 December 2024. Explain how it contributed to a condition
  diagnosed five weeks earlier."
- In submissions: post-onset stressors go, at most, to the COURSE of the condition, not
  its CAUSE — and this is a liability appeal, not a quantum assessment.

## 3. HOW THE MATERIAL WOULD ENTER — WATCH THE VECTORS
1. **The 2025 clinical records** (psychiatrist/GP notes referencing arrest, homelessness,
   court dates) — likely already captured by the Respondent's NNPDs. ⭐ When Matheson's
   updated list + NNPD copies arrive (committed "this week"), CHECK EXACTLY which clinical
   records went in and their date ranges. This is the primary vector.
2. **Cory's own emails to MSH** (30 Mar 2025 to Hughes; the Oct 2025 letter) — already in
   MSH's hands; usable only via MSH → Regulator supply (over-supply pattern, second instance).
3. **The Taylor screenshots** (Jan 2024 — different matter; §4A/4B answers it).

## 4. IF THEY OPEN THE DOOR, IT SWINGS BACK ON THEM
The arrest story cannot be used in part. If any of it goes in, completeness brings in:
the withdrawal and vacation within 30 hours; the strike-out "upon no evidence from the
aggrieved"; the bond released solely to him; the officers' own BWC assessments; and the
fact the events cost him a CONFIRMED return to work (21 Feb 2025 written confirmation,
7:00am 24 Feb — MSH's own record). A respondent inviting a documented police-misconduct
complaint into a de novo hearing, to attack a man whose diagnosis pre-dates all of it,
is a respondent handing Dwyer a sympathy-and-credit disaster. Competent counsel (Willson)
knows this — which is why the realistic deployment is a sanitised line inside an expert
report, and why §2's cross-examination answer matters most.

## 5. REPORT B INSTRUCTION (when briefed)
The causation report must address the chronology head-on, not avoid it: onset and
diagnosis pre-date the personal events; the 2025 events are intervening stressors relevant
to course/maintenance only; and the report should say so expressly so the point is in
evidence-in-chief, not scrambled for in reply.

## 7. THE ONE PRE-INJURY FRAGMENT — JANUARY 2024 (added 3 Aug, Cory's flag)
The chronology answer does NOT cover the 14 Jan 2024 matter (five months PRE-injury), so it
takes its own defence. **What the Respondent actually holds**: the Taylor screenshots — "I am
with QPS regarding some family stuff", a DFV-leave request, a lateness exchange — plus
whatever the NNPD'd clinical notes say (UNKNOWN — check when the list arrives). **What they
do NOT know**: the matter concerned his 15-year-old SISTER'S conduct toward their MOTHER; a
sub-PPN good-behaviour direction against the sister (a DVO/PPN against her was legally
impossible — s 22(2) DFVP, verified ATT25); he was the assisting adult; ~10 days helping his
mother move; the sister went to NSW. Not his conflict, not his order, not his crisis.

**Their likely play**: undated innuendo — "DV-related matters in his life from early 2024" —
inviting the inference it was HIS domestic violence. **The defence, in order:**
  (a) RELEVANCE — a single unpleaded January morning, followed by **five months of normal
      work before the June injury**, cannot render employment other than "a significant contributing factor"
      against 18 months of pleaded workplace stressors. Object first; explain only if needed.
  (b) THE DATED, BENIGN TRUTH (only if the door is opened) — short, factual, protective:
      "a family matter concerning a child relative, in which I was the assisting adult; no
      order was or could be made against anyone in my household; I gave notice, offered to
      attend my shift, took a short period of leave to help my mother, and worked normally
      for the five months before the injury." NAME NO ONE.
  (c) THE CHILD-SENSITIVITY GATE — any attempt to press detail about the sister meets
      s 159(1)(b)(iii) DFVP (child-identification, criminal penalty) as the sensitivity
      backdrop + a confidentiality-directions application if pressed in open hearing.
  (d) COMPLETENESS — their own screenshots carry his rebuttal ("I will be at my shift...
      I have had to attend the police station directed by police") and their manager's
      same-morning "I'm sorry to hear about your family situation".

**The pregnancy**: the sister's pregnancy (newborn by Apr 2025) is HER event, not his
stressor; it is pleaded nowhere, appears in no known record as affecting him, and gets the
same treatment — "put a date on it, put a document on it" — there is no document. ⚠ VERIFY
when the NNPD list arrives whether any 2024 clinical note references the family matters at

## WHAT TO DO WITH THIS

Items 1, 2 and 3 are the ones that matter, and they matter for a single reason:
**they establish knowledge in the decision-making unit.** Under s 306 IR Act and
s 113(2) WHS Act the onus shifts to the employer once the protected act, the detriment
and knowledge are established. Knowledge is normally the hard part. Here it is on the
Commission's own service list and in the Regulator's own disclosure.

**Discipline rule 1 applies without exception: none of this reaches paper as an
allegation of coordination or collusion.** It is held, it is evidence of knowledge, and
it is deployed — if ever — through process, never through accusation.

>>> skill/references/DELEGATE-STATUS-what-it-changes.md :: text
# ⭐ DELEGATE STATUS — what it changes (verified 4 Aug 2026)
> Cory confirmed 4 Aug that he is an OFFICIALLY appointed union delegate (Together Qld).
> This was not previously in the file. It changes the protective picture, the consultation
> standing, and the way the whole matter looks. Verified against EB12 and the IR Act 2016.

## 1. THE AGREEMENT EXPRESSLY RECOGNISES THE ROLE — EB12 cl 3.1.5 (verbatim)
"The employer acknowledges the constructive role democratically elected union delegates
undertake in the workplace in relation to union activities that support and assist members.
**That role is to be formally recognised, accepted and supported to participate effectively
in consultative structures, perform a representative role, and further the effective
operation of grievance and dispute settlement procedures.**"
Also: cl 3.1.6 (employees given full access to delegates during working hours to discuss any
employment or industrial matter); cl 3.1.8 (convenient access to facilities — telephone,
computer, email, meeting rooms, notice boards — and "management will respect the privacy of
delegates during the use of such facilities"); cl 3.1.4 → HR Policy F4 Union Encouragement
(Schedule 2); cl 3.6.4 (delegate may request resignation reports from local HR to monitor
timeframes — a data right relevant to the turnover limb).

## 2. IR ACT PROTECTION — verified ss 290, 291
s 290 "engages in industrial activity" includes: being an **officer or member** of an
industrial organisation; **organising or promoting a lawful activity for or on behalf of**
the organisation; **participating in** such activity; **representing or advancing the views,
claims or interests** of the organisation; and **giving or distributing information, or
organising or encouraging discussion, about wages, employment conditions and WORKPLACE
RIGHTS** for or on behalf of the organisation.
s 291 "Protection": "A person must not take adverse action against another person because
the other person — (a) is or is not... an officer or member of an industrial organisation;
(b) engages, or has at any time engaged or proposed to engage, in industrial activity..."
**Note in the Act: this is a civil penalty provision.** Reverse onus applies (s 306).

## 3. WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES
1. **A fifth protected attribute.** On top of workplace rights (IR), WHS s 106(h)/(j),
   PID s 40, and AD Act impairment — he now also holds **industrial activity/delegate**
   protection. Any adverse act must survive all five.
2. **His consultation standing rises.** He is not merely an affected worker asking to be
   consulted under ss 47-49 — the agreement says the delegate role is to be "formally
   recognised, accepted and supported to participate effectively in **consultative
   structures**" and to "further the effective operation of **grievance and dispute
   settlement procedures**." That is precisely what he has been doing. Excluding, silencing
   or ignoring a delegate in a consultation and dispute process runs against cl 3.1.5 itself.
3. **The picture changes.** "Employee with a complaint" becomes "the elected delegate for
   the room, excluded from the workplace and unpaid, while raising WHS and industrial
   matters on behalf of members." That is the archetypal general-protections shape.
4. **Union interest rises.** Unions run delegate matters they would not run for a member;
   delegate adverse-action is an organisational issue, not an individual one. ⭐ ACTION:
   tell Petering/Moran expressly that the exclusion has occurred while he holds delegate
   office, and ask whether the union wishes to take carriage of that limb.
5. **Facilities/access limb.** cl 3.1.6/3.1.8 — exclusion from the workplace also cuts
   members off from their delegate and cuts the delegate off from the facilities the
   agreement guarantees. Not a headline claim; a real one, and it belongs to the MEMBERS
   as much as to him.

## 4. DISCIPLINE
- Delegate status is a SHIELD and a standing, never a licence. It confers no power to
  inspect, compel or direct (that is the HSR role — see DELEGATE-VS-HSR-powers.md).
- Do not deploy it as a threat or as "you can't touch me". State it once, factually, where
  it is relevant: in the Stage 2 referral and in any union correspondence.
- ⚠ VERIFY before it enters any filing: date of appointment/election, the work area covered,
  and whether MSH has been notified of the appointment in writing (knowledge matters for
  any s 291 claim). If MSH was never told, obtain the union's confirmation of the date and
  provide it prospectively — knowledge from that point forward is then undeniable.

## 5. WHAT LAWFUL DELEGATE ACTIVITY ACTUALLY COVERS (and the one line that must hold)
PROTECTED (s 290, verified): organising or promoting lawful union activity; participating
in it; **representing or advancing the views, claims or interests of the union**; and
**giving or distributing information, or organising or encouraging discussion, about wages,
employment conditions and workplace rights** for or on behalf of the union. Plus EB12
cl 3.1.5 (representative role; furthering grievance and dispute procedures), cl 3.1.6
(member access to the delegate on any employment or industrial matter), cl 3.1.8
(facilities), cl 3.6.4 (resignation/turnover reports from local HR), cl 3.6.3 (raising
issues at the HCF or equivalent).
⇒ AVAILABLE EVEN WHILE EXCLUDED: representing members, raising collective issues with
management, requesting the cl 3.6.4 turnover report, participating in consultative
structures, and communicating with members about conditions and rights.

⛔ THE LINE THAT MUST HOLD — the delegate role is for the MEMBERS' matters, never his own.
- He must NOT use delegate standing to canvass colleagues about HIS case, gather evidence
  for it, or discuss his dispute with members. That would be misuse of office, attackable,
  and dangerous for the colleagues involved. Witness accounts remain governed by the
  existing rule: voluntary, in their words, on their initiative, never solicited.
- He must not hold himself out as speaking FOR the union without its authority. Delegate ≠
  authorised officer. Anything expressed as the union's position needs Together's sign-off.
- Unlawful activity is expressly NOT protected (s 290(d)-(g)).

## 6. ⭐ THE STRATEGIC OPTION THIS OPENS — THE COLLECTIVE ROUTE
The tabled package (hazard matrix, proposals, methodology, assessment request) is already
written about the ROOM, not about him: no allegations, no personal grievance, no reference
to his dispute. It can therefore properly be advanced as a **delegate's collective
submission on the conditions of the work area**, through the consultative structure —
rather than only as one affected worker's ss 47-49 contribution.
WHY IT IS STRONGER THAT WAY: cl 3.1.5 obliges the employer to support the delegate role in
consultative structures; a collective submission cannot be answered as a personal
grievance; refusal becomes a refusal to consult the workforce, not a refusal to accommodate
an individual; and the union's weight sits behind it.
⚠ CONDITIONS BEFORE DOING IT: (a) speak to Petering/Moran FIRST — the union may want
carriage, and acting without them causes friction; (b) keep his personal dispute entirely
in his own name, in separate correspondence, on separate days; (c) the collective document
must stay genuinely collective — not a vehicle for his case; (d) expect MSH to argue he is
conflicted, and be ready to answer that the document contains no personal claim and any
worker or the union could adopt it unchanged.

Email, Cory → Amy Mo (WorkCover), 26 Aug 2024, "Subject: Union Delegate", ref S23LW142013,

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES:

>>> skill/references/DELEGATE-VS-HSR-powers.md :: text
# UNION DELEGATE vs HSR — which role actually carries powers (verified 4 Aug 2026)
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Cory raised whether he has "powers under a union delegate".
> ⚠ FIRST FACT TO ESTABLISH: nothing in the record shows he holds either role. He is a
> union MEMBER (Together Qld; Moran background, Petering industrial officer). Member ≠
> delegate. Delegate ≠ HSR. The powers differ enormously.

## 1. UNION DELEGATE — representational, agreement-sourced
A delegate is elected/appointed by union members in a workplace. Powers come from
(a) the certified agreement's union-representation/delegate clause, and (b) IR Act
protections for industrial activity (s 284) — NOT from any statutory investigative power.
Typical content: reasonable paid time to represent members, access to facilities, notice
of changes, delegate training leave, right to be present in members' meetings.
⇒ Useful, protective, and it makes his activity plainly "industrial activity" for adverse
action purposes. It confers NO power to inspect, compel information, or issue notices.
⚠ Requires actual appointment through the union. Cannot be self-declared.

## 2. ⭐ HEALTH AND SAFETY REPRESENTATIVE (WHS Act ss 68–72, 85, 90) — the real powers
Elected by the work group. s 68 powers and functions, verified text:
- represent the workers of the work group in WHS matters;
- **monitor the measures taken by the PCBU in compliance with the Act**;
- **investigate complaints from members of the work group about WHS**;
- **inquire into anything that appears to be a risk to health or safety arising from the
  conduct of the business**;
and in exercising those functions may —
- **inspect the workplace** on reasonable notice (and immediately, without notice, after an
  incident or where there is serious risk from immediate/imminent exposure);
- accompany an inspector, or a WHS entry permit holder, during an inspection;
- be present at WHS interviews between a worker and the PCBU or an inspector (with consent);
- **request the establishment of a health and safety committee**;
- **request and receive information concerning the WHS of workers in the work group**;
- **request the assistance of a suitable entity** (this is the route to bringing in outside
  help — including a regulator's inspector);
plus, under Div 6/7: **direct unsafe work to cease**, and **issue provisional improvement
notices (PINs)**.
LIMITS (also verified): s 68(3) — no access to personal or medical information about a
worker without consent unless de-identified; s 69 — powers limited to that work group;
training is prescribed (the PCBU must allow the HSR to choose and attend training and pay
the fees — penalty for failing to facilitate), and the cease-work/PIN powers require the
prescribed training to have been completed.

## 3. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR HIM, HONESTLY
- The HSR route is the only one that carries investigative-style powers — and it is
  designed for the WORK GROUP's safety, not for running a personal dispute. Using HSR
  powers to advance his own case would be visible, criticisable, and would taint both.
- ⚠ He is currently excluded from the workplace. An excluded worker cannot practically
  discharge HSR functions, and standing for election now would read as positioning.
- ⭐ WHAT IS AVAILABLE AND CONSTRUCTIVE NOW: **request that a work group be determined and
  an HSR be elected for Switchboard Services** — a request any worker may make, which the
  PCBU must facilitate. He does not need to be the HSR. An HSR existing at all creates a
  permanent consultation channel with statutory powers, independent of him, which is
  precisely the structural fix his tabled package argues for (and it survives whatever
  happens to him personally).
- If elected later, in calmer circumstances, the powers above become available — including
  requesting information and requesting the assistance of a suitable entity.

## 4. THE ASK, IF HE WANTS IT ON THE RECORD (Stage 1/2 or the tabled discussion)
"I ask that a work group be determined for Switchboard Services and that the election of a
health and safety representative be facilitated, as the Act provides. I am not seeking the
role; I am asking that the room have one."
⇒ Neutral, constructive, statutory, and unanswerable — and it converts a personal dispute
into a structural improvement the Health Service cannot reasonably refuse.

## ⚠️⚠️ 3.1 REDEPLOYMENT IS NOT A FAVOUR — IT IS THE STATUTORY OUTCOME OF THE PROCESS THEY ARE RUNNING
**PS Act s 107** — after a div 5 medical report, the chief executive may:
> *"(a) **transfer or redeploy** the employee; or (b) if it is not reasonably practicable to transfer
> or redeploy the employee— … **retire** the employee."*

⇒ ⛔ **If the RFMI is the front end of div 5, transfer/redeploy is where it ends.** That is the risk
in the current process, and it is why the RFMI response asks at Part 8 **what decision is
contemplated and under what instrument**.
⭐ **s 131(1)(g)** — a **transfer decision is appealable** to the IRC. ⚠️ But **s 132(4)(a)** bars a
*fair treatment* appeal against div 5 decisions, so the appeal must be framed as a **transfer
decision**, not a fair treatment one. **Get this right or lose the route.**

# PART 4 — WHY IT READS AS ADVERSE ACTION, IN THE STATUTORY WORDS
**IR Act s 282(1)** — adverse action is taken if the employer:
> *"(b) **injures the employee in the employee's employment**; or (c) **alters the position of the
> employee to the employee's prejudice**"*

⇒ ⭐⭐ **Neither requires a dismissal.** Removal of duties, unrostered supernumerary status, removal
from the department, exclusion, leave debiting and non-payment all sit comfortably within (b) and (c).
⇒ **s 284** — the workplace rights are engaged (Agreement benefit; ability to start a process; ability
to make a complaint or inquiry about employment).
⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **s 306 — he does not prove the reason. They disprove it.**
⇒ **s 571** — accessorial liability reaches individuals. **s 307** — advising, encouraging, inciting.
⇒ **PID Act s 40(5)** — enough that the disclosure is **a substantial ground**, *"even if there is
another ground"*.

| 5 | Name the process | QH-IMP-401-5 (worker must be told the process + dispute path); cl 1.11.1 information objective | Identify in writing: instrument, steps, decision-maker, end-decision. If none exists: adopt the Workplace Rehabilitation Standard's own framework — a documented RTW plan AGREED WITH THE WORKER, with review dates |
| 6 | Separate the conflicted functions | s 89 PS Act; Code cl 1.2 | Decisions on my attendance/duties/pay by an officer outside Corporate Services; the delegation and any s 89(2) authorisation in writing; Stage conductors nominated by HR; conflicts recorded per the ordinary register |
| 7 | Feedback on the WHS matters raised | cl 7.1.11 ("appropriate feedback... to employees who raise WHS matters") | A written response per matter raised — even one line each: received, assessed, outcome. A table would do |
| 8 | The records | Dispute §4(e)–(f); Sch 2 preserved policies | E12 + E13 copies; the 12-month roster/payroll record — ordinary HR production, no order needed |
| 9 | Information handling | IP Act QPPs 6/11; HR Act ss 25/26(2)/58; (the CE letter (a)–(c)) | Confine, correct, confirm non-dissemination — per the letter; extends to any further sensitive material the disclosure list reveals |
| 10 | The substance of the safety report investigated | Clinical governance; PID handling obligations | ⛔ SEQUENCED — not tabled now. When the PID channel turns: assessment of the substance by officers outside the implicated chain, on the material already provided, outcome advised in writing |

## THE CONSULTATION ARCHITECTURE (standing, all items)
- I attend any discussion at any time, with a support person and my union representative.
- Meetings occur ALONGSIDE, never instead of, written responses (his existing line — keep).
- Everything agreed is confirmed in writing before it is treated as resolved; nothing is
  signed in the room.
- Participation waives nothing: cl 1.11.4 (no prejudice by continuation), and every clock
  continues unless a written agreement says otherwise.
- Tone standing order: every proposal is offered as the ORDINARY way — "this requires no
  restructuring and no findings about anyone" — the same register as the CE letter.

## WHY THIS DOCUMENT EXISTS
When any door opens (Stage 1/2, scoping, an s 89 reallocation, a settlement conference), he
is never the party who has to be asked "well, what do you want?" — the constructive,
instrument-anchored, immediately-implementable answer is already in hand. The party with
the plan runs the meeting.

# ANNEX A — THE SWITCHBOARD OPERATING MODEL (Cory's substantive reform proposals, 4 Aug 2026)
> His controls package for the assessment/controls consultation, cl 7.1.5 forums, or Stage 2.
> Each proposal = a CONTROL tied to a Code hazard category and an evidence anchor already in
> the record. Tabled as work design, never as criticism of any person. Near-zero cost.

## A1. CONSULT-BEFORE-DIRECTIVE ("operators asked first")
No operational change to Switchboard processes issues without prior consultation with the
operators who work the board. Rationale: the Switchboard is a real-time expert system (affidavit
¶7 — six concurrent platforms); operators hold the operational knowledge; in a fast-paced
direct environment a directive drafted away from the room routinely misfires (the MASPER
example, ¶27). ⭐ FRAMING: this is not an inversion of management — WHS ss 47–49 ALREADY
require consultation on changes affecting health/safety; the proposal is simply compliance,
systematised. Controls: role clarity + change management (Code categories). Evidence anchor:
¶¶26–28 (unilateral "effective immediately" directives; consultation raised 16 Jun 2023 and
15 May 2024, never actioned).

## A2. THE ROTATIONAL INTEGRATED MANAGER ("on the phones, in the room")
The Switchboard manager works a regular rostered rotation ON the board — on the phones,
physically integrated into the room (e.g., a minimum number of console shifts per fortnight).
Rationale: management decisions about a real-time environment require direct current knowledge
of it (work-as-done vs work-as-imagined — the Code's own logic); presence fixes availability;
comms-centre team leaders working consoles is the standard model in emergency communications.
Controls: support/supervision availability + erratic-presence hazard. Evidence anchor: ¶¶20,
26 (manager "frequently not contactable"; presence "erratic"; Item 9 security-access records).

## A3. COMPLAINT-RESPONSE SERVICE STANDARD
Complaints/escalations emailed to Switchboard management: acknowledged within 1 business day,
substantively answered within 3; automatic escalation to the CLS pathway (Ms Forrest's own
7 Jul 2026 description) if the manager is unavailable — nothing sits for days, and nothing
returns to accumulate at the operator's console. Controls: organisational justice
(informational fairness) + workload. Evidence anchor: ¶¶19–20 (complaints "returned to, and
accumulated at, the Switchboard"; "often left unresolved" — his 15 May 2024 words).

## A4. ONE RULEBOOK FOR THE ROOM
The manager-in-rotation is subject to the same frameworks as operators: the roster rules,
minimum-notice requirements, FRMS breaks, leave processes — applied identically. Rationale:
organisational justice is consistency; the record's defining defect is asymmetry (deadlines
for him, none for them; leave rules enforced downward, not upward). Controls: organisational
justice (procedural fairness). Evidence anchor: the substitution pattern; the asymmetry pair;
¶¶32–40 (fatigue/leave handling).

## A5. PATIENT SAFETY AS THE DESIGN PRINCIPLE
(a) Clear ownership + backup for SPOK/on-call roster accuracy (the emergency-paging
dependency, ¶¶6, 17, 29); (b) directory-update access restored with a backup pathway (the
single-person bottleneck of the 18 Jul 2023 access restriction, ¶22); (c) a defined escalation
path when a DSO or the manager is unavailable (¶¶15, 18, 20). Every element maps a documented
failure to a control. Evidence anchor: ¶¶6–25 + the Respondent's Form 24 admission that
contact-detail accuracy is "a critical function... to ensure... patient safety".

## TABLING RULES
- These are CONTROLS proposed IN consultation — table at the assessment's controls stage,
  the cl 7.1.5 forum, or Stage 2. Never in open correspondence as demands.
- Always the room, never the person: "the model", "the role", "the rotation" — no names.
- Lead with A5 (patient safety) — it is the anchor that makes A1–A4 obviously reasonable.
- Cost framing: near-zero — rostering and process changes only; no new positions.

## A6. THE 24/7 ON-SHIFT SUPERVISOR (added 4 Aug, Cory's refinement)
A rostered shift-supervisor FUNCTION on every shift, rotating among trained operators, held
while working the board, carrying an in-charge allowance/classification increment.
Controls: POOR SUPPORT (supervision present 24/7, incl. the weekend vacuum ¶18) + INADEQUATE
REWARD & RECOGNITION (a career pathway inside the room — the one Code category previously
untreated) + ISOLATED WORK + ROLE CLARITY (a named escalation point every shift) + the
single-person-dependence lesson (Stibbard ¶22). Cost honesty: the one non-zero-cost proposal
(modest per-shift allowance) — framed as offset by turnover/absence reduction; QAS/000-centre
standard model. Role not person: open by rotation and merit.

## A7. EVIDENCE-BASED ROSTERING (added 4 Aug)
Rosters built from the demand data the room already generates (his ¶9 monthly stats, console
volumes, code activity): coverage matched to peaks; FRMS breaks built into design (10-hour
minimum enforced structurally — the Stressor 3 fix); proper notice; equity visible on the
roster's face (converts the "roster was equitable" contest into a measurable). Controls:
FATIGUE + HIGH DEMANDS + ORGANISATIONAL JUSTICE. The data exists; the ask is only that the
roster be built from it.

# ANNEX B — EXTERNAL FRAMEWORKS VALIDATING THE MODEL (researched 4 Aug 2026)
> The authority backing for each proposal if challenged at consultation. "This is the
> standard model" now carries citations. Strategy layer — cite orally/if pressed.

| Proposal | Validating framework |
|---|---|
| Evidence-based rostering (P7) | **APCO Project RETAINS** — the emergency-communications industry's staffing/retention toolkit (staffing tool built from three national workforce surveys); **NENA staffing + daily-performance standards** (NENA-STA-014.2-2025); **Erlang C** workforce modelling — the universal call-centre staffing method |
| 24/7 on-shift supervisor (P6) | Standard PSAP/ECC room design literally builds a **supervisor console** into the floor plan; supervisor-support systems (e.g. ConsoleALERT-class) exist because 24/7 on-floor supervision is the industry baseline; APCO/NENA QA standard assumes supervisory review structures |
| Structured handover + decision log (P8) | **ISBAR** — the clinical handover protocol already mandated across Australian health incl. QH clinical settings; **NSQHS Standard 6 (Communicating for Safety)** — the hospital's own accreditation standard for structured clinical communication. Framing: the hospital already requires structured handover at every clinical interface — the proposal extends the hospital's own standard to its communications hub |
| The whole mapping / assessment approach | **ISO 45003** (psychological health & safety at work — guidelines for managing psychosocial risk, sitting on **ISO 45001**); SafeWork Australia model framework, of which the QLD 2022 Code is the local instance |
| Recognition/retention pathway (P6) | APCO RETAINS retention + employee-satisfaction tools — the industry's own finding that recognition and progression are the retention levers in comms centres |

⭐ The killer framing available at any table: "None of this is novel. The emergency
communications industry standardised on-floor supervision and data-based staffing decades
ago; the hospital itself mandates structured handover in every clinical area under its own
accreditation standards; and ISO has published the international guideline for exactly this
kind of psychosocial risk management. The Switchboard is the one emergency communications
room in the building that has none of it."

# FORENSIC ASSESSMENT — THE REQUEST, ITS AUTHORITY, AND THE 31 JULY SEQUENCE

> Built 31 July 2026 from the full corpus (`corpus/FULL_CORPUS.md`), the source PDFs, and PDF
> metadata. **Every quotation is from a document in this repo. Times converted to AEST.**
> Supersedes the timing analysis in `31JUL-error-and-rush-assessment.md` §A and the origin dating in
> earlier files.

# PART 1 — THE INSTRUMENT CHANGED FUNCTION. THAT IS THE CASE.

## 1.1 What the ECC was asked for — 5 May 2026, 14:38

> **Taylor → Cory:** "To ensure we have a clear understanding of your current capacity and can
> **provide the most appropriate support in the workplace**, could you please arrange for the
> attached Employee Capabilities Checklist (ECC) to be completed by your GP?
> Once the ECC has been returned together with a supporting Medical Certificate, I will review the
> information provided and we can then **discuss the next steps to ensure you are supported and
> working safely**."

**Read what is not there.** No condition. No consequence. No suggestion he cannot attend. No
statute. The stated purpose is **support for a person who is working** — *"in the workplace"*,
*"working safely"*.

## 1.2 ⭐⭐ HE WAS WORKING, ROSTERED, WITH THE ECC OUTSTANDING — 13 and 21 May

> **13 May 2026** — Taylor circulates **"Switch Roster PP26"**. He is on it.
> **19 May 2026, 10:21** — Taylor: *"Hope you are well, just following up on below email and ECC
> progress."* **No consequence stated. No deadline. No Act.**
> **21 May 2026, 16:00** — **Cory → Taylor:** *"1. **ECC progress** — I have an appointment booked
> for **5 June** to get the ECC completed… 2. **Tomorrow's roster** — I also have a court mention in
> Brisbane tomorrow at 10am and **I'm currently rostered on the morning shift**. In order of
> preference, I'd like to: swap my morning for someone's afternoon shift, or come in around 1pm…"*

⇒ **On 21 May he is rostered, at work, arranging a shift swap, with the ECC outstanding and an
appointment three weeks away — and nobody suggests he cannot attend.**

**This is the single most important document in the sequence.** It is documentary proof, in his own
hand and unanswered by any contrary word from MSH, that **for at least sixteen days the ECC was not
a precondition to attendance.** MSH treated it as a support measure, because that is what it said it
was.

## 1.3 The conversion — 26 June 2026, 10:42

> **Taylor → Cory:** "**Until we receive appropriate medical clearance, including a completed
> Employee Capacity Certificate (ECC), we are unable to facilitate your return to work.**… As your
> employer, we have a legal obligation under **section 19 of the Queensland Work Health and Safety
> Act 2011**, which sets out the primary duty of care to ensure, so far as is reasonably
> practicable, the health and safety of workers…
> Please note regards to your shifts this weekend — **if we have not received the documentation with
> adequate time to review, you will be unable to return to work.**"

⇒ **Same document. Same manager. Opposite function.** On 5 May it existed so he could be *supported
at work*. By 26 June it is the thing standing between him and the workplace, and a statute has
appeared to justify it.

## 1.4 ⭐ THE CONVERSION WINDOW IS 19 MAY – 26 JUNE, AND SOMETHING IS IN IT
Between the last "no consequence" follow-up and the bar:
| 24 May 2026 | **"FW: Conflict of interest — Update"** — in **two** packs (01 and 03) |
| 31 May 2026 | **"EMR Approval"** — Taylor |
| 5 Jun 2026 | **MSH's 28-page objection to the 64G, signed by the Chief Executive** (K-LM26/729) |
| 23 Jun 2026 | **The 64G application is filed and sealed** |
| **26 Jun 2026** | **The ECC becomes a bar to attendance** |

⚠️ **DO NOT PLEAD THIS AS CAUSATION.** It is a sequence, not a proven link, and asserting otherwise
would repeat the error corrected at §3.13 of `MASTER.md`. **[ ] Read the 24 May conflict-of-interest
item and the 31 May EMR item before drawing any inference at all.** Recorded as a window to
investigate, nothing more.

## 1.5 The ECC arrives and is inverted — 3 July 2026

| Time (AEST) | |
|---|---|
| **14:32** | ECC delivered to Injury Management, certifying **fit with restrictions** |
| **14:34** | Cory → Taylor: *"the doctor filled out the form. I sent it off to the Injury Management team today."* |
| **14:49** — **15 minutes later** | **Taylor:** *"As you have not confirmed leave type for the past pay period — I will continue to process as **Sick leave / Sick leave no pay**"* |
| **15:18** | **Cory:** *"It certifies me **fit to resume from 3 July 2026**. Could you please **confirm I'm right to attend**, or otherwise let me know my next returning shift."* |
| — | ⭐ **That question has never been answered.** |
| **17 Jul** | Taylor: *"I will be submitting your leave as **income protection no pay** from the 13th July 26"* |

⇒ **Fifteen minutes after being told the certificate had been provided, the response was about leave
type — not about returning.** The certificate said *fit*. The direct question *"confirm I'm right to
attend"* went unanswered, and the leave treatment moved from **accrued leave → sick leave no pay →
income protection no pay**.

# PART 2 — THE LEGAL AUTHORITY, TESTED ACT BY ACT

**Four distinct things were done. They require different authority. Only one of them has any.**

## 2.1 The information request — ✅ SUPPORTABLE
| Basis | Effect |
|---|---|
| Implied contractual power to give **reasonable and lawful directions** | The true source. Bounded by **reasonableness** |
| **G03 cl 3** | supporting information "**where necessary**, to either identify required workplace adjustments and/or assess the suitability of proposed adjustments" |
| **IP Act, QPP 3.3(a)** | sensitive information requires **consent** *and* **reasonable necessity** |
| **AD Act s 124(3)** | onus on MSH to prove the information was "reasonably required" |

⇒ **The 5 May request was properly founded.** It was necessary, proportionate, framed as support,
and Cory complied — he booked the appointment and produced the certificate.
⇒ **Three independent necessity tests apply to the 31 July request**, and each is a live question.

## 2.2 The exclusion from the workplace — ❌ NO AUTHORITY
**Cited: WHS s 19 (26 June) and, from 29–31 July, ss 17 and 19.**

> **s 19(1)** "A person conducting a business or undertaking **must ensure**, so far as is reasonably
> practicable, the health and safety of workers…"
> **s 17** a duty to ensure health and safety "requires the person to **eliminate** risks… or
> **minimise** those risks so far as is reasonably practicable."

⇒ **Both are duties imposed on MSH. Neither confers any power over a worker.** A duty to ensure
safety is not a power to exclude, and the Psychosocial Code 2022 treats psychosocial hazards as
**features of the work**, controlled by the PCBU. **Removing the worker is not a control — it is the
avoidance of the assessment.**
⇒ **G03 says the opposite.** cl 1.1: adjustments exist so employees "**continue work during their
recovery**". cl 1: managers must ensure work "**do[es] not unreasonably prevent employment for
people**".
⇒ **The reasonableness limb fails on MSH's own record.** A direction not to attend, maintained for
five weeks against a certificate of fitness, with **no risk assessment**, **no consultation under
WHS ss 47–49**, and **no answer to "confirm I'm right to attend"**, is not a reasonable direction.

## 2.3 The leave treatment — ❌ NO AUTHORITY, AND THE ONE STATUTORY LINK WAS NEVER INVOKED
Accrued leave → **sick leave no pay** (3 Jul) → **income protection no pay** (17 Jul).

> **PS Act 2022 s 105:** "The employee **must not be given sick leave** for any period during which
> the employee **fails to comply with a requirement under section 104(b)**."

⇒ **s 105 is the only statutory link in the entire division between a medical-information process
and leave.** It operates **solely** where an s 104(b) requirement to submit to examination is not
complied with. **s 104 was never invoked. s 105 supplies nothing here.**
⇒ **And Cory did not fail to comply with anything.** He booked the appointment, attended, and
produced the certificate.
⇒ **Absence caused by the employer's own direction is not the employee's leave.** Nothing cited
permits debiting it.

## 2.4 ⭐ THE POWER THAT EXISTS AND WAS NEVER USED
> **PS Act 2022 s 103** applies if — "(a) the employee **is absent from duty** **or** the chief
> executive is reasonably satisfied the employee **is not performing** the employee's duties
> satisfactorily; **and** (b) the chief executive **reasonably suspects** that the absence or
> unsatisfactory performance **is caused by** mental or physical illness or disability."
> **s 104** "The chief executive **may** (a) appoint a doctor… and (b) **require the employee to
> submit** to the medical examination."

⇒ **This is the only statutory power to compel medical examination, and it was never cited — not
once, by any of four officers, across five weeks.**
⇒ ⭐ **And the gateway cannot be met.** No performance issue has ever been put to Cory. That leaves
absence — **and the absence is MSH's own act.** An employer cannot exclude a worker and then rely on
the resulting absence as the gateway to a power over him. **s 103 is not satisfied on facts of MSH's
own making.**

## 2.5 The 31 July request itself — ❌ FOUR DEFECTS ON THE FACE
| | |
|---|---|
| **Q6** | asks whether he can perform the role *"**without restrictions or modifications**"* — when **G03**, cited in the same letter, and **AD Act s 34** ask about **genuine occupational requirements *with* reasonable adjustment**. **The wrong test, under their own policy.** |
| **Q9** | *"**If we are not able to accommodate** the restrictions… is Mr Shepherd able to safely return?"* — **G03 cl 2** places the onus on **Queensland Health** to prove an adjustment unreasonable, tested against **the whole organisation**. It asks the doctor to discharge MSH's onus. |
| **Q3** | asks a **general practitioner** whether a **workplace** is safe under existing reporting arrangements — a **s 19 duty on the PCBU**. |
| **Q2** | rests on *"the Health Service **is not aware of any concerns being raised**"* — **eight weeks** after its own **Chief Executive** engaged **PID 24-ESU-1130 by reference number** in the 5 June objection. |

## 2.6 ⚠️ WHAT MUST BE CONCEDED — state it before it is put
1. **The WHS Act was cited on 26 June, before any challenge.** The "citations were reasoned
   backwards" framing **does not hold for the WHS Act** and must not be run.
2. **The 5 May request was legitimate**, and MSH offered a **consent mechanism** on 31 July —
   operating the correct legal model under QPP 3.3 even if it never articulated it.
3. **The theory is coherent, not absurd.** Forrest articulated it on 7 July: unresolved matters
   involving line management → cannot assess the psychosocial risk → cannot safely permit a return.
   **Engage it; do not dismiss it.** Its answer is that **the thing MSH says it cannot understand is
   the thing it holds the file on** — the PID, the October 2025 complaint, the February 2026
   complaint, and two years of correspondence.
