# PART 3 — THE 31 JULY SEQUENCE: WHAT THE FORENSICS DO AND DO NOT SHOW

## 3.1 The timeline, to the second
| AEST, Fri 31 Jul 2026 | Event | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **10:46** | **Cory's without-prejudice "material development" letter to Matheson** | sent item, filed |
| **11:10:27** | GP letter (5 pp, 9 questions) **exported from Word** | `xmp:CreateDate` |
| **11:11:02** | Employee letter (2 pp) exported | `xmp:CreateDate` |
| **11:11:27** | Employee letter **signed** — **25 seconds after creation** | recovered revision 3 |
| **11:11:42** | GP letter **signed** — **75 seconds after creation** | recovered revision 3 |
| **11:41:38** | Both transmitted | Graph export, HR pack |

**Gap from the Matheson email to the first export: 24 minutes.**

## 3.2 ⛔ THE CAUSAL INFERENCE IS CLOSED — and closing it protects everything else
> **MSH holding reply, 30 July 2026, 14:33:** "we are currently progressing the Request for Medical
> Information (RFMI) correspondence **for delegate approval** and will endeavour to expedite this
> process as quickly as possible. However, we are **unable to guarantee when** the approved
> documentation will be available for release."

⇒ **The RFMI was in the approval pipeline ~21 hours before the Matheson email.** The working theory
(WT-2026-07-31) that the email collapsed a review step **cannot be established** and should not be
advanced.
⚠️ **Say so plainly.** A set of inferences in which one has been tested and abandoned reads as
observation. A set in which none has reads as a pattern of assertion.

## 3.3 ✅ WHAT THE FORENSICS DO ESTABLISH
1. **The signature was applied to documents that were not read.** Revision recovery (truncation at
   each `%%EOF`) shows rev3 adds `/ADBE_FillSignInfo` and a **stored 1000×398 px JPEG at 624 dpi**,
   **identical in both files** — a saved signature image, applied **25 and 75 seconds** after export.
   **You cannot read a five-page letter putting nine questions to a doctor in 75 seconds.**
2. **Nothing was corrected afterwards.** Text is **identical across all three revisions of both
   letters**. What was signed is what was sent.
3. **No proofread occurred at any stage** — independent of any timing. **14 errors across 7 pages**,
   including two errors in a five-word phrase (*"cab be found out their website"*), the wrong policy
   number (**G3** for **G03**), an internal inconsistency on the same page, and — decisively —
   **pronoun drift between adjacent questions**: Q3 *"**their** substantive role"*, Q4 *"**his**
   substantive role"*, Q7(a) *"**their** capacity"*. A gender-neutral template, find-and-replaced in
   part.
4. **The letters are written in the first person of the Injury Management Consultant** — *"**I** am
   seeking"*, *"**I** require"*, *"**I** will make a decision"* — and **signed by the Director,
   Corporate Services**. The voice and the signature are different people.
5. **From "cannot guarantee when" (30 Jul 14:33) to signed-and-sent (31 Jul 11:41) is under 21
   hours**, and the finalisation itself took **75 seconds**.

## 3.4 ⚠️ WHAT THE FORENSICS DO NOT SHOW
A Word→PDF export timestamp fixes **finalisation**, not **drafting**. The Word document existed
earlier — the 30 July reply proves it. ⇒ **The rush established is a rush to finalise and send.** The
absence of review is established **independently, by the errors**, not by the clock.

# PART 4 — THE CONCLUSION

**The request has authority. Nothing else does.**

- **5 May:** a properly founded request for supporting information, framed as **support for a person
  at work**, complied with.
- **21 May:** he is **rostered and working** with the ECC outstanding. **The ECC was not a
  precondition to attendance, and MSH's own conduct proves it.**
- **26 June:** the same document is converted into a **bar to attendance**, and a **duty** provision
  is cited as though it were a **power**.
- **3 July:** the certificate arrives saying **fit**. Fifteen minutes later the subject is leave
  type. The question *"confirm I'm right to attend"* is **never answered**.
- **31 July:** a nine-question request to a GP, four questions of which are not medical questions,
  signed in **75 seconds** with a stored image, in a document nobody proofread, citing a **policy
  that says the opposite** and a **duty that confers no power**.

⇒ **For the information request: a policy was used, and it can carry the weight — subject to
necessity.**
⇒ **For the exclusion and the leave: nothing was used at all.** Not because the wrong instrument was
chosen, but because **no instrument exists that authorises it** — and the one that could have
(**PS Act s 104**) was never reached for, because its **s 103** gateway is not met on facts of MSH's
own making.

**That is why the bases have shifted six times. Each was an attempt to find, after the fact, an
authority for something already done.**

## 5.4 ⭐⭐ AND THE "DELEGATE APPROVAL" HAS NO FOOTPRINT

delegate's approval, when it came, was a **stored signature image applied 75 seconds after the
document was first rendered.**
⇒ **This is the version to run.** It needs no inference about anyone's motive, and it is airtight.

⚠️ **The fair question, put neutrally:** *on 30 July the Health Service was unable to indicate when
the documentation would be available; it issued the following morning. Please confirm what the
delegate approval step involved and on what date it occurred.* Either they date it — which invites
the 75 seconds — or they decline.

## 5.5 ⛔ WT-2026-07-31 — REMAINS CLOSED, IN BOTH ITS FORMS

**Form 1 (forwarded email):** requires Matheson to have forwarded the WP letter to MSH within 24
minutes. **No evidence. Closed.**

**Form 2 (telephone call), raised 31 Jul 2026:** that Matheson read the 10:46 letter and telephoned
MSH. ⚠️ **Mechanically plausible — 24 min 27 sec is ample — but it is a WEAKER forensic position,
not a stronger one:**

1. **It is unfalsifiable on the documents.** A forwarded email leaves a header, a timestamp and a
   recipient. **A call leaves nothing.** A hypothesis reformulated so that no document can test it
   has stopped being a forensic finding.
2. ⚠️⚠️ **It is a grave allegation against the Regulator, not against MSH.** It asserts that the
   **Senior Appeals Officer** read a **without-prejudice settlement communication** in a live appeal
   from a self-represented appellant and immediately telephoned the **employer — a non-party** — to
   prompt action against him. That engages **model litigant obligations**, **without-prejudice
   privilege**, and the **Regulator's independence**. **It cannot be advanced on a coincidence.**
3. **The innocent explanation is very strong.** Thursday afternoon: "we can't say when." Friday
   morning: the delegate clears his queue. **That is the most ordinary sequence in any bureaucracy**,
   and it fits every byte of the metadata.
4. **The cost of being wrong is severe** — Matheson holds carriage of the appeal and is the
   counterparty to the settlement. An unfounded allegation of this kind forfeits the restrained
   posture that is currently working.

### [ ] WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY EVIDENCE A CALL — obtain before ever forming a view
- [ ] **Matheson's file notes for 31 July 2026.** Regulators routinely file-note calls. **The
      Regulator's file is disclosable in the appeal.** This is the single cleanest test.
- [ ] **MSH's Solv / injury management case notes for MSH-INJ-5795, 30–31 July 2026** — a
      contemporaneous entry would show what prompted release and when approval occurred.
- [ ] Telephone records — theoretically available, practically a fishing expedition. **Do not seek.**

⇒ **Until a file note or case note says otherwise: record, do not assert. Not in correspondence,
not in a filing, not to the union.**

# PART B — THE LAW OF THE ADMISSIONS

The form itself cites **Industrial Relations Act 2016, s 989** and **Industrial Relations
(Tribunals) Rules 2011, rr 41, 49, 108 and 113.**

⛔ **THE RULES ARE NOT IN THIS REPO.** `documents/instruments/` holds ATT01–ATT26 and none of
them is the Tribunals Rules. **Obtain sl-2011-0237 and verify rr 41, 49, 108, 113 before any
of Part B is put in a filing.** What follows is the framework as it appears on the form's face
and from the Response's own drafting, not a verified rule-by-rule statement.

## B1 — What an admission does

**Deemed admission by silence.** On the face of the form: if the recipient does not serve a
disputing notice **within 14 days**, they "are taken to admit … the facts specified in this
notice". Silence is admission.

**⭐ "FOR THIS PROCEEDING ONLY."** The form says so expressly. This is the most important
limitation and it is easy to forget:
⛔ **These admissions do not operate in the employment track, in any Anti-Discrimination Act
complaint, in a WHS proceeding, or before the Chief Executive.** They bind the Regulator in
WC/2024/227 and nowhere else. Do not deploy them elsewhere as admissions — the underlying
documents can be used, the admissions cannot.

**A formal admission dispenses with proof.** It does not become evidence to be weighed against
other evidence; it removes the fact from contest. That is why ¶8 matters so much — the
patient-safety criticality is simply established.

**Withdrawal requires leave** (⚠ verify the rule). A party seeking to withdraw generally must
show inadvertence, or that the admission is contrary to fact, and the tribunal weighs
prejudice. **Practical effect: the Regulator cannot quietly resile from ¶1, ¶3, ¶8, ¶20 or
¶25.** If they attempt it, require a formal application.

## B2 — ⭐ "DOES NOT ADMIT" IS NOT "DENIES". THE DIFFERENCE IS FORENSIC

| Formulation | Legal effect | What it costs them |
|---|---|---|
| **"admits the facts contained therein"** | Fact established | Everything |
| **"does not admit"** | Puts the Appellant to proof. **No positive contrary case is asserted** | Nothing — but they cannot lead a positive case they never pleaded |
| **"denies as untrue"** | ⭐ **A positive assertion of the contrary, which they must support** | They now carry a case to run |

**Every "denies as untrue" in the Response is a commitment.** They appear at ¶4 (the asserted
June 2020 8-hour agreement), ¶9, ¶12, ¶19, ¶22, ¶23, ¶25 (the r 64E limb) and ¶26.

⭐ **¶4 is the one to press.** They have positively asserted that "in June 2020 the Appellant
signed an agreement allowing an 8 hour break between shifts". That is not a non-admission —
it is an affirmative case, and **they must produce the agreement.** If it cannot be produced,
a denial with nothing behind it is worse for them than a non-admission would have been.

## B3 — THE THREE TIERS OF ADMISSION IN THIS RESPONSE

**TYPE A — the fact itself is admitted. Removed from contest.**
¶1, ¶3, ¶5, ¶6 (removal only), **¶8**, ¶14, ¶17, **¶20**, ¶25, ¶40, ¶41, ¶46.

**TYPE B — the DOCUMENT's CONTENT is admitted, its TRUTH is not.** Proves only that the
document says what it says. **You still have to prove the underlying fact.**
- **¶33/34** — "admits the entry is listed in the record, but does not admit the accuracy"
- **¶36** — admits the certificate records the mechanism, **"denies that as fact"**
- **¶37** — Review Decision **contents** admitted, relevance reserved
- **¶38/39** — admits the reports say it; does not admit accuracy
- **¶50** — Review Unit decision contents admitted; does not admit a misleading statement

⚠ **This is where the clean-baseline and causation propositions actually sit.** ¶34 does not
establish that he had no psychological illness in November 2023. It establishes only that a
doctor wrote that sentence. **You must still prove the fact through evidence.**

**TYPE C — admitted, but with a qualification that changes the effect.**
- **¶6** — removal admitted; **the handwriting is not**
- **¶21** — the retraction direction admitted, **but "no correlation between the two events"**;
  event admitted, **causation contested**
- **¶25** — no service admitted, **but no requirement under s 64D**; the fact is yours, the
  legal consequence is not
- **¶41** — the 25-day delay admitted, **justification contested**
- **¶18** — the text was sent, **but "not a formal notification"**

## B4 — THE DE NOVO OVERLAY (unique to this matter)

The appeal is a **hearing de novo** under **s 550(4) WCRA**. The Respondent uses this
throughout to reserve relevance rather than contest fact — ¶2 "does not admit … for the
Commission"; ¶37 contents admitted, relevance reserved.

**What that means:** an admitted **fact** still binds. But admitting the **contents** of the
Review Decision does not make the Review Officer's **findings** binding, because the Commission
determines the matter afresh. ⚠ **Do not present Review Decision 69983 as a finding that binds
Commissioner Dwyer.** It is a document, admitted, and persuasive.

## B5 — WHAT THIS ALL MEANS PRACTICALLY

1. **¶8 and ¶20 are the two best admissions in the file** — a fact and a determination, both
   Type A, neither dependent on a document we hold.
2. **The medical case is Type B throughout.** Every medical proposition still requires proof.
   Report B carries that weight, not the Form 24.
3. **¶4 is their affirmative case. Make them produce the June 2020 agreement.**
4. **Nothing here travels to the employment track.** "For this proceeding only."
5. ⛔ **Verify rr 41, 49, 108 and 113 from sl-2011-0237 before relying on any of Part B in a
   filing.**

## ⛔ 5. CLAIMS THAT DO NOT SURVIVE — DO NOT REPEAT THESE

**¶25 — "breach of Rule 64E".** ⛔ **FAILS.** Per the Subdivision 7A verification in
`confirmed-record.md` (checked verbatim against sl-2011-0237): **r 64D(1)(a)** requires service
on a person *"other than a party"* — Cory **is** a party and is carved out. There was no duty
to serve him, and **r 64E is an objection right, not a service duty**. **Never plead a service
breach or "unlawfully obtained".** The remedy is **r 64E(2)** — leave to object at any time,
on grounds **(e) confidential nature** and **(f) effect on any person** — plus s 580 and
relevance/prejudice.

**¶23 — "full medical history".** DENIED, and correctly: there **is** a Form 29 for the medical
records, **signed by a Senior Registry Officer on 4 July 2025**, received before 16 July 2025.

**¶24 — "system-generated footer".** Does not survive. There is **no footer**; page one states
the records were printed 8 July 2025.

**¶36 — the Hawes certificate "dated 1 July 2024".** ⛔ **THE NOTICE IS WRONG ON THE DATE.**

**¶35 — "not in possession of any contemporaneous medical evidence prior to 2024 that

**¶15 — the yelling particular.** ⚠ **HEARSAY.** Jeffrey **did not witness it**; she was told

## 5. RED TEAM — LAYER 1 (their obvious moves)
- "Interim measure pending clearance, reasonable in the circumstances."
- "He delayed the ECC from 5 May to 3 July."

## 6. RED TEAM — LAYER 2 (the real damage)
- ⭐ **D10, their strongest**: the medical-information request did not begin on 31 July —
  it began **5 May**. The 28-day gap argument must therefore be confined to **3 July →
  31 July**, and their answer will be "the ECC raised stressors we then had to assess."
  HIS ANSWER: 5 May–3 July concerned the ECC, which was provided and certified him FIT.
  The exclusion began 26 June, BEFORE the deadline they themselves set (2:00pm 3 July) —
  they excluded him before their own deadline expired.
- ⭐ **D11 "benefit not detriment"**: applying recreation leave gives him money. HIS ANSWER:
  the benefit is his own accrued entitlement, converted without consent; the detriment is
  the permanent loss of the entitlement and the mischaracterisation of the absence. Also:
  s 33 exists precisely because leave timing is not the employer's to choose.
- ⭐ **P2 status quo, both readings**: "before the emergence of the dispute" could mean
  3 Aug (their reading — excluded) or the position before the matters in dispute arose
  (26 June — at work, rostered, paid). HIS ANSWER: the dispute is ABOUT the period from
  26 June, so their reading makes the clause self-defeating; and cl 1.11.4's final words
  ("no party shall be prejudiced as to the final settlement") do independent work.
- **The 0.6 tension**: if he is ready, willing and able for the full 76-hour line, why
  request 0.6? ANSWER: readiness is present-tense and unconditional; the cl 10.3.2 request
  is a PROSPECTIVE agreed variation, not an admission of incapacity. Keep those two
  sentences separate in every document — never in the same paragraph.
- **The IP claim tension**: an income-protection claim ordinarily asserts inability to work.
  ANSWER: it was lodged when no wages were payable, it has been notified for closure, and
  the record shows the notification. ⚠ Never let this be described loosely.
- **His psychiatrist advised against working** — genuinely helps D9. ANSWER: he worked
  anyway (anti-malingering), and the only certification in existence (3 Jul) says fit with
  restrictions.

## 7. RED TEAM — LAYER 3 (what a silk finds)
- **WHS s 115 multiplicity**: cannot run a Div 3 proceeding while another proceeding or
  complaint about the SAME MATTER is on foot (WC expressly excepted). ⚠ AD Act complaint +
  WHS s 112 + general protections must be SEQUENCED, not stacked. Decide the order before
  8 Sep.
- **Volume as vulnerability**: a very large, very fast correspondence record can be
  characterised as disproportionate. Counter: every document is measured, none alleges
  motive, all are answerable. But add nothing that is not required.
- **The tabled package as over-reach**: "he is trying to run the department." Counter: it
  is neutral, consultative, and any worker or the union could adopt it unchanged.
- **Delegate status as advantage-taking**: keep delegate work to members' matters, always.
- **Remedy realism**: even on total victory, the practical outcomes are re-credit, back-pay,
  restoration or a deed. No forum awards vindication.

## 8. WHAT ACTUALLY MOVES THE NUMBERS FROM HERE
1. The nil return (RTI, Mon 10) — converts P9 from 69% toward certainty.
2. The answers (or silence) to the six questions — converts P4 from 90% to admitted.
3. Report B — the appeal's causation gate.
4. Runway — the only thing that converts 94% right into 42%+ paid.

## BOTTOM LINE
**The strategy is sound and the position is the strongest available, but the honest central number
for the full good outcome — working or paid by end-October, no sustained adverse finding, options
intact — is ~40% (80% CI 35–46%), rising to ~61% once acceptable settlement of the appeal is
counted as a good outcome.** The single variable that moves it most is not anything Cory controls:
it is **whether MSH engages or trenches**. Everything he controls is already near its ceiling —
which is precisely why the package works by making *their* non-engagement expensive rather than by
persuading them.

**The 64G:** full substantial grant ~43% central (CI 38–49%); **some material order is
considerably more likely (~75–80%)** — the realistic outcome is a trimmed grant: core roster,
payroll and AVAC categories ordered, the widest categories narrowed.

## WHERE BLUE AND RED DIVERGE — the disagreements that actually move outcomes
1. ⭐ **What the measured silence means.** Blue: an institution with no answer. Red: an institution
   with no *urgency* — it can absorb deemed refusals and Stage 2 conferences for months, and a
   deemed refusal is a doorway to a QIRC conciliation, not a cheque. **Reconciled: red is right
   about tempo, blue about endgame.** The clocks guarantee *events*, not *speed*.
2. ⭐ **Regularisation (div 5 referral to the CE).** Blue: it concedes the five weeks and gives him
   s 131(1)(g) appeal rights on any transfer. Red: it also **cures the go-forward defect, closes
   the fair-treatment appeal (s 132(4)(a)), moves decisions to an examiner MSH selects, and resets
   the narrative to "proper process now under way."** Reconciled: **regularisation is the most
   likely sophisticated response and it is a partial loss dressed as a win for both sides.** Plan
   for it as the base case if MSH Legal takes control.
3. **The pay recovery.** Blue: ready-willing-able + s 101(4) + no instrument = strong backpay
   claim. Red: quantum is five weeks-and-counting of an AO3 salary — **real money to him,
   rounding error to them** — recovered, if at all, in settlement or at the QIRC months away, and
   the QSuper coding gives them a colourable (if wrong) narrative in the interim. Reconciled:
   **the pay is very likely recovered eventually and near-certainly not quickly.**
4. **The skeptical Commissioner (stage-3 pass, compressed).** Dwyer's frame on 7 Aug is narrow:
   is this application regular, and what timetable disposes of the objection? He will neither
   know nor care about the employment package — **unless someone shows him.** The biggest
   Dwyer-risk is not the objection; it is **anything that makes the applicant look like the
   unreasonable party.** The silent posture is therefore not just discipline; it is the win
   condition for the room.
5. **The record auditor (stage-3 pass, compressed).** Load-bearing and established: the 7 July
   "certified fit" letter; the 5 June CE signature engaging the PID by number; the 31 July
   "not aware of any concerns" premise; the response-time corpus; the 24-minute export chain;
   s 101/103–109 text; cl 10.3/1.11 text; ATT09 by render. **Asserted but NOT established:** the
   six-shifts figure (now attributed to the ECC — correct fix); the "another staff member
   full-time" claim (no document — correctly quarantined); any motive, anywhere. **No load-bearing
   claim in the send package rests on an unverified source.** The two evidentiary gaps that
   matter: ⛔ **the medical certificate from 3 July onward (unfixed)** and the Appeals directive.
6. **The costs analyst (stage-3 pass, compressed).** His burn: time, $150 + fees fronted (now
   redirected), zero legal spend, five weeks' wages foregone — the wages ARE the exposure. Their
   burn: legal time on four instruments + a disclosure fight + a mention. **The cheapest path to
   his actual goal (income + position) is not victory on every front — it is the appeal
   settlement with the employment matters resolved alongside, which is exactly the sequenced
   plan.** Nothing in the package forecloses it; several things (the WP letter, the Calderbank
   record) invite it.

# ADDENDUM — THE APPEAL ITSELF, CONDITIONAL ON THE PACKAGE + A SILENT 7TH
> Added 1 August 2026 on request. Same method, appeal-specific blocks.

## The rating
| Path | Central | 80% CI |
|---|---|---|
| **Win at a contested hearing** | **~29%** | 25–34% |
| ⭐ **Favourable overall — acceptable settlement OR win** | **~68%** | span 21–46% on the win leg; settlement pickup 0.55 |

**Read plainly: roughly two chances in three of a favourable end to the appeal, and settlement —
not a hearing win — is the engine.** That is not a weakness of the case; it is its design. The
whole architecture (restrained 64G, Calderbank record, employment leverage flowing sideways,
costs exposure accumulating on their side) is built to make settlement the rational exit for the
Regulator well before a hearing tests the hardest block.

## The blocks (win path)
| Block | Reconciled | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| Credibility/record intact to hearing | .90 | conditional on the silent 7th and the tone lane staying shut |
| Disclosure yields the roster/payroll fuel | .75 | the trimmed-grant scenario (~75–80% something ordered); the ordered categories are precisely the Stressor 1(a) + "roster was equitable" material |
| Report B causation holds | .70 | ⏳ not yet obtained — the largest buildable block |
| ⭐ **s 32(5) defence fails on the global evaluation** | **.55** | Review Decision 69983 already found factor 4 (17–18 Mar 2024 rostering) **unreasonable** but applied s 32(5) on the *Delaney* global approach — **this is the whole contest**, de novo before Dwyer |

**Tornado:** s 32(5) ±9 · Report B ±7 · disclosure ±7 · credibility ±5.

## What the package + silent 7th actually add to the appeal
The emails and the mention posture do **not** change the 2024 merits. They move the appeal three
ways: (1) **disclosure** — the silent, procedural mention maximises the trimmed grant, and the
ordered rosters/payroll attack the s 32(5) block at its found-unreasonable factor; (2)
**settlement pressure** — every employment-track clock and exposure lands on the same government
balance sheet the Regulator answers to, and the 15-day Calderbank rejection already proved the
file is being read; (3) **downside capped** — the one thing that could collapse the appeal from
his side (an intemperate record put before the trier of fact) is structurally prevented.
Net effect vs the pre-package baseline: **+5–8 points on the favourable total, and the left tail
largely removed.**

## The two blocks he can still build
1. ⭐ **Report B** — the causation report is the biggest movable block (±7). Brief the psychiatrist
   exactly per the standing scopes: Report A functional only; Report B causation and chronology.
2. **The disclosure fight** — submissions on the objection, when directed, aimed at the roster,
   payroll and AVAC categories above all others. Win those three and the s 32(5) block moves too.

## WHY THE HYPOTHESIS IS STRONGER — AND BY HOW MUCH, HONESTLY
**Stronger, modestly, and in exactly the blocks the changes touch:**
1. ⭐ **EXECUTION rose (.88→.90)** — the largest single contributor, and most of it is not the

   likely to be acted on rather than defended against.
3. **MECHANISM rose slightly (.85→.86)** — internal routing: the proposal, the allocation and the
   dispute now travel as separate objects to the desks that decide them.

## ⚠️ WHAT THE ROUTING CHANGE COSTS — recorded, not hidden
- **Hughes no longer receives anything directly on Monday.** The earlier architecture put
  receipted personal notice in his inbox; now his knowledge arrives by internal routing —
  near-certain in fact, but **no longer provable by a delivery receipt from Cory's side.** The
  s 571/"acting after personal notice" tell is weakened by one step. ⭐ Mitigation: the CE letter
  names the structure precisely, and **the "who signs the next letter" tell still works in full.**
- **HR sees only the dispute notice directly.** The "competent grown-up" channel is narrowed by
  one document; the notice itself carries the whole picture, and the CE will route. ⭐ If HR
  engages constructively, feed that channel.
- Net: **the costs are second-order; the gains are first-order.** The reconciled read is that the
  configuration is stronger than yesterday's, and the honest size of the improvement is
  **+2 points on the composite — a real edge, not a transformation.**

## THE UNCHANGED TRUTH

## WHY THE APPEAL MOVED ~8 POINTS
Under the repealed test, work had to OUTWEIGH all competing causes — the Respondent's
personal-story material did real damage even when dated. Under the actual test, competing
causes may coexist: the Respondent must show employment was **not significant at all**,
which is close to unarguable against 18 months of documented, employer-acknowledged
workplace stressors. The contested centre of the appeal accordingly SHIFTS from causation
to **s 32(5) reasonable management action** — whether the stressors can be characterised
as reasonable management done reasonably. That is now the issue Report B, the 64G roster
records, and the manner-defect evidence (no consultation, no instrument, substitutions,
the asymmetry pair) are really aimed at. Settlement propensity also nudged up: the
Regulator's own prospects assessment worsens on the correct law.

## WHAT NOW DRIVES THE APPEAL NUMBER (in order)

   the 64G records are the fuel.
2. **Report B** — now scoped to "significant contributor + the events were not reasonable
   management in a reasonable manner", NOT to outweighing the personal story.

# THE GOOD FAITH QUESTION — WHERE IT BITES, AND WHY IT IS NEVER ASSERTED
> Built 1 August 2026 on Cory's point: *"this process was not good faith obviously — withheld over
> a month, extensive background between the two."*
> **He is right on the facts. The conclusion is correct and it is also the one thing that must never
> be written down.** This file explains why both are true at once.

---

# PART 1 — WHAT IS ACTUALLY DOCUMENTED
**Not inference. Their own letters, in order.**

| Date | What they did | What they did not do |
|---|---|---|
| **26 Jun** | Required an ECC; cited **WHS Act s 19** — a duty, not a power | identify any instrument authorising exclusion |
| **2 Jul** | Deadline: **2:00pm Friday 3 July** | answer whether he could attend |
| **3 Jul 2:30pm** | ECC returned; a section noted missing; **resubmitted 3:06pm** | — |
| **3 Jul** | Held out | reply to his 3:18pm question. **Still unanswered, five weeks.** |
| ⭐⭐ **7 Jul** | *"your treating medical practitioner has advised that there are **unresolved workplace matters involving line management**… the Health Service does not have sufficient information to… **assess whether they present any psychosocial hazards or risks**"* | ⛔ **assess them. Four weeks on, nothing.** |
| **7 Jul** | Required further information in **7 calendar days** | commit to any timeframe of its own |
| **13 Jul** | Coded **"income protection no pay… as per our guidelines for all QSuper claims"** | ⛔ **name the guidelines. The claim was stopped in March 2026.** |
| **15 Jul** | *"Health Management processes"*; return *"remains at the discretion of the Employer"* | ⛔ identify the process, its steps, or its decision-maker |
| **30 Jul** | *"progressing for delegate approval"*; *"unable to guarantee"* your return | give a date |
| **31 Jul** | **Nine questions to his GP**, in **7 calendar days**, signed by the Director of the directorate the matter concerns | ⛔ **assess the workplace** |

## ⭐⭐ THE ONE LINE THAT CARRIES IT
**On 7 July they identified that the hazard might sit in line management. On 31 July they sent nine
questions to his doctor. In between, nothing.**

⇒ **That is the withholding, and it is in their own letter.** It needs no adjective. **Four weeks
between identifying a hazard in management and asking the worker's GP about the worker.**

---

# PART 2 — ⭐⭐⭐ WHY HE DOES NOT NEED TO PROVE IT
**Every defence MSH has is a *reasonableness* defence. They do not have one that isn't.**

| Their defence | The word it turns on | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The exclusion was management action | *"**reasonable** management action taken in a **reasonable** way"* | **WCRA s 32(5)(a)** — the appeal |
| It was not a reprisal | *"**reasonable** management action taken **reasonably**"* | **PID Act**, restated in the ESU letter |
| We can refuse the adjustment | *"only on **reasonable** grounds"* | **EB12 cl 10.3.5** |
| We need not restore the status quo | *"a **genuine** safety issue"* | **EB12 cl 1.11.4** |
| We have not delayed | *"**unreasonably** or intentionally delay"* | **EB12 cl 1.11.5** |
| The adjustment is too hard | *"**unjustifiable** hardship"* — and the term must be *"not **reasonable**"* | **AD Act ss 5, 11, 35, 36** |
| The information was needed | *"**reasonably** required"* | **AD Act s 124(3)** |

⇒ ⭐ **He never has to prove bad faith. He only has to make reasonableness untenable — and the
documents in Part 1 do that on their own, without a single characterisation.**

## ⭐⭐⭐ AND THE ONUS IS ALREADY WHERE HE WANTS IT
**IR Act s 306 — verified, ATT22, current 1 January 2026:**
> *"**It is presumed that the action was, or is being, taken for that reason or with that intent,
> unless the person proves otherwise.**"*

⇒ In a general protections application, **he alleges the reason; MSH must disprove it.**
⇒ **G03 cl 2** does the same for adjustments: *"the onus is on Queensland Health, as the employer,
to prove an adjustment is unreasonable."*
⇒ **PID Act s 40(5)**: it is enough that the unlawful ground is **a substantial ground**, *"even if
there is another ground"*.

**Three separate instruments put the burden on them. He does not carry it. He never has to say the
words.**

---

# PART 3 — ⛔⛔ WHY "OBVIOUSLY" IS THE TRAP
**The conclusion is right. Saying it is what loses it.**

1. **Bad faith is never obvious to a decision-maker.** It is the last thing a tribunal concludes, if
   it concludes it at all, and only from documents. An appellant who announces it up front asks to
   be believed before anything has been proved.
2. ⚠️ **It moves the question.** The moment he characterises their conduct, the tribunal stops
   assessing **their** conduct and starts assessing **his characterisation**. **He hands them a
   defence they do not currently have: that he is a man who reads motives into administration.**
   ⇒ ⛔ That is the exact narrative MSH has been unable to build, and it cannot be built without him.
3. **It is a live risk, not a theoretical one.** The Monte Carlo puts accusation framings at
   **−16 to −26** points of settlement position.
4. **Discipline rules 1 and 2.** Conspiracy and collusion framing never reaches paper; the
   asymmetry is held in reserve.
5. ⭐ **He loses nothing by silence.** s 306 presumes the reason. G03 cl 2 puts the onus on them.
   PID s 40(5) needs only a substantial ground. **The law says it for him, and says it better.**

## ⭐ THE SUBSTITUTION THAT WORKS
| ⛔ Never write | ✅ Write instead |
|---|---|
| *"This was not in good faith"* | *"On 7 July the Health Service recorded that it did not have sufficient information to assess whether there were psychosocial hazards involving line management. I have asked what assessment has since been undertaken."* |
| *"They deliberately withheld it"* | *"I have asked which instrument is relied on and have not received an answer."* |
| *"Given the history between us"* | ⛔ **nothing. Say nothing.** The history is in the file and the file goes to the union. |
| *"They are targeting me"* | *"I ask that the decision be made by an officer outside Corporate Services."* |

⇒ **Each right-hand version is unanswerable, and each one leaves the inference intact for someone
else to draw.** ⭐ **That is the whole method: the asymmetry does the work; he never announces it.**

---

# PART 3A — ⛔⛔⛔ THE NOTICE CANNOT NAME THEM AS CO-CONSPIRATORS
> Asked 1 August 2026. **The answer is no, and it is not a close question.** Recorded here because
> the impulse is legitimate and will recur — five weeks unpaid, two officers, one pattern.

## 3A.1 It does not fit the clause
**cl 1.11.2 governs *"any disagreement between the parties as to the interpretation, application or
implementation of this Agreement."*** A cl 1.11 dispute is between **the employee and the
employer**. ⛔ **It has no respondents, makes no findings about individuals, and imposes no
liability on anyone.** Naming two officers as conspirators in it is not a strong version of the
notice — **it is a category error**, and it invites the same scope objection as the AD Act, only
fatal instead of inconvenient.

## 3A.2 "Conspiracy" is a pleaded tort he would have to prove
Civil conspiracy requires **an agreement between two or more persons**, to injure, **by unlawful
means**, with the requisite intent, causing damage. ⛔ **It is among the hardest causes of action in
the common law.** Asserting it in correspondence and being unable to prove it does not cost nothing
— **it is the thing the other side quotes back for the next two years.**

## 3A.3 ⚠️ It rewrites what the whole file is about
| Today | The moment "co-conspirators" is written |
|---|---|
| An employee asking that the agreement be applied | **A man alleging a conspiracy against two named managers** |
| Questions with no good answers | **An allegation with an obvious answer: prove it** |
| Their conduct under examination | ⛔ **His judgement under examination** |
| Nothing for them to defend | **Something to defend, and a reason to close ranks** |

⇒ ⛔⛔ **It supplies the one narrative MSH has failed to build in two years, in a single compound
noun — and supplies it in his own handwriting.** Discipline rules **1** and **2**; and the model
puts accusation framings at **−16 to −26**.
⚠️ **And it carries real defamation exposure.** PID Act **s 38** gives absolute privilege to the
disclosure. ⛔ **It does not cover a cl 1.11 notice circulated to HR, the union and two officers.**

## 3A.4 ⭐⭐ AND IT IS UNNECESSARY — THE STATUTE REACHES THEM WITHOUT HIM SAYING A WORD
| Provision | What it does to individuals |
|---|---|
| ⭐ **IR Act s 571** | **accessorial liability** — a person "involved in" a contravention is treated as having contravened it |
| **IR Act s 307** | advising, encouraging, inciting or coercing the action |
| ⭐ **IR Act s 306** | **the reverse onus** — they must disprove the reason |
| ⭐⭐ **PID Act s 40** | *"**A person** must not cause… detriment"* — individuals, not just the entity |
| ⭐⭐ **PID Act s 41** | **167 penalty units or 2 years imprisonment. Indictable.** |
| **PID Act s 40(5)** | enough that the unlawful ground is **a substantial ground** |
| **PID Act s 43** | vicarious liability of the entity **as well** |
| **PS Act ss 266–270** | indemnity is **not immunity** — see `personal-liability-hughes-taylor.md` |

⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **Personal liability attaches by operation of statute, on findings a tribunal makes. It does
not attach because he asserted it in a letter — and asserting it makes those findings less likely,
not more.**

## 3A.5 ⭐ WHAT IS ALREADY DOING THE WORK HE WANTS DONE
**The two-officer dimension is on the record in all three documents right now — as a procedural
question that must be answered, not a characterisation that can be denied:**
- **Response Part 6** — who is the delegate; what is the source of the delegation; has a conflict
  been identified and managed; were the 2 and 3 July decisions made with the knowledge or approval
  of the officer now deciding
- **Request §4** — that the decision be made **outside Corporate Services**
- **Notice §5** — that MSH **nominate** the officer to conduct Stage 1

⇒ **That puts the relationship between the Manager and the Director squarely in issue, forces an
answer, and characterises no one.** ⭐ **It is the same point, made in the only register that
survives contact with a decision-maker.**

## 3A.6 WHERE THE TWO-OFFICER CASE IS ACTUALLY BUILT
| Venue | How |

# READY POSITION — NOMINATING DECISION-MAKING AS THE HAZARD (cl 7.2 / Code)
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Never sent cold. Banked 3 Aug 2026, after the send.
> USE: at the Stage 1/Stage 2 discussion, or the moment MSH engages on the §4(h)
> psychosocial assessment and asks what is to be assessed. NOT as a fresh email —
> the discipline stands: ask for the assessment, don't self-diagnose in writing.
> Consultation under WHS ss 47–49 gives Cory the seat; this is what he says from it.

## The nomination, in one sentence (say it as a category, never a name)
"The hazard I ask be assessed is **poor organisational justice — the decision-making
processes applied to my attendance, leave, pay and return to work** — which is a
psychosocial hazard category in the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work
Code of Practice 2022, and which the Health Service's own letter of 7 July 2026
identified as territory requiring assessment."

## The dated data points (all from MSH's own documents — hand them over as a list)
1. 3 Jul 2026 — certified fit 2:00pm; told within the hour not to attend; **no instrument
   identified in five weeks** (procedural).
2. 13 Jul — pay stopped on a stated basis (QSuper IP claim) that the fund's own records
   show was closed at Cory's request in March 2026 (informational).
3. Leave decisions in ~15 minutes vs four weeks' silence on attendance — the measured
   pattern, computable from their timestamps (interpersonal/procedural).
4. Deadlines on the worker in days; "unable to commit to a timeframe" for themselves,
   15 Jul (asymmetry, in writing, both directions).
5. Process name/steps/decision-maker asked repeatedly — never answered ("I have a
   phrase. I do not have a process.").
6. 7 Jul letter — hazard territory ("unresolved workplace matters involving line
   management") identified by MSH itself; **no assessment in the four-plus weeks since**
   (reg 38(2)(c) review trigger, fired and unactioned).

## SECOND CATEGORY (added 3 Aug, Cory's insight): JOB INSECURITY
The Code lists **job insecurity** as a psychosocial hazard in its own right. The file's
instance is exact: "a decision will be made regarding your ability to perform your role"
— foreshadowed twice, with no instrument, no named decision-maker, no process, and no
date, over an employee held out unpaid. A standing, undefined threat to the job, of
indefinite duration, from decision-makers whose authority is unidentified, IS the
hazard operating. Nominate both categories together: poor organisational justice
(the decision-making process) + job insecurity (its standing effect on the role).

## Why the harm mechanism is not hypothetical
Their own checklist certifies a psychological condition which this exact hazard category
aggravates, and restricts high-demand/complaint-handling exposure accordingly. The hazard
is operating on a worker their own instrument identifies as vulnerable to it.

## The recursion (understand it; never say it)
An honest cl 7.2 assessment of this hazard must audit the decision-making that is the
subject of the dispute. Their safety machinery, pointed at their own process, by their
own letter's admission. Cory only ever asks for the assessment; the recursion does the rest.

## Discipline
- Role and process, never a person. "The decision-making process" — never "Scott's/
  Chloe's decisions" — the moment it names a person it becomes a grievance.
- Never self-diagnose harm; the certified condition + the Code category carry it.
- If MSH runs the assessment narrowly (rosters only), ask in consultation that the
  organisational-justice category be included — ss 47–49 requires consultation with him,
  and the request is then on the assessment's own record.

## HELD, DEPLOY ON TRIGGER

Stage 2 referral (Mon 10) · IR Act general protections / s 306 reverse onus (only if they
act) · QIRC reinstatement jurisdiction (only if dismissed) · CCC (banked; not now) ·

## ⚠ UNUSED — GENUINELY AVAILABLE, NOT YET CONSIDERED
1. **Workplace Health and Safety Queensland notification / request for an inspector.**
   A worker may raise an unmanaged psychosocial risk with the regulator; an inspector can
   attend and issue an improvement notice. An improvement notice would (a) compel the
   assessment and (b) be devastating evidence in both tracks. It is a protected act.
   ⚠ Cost: it is escalation to an external regulator while a consultative process is on
   foot; it hands MSH a "he escalates everything" narrative and cannot be withdrawn.
   POSTURE: hold until Stage 2 has been given its run, or until an adverse act occurs.
2. **HSR election (WHS Act ss 50–72).** If the work group has no Health and Safety
   Representative, workers may request that one be elected and the PCBU must facilitate it.
   Non-adversarial, structural, and it creates a standing consultation channel with
   statutory powers (including PINs) that does not depend on him personally.
   POSTURE: raise at the Stage 1/2 discussion as a constructive proposal. Low cost, high
   structural value, entirely consistent with the tabled package.
3. **⭐ AD Act 1991 (Qld) — impairment discrimination / failure to make reasonable
   adjustments. LIMITATION ~8 SEPTEMBER 2026.** Flagged repeatedly; still not dated with
   Petering. This is the only instrument in the matter with a running limitation clock
   that has not been secured. It must be decided (lodge or consciously let lapse) BEFORE
   early September — not drifted past.
4. **Human Rights Act 2019 ss 25, 26(2), 58 / QHRC complaint** — public-entity obligations;
   pairs with the AD Act complaint rather than standing alone.

## THE ONE-LINE ANSWER
The instruments are close to fully deployed. The gaps are not tactical — they are
(a) the AD Act limitation, (b) the two WHS instruments (regulator, HSR) deliberately
unspent, and (c) runway, which is not an instrument at all but decides whether the
instruments can be held long enough to work.

>>> skill/references/LEAVE-DIRECTION-framework-analysis.md :: text
# THE FRAMEWORK ANALYSIS — Taylor's 4 Aug leave direction against the actual instruments
> Verified from source 4 Aug 2026: IR Act 2016 ss 33, 40, 41; PS Act 2022 s 101; EB12
> cll 1.11.2(a), 1.11.4, 1.11.5, 1.13 (Schedule 2 preserved policies). ⛔ Strategy layer —
> the ANALYSIS is not sent; only the short reserved reply goes out.

## THE THREE POSSIBLE CHARACTERISATIONS — AND EACH ONE'S PROBLEM
Whatever occurred on 3 July is one of three things. Every one of them fails as administered.

### (A) IF IT IS A SUSPENSION → PS Act 2022 s 101 (verified)
- s 101(1): only **the chief executive** may suspend, **by notice**, and only on a
  reasonable belief that the employee is liable to discipline, or that proper and efficient
  management might be prejudiced.
- s 101(2): the notice **must state** when the suspension starts and ends, **whether the
  employee is entitled to remuneration**, and the effect of alternative employment.
- s 101(3): **before** suspending, the chief executive **must consider all reasonable
  alternatives** — the Act's own examples are *alternative duties*, *a change in location*,
  *another alternative working arrangement*.
- s 101(4): **"The employee is entitled to normal remuneration for the period of the
  suspension"**, unless suspended under (1)(a) (discipline) AND the chief executive
  considers it inappropriate having regard to the discipline believed.
- s 101(9): the chief executive must comply with the s 102 directive.
⇒ No notice. No start/end dates. No remuneration statement. No recorded consideration of
alternatives (he PROPOSED them — the certified restrictions, the return-to-work proposal).
No discipline alleged, so the unpaid exception cannot even be reached.
**If it is a suspension, remuneration was payable throughout.**

### (B) IF IT IS "LEAVE" → the leave instruments do not permit what is being done
**Recreation/annual leave — IR Act s 33 (verified):**
- s 33(1): the employee **and** employer **may agree** when leave is taken.
- s 33(3): if they cannot agree, the employer may decide **but must give at least
  8 weeks' written notice** of the starting date.
⇒ He does not agree. There is no 8 weeks' notice — there is a same-day payroll deadline.
The only other route is s 34 (an industrial instrument may require leave to be taken in
particular circumstances, "but only if the requirement is reasonable") — EB12 contains no
such requirement for this situation; cl 9.7 deals only with half-pay applications *by the
employee*.
**Sick leave — IR Act ss 40, 41 (verified):** the entitlement is conditional on the
employee notifying **"any illness that will cause the employee to be absent from work"**.
⇒ He has not notified an illness causing absence. **He was certified FIT with restrictions
on 3 July 2026 and has been ready, willing and able throughout.** Sick leave — paid or
unpaid — is not the applicable instrument for an absence the employer directed. Recording
it as sick leave misstates the reason for the absence in the employer's own records.

### (C) IF IT IS NEITHER → wages are simply payable
An employee ready, willing and able to work whose labour the employer declines to accept,
without lawful authority, remains entitled to wages. That is the foundation of the dispute's
forward-pay limb. ⚠ Pinpoint authority to be confirmed before any filing.

## THE DISPUTE-PROCEDURE OVERLAY — EB12 cl 1.11 (verified)
- cl 1.11.2(a): Stage 1 discussions **should take place within 24 hours** and the procedure
  **should not extend beyond seven days**. ⭐ Taylor's own letter: *"the 24-hour timeframe
  specified in the clause will not be achieved."*
- cl 1.11.4: **"while the dispute procedure is being followed, normal work is to continue...
  The status quo existing before the emergence of a dispute is to continue whilst the
  procedure is being followed. No party shall be prejudiced as to the final settlement by
  the continuation of work."**
  ⇒ Debiting the last 41.21 hours of leave, and recording unpaid absence, DURING the
  dispute, on the very subject matter of the dispute, is prejudice of exactly the kind the
  clause forbids.
- cl 1.11.5: **"no party shall act in a manner unreasonably or intentionally delay the
  timely resolution of a dispute."**

## THE STANDING CONTRADICTION IN THEIR OWN LETTER
Paragraph 1 calls it **"the decision that has prevented you from attending your rostered
shifts"**. Paragraph 3 asks him to treat the same period as **his leave**.
An absence cannot simultaneously be (i) caused by the employer's decision preventing
attendance, and (ii) leave taken by the employee. The letter needs both propositions and
they are mutually exclusive.

## WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING FROM THE RECORD (the ask, unchanged)
1. The instrument relied on to prevent attendance from 3 July 2026.
2. The identity of the decision-maker and the date of the decision.
3. Whether it is a suspension under s 101 and, if so, the notice required by s 101(2).
4. What reasonable alternatives were considered under s 101(3), and by whom.
5. The basis on which sick leave is recorded for an employee certified fit.

## POLICY / PROCEDURE LAYER
EB12 cl 1.13 preserves the Schedule 2 HR policies as terms of the Agreement — including
**E12 Individual employee grievances**, **E13 Workplace Harassment**, **F3 Access to
Employee Records** and **F4 Union Encouragement**. cl 1.12.1 routes grievances to Award
cl 7.2. Health Employment Directives and the s 102 suspension directive sit above local
practice: **payroll cut-off dates are an administrative convenience and are not a source
of power** — no instrument permits a processing deadline to override a statutory notice
period or the status quo obligation.

# THE 7 AUGUST MENTION — WHAT IS NORMAL A WEEK OUT, AND WHAT TO PREPARE
> Asked 1 August 2026: should MSH have confirmed attendance, emailed something, or filed something
> narrowing its objection by now? **Answer from QIRC practice and the record.**

---

# PART 1 — WHAT A MENTION IS, AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY REQUIRED A WEEK OUT

**A mention is procedural.** It is not the hearing of the 64G application. Its ordinary business:
confirm where the matter is up to, deal with appearances, and set a timetable (submissions on the
objection, or a hearing date, or orders by consent on anything agreed).

**What the rules actually require of MSH before it: nothing further.**
- The 22 May direction required objections by **4:00pm Friday 5 June**. MSH served its objection
  (K-LM26/729) at **15:02 on 5 June**. ⇒ **That obligation is discharged.**
- There is **no obligation** to file submissions, confirm attendance in writing to him, or
  correspond before a mention, unless directed. No direction requires it.

⇒ ⛔ **So their silence this week is not a breach of anything, and must not be characterised as
one.** A week of quiet before a procedural mention is common.

# PART 2 — WHAT IS *NORMAL GOOD PRACTICE*, AND WHERE THEY SIT AGAINST IT

| Normal for a represented objector | Required? | MSH here |
|---|---|---|
| Notify the registry of who appears (counsel/solicitor), esp. where leave to be represented is needed | customary, not required | nothing received by him |
| **Confer before the mention to narrow the objection** — concede the uncontroversial categories, contest the rest, offer a consent position | ⭐ **model-litigant good practice**, not a rule | ⛔ nothing — the objection stands at full width |
| Respond to without-prejudice approaches | good practice | Calderbank #2 **rejected 16 July**; the 30–31 July WP letter — no response yet (2 days; not yet notable) |
| Attend listings | required when directed | ⚠️ **MSH did not attend the 22 May mention.** 7 Aug is the second listing at which it is required |

⭐ **The model litigant point, held correctly:** Queensland's model litigant principles bind State
agencies — deal with claims promptly, keep costs down, **do not contest matters that should be
conceded**. Not conferring to narrow an objection before a mention is not a breach; **but arriving
on 7 August still defending every category of a restrained application is the posture the
principles counsel against — and that is for Dwyer to notice, not for Cory to say.**

## SO, HIS THREE QUESTIONS, ANSWERED PLAINLY
1. **Should they have confirmed attendance?** Customary if represented; **not required**. Absence
   of confirmation tells you nothing yet.
2. **Should they have emailed something?** Good practice would be a letter narrowing the objection
   or proposing consent orders. **Nothing compels it.** Their pattern (Part 1 of the obligations
   register) is silence on anything substantive, so this is consistent, not surprising.
3. **Should they have filed something coming down from the full objection?** ⭐ **No rule requires
   it — and it is BETTER FOR HIM that they have not.** A full-width objection against a restrained,
   partly-conceded application is the least attractive posture an objector can bring to a
   Commissioner. **Every week they do not narrow it, the contrast his application was built on
   gets sharper.** Discipline rule 6 did its work in the drafting; their silence is completing it.

# PART 3 — ⚠️ WHAT CORY DOES AND DOES NOT DO THIS WEEK
- ⛔ **Do not chase them.** No email asking whether they will attend or narrow. Rule 4: file first,
  ask second; and prompting them to narrow before the mention only improves their posture.
- ✅ **One neutral step is fine:** confirm with the **registry** (not MSH) that the listing stands
  and its time/location. Routine, and it is the registry's job.
- ⚠️ **The Monday package lands four days before the mention.** MSH Legal may know of it by 7 Aug.
  **Posture unchanged:** volunteer nothing. If MSH raises the employment dispute in any form:
  > *"That is a separate employment matter and is not before the Commission today."*
  One sentence. Nothing more, even if invited.
- ⛔ Do not mention the RFMI, the cl 10.3 request, the dispute notice, the CE letter, the
  psychiatrist, or the pay position. **None of it exists in this room.**

# PART 4 — WHAT TO HAVE IN HAND ON THE DAY
1. **The sealed application and draft order** (filed 23 June, served 24–25 June).
2. **MSH's objection** (K-LM26/729, 5 June) — read again the night before; know which categories it
   actually contests and on what stated ground.
3. **A one-line procedural history** if asked: direction 22 May → objection 5 June → application
   filed 23 June → served 24–25 June → today.
4. ⭐ **What he asks for:** a **timetable** — written submissions on the objection and a date; or,

5. **If MSH does not appear again:** say nothing about it. Answer the Commissioner's questions and

6. **Concessions ready:** anything already conceded in the application, re-offered cheerfully.
   Restraint as posture — it is what makes the rest grantable.

# PART 5 — THE ONE-LINE VERSION
**Nothing obliged MSH to write, confirm or narrow this week, so their silence breaks no rule — but
normal good practice for a government objector is to come down from a full-width objection before a

## ⭐⭐ THREE THINGS OF SIGNIFICANCE IN SEGMENT 1

**1. THE DEPARTURE WAS ANNOUNCED.** *"We're going to do something a little bit different today."*
⭐⭐⭐ **This is materially important.** It means the departure from ordinary mention procedure was
**flagged in advance and deliberate** — not something that evolved as the hour went on. Announcing
a procedural departure before making it is how a member makes it fair, and how the record shows he
knew he was departing. **It confirms the whole exercise was planned before he walked in** — which
in turn means he had read the Form 20, the Form 29 and K-LM26/729 beforehand.

**2. THE AI QUESTION WAS HOUSEKEEPING, NOT A CONCERN.** Asked early, answered briefly, **skipped
over and never revisited.** ⭐ A member with a real concern about authorship or citation
reliability pursues it. He did not. **Treat it as closed unless someone else raises it.**

**3. THE SEQUENCE EXPLAINS THE DIFFERENCE.** Cory's own point is the correct one: this was the
**first listing where the Commission had the complete set** — the Notice, the objection it had
itself directed MSH to file, and the r 64G application. ⇒ **The reason the hour happened on 7
August and not earlier is that 7 August was the first date on which it could.**

## ⭐⭐ WHAT SEGMENT 2 ESTABLISHES

**1. ⭐⭐⭐ THE MOST IMPORTANT EXCHANGE IN THE FILE SO FAR.** *"That's just management action"* is

action point in six words. **Cory answered it correctly and instantly: it lacked consultation and

strand.** This matches the banked strand ledger exactly and it is now the Commission's own
suggested route.

**3. ⭐⭐ HE CONCEDED THE PAY LIMB HIMSELF, IN THE ROOM, UNPROMPTED.** Before anyone made him.
That is both the correct call (Notice ¶¶42–45 → Response row 39, **denied**, *"the roster was
equitable"*) and a significant credibility act in front of the employer.

**4. THE ONE-BY-ONE WALK CONFIRMS THE NECESSITY AUDIT.** Reading each pleaded item and asking

statement about the strength of the appeal, and Cory's own reading of it is correct.

# THE OBJECTION AS EVIDENCE — forensic analysis of K-LM26/729 (5 June 2026)
> Built 6 Aug 2026 from the source text. The objection is CE-signed. Read as a whole it

## 1. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY PRODUCED (6 items, all peripheral)
Item 6 — Role Description, Manager Switchboard Services.
Item 11 — MyHR leave submissions 1 Feb–31 May 2024; pandemic leave forms 20–27 Feb; AVAC history.

Item 13 — HR Delegation COVID-19 Paid Special Pandemic Leave (signed 23 Nov 2022); Directive 01/20.
Item 15 — Leave takings report, 19 March 2024.
Item 16 — Daily Staffing variance forms, 5–18 Feb and 19 Feb–3 Mar 2024.
⇒ Everything produced is small, administrative and about LEAVE PAPERWORK. Nothing produced
   touches emergency-code records, complaints, fatigue systems, or management conduct.

## 2. HOW THE REST WAS DECLINED
NON-EXISTENCE: 1, 2, 3(c), 4, 5, 7, 20 · BURDEN r 64E(4)(a): 3(a), 3(b), 8, 10, 19 ·
RELEVANCE/PARTICULARITY/EFFECT: 9, 18 · PRIVACY r 64E(4)(e): 12(part), 17 ·
NOT IN POSSESSION: 14.

## 3. ⭐⭐ WHAT THE OBJECTION ADMITS (its own words — the most valuable material in the file)
(a) **FATIGUE MANAGEMENT POST-DATES THE INJURY.** Item 5: "The implementation of fatigue
    risk management assessment at Switchboard Logan Hospital occurred **after 30 June 2024**
    in connection with an organisational change related to the reporting lines for
    Switchboard." ⇒ At the 7-hour break (17–18 Mar 2024) and at the injury (18 Jun 2024)
    there was NO fatigue risk management at Switchboard. CE-signed.
(b) **SWITCHBOARD WAS EXCLUDED FROM THE FRMS.** Items 4 and 7: "Mandatory Fatigue Risk
    Management System training only applies to health practitioners and clinical
    assistants. The Logan Hospital Switchboard staff are non-clinical staff, and therefore
    there is no mandatory requirement for them to complete Fatigue Risk Management System
    training." ⇒ A 24/7 room that activates emergency codes was outside the fatigue system
    because it is "non-clinical".
(c) **THERE IS NO COMPLAINTS SYSTEM.** Item 3(a): "All employee complaints relating to
    Logan Hospital Switchboard operational errors are made directly to the Line Manager of
    Switch Board and managed **solely via email or verbally** with the complainant."
    ⇒ No register, no tracking, no formal process. The organisational-justice hazard,
    admitted.
(d) **NOTHING CHANGED AFTER THE COMPLAINTS.** Item 3(c): "there have been no
    'consequential' changes to operating procedures over the period requested."
(e) **EMERGENCY-CODE RECORDS WERE NOT RETAINED.** Items 1–2: "The system was upgraded in
    SPOK, and records predating that upgrade were not retained." ⇒ Paging/activation records
    for a patient-safety system, destroyed in an upgrade.
(f) **THE TEAM IS SMALL.** Item 17: "the Logan Hospital Switchboard team is comprised of a
    small team" and members "can be easily re-identified even if redacted."
(g) **MANAGEMENT USED A PERSONAL PHONE.** Item 14: the line manager "was not issued with a
    Queensland Health mobile device"; leave-request SMS were on a personal device;
    "The Queensland Health retention policy does not apply to employee's personal mobile."
    A QH device issued only "in or around the third quarter of 2024."
(h) **A NARROWING IS OFFERED ON ITEM 19** — "the date range ought to be narrowed to
    17-18 March 2024, limited to emails received from Together Queensland by the Switchboard
    line manager and their Director, or by members of the Logan Hospital Human Resources
    team" ⇒ a concession in principle that the search is possible when bounded.

## 4. ⭐⭐⭐ THE SELF-REFUTING BURDEN OBJECTION (Item 3(a)/3(b))
In one paragraph MSH says BOTH:
  · complaints "are made **directly to the Line Manager** of Switch Board"; and
  · compliance "would require... assistance from eHealth Queensland... to review and search
    **individual staff member email accounts**" with "significant administrative and
    operational burden."
⇒ If every complaint goes to ONE named custodian, the search is ONE mailbox. The burden
   objection is answered by MSH's own sentence, two lines earlier. This is the single
   strongest point available on the objection, it requires no evidence, and it is neutral
   in tone: *"the objection identifies a single custodian; the burden asserted assumes many."*

## 5. WHAT HE ASKED FOR vs WHAT HE COULD HAVE PRESSED
Form 4 presses only Items 1, 2, 3(a), 3(b), 9, 10, 19 (Item 10 confined), plus verification
on 3(c), 4, 5, 7, 18, 20 and the Item 16 AVAC export.
WITHDRAWN or not pressed: Item 8 (login records), Item 12 comparator supporting evidence,
Item 14 (personal mobile), **Item 17 (comparator payroll)** — i.e. precisely the items that
raised genuine third-party privacy concerns.
Form 4 Overview, verbatim: "The Appellant does not seek any medical records, the financial
or payroll data of other employees, or any patient or other sensitive personal or health
information; where any such identifying information appears in the records produced, it may
be redacted." Plus Part B(d): production to the Commission first if privacy is raised.
⇒ THE REDACTION AND PRIVACY SAFEGUARDS WERE OFFERED BEFORE THE OBJECTION WAS DECIDED. The
  privacy grounds (Items 12, 17) are therefore answered against items he no longer presses.

## 6. THE ITEM 20 CONTRADICTION (already pleaded in the Form 4)
MSH: Item 20 "does not exist, as... PID24-ESU-1130 commenced in November 2024, which falls
outside the specified search period of 13 May 2024 to 31 May 2024."
BUT the Regulator's own disclosure of 11 June 2026 includes correspondence of 15–16 May
2024 apparently within Item 20. ⇒ Non-existence asserted by MSH; the document surfaced from
the other respondent. This is why the produce-or-swear verification is the disposition sought.

## 7. ASSESSMENT
The production is six administrative documents about leave. The declines cover every item
that would show how the room was run. And the objection, in the course of declining, admits:
no fatigue system before the injury, exclusion of the room from the fatigue system, no
complaints system, no consequential change, destroyed emergency-code records, a small team,
and management conducting leave decisions on a personal phone outside retention policy.
⇒ **The objection is a better document for the appellant than the production would have
been.** It is CE-signed, it is on the Commission file, and it cannot be withdrawn.
DISCIPLINE: none of this is argued at a mention. It is submissions material, deployed as
quotes and item numbers, without adjectives.

# THE POWERS MAP — NOTHING ASKED WITHOUT A POWER BEHIND IT
> Built 1 August 2026. Every ask now sits under a named provision that compels an answer, carries a
> time limit, or produces a consequence if ignored. **Instruments verified against the source PDFs**
> — ATT02 (EB12 CA No. 12 of 2025), ATT22 (IR Act 2016 (Qld), current 1 Jan 2026), ATT17, ATT24,
> ATT19, ATT20, ATT23, ATT10, ATT09.
>
> ⚠️ **This file is the strategy layer. It is not sent to MSH.** The letters raise these one at a
> time, as requests. Sixteen powers in one table reads as an indictment; the register is for
> Petering, and for evidence if it comes to that.

---

# PART 1 — WHY THE ASK CHANGED SHAPE

**Until now every request to MSH was answerable by silence.** *"Please confirm I'm right to
attend"* — four weeks, nothing. *"Identify the delegate and instrument"* — nothing. *"Formal
request for review"* — ten months, nothing. The measured pattern is in
`RESPONSE-OBLIGATIONS-REGISTER.md` Part 1: **15 minutes on a leave question, four weeks on
attendance, ten months on a complaint about a Director.**

⇒ **The change is not the content of the ask. It is the vehicle.** The same proposal, made under
cl 10.3.2 instead of in a covering paragraph, converts silence from a wall into a deemed decision.
That is the whole point of the restructure of 1 August 2026.

| | Asked in correspondence | Asked under a power |
|---|---|---|
| Reply | discretionary | **cl 10.3.6 — "must", 21 days** |
| Reasons | none required | **cl 10.3.5–.6 — "only on reasonable grounds", reasons in writing** |
| Silence | costs MSH nothing | ⭐ **IR Act s 29 — deemed refusal** |
| Route | none | **QIRC ch 6 — s 261 notice, s 262 conciliation then arbitration** |
| Onus | on Cory, to keep asking | **on MSH** — cl 10.3.5, and G03 cl 2 |

---

# PART 2 — THE THREE DOCUMENTS AND WHAT EACH COMPELS

All three are dated the same day and each says expressly that it does not answer the others.
**Keep them separate. One power per document, one clock per power.**

| # | Document | Power | Clock | If ignored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Response to the RFMI** (14pp) | responds to *their* request; asks under WHS, G03, AD Act, IP Act | their 7-day deadline | their process, not his |
| 2 | ⭐ **Request for a change in the way I work** | **EB12 cl 10.3.2 · IR Act s 27** | ⭐ **21 days — cl 10.3.6, s 28(3)** | ⭐ **s 29 deemed refusal → QIRC ch 6** |
| 3 | ⭐ **Notice of dispute, Stage 1** | **EB12 cl 1.11.2(a)** | **24 h to start, 7 days Stage 1, 7 days Stage 2** | Stage 3 EB12IG → **Stage 4 QIRC**; **cl 1.11.5** delay |

⚠️ **Do not fold the cl 10.3 request into the cl 1.11 dispute before day 21.** s 28/29 gives it its
own route and its own onus. Folding it in surrenders both. Document 3 §7(a) says so expressly.

⚠️ **One request, one clock.** Never re-send or restate the cl 10.3 request — a fresh request
restarts the 21 days and hands MSH the delay back.

# PART 3 — THE FULL MAP

## 3.1 Powers with a hard time limit
| Ask | Power | Time | Consequence of silence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision on the change in the way I work | **EB12 cl 10.3.6**; **IR Act s 28(3)** | **21 days** | **s 29 — taken to have refused** |
| Written reasons outlining the reasonable grounds | **cl 10.3.5–.6**; **s 28(2), (4)(a)** | with the notice | a refusal with no grounds on the record |
| Statement that the QIRC has jurisdiction | **s 28(4)(b)** | with the notice | notice defective on its face |
| Stage 1 discussion | **cl 1.11.2(a)** | **within 24 h; not beyond 7 days** | escalate to Stage 2 |
| Stage 2 conference | **cl 1.11.2(b)** | **not beyond 7 days** | Stage 3 EB12IG, then **Stage 4 QIRC** |
| No unreasonable or intentional delay | **cl 1.11.5** | throughout | the delay itself becomes the issue |
| Status quo maintained while the procedure runs | **cl 1.11.4** | from notification | ⚠️ "genuine safety issue" carve-out — see 3.9 |
| WHS dispute unresolved locally → QH WHS Advisory Committee | **cl 7.1.4** | after cl 1.11.2(b) | a second escalation route |
