# TAKING FULL ADVANTAGE OF THE 31 JULY REQUEST

> Built 31 July 2026. **Everything here rests on MSH's own words in their own letter.**
> The principle throughout: **comply properly, and hold them to what they wrote.**
> ⚠️ **The line:** using their undertakings, asking proper questions and obtaining evidence he is
> entitled to is legitimate. Inflating costs, instructing the clinician's conclusions, or
> manufacturing claims is not — and would destroy everything below.

---

## A. THE MONEY

> *"**MSH will meet your reasonable costs of preparing this report** and we appreciate your assistance
> with this request. **Please send invoices to Michelle Harrison, Injury Management Consultant**…"*

Unqualified. No cap. Invoice address supplied. Signed by the Director.

| Action | Why |
|---|---|
| 1. **Obtain a written fee estimate** from the psychiatrist covering **attendance + report** | *"Reasonable"* is undefined. Specialist reports run $1,500–$3,500+ |
| 2. **Send the estimate to Injury Management and ask them to confirm acceptance IN ADVANCE** | Converts an open undertaking into a fixed agreement. Removes the after-the-fact argument |
| 3. **Ask expressly whether the undertaking covers the consultation as well as the report** | A report requires an attendance. Get it in the same email |
| 4. **Invoice Report A only. Never a combined invoice.** | ⚠️ **The integrity line.** Report B is his own cost. One attendance, two scoped reports, two invoices |
| 5. Claim **Dr Ma's** fee for the GP-allocated questions too | Same undertaking. It says "this report", and their own letter directs part of the work to the GP |

⭐ **Collateral benefit:** he has been self-funding medical costs through five weeks unpaid. This
shifts that — **and it makes the appeal report affordable**, because the attendance is covered.
**That constraint on the case disappears.**

---

## B. THE MEDICAL EVIDENCE

### B1. Their questions legitimise the specialist
They asked about **the psychiatrist's own report of 13 Feb 2025** (Q7), the **clinical basis** for the
stressors (Q1(b)), **foreseeable risk and necessary controls** (Q1(d)), and **exacerbating tasks**
(Q8). **A GP cannot answer those.** Referring is compliance, not opportunism.

### B2. ⭐⭐ Q1(d) is the gift — it asks for a prescription
> *"…what **specific workplace controls or adjustments you consider medically necessary** to manage
> that risk."*

⇒ **They have invited a specialist to prescribe controls.** Once those controls are in writing:
- **WHS s 19** — they must eliminate or minimise the risk so far as reasonably practicable. **They
  are now on notice of the specific controls a specialist says are necessary.**
- **G03 cl 2** — the onus is on **Queensland Health** to prove an adjustment unreasonable, tested
  against **the whole organisation**.
- Refusing a specified control becomes a **decision they must justify**, not a silence.

### B3. The current-exacerbation finding
A clinician may properly find that **prolonged exclusion, uncertainty as to return, and unresolved
line-management matters are recognised psychosocial hazards** currently exacerbating his condition —
because **Q1(d) asks for exactly that**, and the **Psychosocial Code 2022** lists poor organisational
justice, poor procedural fairness and poor support as hazards.
⭐ **Effect: continuing the exclusion after receiving that report becomes a knowing failure to
control a notified hazard.**
❌ **The clinician must NOT opine on lawfulness, breach or conflict.** Outside the field; it
discredits the whole report. **Cory argues the law; the doctor describes the harm.**

### B4. Scope discipline
| **Report A — MSH-funded** | **Report B — his own** |
|---|---|
| Current capacity · restrictions · **controls required** · **current exacerbating factors** | **Causation of the June 2024 injury** · chronology · severity over time |
| Goes to **Injury Management only** | His file |

⚠️ **Never instruct the conclusion.** The referral letter is disclosable. Provide the questions, the
ECC, the role description and a **neutral dated chronology**. Nothing else. An independently reached
opinion is unanswerable; a coached one is worthless.

>>> skill/references/SAFETY-ADVISOR-LENS-question-set.md :: text
# THE SAFETY-ADVISOR LENS — the high-exposure-environment method applied to the switchboard
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Banked 4 Aug 2026. A framing exercise: how an advisor from a high-risk
> operational environment (detention-contract grade) would assess the room, and the question
> set that lens produces. NOT a credentials claim — Cory claims no qualification he does not
> hold. The deployment is always: "these are the questions any competent assessment starts
> with." Read with ASSESSMENT-DESIGN-gold-standard.md and HAZARD-NOMINATION-decision-making.md.

## 1. THE METHOD (six habits of high-exposure safety practice)
1. **Exposure profile first** — what the room absorbs (call types, codes, death notifications,
   aggression, single-operator periods) from LOGS, not position descriptions. First question of
   any assessment: "where is the exposure register?" No register = finding #1 before any interview.
2. **Leading indicators from records** — leave clustering, sick trends, turnover, overtime,
   complaint response times. Records can't be socially pressured into silence.
3. **Full-cycle observation** — the 3am state is the true state. Never assess on day shift only.
4. **Welfare conversations built for candour** — private, voluntary, non-attributable; the real
   answer comes at the third question or not at all.
5. **The normalisation check** — silence is itself a hazard indicator; drift ("part of the job",
   reporting stopped because nothing happened) is what kills people in high-exposure rooms.
6. **Report above the assessed chain, with review dates** — findings that land on the assessed
   manager's desk die there; a control nobody re-checks no longer exists.
Doctrine: individual-level responses (resilience training, EAP, "self-care") = admission of
failure under the hierarchy (Reg 36). Redesign the work first.

## 2. WHAT THE LENS SEES IN THE SWITCHBOARD (instant pattern-match)
- Distressing-call exposure, no register, no debrief practice
- After-hours single-operator isolation, no named welfare owner at 3am
- Fatigue managed through workers' own personal leave (matrix row 10 — the classic
  leading-indicator signature)
- Complaints unanswered 6 days = dead reporting channel = normalisation drift in progress
- Changes made without consultation records
Any two together trigger an assessment in high-exposure practice. This room has all five.

## 3. THE QUESTION SET
### Tier 1 — of the system (scoping consultation / Stage 2 asks)
1. Where is the register of distressing-call and aggression exposure, and who reviews it?
2. What happens in the 15 minutes after a distressing call — who checks the operator, recorded where?
3. Who holds welfare responsibility for the lone operator at 3am? Name and position.
4. Twelve-month roster beside the leave records: who manages fatigue — the system or the
   workers' own leave balances?
5. Documented response time to the last five concerns raised by operators in this room?
6. Consultation records for the last three changes made to this room?
7. When did this room's own data last reach a level of the organisation with power to act?

### Tier 2 — answerable from records alone (64G / RTI / dispute §4(f)-shaped)
Leave + sick-leave trends vs hospital average; turnover/vacancy history; overtime and
single-up frequency; complaint logs with response times. A room can stay silent; its
records cannot.

### Tier 3 — the independent assessor's interview themes (proposed at methodology consultation)
- What does a bad shift look like, and what happens afterwards?
- Who would you tell, and what happened the last time you told them?
- ⭐ "What have you stopped reporting because nothing happened last time?" — the single most
  diagnostic question in a normalised environment; the one an in-house process never asks.

## 4. DISCIPLINE
- ⚠ Cory is EXCLUDED from the workplace: he does NOT canvass colleagues. Tier 1/2 deploy to
  the system (consultation, Stage 2, tabled documents, disclosure machinery). Colleague
  accounts arrive ONLY per the witness-prompt rules (voluntary, their words, their initiative).
- Never framed as personal expertise — framed as the questions any competent assessment
  starts with, which the independent assessor can now answer.
- The record already shows him running this method without the title: PT safety report,
  response-time complaint, the leave-as-fatigue-control observation, Form 29's structure,
  the hazard nomination. Exposure noticed → indicators logged → reported upward → escalated
  when the channel went dead. The system's job was to receive it; the record shows what it
  did instead.

>>> skill/references/SETTLEMENT-APPROACH-protocol.md :: text
# WHEN THE APPROACH COMES — protocol. Banked 5 Aug 2026.
> For the moment MSH (or the Regulator) opens resolution. Written in advance so nothing
> is improvised under relief.

## 1. RECOGNISE IT
It will not say "settlement". It looks like: a new senior signatory; "a discussion about
arrangements going forward"; "without prejudice"; an invitation to meet with someone from
HR you have not dealt with; or a quiet payroll correction followed by a call. Treat ANY of
these as the approach.

## 2. FIRST 24 HOURS — three rules
(a) DO NOT respond substantively on the spot, by phone or in a meeting. "Thank you — I'd
    like to consider that and respond in writing." Then send a same-day written record of
    what was said (meeting-record protocol).
(b) GET IT IN WRITING. No term exists until it is written.
(c) TELL THE UNION (Petering) before responding. If a delegate/collective limb is running,
    they need to know the personal matter is moving.

## 3. CHECK THE FORM (this decides everything)
- ACCEPTANCE of the claim (Regulator concedes) = statutory entitlements flow; best form.
- DEED = negotiated; every clause must be read against §4.
- "Informal arrangement" / verbal assurance = NOT a resolution. Consent orders or written
  terms only. (Same rule as the mention: dates on paper.)

## 4. ⛔ DEED RED LINES (rule 9 and its companions)
1. Releases the COMPENSATION CLAIM ONLY. No employment releases. No release of anything
   arising after 26 June 2026.
2. NO confidentiality/non-disparagement clause that would gag the WHS material, the
   assessment request, the tabled package, or his ability to speak to a regulator, the
   union, or a health and safety representative.
3. Nothing restraining future work, training, or industry participation.
4. Nothing that withdraws or nullifies the PID, the s 89 disclosure, or protected acts.
5. Nothing that requires him to withdraw the assessment request (see §6).
6. Tax/super treatment specified; medical costs to date reimbursed; leave RE-CREDITED not
   "paid out" (re-credit preserves the entitlement, payout extinguishes it).

## 5. THE RECONCILIATION LEDGER (have it ready BEFORE negotiating)
Wages withheld from 13 Jul (and the 26 Jun-13 Jul characterisation issue) · every leave
hour debited, with dates · superannuation on unpaid wages · self-funded medical costs ·
the ART overpayment position (do not let MSH's settlement wash into ART's recovery) ·
any interest/penalty entitlements. A number you can state in one line beats a number you
have to construct in the room.

## 6. ⭐ PROTECT THE ASSESSMENT
His resolution and the workplace assessment are in tension: a deed that resolves him lets
the assessment die. Before/while negotiating —
  (a) transfer the request to the UNION as a collective work-group matter; and/or
  (b) support an HSR election for the work group.
Either gives the assessment an owner who survives his settlement. Do this EARLY — after an
offer arrives it looks like a bargaining chip.

## 7. TIMING DISCIPLINE
Never accept the first number. Never negotiate while acutely distressed. Take 48 hours on
any substantive term. Keep every clock running while negotiating (Stage 2, cl 10.3.6,
RTI, mention timetable) — withdrawing machinery mid-negotiation is the classic error and
it always reduces the final number.

>>> skill/references/STAGE1-SCRIPT.md :: text
# STAGE 1 — THE SCRIPT AND MEETING DISCIPLINE
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Prep for the cl 1.11.2(a) Stage 1 discussion, whoever conducts it
> (Taylor, or an officer HR nominates under Part 5). Support person + union present.
> Banked 3 Aug 2026. Companion: HAZARD-NOMINATION-decision-making.md.

## 0. WHAT STAGE 1 IS, REALISTICALLY
Local-level resolution attempt. Nothing binding gets decided in the room. The realistic
outputs are: (a) things said by them that become record, (b) things asked by you that
become record, (c) possibly one or two easy concessions (E12/E13, the payroll record,
a process name). Win condition: every ask restated calmly, nothing conceded, everything
minuted. The dispute resolves on paper afterwards or proceeds to Stage 2 on 10 Aug.

## 1. OPENING STATEMENT (60 seconds, verbatim-ready)
"Thank you for meeting me. I want this resolved at Stage 1 if it can be. My notice sets
out what the dispute is, so I won't repeat it — I'd like to work through the eight
things I've asked for at Part 4, and hear the Health Service's position on each. My
position on all of them is the same: I am certified fit, I have offered my services in
writing since 3 July, I want to work, and I want the ordinary processes to apply. I'm
not here to make any complaint about any person."

## 2. THE EIGHT ASKS, IN MEETING ORDER (§4(a)–(h))
Work the list; for each, ask, listen, note WHO answered and WHAT was said:
  (a) What is this process called — instrument, steps, decision-maker, end-decision?
  (b) Am I suspended? Under what? With pay?
  (c) Return me to my roster under cl 1.11.4 — or name the instrument in writing.
  (d) The pay: period from 3 July paid, leave re-credited, permanent-line shifts paid
      as they fall until return or a power is named. Which QSuper guidelines?
  (e) E12 and E13 copies.
  (f) The 12-month roster/payroll record.
  (g) Feedback under cl 7.1.11.
  (h) The psychosocial risk assessment under cl 7.2, with me consulted.

## 3. THE HAZARD FRAMING — WHEN (h) COMES UP
Only if the assessment is discussed. Then, verbatim:

"On the assessment — the Health Service's own letter of 7 July identified unresolved
workplace matters involving line management and said it could not yet assess whether
they present psychosocial hazards. Four weeks on, I'd like that assessment done, and I
ask to be consulted in it as clause 7.2.2 provides. When it is scoped, I will be asking
that two hazard categories from the Code of Practice be included: **poor organisational
justice — that is, the decision-making processes that have been applied to my
attendance, leave, pay and return to work** — and **job insecurity**, because a decision
about my ability to perform my role has twice been foreshadowed without an instrument,
a decision-maker, or a date. I can provide the dated instances in writing if that
helps the assessor."

### How this "applies to the entire management of Corporate Services and the line manager"
IT ALREADY DOES — through the process, never the org chart. "The decision-making
processes applied to my matters" captures every decision by anyone in Corporate
Services and line management, because they made all of them. Their own 7 July letter
supplies the only unit-level phrase ever needed: "workplace matters involving line
management" — QUOTE THEIRS, never coin your own. The assessment's scope then reaches
the whole chain by definition, without one name or unit being accused by you.

## 4. THE FOUR QUESTIONS THEY MAY PUT — SCRIPTED ANSWERS
- **"Are you accusing Chloe / Scott / management?"**
  "No. Clause 1.2 of the Code of Conduct says a conflict of interest is not wrongdoing
  in itself, and my notice says I make no allegation against anyone. I'm asking about
  process and authority, not about people."
- **"Shouldn't we wait for your medical information first?"**
  "That's a separate lane and I'm engaging in it — my response is in and the next step
  there is the Health Service confirming which questions it presses. This dispute is
  about attendance, roster, leave and pay under the agreement, and clause 1.11.4 says
  the status quo continues while it's followed."
- **"Can we handle this informally / will you withdraw the notice?"**
  "I'd welcome an informal resolution — resolving it IS the point of Stage 1. The
  notice stays open until what we agree is confirmed in writing; that protects both
  of us."
- **"What's this letter to the Chief Executive about?"**
  "That's correspondence with her office under section 89 and I'd rather let her
  office deal with it. It doesn't ask for anything from this meeting."

## 5. MEETING DISCIPLINE
- Take your own notes: time, attendees, who said what on each of the eight asks.
- Ask at the end: "Can I have the outcomes of today confirmed in writing?" — every
  time, whatever the outcomes are.
- AGREE to anything good immediately (return date, pay fix, assessment scoped) —
  subject to written confirmation. Concede nothing else: no narrowing of the dispute,
  no withdrawal, no new medical undertakings beyond the response already sent, nothing
  signed in the room.
- If it gets warm: "I don't think we'll resolve that limb today — can we note our
  positions and move to the next item?" Never argue a point twice.
- Close: "Thank you. To keep to the clause, if the dispute is still unresolved by
  Monday I'll refer it to Stage 2 as clause 1.11.2(b) provides — I'd much rather we
  resolve it before then."

## 6. AFTER
Same day: write your own file note (who, when, each ask → each answer), save it, send
NO summary email unless theirs is wrong — if their written outcome misstates anything,
correct it once, factually, within 24 hours. Diarise: Mon 10 Aug Stage 2 referral if
unresolved (one line, does not self-execute).

# THE POWER THEY ARE ACTUALLY ENACTING — AND WHAT HAPPENS IF THEY DISMISS
> Built 1 August 2026 on Cory's two questions. **Verified against ATT19 (PS Act 2022, current
> 1 July 2026) and ATT22 (IR Act 2016 (Qld), current 1 January 2026).**
> ⛔ **Strategy layer. None of the analysis goes to MSH — only the question at §4(b) of the notice.**

---

# PART 1 — ⭐⭐⭐ THE POWER IS s 101. THEY HAVE USED ITS EFFECT WITHOUT ANY OF ITS CONDITIONS.

**"Hold an employee out of the workplace" has a name in the Public Sector Act. It is
suspension — s 101.** Read what it requires.

| **s 101 requires** | **What happened** |
|---|---|
| **(1)** *"A public sector employee's **chief executive** may, **by notice**, suspend the employee from duty"* | ⛔ A **Manager** on 2 July; a **Director** on 31 July. No notice of suspension has ever issued |
| **(1)(a) or (b)** the CE reasonably believes the employee is **liable to discipline**, **or** that **"the proper and efficient management of the entity might be prejudiced"** | ⛔ The 31 July letter records the Health Service is **not aware of any performance or conduct concerns** raised for appropriate management |
| **(2)(a)** the notice **must state** *"when the suspension **starts and ends**"* | ⛔ **Five weeks, no start date, no end date.** He has asked for a date repeatedly |
| **(2)(b)** the notice **must state** *"**whether the employee is entitled to remuneration** for the period"* | ⛔ Never stated. Leave debited, then no pay from 13 July by reference to a **closed** QSuper claim |
| ⭐⭐ **(3)** *"**before** suspending the employee, the chief executive **must consider all reasonable alternatives**"* — examples given: **"alternative duties"**, a change in location, **"another alternative working arrangement"** | ⛔⛔ Interim duties were **refused "in any capacity"** on 15 July. **The statute makes alternative duties a mandatory pre-condition; MSH refused them outright** |
| ⭐⭐⭐ **(4)** *"**The employee is entitled to normal remuneration for the period of the suspension**, unless (a) the employee is suspended under subsection (1)(a) [discipline]; **and** (b) the chief executive considers it is not appropriate…"* | ⛔⛔⛔ **Unpaid since 13 July** |
| **(9)** the CE *"**must** comply with the directive made under section 102"* | ⏳ no directive identified |
| **s 131(1)(f)** | a **suspension without pay decision is appealable** |

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE FORK, AND IT HAS NO GOOD EXIT
**s 101(4) makes remuneration the default. The only exception is a s 101(1)(a) *discipline*
suspension where the CE decides otherwise.** So:

- **If it is s 101(1)(b)** — *"proper and efficient management might be prejudiced"* — then
  ⭐ **there is no exception at all and he must be paid in full.**
- **If it is s 101(1)(a)** — discipline — then MSH must reasonably believe he is **liable to
  discipline**, which its own letter of 31 July disclaims, and which has never been particularised
  to him in two years.
- **If it is neither** — then he is not suspended, and the question at §2.6 stands: **what is it?**

⇒ ⭐⭐ **On any reading of s 101 he should have been paid.** The power that fits would have given
him **a chief-executive decision-maker, a start and end date, a stated position on pay,
consideration of alternative duties, full remuneration, and an appeal right.**
**He has received none of the six.**

## ⭐ HOW IT IS PUT — AND IT IS ONE SENTENCE, WITH NO CITATION
**Stage 1 notice §4(b):**
> *"That I be told whether I am suspended from duty. If I am, I ask to be told **by whom, under what
> provision, from what date to what date, and whether I am entitled to remuneration for the
> period**. If I am not suspended, I ask to be told what my status is."*

⭐⭐ **That is s 101(1) and s 101(2) read back to them as a question, without naming the section.**
It asks for exactly what a valid suspension notice must contain.
- Answer **"yes, suspended"** → every condition above becomes live, and **s 101(4) means pay**.
- Answer **"no"** → then he is an employee not suspended, not on approved leave, willing and
  available, and not being paid.
- Answer **nothing** → five weeks becomes six, against **cl 1.11.5**.

⛔⛔ **DO NOT CITE s 101 TO THEM.** Naming it lets them issue a compliant notice tomorrow and cure
everything prospectively — with a start date of tomorrow, not 3 July. **The five weeks is only
unprotected while they have not noticed the problem.**

---

# PART 1A — ⭐⭐⭐ THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT: ASKING IS NOT EXCLUDING
> Cory, 1 August: *"they can not exclude me based on this request — they could make the request,
> but where have they power? if it was a concern, none."*
> **This is the cleanest statement of the case, and it is right. Two separate acts, two separate
> authorities, and they have conflated them for five weeks.**

## 1A.1 The two acts
| Act | Authority | Position |
|---|---|---|
| **Asking for medical information** | a lawful and reasonable direction; or **PS Act s 104** (CE + appointed doctor) | ⚠️ **Concede this. They may ask.** Fighting it wastes the strong point |
| ⭐ **Declining his services while they wait** | ⛔ **nothing identified in five weeks** | **This is the gap** |
| ⭐⭐ **Declining to pay him while declining his services** | ⛔ **nothing identified, and it is a third act again** | **This is the hole** |

⇒ **A power to request is not a power to exclude, and a power to exclude is not a power to withhold
wages.** ⛔ **There is no provision anywhere in the PS Act, the certified agreement, G03 or
QH-IMP-401-5 which says that pending receipt of medical information an employee may be held out of
the workplace without pay.** If it existed it would have been cited by now; they have been asked
three ways.

## 1A.2 ⭐⭐⭐ READY, WILLING AND ABLE — THE PROPOSITION UNDERNEATH ALL OF IT
**An employee who is ready, willing and able to work, and who tenders performance, is entitled to
wages. If the employer elects not to accept the services, the wages remain payable.** The employer's
election does not discharge the obligation.

⭐ **That is why PS Act s 101(4) makes suspension paid by default — the statute reflects the general
position, it does not create an exception to it.**

⚠️ **Their only answer is "he may not be able" — and their own letter closes it.**
The 7 July 2026 letter: ***"you have been certified fit to return to work effective from 3 July
2026."*** ⇒ **On MSH's own document he is certified fit.** Restrictions are not incapacity.

⇒ **Stage 1 notice §4(d) now puts it in exactly that form** — ready, willing and able; services
offered and not accepted; no work provided; no leave asked for — and then the single question:
> *"I do not say the Health Service may not seek medical information. **It may ask.** What I have not
> been able to identify is the provision under which, **having asked, it may both decline my services
> and decline to pay me.** If there is one, I ask to be told what it is."*

⭐ **Conceding the first half is what makes the second half unanswerable.** Discipline rule 6 —
restraint as posture; concede what is available and it makes the rest grantable.

## 1A.3 ⭐⭐ AND IF THE CONCERN WAS GENUINE, SIX LAWFUL COURSES WERE OPEN. NONE WAS TAKEN.
| Available | What it required | Used? |
|---|---|---|
| **PS Act s 101** suspension | CE, notice, dates, alternatives considered — **and pay** | ⛔ no |
| **PS Act s 104** medical examination | CE, **appointed** doctor, examination; **s 105** the only basis for withholding leave, and only on **non-compliance** | ⛔ no — nine questions to his own GP |
| **WHS Reg 36** hierarchy of control | substitute, isolate, engineering, administrative, PPE — **in order** | ⛔ no assessment at all |
| **Suitable / alternative duties** | QH-IMP-401-5 §2.1; **s 101(3)** makes it a mandatory pre-condition | ⛔ **refused "in any capacity"**, 15 Jul |
| **Paid special leave** under the applicable directive | a decision, and money | ⛔ no — his own leave, then nothing |
| **Consultation** — WHS ss 47–49 | mandatory | ⛔ none, before or since |

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE FINDING — AND IT ALLEGES NOTHING
**Six lawful courses were open. Each one requires either a senior decision-maker, a written record,
or money. None was taken.**

**The course actually taken required no instrument, no decision-maker, no date, and no cost to the
Health Service — because it was funded out of his leave, and then out of nothing.**

⛔⛔ **Never write that last sentence to MSH.** ⭐ **Put the six-row table in the union brief and
let Petering say it.** Every row is a document; the inference assembles itself.

# PART 2 — IF THEY DISMISS

## 2.1 ⚠️ THE PRECEDENT IS IN HIS OWN FILE
**8 October 2024 — "abandonment" termination while he was on continuous medical certificates.
Later reinstated.**
⇒ **This is not hypothetical. They have done it before, by the same mechanism, in the same
circumstances.** He is currently absent, unpaid, and coded "income protection no pay".
**Abandonment is the live risk.**

⭐ **The guard is already built in.** Every one of the three documents ends: *"I confirm again that
I am engaging with this process and want to return to work."* **That sentence is not politeness. It
is the abandonment defence, dated and repeated.** ⛔ **Never send anything to MSH without it.**

## 2.2 ⭐⭐ THE REQUEST ITSELF IS PROTECTIVE — THIS IS THE REASON TO SEND IT
**IR Act s 284 — meaning of workplace right. All three limbs are engaged by the package:**
- **s 284(1)(a)** — *"has a right to the benefit of, or has a role or responsibility under, an
  industrial law, **industrial instrument**"* ⇒ **cl 10.3.2** (certified agreement) and **s 27** (industrial law)
- **s 284(1)(b)** — *"is able to **start, or participate in, a process** or proceedings under an
  industrial law or industrial instrument"* ⇒ **the cl 1.11 dispute**
- **s 284(1)(c)(ii)** — *"is able to make a **complaint or inquiry**… in relation to the person's
  employment"*

**s 285 — Protection.** A person must not take adverse action *"because the other person (i) has a
workplace right; or (ii) has, or has not, exercised a workplace right; or (iii) **proposes to**…
exercise a workplace right"*, or **(b) "to prevent the exercise of a workplace right"**.

**s 282 — adverse action** by an employer is where the employer *"(a) **dismisses** the employee; or
(b) **injures the employee in the employee's employment**; or (c) **alters the position of the
employee to the employee's prejudice**; or (d) discriminates between the employee and other
employees"*.

⇒ ⭐⭐ **He does not need a dismissal.** Five weeks of unpaid exclusion is capable of being
**s 282(1)(b) and (c)** already.

⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **And sending the three documents creates a dated exercise of a workplace right.**
Before today, adverse action had no anchor. **After today, everything MSH does is measured against
a documented date — and s 306 presumes the reason.**

## ⭐⭐ 2.2A WHICH REGIMES ARE LIVE — ASKED 1 AUGUST 2026
| Regime | Live? | Trigger | Needs a step? |
|---|---|---|---|
| ⭐⭐ **PID Act reprisal, ss 40–43** | ✅ **LIVE NOW** | he **has made** a PID — determined **24 Dec 2024**, ESU letter 24-ESU-1130 | ⛔ **none. It attaches to any detriment from today** |
| ⭐⭐ **IR Act general protections, ss 282–285** | ✅ **LIVE NOW, and stronger from Monday** | **s 284** workplace rights — all three limbs exercised by the four documents | the documents **are** the step |
| **AD Act discrimination, ss 11, 15** | ✅ **live as conduct** | impairment; the treatment itself | complaint within **s 138 — 1 year** |
| ⚠️ **AD Act victimisation, ss 129–130** | ⛔ **NOT live** | needs an **AD Act** allegation, complaint or proceeding | ⭐ **s 130(1)(a)(ii)** covers *"intends to allege"*; **(1)(b)** covers where **they believe** he intends to |

⭐ **He does not need to enliven s 130.** **PID s 40 is live, requires no step, and is stronger** —
167 penalty units or 2 years, a tort with exemplary damages, and vicarious liability on the entity.
⭐ **And the cl 10.3 request was deliberately drafted NOT to trigger s 130** — Part 5.3 says *"I have
made no complaint under the Anti-Discrimination Act, and this letter is not one."* **That was a
choice, not an omission.** Alleging a contravention re-opens the tone lane for a protection he
already has by a better route.

## ⭐⭐ 2.2B **PID Act s 44 — THE BRIDGE, AND A ONE-WAY DOOR**
> **s 44(1)** *"A person may make a complaint **under the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 about a
> reprisal**."* **(2)** dealt with under AD Act **chs 6 and 7** *"as if the complaint were about an
> alleged contravention of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991."*

⇒ ⭐ **A PID reprisal can be taken into the QHRC machinery directly — no discrimination allegation
required.** So the AD Act *is* available to him on reprisal, by a different door than s 130.

⛔⛔ **BUT s 44(3) IS AN IRREVOCABLE ELECTION, BOTH WAYS:**
- **(3)(a)** commence **s 42 court proceedings** → ⛔ **cannot subsequently complain under the AD Act**
- **(3)(b)** make an **AD Act complaint** about the reprisal **and it is accepted** → ⛔ **cannot
  subsequently commence s 42 proceedings**

| | **s 42 — District/Supreme Court** | **AD Act complaint — QHRC → QIRC** |
|---|---|---|
| Remedy | ⭐ tort damages **including exemplary** | AD Act remedies, generally smaller |
| **WCRA** | ⭐⭐ **s 42(6) — the WCRA does not apply** ⇒ preserved **independently of the WC claim** | — |
| Cost / speed | high, slow, judge without jury (s 42(3)) | cheap, conciliation first, faster |
| Prosecution | **s 42(5)** — available even if no s 41 prosecution | **s 44(4)** — same |

⚠️⚠️ **DO NOT COMMENCE EITHER WITHOUT ADVICE.** ⭐ **This is the single most consequential
irreversible choice in the whole matter, and it is made by the act of filing, not by any decision
he announces.** Take it to counsel, not to Petering — it is outside the union's demarcation.

## ⭐⭐ 2.2C **s 45 — THE DEFENCE IS NARROWER THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. CORRECTION.**
Earlier files state the defence as *"reasonable management action taken reasonably is not a
reprisal."* **That understates his position.** The section actually reads:

> **s 45(2)** *"a manager may take reasonable management action in relation to an employee who has
> made a public interest disclosure **only if the manager's reasons for taking the action do not
> include the fact that the person has made the public interest disclosure**."*

⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **Read with s 40(5) — where it is enough that the unlawful ground is *a substantial ground*,
"even if there is another ground" — the two together mean: if the disclosure is among the reasons at
all, in any material way, the management-action shield fails.** It is not enough that the action was
otherwise reasonable.

⭐ **s 45(3)** — *"manager"* means *"a person to whom the employee reports or a person who **directly
or indirectly supervises** the employee"*. ⇒ **Covers the Manager and the Director both.**

## 2.3 THE ROUTES, IF IT HAPPENS
| Route | Provision | Test | ⏰ Time limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General protections** | **IR Act ss 282, 284, 285** | adverse action for a workplace right | ⚠️ **s 310 — 21 days** from when the dismissal took effect; extension only on **"exceptional circumstances"** |
| ⭐ **Reverse onus** | **s 306** | *"presumed… unless the person proves otherwise"* | — |
| **Accessorial liability** | **s 571** | persons involved in the contravention | — |
| **Unfair dismissal** | **ss 316, 317** | *"harsh, unjust or unreasonable"* | ⚠️ **21 days**; extension available on an application *"made at any time"* |
| ⭐ **Reprisal** | **PID Act ss 40–42** | **s 40(5) — a substantial ground suffices** | tort; **s 43** entity vicariously liable |
| **Discrimination** | **AD Act s 15(1)(c)**, and **s 15(2)** — *"dismissing includes ending the particular work of a person by… **failure to provide work***" | — | **s 138 — 1 year** |
| **PS Act appeals** | **s 131(1)(c), (f), (g)** — disciplinary, suspension without pay, transfer | — | ⏳ **Appeals directive — NOT HELD** |

## 2.4 ⚠️ WHAT TO DO THE DAY IT HAPPENS — 21 DAYS IS THE SHORTEST CLOCK IN THE MATTER
- [ ] ⭐ **Petering, same day.** Two 21-day clocks run from the dismissal taking effect.
- [ ] ⛔ **Do not resign, and do not accept any characterisation of abandonment.** Reply the same
      day: *"I have not abandoned my employment. I have been willing and available to work
      throughout and have said so in writing on [dates]."*
- [ ] **Preserve the letter, the envelope, the metadata and the date it took effect.**
- [ ] ⛔ **Do not argue the merits in the reply.** Assert availability, ask for the reasons and the
      decision-maker, and stop.

>>> skill/references/THE-28-DAY-GAP.md :: text
# THE 28-DAY GAP — why the "we needed medical information" defence fails on its own dates
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Banked 4 Aug 2026 (Cory's formulation). The single strongest manner
> argument in the matter. Deploy in the Stage 1/2 discussion, in any s 32(5) submission,
> and in the AD Act limb — NEVER with motive language. The dates carry it alone.

## THE SEQUENCE
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 3 Jul 2026, 2:32pm | ECC provided by the deadline. **Certified fit for work with restrictions.** |
| 3 Jul, within the hour | Told he could not attend. Excluded. |
| 3–31 Jul | **Nothing. 28 days.** No request for medical information, no instrument identified, no return date. |
| 13 Jul | Pay ceases. Leave debited. |
| 15 Jul & 30 Jul | Health Service in writing: "unable to commit to a timeframe" / "unable to guarantee when". |
| 31 Jul, 11:43am | Request for Medical Information issued — **7-day deadline**, plus "I will make a decision regarding your ability to perform your role." |

## THE ARGUMENT (deployable wording, no motive)
1. The stated reason for exclusion was the need for medical clearance.
2. If that were the operative reason, the request for medical information would have been
   made on or about 3 July. It was made on 31 July — **four weeks later**.
3. Across those four weeks he was excluded, unpaid from 13 July, and his leave was debited,
   while the information said to be necessary was not sought at all.
4. **The exclusion therefore cannot be explained by the stated reason.** A reason that is
   not acted on for 28 days is not the reason the action was taken for.

## THE LESS-RESTRICTIVE-MEANS LIMB
Medical information can lawfully be sought from an employee **who is at work**, or at
minimum **who remains on pay**. Nothing in G03, the WHS Act or the agreement requires an
employee to be excluded and unpaid while an employer gathers medical information; no
instrument requiring it has ever been identified. The employer had at least three
available options and took the most restrictive:
  (a) request the information while he continued in the role on the certified restrictions;
  (b) request it while he remained on full pay pending clearance;
  (c) request it with a timeframe proportionate to psychiatric appointment availability.
It also attached a decision-threat to the request, which none of (a)–(c) requires.

## THE ASYMMETRY THAT SEALS IT
The employer twice recorded in writing that it could not commit to any timeframe of its
own (15 Jul, 30 Jul), then imposed seven days on him (31 Jul). No clock binds them;
day-counts bind him.

## WHERE IT LANDS
- **s 32(5) manner** — the substance defence ("we were entitled to seek medical
  information") is legitimate in the abstract and collapses on these dates. The action
  is not shown to be reasonable *in the way it was taken*.
- **Employment track** — exclusion and pay cessation without an identified instrument,
  and without the less-restrictive alternatives being taken or explained.
- **AD Act limb (limitation ~8 Sep)** — reasonable adjustment was available and certified
  (work with restrictions); exclusion without pay is the antithesis of adjustment.
- **cl 10.3 / dispute** — supports the forward-pay limb: the power to stop pay was never
  identified, and the justification offered does not fit the chronology.

## DISCIPLINE
State the dates; state the available alternatives; stop. Never say "the real reason was".
The gap does the work, and a decision-maker who notices it themselves is worth more than
one who is told.

# THE ACCEPTANCE EXIT — their way out of the whole mess (Cory's thesis, 4-5 Aug 2026)
> ⛔ Strategy layer. The convergence prediction: the matter resolves through CLAIM
> ACCEPTANCE because it is the only exit that requires no one at MSH to own anything.

## THE THESIS
Every other exit needs an owner (answer the instrument question, refuse special leave,
dismiss, keep not paying). Acceptance is externally decided (the Regulator concedes the
appeal) and MSH merely "responds": pay normalises, RTW runs under the WCRA rehab
framework, leave re-credits in reconciliation, medical flows through proper channels,
the ART/IP tangle dissolves, and everything done since 26 June gets retrospectively
narrated as "awaiting the compensation outcome." The narrative is false but it is the
price of the exit, and the exit pays him. Cascade: Fri 7 Aug production conceded (fight
spent; won't renew orally before Dwyer) → records inevitable → appeal repriced →
acceptance/settlement → employment normalises under statute.

## HIS POSTURE (critical)
- NEVER propose it. The exit works because they discover it; proposed by him it becomes
  a demand to resist. His job: keep pressure symmetrical, keep every clock running,
  keep the off-ramps lit. (Calderbank #3 machinery = the vehicle if it comes as offer.)
- FORM MATTERS: acceptance (statutory entitlements) > deed. If deed: rule 9 absolute —
  releases the COMPENSATION CLAIM ONLY; no employment releases; nothing touching the
  26-Jun-onward accruals, the protected-acts record, or the WHS/assessment work; no gag.
- Managed-on-WorkCover has employer levers too (insurer IMEs, rehab compliance,
  certificate cycles, same IM team running RTW under supervision). Discipline unchanged:
  treating doctors primary, everything in writing, meeting-record protocol at every RTW
  conference, same-day filing.
- Backdating/reconciliation: weekly comp vs withheld wages vs debited leave must be
  reconciled item-by-item at resolution — keep the ledgers ready.

# THE BOARD — EVERY LEGAL ELEMENT: WHAT IS SET UP, AND WHAT THEIR NEXT MOVE COMPLETES
> Built 2 August 2026, on the eve of the send. The capstone ledger. For each regime: which

# PART 1 — ESTABLISHED NOW (no further act by anyone required)

| Element | Regime | How it is complete |

>>> skill/references/THE-INVERSION-worker-as-hazard.md :: text
# ⭐⭐⭐ THE INVERSION — THE WORKER TREATED AS THE HAZARD
## The single proposition the whole employment case reduces to

> Built 31 July 2026. All provisions verbatim from **ATT24** WHS Regulation 2011 (Qld) current
> 29 Mar 2026, **ATT17** WHS Act 2011, **ATT22** IR Act 2016, **ATT05** Psychosocial Code 2022.
> **This is a proof from the instruments, not an inference about anyone's state of mind.**

---

## 1. THE PROOF

### 1.1 Isolation is a control applied to hazards
> **Reg 36(3):** "The duty holder must minimise risks, so far as is reasonably practicable, by doing
> one or more of the following— (a) **substituting** (wholly or partly) **the hazard** giving rise to
> the risk…; (b) ⭐ **isolating the hazard from any person exposed to it**; (c) implementing
> **engineering controls**."
> **(4)** "If a risk then remains… by implementing **administrative controls**."
> **(5)** "If a risk then remains… **personal protective equipment**."

**Five levels. Every one operates on the hazard, the work, or the exposed person's protection.
Removing the exposed person is not among them at any level.**

### 1.2 What MSH actually did
> **Taylor, 26 Jun 2026:** "**we are unable to facilitate your return to work**… we have a legal
> obligation under **section 19** of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011…"

**The control applied was: remove Cory from the workplace, and keep him removed, expressly in
discharge of the s 19 safety duty.**

### 1.3 ⭐⭐ THE BIND — there is no third reading
| If MSH says | Then |
|---|---|
| *"We applied a control under reg 36"* | **The only control that removes a person from a workplace is isolation — and isolation is applied to the hazard.** They classified him as the hazard. |
| *"We did not treat him as the hazard"* | **Then no recognised control was applied at all**, and the exclusion has no basis in the risk-management framework they invoked. |

**They cannot have both.** They invoked s 19 to justify the act. **s 19 is discharged through
part 3.1, and part 3.1's hierarchy has no step called "exclude the worker."**

---

## 2. AND THE IDENTIFIED HAZARD WAS MANAGEMENT

> **ECC, 3 July 2026, stressor (4):** "**unresolved workplace matters involving line management**"

> **Reg 55A:** "A psychosocial hazard is a hazard that— (a) arises from, or relates to— (i) **the
> design or management of work**;… or (iv) **workplace interactions or behaviours**; and (b) may
> cause psychological harm."

⇒ **On the face of the regulation, the hazard identified in MSH's own document is the management of
work.**
⇒ **The person removed was the worker exposed to it.**

**That is the inversion, stated without adjectives: the hazard was identified as management; the
control applied was to remove the person exposed.**

> **Reg 35(a):** "**eliminate** risks to health and safety **so far as is reasonably practicable**"

Elimination is the **first** obligation, and it operates on the risk — not on the person carrying it.

---

## 3. ⭐⭐ THE SELF-ASSESSMENT PROBLEM — THE SHARPEST POINT IN THE FILE

**Switchboard Services reports to Corporate Services.** *(LBH_HR, 21 Feb 2025: "Corporate Services
(where Switchboard is now reporting)".)*

**The identified hazard is the management of work — within Corporate Services.**

⇒ **If the psychosocial risk assessment for Switchboard Services is conducted by, or under the
authority of, Corporate Services, then the assessor is determining whether the assessor is the
hazard.**

⚠️ **That is not merely a conflict of interest requiring management under Code of Conduct cl 1.2.
It is a process structurally incapable of producing a valid assessment** — because the honest
finding may be that the assessing officer is the source of the risk.

⭐ **And it may explain the central absence in this matter:** no psychosocial risk assessment has ever
been produced, in five weeks, despite s 55C making it mandatory and despite MSH's stated position
being that it *cannot assess the risk*. **A process that cannot honestly reach its own finding tends
not to be run.**

⇒ **Which is why the alternative decision-maker (§ Part 6.1 of the response) is not a courtesy. It is
the precondition of a lawful assessment.**

---

## 4. THE CONSEQUENCES THAT FOLLOW

| Instrument | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Reg 55C(1)** | Managing psychosocial risk is **mandatory**. No assessment = duty unmet. |
| **Reg 34–36** | Hazards must be identified, risks eliminated or minimised, **and the hierarchy applied in order**. Exclusion is not in it. |
| **WHS Act s 47** | Consultation with the affected worker is **mandatory**, and carries a penalty. |
| **s 48(1)(b)(ii)** | The worker must be able **to contribute to the decision-making process** — the very process that removed him. |
| **G03 cl 1.1** | Adjustments exist so employees "**continue work during their recovery**". |
| **G03 cl 1** | Managers must ensure work "**does not unreasonably prevent employment for people**". |
| **Psychosocial Code 2022** | Hazards are **features of the work**, controlled by the PCBU. |
| **WCRA s 32(5)** | Management action must be reasonable **and taken in a reasonable way** — and the manner here was to apply to a worker the measure reserved for hazards. |

---

## 5. ⚠️ ON "BULLYING" — THE HONEST ADVICE

**The remedy exists.** IR Act 2016 ch 7:
> **s 272(1)** an employee is bullied if, **while the employee is at work**, an individual or group
> **repeatedly behaves unreasonably** towards them **and** that behaviour **creates a risk to the
> health and safety** of the employee.
> **s 272(2)** "does **not** apply to **reasonable management action carried out in a reasonable
> manner**."
> **s 273** an employee who **reasonably believes** they have been bullied **may apply** to the
> commission.
> ⭐ **s 274** "The commission **must start to deal with** an application… **within 14 days**."
> **s 275(2)** the commission may make **any order it considers appropriate** (other than payment of
> money) **to prevent** the employee from being bullied.

### ⛔ BUT DO NOT FILE IT NOW, AND DO NOT USE THE WORD IN CORRESPONDENCE
1. ⚠️ **"While the employee is at work."** He has been excluded since **3 July 2026**. The
   jurisdictional foothold is weakest at exactly the moment he is out of the workplace.
2. ⚠️⚠️ **s 275(1)(b)(ii) — the commission must be satisfied there is a risk he will *continue* to
   be bullied.** **If he is not in the workplace, MSH will say there is no continuing risk and no
   order can be made.** This is the standard answer to stop-bullying applications by absent workers.
   ⭐ *Though note the trap it creates for them: to defeat it they must assert he is not returning —
   which concedes the exclusion. **Hold that; do not spring it yet.***
3. ⚠️ **s 272(2) is their whole defence** — "reasonable management action carried out in a reasonable
   manner" — the same fight as **WCRA s 32(5)**. Running it twice, in two forums, before the first is
   resolved, is not sound.
4. ⛔ **The word "bullying" in correspondence forfeits the register.** It converts a regulatory
   argument he is winning — *hazard, risk, control, hierarchy* — into an allegation with a defined
   threshold **he** must meet, and invites the reasonable-management-action answer by return.

⇒ ⭐ **Use the regulation's language, not the accusation.** "The identified hazard is the management
of work; the control applied was the removal of the worker; the hierarchy at reg 36 does not provide
for that." **That is unanswerable and it never once says the word.**
⇒ **Keep ch 7 in reserve.** It becomes available and much stronger **once he is back in the
workplace** — at which point s 272(1)(a) and s 275(1)(b)(ii) are both satisfied.

---

## 6. THE PROPOSITION, IN ONE PARAGRAPH

Metro South Health invoked **s 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act** to justify keeping Mr Shepherd
out of his workplace. Section 19 is discharged through the risk-management process in **part 3.1 of
the WHS Regulation**. That process requires hazards to be identified, risks eliminated so far as
reasonably practicable, and, if not, minimised through a prescribed hierarchy in which the second
step is **isolating the hazard from the persons exposed to it**. **Removing an exposed worker is not
a control measure the regulation recognises at any level.** The hazard the Health Service's own
document identifies is *"unresolved workplace matters involving line management"* — a hazard arising
from the management of work and from workplace interactions, within the very directorate that
excluded him. **The Health Service therefore either treated the worker as the hazard, or applied no
recognised control at all.** And the assessment that would have determined the question was never
performed — by a directorate that would have had to assess itself.

>>> skill/references/THE-MIRROR-turning-the-request-back.md :: text
# ⭐⭐⭐ THE MIRROR — TURNING THE REQUEST BACK
## The comprehensive strategic framing

> Built 31 July 2026 from the verified instruments. **The organising insight:**
> **All nine of their questions are questions about the worker. Not one is a question about the
> work.** Every provision that governs the subject matter asks the opposite.

---

# PART 1 — THE MASTER FRAME, IN ONE LINE

> **They asked: is he safe to be returned to the workplace?**
> **Every instrument asks: is the workplace safe to return him to?**

**That is the whole reversal.** It requires no allegation, no motive, and no adjective — only the
statute.

| Their question | The question the law asks | Provision |
|---|---|---|
| Is **he** medically fit to return? | Has the **PCBU** ensured, so far as reasonably practicable, the health and safety of workers? | **WHS s 19(1)** |
| Can **he** follow a lawful and reasonable direction? | Have **lawful and reasonable directions** been given — and under what instrument? | implied power; **six shifting bases, none identified** |
| Is **he** fit under the **existing reporting arrangements**? | Have the **existing reporting arrangements** been assessed as a psychosocial hazard? | **Reg 55A(a)(i), (iv)** — the ECC's stressor (4) is line management |
| Can **he** perform the role **without restrictions or modifications**? | What are the **genuine occupational requirements**, and what adjustment enables them? | **G03**; **AD Act s 34** |
| If **we can't accommodate**, can **he** safely return? | What accommodation was **assessed and found unreasonable**, against the **whole organisation**, on **whose onus**? | **G03 cl 2** — *"the onus is on Queensland Health"* |
| What **controls** are medically necessary? | What controls has the **PCBU** identified and implemented, in the **prescribed order**? | **Regs 34–36** |

---

# PART 2 — THE FOUR CONCERNS, EACH TURNED BACK ONTO ITS PROVISION

## 2.1 "Directives without consultation"
**Their frame:** can he follow lawful directions? *(Q2)*
**The mirror:** **consultation is not optional and it is not an adjustment. It is the precondition of
a direction being reasonable.**

> **WHS s 47(1):** the PCBU "**must**… **consult**… with workers… **directly affected by a matter
> relating to work health or safety**."
> **s 48(1)(b)(ii):** workers must have a reasonable opportunity ⭐ **"to contribute to the
> decision-making process"**.
> **Reg 38(2)(b):** controls must be reviewed **"before a change at the workplace that is likely to
> give rise to a new or different risk"**.
> **Code 2022 — POOR ORGANISATIONAL CHANGE MANAGEMENT:** *"**not consulting workers on changes in the
> workplace that affect them**… or genuinely considering their views."*
> **EB12 cl 7.1.11** — feedback on WHS matters. **cl 7.2** — psychosocial risk assessment.

⇒ **Evidenced:** Taylor, 15 Apr 2024 — *"Ellen and myself have added Afterhours on call…
**This new process is effective from today.**"* Against MSH's own 2022 roster change, circulated
repeatedly *"for Consultation"* over four months. **They know how. They chose not to.**

## 2.2 "Risks to the department"
**Their frame:** is *he* a risk? *(the exclusion)*
**The mirror:** **the risk the regulation is concerned with is a feature of the work.**

> **Reg 55A:** a psychosocial hazard arises from **"the design or management of work"** or
> **"workplace interactions or behaviours"**.
> **Reg 36(3)(b):** the hierarchy of control requires **"isolating the hazard from any person exposed
> to it"**. ⭐ **Removing the exposed person appears nowhere at any level.**
> **Reg 55D(2)(d):** controls must have regard to **"the systems of work, including how work is
> managed, organised and supported"**.

⇒ **The Code's hazard list contains no category called "the worker".** Every named hazard is
organisational. **So a control directed at the worker cannot be a response to any of them.**

## 2.3 "Patient safety is the core function"
**Their frame:** a medical question about one employee.
**The mirror:** **a s 19 question about the safety of workers *and other persons*.**

> **WHS s 19(1)–(2):** the PCBU must ensure the health and safety of **workers** and **"the health
> and safety of other persons is not put at risk from work carried out"**.

⇒ The unit routes **emergency and after-hours calls**, on a **24/7 continuous shift roster** — from
**their own Role Description**. Changing call routing without consulting the operators who action it
is a **clinical** risk, not merely an industrial one.
⇒ ⭐ **And this is his consistent position since 2024, not a litigation position:**
*"**Failure to consult putting patients at risk**"* (30 Aug 2024) · *"most critically, **patient
safety**"* (15 May 2024).
⚠️ **State as concern, never as leverage. Never attribute current risk to his own absence.**

## 2.4 ⭐⭐ "Not being able to speak up" — THE NEWEST AND SHARPEST ROUTE
**Their frame:** why has he raised so much? *(Q2's premise: "not aware of any concerns being raised")*
**The mirror:** **raising a work health and safety concern is a protected act, and detriment for it
is an offence.**

> **WHS s 105(1)(a):** discriminatory conduct includes where a person **"(iv) alters the position of a
> worker to the worker's detriment"** or **"(iii) puts a worker to his or her detriment in the
> engagement of the worker"**.
> **WHS s 106(h):** it is a **prohibited reason** if the worker *"**raises or has raised or proposes
> to raise an issue or concern about work health and safety** with— (i) **the person conducting a
> business or undertaking**… (iv) a health and safety representative… (vii) **another worker**…"*
> **s 104(1):** *"A person must not engage in discriminatory conduct for a prohibited reason."*
> **Maximum penalty — 1,000 penalty units.**
> **s 107:** the same penalty for anyone who **"request[s], instruct[s], induce[s], encourage[s],
> authorise[s] or assist[s]"** it.

⭐ **Note s 106(h)(vii): raising a concern with *another worker* is protected.** The 15 May 2024
all-staff email — the one Reese asked him to recall — is on its face the raising of a WHS concern
with other workers.
⚠️ **s 104(2): the prohibited reason must be the DOMINANT reason** — a higher bar than IR Act s 305
(*"include that reason"*). **The IR Act route remains the easier one. Record this; lead with s 285.**

---

# PART 3 — THE SIX QUESTIONS THAT DO THE WORK

**Every one is neutral, sourced, and answerable. Every possible answer helps.**

1. **The psychosocial risk assessment** for the role and work unit; the **hazard register**; the
   **control measures** in place; and the record under **s 55D(2)** of the matters had regard to.
2. ⭐ **The date of the last assessment conducted with input from the workers in the unit**, and the
   record of that consultation under **s 48(1)(c)–(d)** — the views, how they were taken into
   account, and how the outcome was communicated.
3. **The genuine occupational requirements** of the AO3 Switchboard role, and which of them is said
   not to be met.
4. **What adjustment has been assessed and found unreasonable**, tested against **the whole
   organisation** as **G03 cl 2** requires, and by whom.
5. **The delegate** who approved the request, the **instrument of delegation**, and the **date** of
   approval.
6. Whether a **health and safety representative** is in place for the unit, and MSH's **published PID
   procedures** under **PID Act s 28(2)**.

---

# PART 4 — WHY THIS FRAMING IS THE RIGHT ONE

| It never | It always |
|---|---|
| Alleges bad faith | Cites a provision |
| Names a motive | States a duty |
| Says "bullying", "reprisal", "conspiracy" | Says **hazard, risk, control, consultation** |
| Asks them to admit anything | Asks them to **produce a document** |
| Depends on anything unproved | Rests on **their own words and the in-force text** |

⭐ **And it is the framing that makes him look like the reasonable party — because on the documents,
he is.** He complied with the 5 May request. He booked the appointment. He produced the certificate.
He asked *"confirm I'm right to attend"*. He has been raising consultation as a **patient safety**
issue since 2024. **He is asking to participate in the work, not to be excused from it.**

## THE CLOSING PROPOSITION
> The Health Service asked nine questions about whether Mr Shepherd is safe to be returned to the
> workplace. **The Work Health and Safety Act asks whether the workplace is safe to return him to.**
> That question has not been asked, the assessment that would answer it has never been performed,
> and the worker whose participation the Act requires in performing it has been excluded from the
> workplace for five weeks while it was not performed.

>>> skill/references/THE-NIL-ASSESSMENT-thesis.md :: text
# THE NIL ASSESSMENT — what follows if Switchboard / Corporate Services was never assessed
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Banked 4 Aug 2026 on Cory's instruction ("I know there has never been an
> assessment on the line of switchboard or corporate services"). ⚠ STATUS: WORKING THEORY, not
> confirmed record — it is his knowledge from inside the room, sufficient to act on, NOT yet
> sufficient to assert in a filing. Conversion route at §5.

## 1. WHAT IT MEANS STRUCTURALLY
The WHS Regulation runs identify → assess → control → review. If no assessment was ever done,
the sequence never started. Consequences:
- There are no controls to review, because none were ever selected against identified hazards.
  Reg 38 review obligations have nothing to operate on.
- "EXISTING CONTROLS IDENTIFIED: None identified" (the matrix column) stops being one operator's
  vantage point and becomes structurally necessary — you cannot have controls for hazards you
  never identified.
- The breach is not an inference from poor outcomes. It is an ABSENCE, provable by a nil record.

## 2. WHAT IT DOES TO EACH MSH DEFENCE
| Their line | What the nil assessment does to it |
|---|---|
| "No concerns were raised" (RFMI Q2) | They never installed the mechanism for concerns to surface — no survey, no register, no assessment. Silence is not evidence of safety where nobody asked. |
| "This is one employee's perception" | Neither side has data — but only ONE side had the legal duty to obtain it. The absence of data is their breach, not his weakness. |
| "Reasonable management action, reasonably taken" (s 32(5)) | Every management action — rostering, substitutions, exclusion, complaint handling — was taken **without any assessment of the psychosocial risk of the work being managed**. Action taken blind is hard to characterise as reasonable IN THE MANNER, which is the contested centre. |
| "The role is unchanged / he cannot perform it" | The role's psychological demands have never been assessed, so the employer's own position on what the role demands rests on nothing but the position description. |

## 3. WHY IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE INJURY
No assessment → no demand data → no evidence-based rostering → within-shift fatigue absorbed by
personal leave → no complaint-response standard → organisational-justice failure → injury. The
absence is not a technicality alongside the harm; it is the mechanism of the harm.

## 4. IT EXTENDS ABOVE THE ROOM
If Corporate Services as a LINE has never been assessed, the unassessed unit is not a room but a
management structure. That reframes the matter from "one worker's complaint" to "a division
operating without the first step of the WHS duty" — and it is the honest frame for the CE letter's
five questions and any later systemic pathway.

## 5. ⭐ CONVERTING BELIEF INTO PROOF — THE NIL RETURN
The most valuable document available in this matter is a **"no documents located"** response.
Include as express RTI/IP categories (Mon 10 Aug):
  (a) any psychosocial risk assessment, hazard identification record, or risk register for
      Switchboard Services, Logan Hospital, 2019–2026;
  (b) the same for Corporate Services, Logan and Beaudesert Health Service;
  (c) any People at Work survey, staff psychosocial survey, or equivalent covering that unit;
  (d) any WHS risk assessment relied on for changes to switchboard rostering or duties;
  (e) any review of control measures under the WHS Regulation for that unit.
A nil return is signed, dated, on their letterhead, and proves the absence from their own records.
⛔ UNTIL IT ARRIVES: never assert "no assessment has ever been done" as fact in a filing or letter.
The tabled documents already do the work in the safe form — "none identified", plus the invitation
to "confirm, correct, or complete" the matrix. Let the nil return supply the proof.

## 6. THEIR PREDICTABLE COUNTER-MOVE
Once they realise the gap, the cheap fix is a rapid desktop "assessment" — no survey, no
observation, business-hours walkthrough, findings low. Pre-empted by the tabled methodology:
the eight phases, the People at Work nomination, the multi-shift observation requirement, and
scope (a)-(h) are already on the record as what an adequate assessment looks like. Any thinner
product is measurable against a document they were given in advance, in consultation.
⚠ Also note: an assessment done in Aug 2026 cannot retrospectively supply controls for the
period in which the injury occurred. A new assessment answers the future, never the past.

## 7. EFFECT ON THE NUMBERS (conditional)
Unproven, it changes nothing. On a nil return, the s 32(5) manner limb strengthens materially
(the whole course of management action was taken without the assessment the Regulation requires):
appeal-win band moves from ~35% toward the high 30s/low 40s, and the settlement propensity rises
more than the hearing number does — a nil return is exactly the document a respondent does not
want read aloud.

## PART B — THE FOUR PROPOSITIONS THE TABLE PROVES

**1. The exclusion originates in a duty used as a power.**
WHS s 19 is owed **to** the worker and operates **"while the workers are at work"**. Every
limb of s 19(3) concerns the employer's own arrangements. Removing the worker does not
discharge the duty; it removes the occasion for it. Cited **26 June, before anything was
challenged** — MSH's own first, unpressured characterisation of its authority.

**2. The authority degrades as the detriment escalates.**
Stated once (26 Jun) · dropped when the consequence became exclusion (2 Jul) · unnamed
legislation (7 Jul) · **nothing at all when the consequence became no wages** (15 Jul) ·
nothing (30 Jul) · returning only after the framework was challenged (29, 31 Jul).
A lawful direction behaves the opposite way.

**3. MSH's own condition was satisfied and the bar did not lift.**
26 June is expressly conditional — *"until we receive… a completed ECC"*. The ECC arrived
3 July certifying fitness with restrictions. A new condition appeared 7 July. That was
satisfied 3 August. The exclusion continued. **A genuine reason is self-terminating;
each of these was replaced rather than resolved.**

**4. No instrument has ever been identified.**
Not PS Act s 101 (suspension). Not Division 5 ss 103–109 (incapacity). No show-cause, no
discipline. Six weeks, four written requests, a formal dispute — and the question *under
what instrument am I excluded* has never been answered.

## PART C — THE TWO SENTENCES FOR THE CONFERENCE

> *"I was certified fit with restrictions on 3 July. Every reason since given for my not
> returning has been answered. I am asking what the current reason is, and under what
> instrument."*

Nothing else. The question is about the **present**, where they have nothing, not the
past, where they have explanations.

## PART D — WHAT DOES NOT GO IN

⛔ The 25/26 June adjacency is **recorded in date order and never asserted as a cause.**
s 306 IR Act puts the onus on MSH; s 284 makes initiating and participating in a QIRC
proceeding a workplace right. Let a reader obliged to explain the sequence notice the two
dates themselves.

⛔ No characterisation of any officer or group. No "tight", "protective", "bullying",
"campaign". Discipline rule 1.

⛔ Nothing about the appeal. Stage 2 is EB12 cl 1.11 — attendance, roster, leave and pay.

⛔ ⚠ OPEN: the last shift actually worked before 26 June is still unverified
(CLAUDE.md immediate task 6). Settle it from the payslips and roster **before** the
referral goes, and state it as a date, not an inference.

# HAVE MSH WALKED INTO A TRAP? — the comprehensive read
> Built 31 July 2026 on the final document set. **Honest assessment, including where the answer is
> "less than you hope".**

---

# 1. THE SHORT ANSWER

**It is not a trap they *must* answer. It is a trap where every available option costs them.**
That is a better position than compulsion, because it does not depend on anyone ordering them to
do anything.

⚠️ **Be clear-eyed: MSH is under no obligation to answer an employee's questions.** They have
already not answered *"confirm I'm right to attend"* (3 Jul), the 28 July request to identify the
delegate and instrument, and the 4 October 2025 complaint. **Assume silence is a real possibility
and make silence expensive.** The documents are built so it is.

---

# 2. THE STRUCTURE OF THE BIND

## 2.1 What they have already said in writing
> **Forrest, 7 July 2026:** "the Health Service **does not have sufficient information to understand
> the nature of these matters or assess whether they present any psychosocial hazards or risks**
> that may affect your proposed return to work."

## 2.2 What the law says about that
> **WHS Regulation 2011 s 55C(1):** "A person conducting a business or undertaking **must manage
> psychosocial risks under part 3.1**."
> **s 55A:** a psychosocial hazard includes one arising from **"the design or management of work"**
> or **"workplace interactions or behaviours"**.
> **WHS Act s 47(1):** the PCBU **must consult** workers directly affected. **s 48(1)(b)(ii):** they
> must have a reasonable opportunity **"to contribute to the decision-making process"**.

## 2.3 ⭐ THE FOUR-WAY BIND — every branch costs them
| If MSH… | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Produces a current assessment** | It is dated, disclosable and testable — **and a specialist can evaluate it clinically**, which is precisely what their own Q1(d) invites. If it identifies management of work as a hazard, the exclusion inverts. |
| **Produces one with no worker input** | **s 47/48 breach on the face of the document.** Consultation is mandatory and carries a penalty. |
| **Produces one that never considered s 55D(2)(d) or (h)** | The determination of controls did not have regard to matters the Regulation **requires** — systems of work and workplace interactions. |
| **Cannot identify when the last worker-input assessment occurred** | ⭐⭐ **The strongest branch.** *"We do not have sufficient information to assess"* is answered: **the information does not exist because the assessment was never performed** — and performing it is mandatory. |
| **Declines to answer at all** | A refusal to state whether a mandatory assessment exists, **to a worker excluded for five weeks on the basis of an unassessed risk.** Goes directly to reasonableness and to s 48(1)(d). |

## 2.4 ⭐ AND THE REQUEST ITSELF TRIGGERS A REVIEW OBLIGATION
> **Reg 38(2):** controls must be reviewed where **"(c) a new relevant hazard or risk is identified"**
> or **"(d) the results of consultation by the duty holder under the Act or this regulation indicate
> that a review is necessary"**.

⇒ **Raising the hazards in writing is consultation output.** It engages reg 38(2)(d) whether they
answer or not. **The obligation attaches on receipt.**

# 3. ⚠️ THE HARD PART — CAN THE ASSESSMENT BE DEPLOYED AT THE APPEAL?

**Less than hoped. Say so now rather than discover it later.**

## 3.1 The mismatch
- **WC/2024/227 concerns the injury of 18 June 2024**, and was rejected on the **s 32(5)** exclusion.
- **A 2026 psychosocial assessment describes the workplace in 2026.**
- ⚠️ **It does not prove what the workplace was in 2023–24.** A Commissioner will see that immediately.

## 3.2 What it *can* do in the appeal — indirectly but genuinely
1. ⭐ **Corroborates that the pleaded stressors are recognised workplace hazards, not perception.**
   The Regulator's SOFC does not admit the stressors. An assessment identifying complaint handling,
   rostering and line-management matters as **psychosocial hazards under a Code MSH must apply**
   makes them features of the work.
2. ⭐ **Feeds s 32(5)'s second limb** — management action must be reasonable **and taken in a
   reasonable way**. Evidence that the employer had no assessment, and no consultation, over a
   sustained period bears on *the way* it acted.
3. **Answers the pre-existing-anxiety line at SOFC ¶8** by locating the cause in work design rather
   than the person.
4. **Continuity of the same hazards across 2024–2026** is itself probative.

## 3.3 ⛔ WHERE IT MUST NOT GO
- **Not into the 64G**, which is about production of records and is filed.
- **Not raised at the 7 August mention.** Ordinary procedural machinery; volunteer nothing.
- **Not as a substitute for the medical causation case**, which is Report B and Dr Krishnaiah.

⇒ **Its real home is the employment track.** Treat any appeal benefit as a bonus, not the plan.

          category live since ~Apr 2025);
      (ii) EMPLOYER'S OWN PAYSLIPS: supplied by MSH to ART covering 7 Apr 2025-14 Jun 2026,
           i.e. the employer's own records evidencing ~14 months of work while on claim;

      benefit. It is NOT proof of a formally agreed reduced-hours instrument with MSH.
      State it only as the sources state it: 14 months of work while on claim, evidenced by
      the employer's own payslips, described in the Checklist as a continuation of existing
