>>> skill/references/WHO-INVESTIGATES-WHAT.md :: text
# WHO ACTUALLY INVESTIGATES WHAT — routing map (verified 4 Aug 2026)
> ⛔ Strategy layer. Corrects a common and costly assumption: NO single body investigates
> "the detriment and harm caused to me". Each has a narrow jurisdiction; most will decline
> while QIRC proceedings are on foot. The tribunal — through HIS OWN proceedings — is the
> body that makes findings about detriment. He is the investigator; QIRC is the fact-finder.

| Body | What it actually does | Reality here |
|---|---|---|
| **RTI / IP access** | NOT an investigation. A document-access process run by MSH's own RTI decision-maker; external review by the Office of the Information Commissioner. | Exactly right for the **nil return**. Produces documents, never findings. 25 business days + extensions. **DO IT (Mon 10).** |
| **QPS (police)** | Criminal offences only. PID s 41 reprisal is indictable, so jurisdiction technically exists. | In practice QPS treats workplace reprisal as civil/employment and refers on. Low return, high credibility cost, and never to be threatened. **NOT the pathway.** |
| **⭐ Workplace Health and Safety Queensland (OIR)** | The WHS regulator: inspects, issues improvement/prohibition notices, investigates Part 6 discriminatory conduct, prosecutes s 104 offences. | **The one external body whose jurisdiction actually fits** — unmanaged psychosocial risk + WHS-based detriment. An improvement notice would compel the assessment. Timing: hold until Stage 2 has run or an adverse act occurs. |
| **QIRC under WHS s 112** | An "eligible person" (incl. the person affected) may apply directly for **injunction, compensation, or reinstatement** for discriminatory conduct. | ⭐ A remedy HE can bring himself, not dependent on any regulator. **s 113(2): the prohibited reason is PRESUMED to be a substantial reason unless the employer disproves it on the balance of probabilities — a legal burden.** ⚠ **s 113(1): 1 YEAR from when he knew or ought to have known the cause of action accrued.** ⚠ **s 115: cannot run this and another proceeding about the SAME MATTER simultaneously — but workers' compensation proceedings are expressly carved out.** |
| **Queensland Ombudsman** | Maladministration in public-agency administrative action. | Usually declines where another remedy (QIRC) exists; makes systemic findings, awards no compensation. Secondary at best. |
| **CCC** | Corrupt conduct. Reprisal for a PID can qualify. | Typically devolves the complaint back to the agency (MSH investigates itself). Banked; not now. |
| **QHRC** | Impairment discrimination, victimisation; conciliation, referral to QIRC. | Real, paired with the AD Act limb. **Limitation ~8 Sep.** |
| **Royal Commission** | Established by executive government into matters of major public importance. | **Cannot be invoked by an individual.** Not a pathway — no application exists to make. |

## THE THREE THINGS THIS CHANGES
1. **The investigation of his harm is his own proceeding.** The 64G/Form 29 machinery, the
   disclosure, the sworn alternative — that IS the investigation, and Dwyer is the finder of
   fact. No external body will do it for him, and waiting for one costs time he does not have.
2. **WHS s 112 is a genuinely underused remedy** — his own application, compensation and
   reinstatement available, and a reverse legal burden under s 113(2) that is stronger than
   most protective provisions. Two limits to diarise: **1 year** (s 113(1)) and the
   **multiple-actions bar** (s 115) — WC proceedings excepted.
3. **WHSQ is the only external escalation with real teeth**, and it is a one-way door.
   Posture unchanged: hold until Stage 2 has run or an adverse act occurs.

>>> skill/references/WHS-s19-a-duty-not-a-power.md :: text
# SECTION 19 IS A DUTY ON THE EMPLOYER ABOUT ITS OWN WORKPLACE — NOT A POWER OVER THE WORKER
> Built 1 August 2026 on Cory's reading. **He is right, and the point is structural.**
> Verified word-for-word against **ATT17** (WHS Act 2011 (Qld), current as at 29 March 2026),
> **ATT24** (WHS Regulation), and **ATT19** (Public Sector Act 2022, current 1 July 2026).

---

# PART 1 — WHERE MSH CITED IT

**26 June 2026, 00:42:50 — Chloe Taylor to Cory** (`pack 02 p.432`; corpus line 4566):

> *"Until we receive appropriate medical clearance, including a completed Employee Capacity
> Certificate (ECC), we are unable to facilitate your return to work… **As your employer, we have a
> legal obligation under section 19 of the Queensland Work Health and Safety Act 2011**, which sets
> out the primary duty of care to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety
> of workers by providing and maintaining safe systems of work."*

Repeated on **2 July 2026**, with the deadline of 2:00pm on 3 July.

⚠️ **Note the sequence, which was corrected earlier and matters here:** s 19 was cited on **26 June,
before Cory challenged anything.** It was not reasoned backwards to meet a challenge. **It is the
Health Service's own first and considered characterisation of its authority** — which is why it is
worth taking at face value and reading closely.

---

# PART 2 — ⭐⭐ WHAT s 19 ACTUALLY SAYS

## 2.1 Subsection (1) — the duty runs *while he is at work*
> **s 19(1)** *"A person conducting a business or undertaking must ensure, so far as is reasonably
> practicable, the health and safety of— (a) workers engaged, or caused to be engaged by the person;
> and (b) workers whose activities in carrying out work are influenced or directed by the person;*
> ***while the workers are at work in the business or undertaking.***"

⇒ **The duty is owed TO the worker, and it operates WHILE HE IS AT WORK.** Removing him from the
workplace does not discharge the duty. **It removes the occasion for it.**

## 2.2 Subsection (3) — every single limb is about the employer's own arrangements
> **s 19(3)** *"…a person conducting a business or undertaking must ensure, so far as is reasonably
> practicable—*
> *(a) **the provision and maintenance of a work environment** without risks to health and safety;*
> *(b) **the provision and maintenance of safe plant and structures**;*
> *(c) **the provision and maintenance of safe systems of work**;*
> *(d) the safe use, handling and storage of plant, structures and substances;*
> *(e) **the provision of adequate facilities for the welfare at work of workers**…;*
> *(f) **the provision of any information, training, instruction or supervision** that is necessary…;*
> *(g) that **the health of workers and the conditions at the workplace are monitored** for the
> purpose of preventing illness or injury of workers **arising from the conduct of the business or
> undertaking**."*

⭐ **Seven limbs. Every one begins with what the employer must PROVIDE, MAINTAIN or MONITOR.**
**Work environment. Plant. Systems of work. Facilities. Information, training, instruction,
supervision. Conditions at the workplace.**

⇒ **Not one of them is a thing the worker must produce, prove, or satisfy.** Section 19 contains
**no power to exclude a worker, no power to suspend, and no requirement that a worker demonstrate
fitness.**

## 2.3 ⭐⭐⭐ THE INVERSION, STATED PLAINLY
**Section 19 is a provision that protects him.** MSH has cited it as the reason to hold him out of
the workplace and stop his pay.

⇒ **A duty owed to the worker has been used as authority against the worker.** That is not a
characterisation — it is what the words of the section do and do not say.

⇒ And it sits directly alongside the reg 36 point already in the file: **the hierarchy of control
at reg 36 sets out, in order, how a duty under s 19 is discharged — and it contains no step for
removing the worker.** The duty points at the workplace; the method points at the workplace.
**Only MSH's application points at him.**

---

# PART 3 — ⚠️ THE HONEST LIMIT, AND WHY IT MAKES THE POINT STRONGER

⚠️ **Do not say "MSH had no power to direct him not to attend."** That overstates it, and a
Commissioner would correct it.

An employer **can** give lawful and reasonable directions, and in some circumstances a direction not
to attend pending medical clearance will be lawful and reasonable. **But that power does not come
from s 19.** It comes from the contract of employment and the common law right to give lawful and
reasonable directions — and, in the Queensland public sector, from a specific statutory scheme.

⭐ **The correct proposition is narrower and much harder to answer:**

> **Section 19 imposes a duty; it does not confer a power. If a power to hold him out of the
> workplace exists, it lies somewhere else — and in five weeks the Health Service has not identified
> it, although he has asked.**

⇒ **That is exactly the question already in the documents.** It does not need to be argued. It needs
to be asked, and then answered by them.

---

# PART 4 — ⭐⭐⭐ AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT *DOES* FIT DOESN'T HELP THEM
**Public Sector Act 2022, ch 3 pt 8 div 5 — "Mental or physical incapacity", ss 103–109.**
This is the statutory scheme in Queensland for exactly what MSH says it is doing. Read against it,
the RFMI is not a s 19 measure at all — it is a s 104 measure taken outside s 104.

| Provision | What it requires | Where MSH stands |
|---|---|---|
| **s 103** — division applies only if **(a)** the employee is absent from duty **or** the CE is reasonably satisfied duties are not being performed satisfactorily; **and (b)** the CE **reasonably suspects** that is caused by illness or disability | a stated entry test | ⛔ **Their own letter of 31 July says the Health Service is not aware of any performance or conduct concerns raised for appropriate management.** And "absent from duty" is circular — **he is absent because they excluded him**. ⚠️ **But see the qualification in `RED-TEAM` Rank 1: ATT18 says absence "may include involuntary absence such as suspension".** The surviving argument is **s 103(b)** — the cause must be the *illness*, and MSH's stated cause is the pending information |
| **s 104** — **the employee's chief executive** may appoint a doctor to examine the employee and require the employee to submit | **the CE**, an **appointed** doctor, an **examination** | ⛔ A Director, Corporate Services, sent **nine questions to the employee's own GP**. No appointment, no examination, no CE |
| **s 105** — sick leave withheld **only** where the employee **fails to comply with a s 104(b) requirement** | the sole statutory basis for withholding leave in this division | ⛔ **He complied with everything asked.** ECC provided 3 July, 2:32pm — 28 minutes before the 2:00pm-Friday deadline had even fully run its course in their own terms |
| **s 106(1)–(2)** — the report must state whether there is an illness that **may adversely affect performance**, its likely effect, and its likely duration | defined scope | ⚠️ The RFMI's nine questions go well beyond it — including causation, which is in issue in the appeal |
| **s 106(3)** — the CE **must give the employee a copy** of the report | disclosure to him, as of right | ⏳ nothing said about disclosure |
| **s 107** — action following the report: **transfer or redeploy**; if not reasonably practicable, **retire** | the exhaustive list of outcomes | ⛔⛔ **There is no step in s 107 for "hold the employee out of the workplace, unpaid, indefinitely."** It does not exist in the scheme |
| **s 109** — the Commissioner's directive on this division **must** be complied with | mandatory | ⏳ no directive identified |

## ⭐⭐ THE FINDING
**The Act contemplates: a stated entry test, the chief executive as decision-maker, an appointed
examiner, a scoped report, disclosure to the employee, and two outcomes — transfer/redeploy, or
retire.**

**MSH has produced: no entry test (disclaimed in its own letter), a Director as decision-maker, the
employee's own GP as examiner, nine unscoped questions, no disclosure position, and an outcome that
appears nowhere in the division — five weeks of unpaid exclusion.**

⇒ **This is why "no instrument has been identified in five weeks" is not an oversight.** ⭐ **The
instrument that fits the conduct is the instrument that most clearly does not authorise it.** Citing
s 19 instead is citing a duty in place of a power.

⚠️ ⛔ **AND THIS IS WHY IT IS NOT ARGUED IN THE LETTERS.** Put ss 103–109 to them now and they can
regularise: refer it to the Chief Executive, appoint an examiner, and cure the defect prospectively.
**Ask the question instead and let them answer it.** RFMI response **Part 8** already asks precisely:
*"what decision is meant by 'a decision regarding your ability to perform your role', and the
instrument under which it would be made"* — and **Part 6** asks for the delegate and the source of
the delegation.

⭐ **That question is a fork with no good exit:**
- Answer **"PS Act s 107"** → s 103's entry test and s 104's chief-executive requirement bite, and
  the exclusion still has no home in the division.
- Answer **"WHS Act s 19"** → a duty has been cited as a power, and reg 36 has no removal step.
- Answer **nothing** → five weeks becomes six, against cl 1.11.5 and the measured response pattern.

---

# PART 5 — ⭐ THE HEALTH-MONITORING PINCER
MSH's best available answer on s 19 is **s 19(3)(g)** — *"that the health of workers and the
conditions at the workplace are monitored"*. It is the one limb that mentions monitoring health, and
it is the natural home for a Request for Medical Information.

**Both roads out of it close:**

**Road 1 — "the RFMI is health monitoring under s 19(3)(g)."**
Then **s 49(e)(iii)** applies: consultation *"is required"* *"when making decisions about the
procedures for— … **(iii) monitoring the health of workers**"*. ⛔ **There was none.** And s 48
requires that he be given a reasonable opportunity to contribute to the decision-making process and
that he be advised of the outcome.
⭐ **This is already in the RFMI response, at Part 7**, in exactly these terms: *"Section 49 requires
consultation … when making decisions about the procedures for monitoring the health of workers. The
present request is a procedure for monitoring my health."* **The trap is already set and already
served.**

**Road 2 — "the RFMI is not health monitoring."**
Then **s 19 does not support the request at all**, and the authority question at Part 8 is
unanswered.

⚠️ **A third feature of (g) worth noticing but never pressing:** the limb is directed at monitoring
*"for the purpose of preventing illness or injury of workers **arising from the conduct of the
business or undertaking**."* ⛔ **Do not go near this in the employment track.** It brushes against
causation, which is in issue in the appeal, and the discipline is that the two tracks stay apart.
**Noted here only so it is not walked into by accident.**

---

# PART 6 — HOW THIS IS DEPLOYED
| Where | What it does |
|---|---|
| ⛔ **Not in a letter as argument** | Arguing it invites them to fix it while there is still time |
| ✅ **RFMI response Part 8** | Asks what the decision is and under what instrument — already served |
| ✅ **RFMI response Part 6** | Asks for the delegate and the source of the delegation — already served |
| ✅ **RFMI response Part 7** | Records that the request **is** a procedure for monitoring health, and cites s 49 — already served |
| ✅ **Stage 1 notice §3** | If they run the cl 1.11.4 *"genuine safety issue"* carve-out, asks for the hazard, the **reg 36 order of consideration**, and why the ECC restrictions do not address it |
| ⭐ **Union brief (Petering)** | **This whole file.** Parts 2 and 4 are the industrial officer's material, not MSH's |
| ⭐ **Held in reserve** | For the reply, once they have committed to an instrument in writing |

---

# PART 7 — THE ONE-LINE VERSION
**Section 19 tells the Health Service what it must do to its workplace, its plant, its systems of
work, its facilities, its information and its supervision. It says nothing about what a worker must
prove before he is allowed through the door. It is a duty owed to him, and it has been cited as
authority against him.**

>>> skill/references/bench-notes-reception.md :: text
# Bench Notes — how the Commission would annotate the Form 29, the MSH response, and the 64G

**Purpose:** a realistic judicial-reception model. Written as Commissioner Dwyer's
working annotations — neutral, close-reading, noting BOTH sides' problems. This is
how the materials likely LAND on the decision-maker. Reserve/strategy; not a filing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## I. BENCH NOTE — on the Notice (Form 29 + Continuation Schedule)

- *Overall:* unusually well-particularised for a self-represented appellant. The
  Continuation Schedule states the matter in issue and cross-refers each category
  to the pleaded Form 9A — **r 64C(1) satisfied, and conspicuously so.** Note the
  phrase-lexicon (Item 3): a server-side filter bounded by named phrase-families —
  this is a *structured search*, not a trawl. Marks against any "fishing"
  characterisation before MSH even raises it.
- *Caution to self:* the Schedule is dense and the pleaded conduct includes
  serious personal allegations (PID, "fraud", reprisal). **Watch for collateral
  purpose** — but note the Notice itself is framed around records of operational
  fact, not the accusations. Keep the two separate when assessing relevance.
- *Breadth:* some windows are wide (Items 8/9, 1 Dec 2023–30 Jun 2024). Query
  whether the full window is necessary or whether a floor (the admitted 17–18 Mar
  shifts) suffices. A candidate for *variation*, not refusal.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## II. BENCH NOTES — on MSH's response, item by item

**Items 1–2 (SPOK):** non-existence conceded (system upgrade); MET spreadsheet
offered. → *No contest. Produce the MET spreadsheet by consent. Note the search
was DONE — "do not exist" is an answer on oath waiting to happen.*

**Item 3(a)/(b) (complaints / mgmt discussion):** objection — expense (64E(4)(a)).
→ *MSH's own answer ("all such complaints made directly to the Line Manager by
email") IDENTIFIES the custodian and the medium. That supports a confined,
single-custodian search, not the seven-month multi-account exercise the objection
describes. Expense met by confinement + r 64I. Particularity already cured by the
phrase-filter. Inclined to OVERRULE, on the narrowed terms.*

**Item 3(c) (consequential SOP changes):** "do not exist — no consequential
changes." → *Note: the ABSENCE of any procedural change in the face of repeated
operational-error complaints is itself relevant to the manner of management
action. Non-existence to be VERIFIED, not merely asserted.*

**Items 4, 5, 7 (FRMS):** cannot comply — "Switchboard non-clinical, no mandatory
FRMS"; assessment "implemented after 30 June 2024." → *This is a significant
ADMISSION. The Respondent's defence is reasonable management action; the
non-party concedes no fatigue-management framework governed the Switchboard at
the material time. Whether that classification was itself reasonable is a hearing
question — but the concession is now fixed. Verify by affidavit.*

**Item 6:** produced. → *No contest.*

**Item 8 (sign-in records):** objection — expense + particularity. → *Particularity
has SOME force (which system — AD, Entra, Citrix?); cured by the Appellant's
re-specification to a single named account/system. The expense passage, however,
reproduces the email-search wording ("review individual staff member email
accounts") — inapposite to a directory sign-in export, which is a date-range query
against existing audit records. Note the differential: MSH says "do not exist" for
seven items but NOT for 8/9 — the records plainly exist and are identified.
Inclined to OVERRULE, subject to a confidentiality regime.*

**Item 9 (access/swipe):** objection — relevance, particularity, effect (b)(c)(f).
→ *MSH's clarification (collocated office, no dedicated swipe) NARROWS rather than
defeats; the Appellant accepts it and re-specifies. Relevance to the pleaded
"erratic presence" (1(a)) is made out. Effect-on-person met by the
Registry-confidential, field-confined regime. Inclined to OVERRULE on conditions.*

**Item 10 (mgmt discussion):** expense. → *As Items 3. Confined to two named
custodians, two months. OVERRULE on narrowed terms.*

**Items 11–16:** largely produced. Item 14 (texts): explained — personal device,
not QH-issued; "device issued ~Q3 2024." → *Reasonable explanation; appropriate
to VERIFY (device-issue date) by affidavit. Item 16: produced, but query the PRN
reconciliation (two PRNs in the Notice not in the produced report) — verify.*

**Item 17 (comparator payroll):** objection — privacy (64E(4)(e)). → *Genuine.
Small team, re-identification risk. The Appellant does NOT press it. No order
needed. Note the restraint.*

**Item 18 (comms book / destruction):** objection — irrelevance; "destruction
appears already conceded on the pleadings." → *If conceded, production is
unnecessary. The Appellant accepts, subject to confirmation. No order; confirm in
the affidavit.*

**Item 19 (union correspondence):** objection — expense + effect; **but MSH
PROPOSES** narrowing to 17–18 Mar, LM/Director/HR recipients. → *The non-party has
itself supplied the cure. Make the order in MSH's OWN proposed terms. Effect on
Together Queensland (affected party) met by the 7-day-notice + liberty-to-apply
mechanism the Appellant offers.*

**Item 20 (response to PID disclosures):** "do not exist — PID ref commenced Nov
2024, outside the 13–31 May window." → *The reference-number point is technical:
the Appellant seeks the SUBJECT MATTER (the operational/HR response to the May
disclosures), re-specified by subject not by reference number. The technicality
does not answer the request as re-specified. Verify any maintained non-existence,
having regard to the contemporaneous correspondence.*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## III. BENCH NOTE — on the 64G application and disposition

- *Posture:* the application is restrained and procedural. The Appellant has
  CONCEDED or not pressed Items 12(bal), 17, 18 — and adopted MSH's own narrowing
  on 19. **The concessions certify the necessity of what remains.** This is an
  applicant asking for less than the Notice, not more. Disposition is
  straightforward.
- *The contested core (3(a), 3(b), 8, 9, 10, 19, 20):* records that exist or whose
  existence is the very thing to be verified; held only by the non-party; directly
  relevant to pleaded, contested facts (erratic presence; the manner of management
  action; the response to operational-error complaints). Expense met by
  confinement + r 64I. Privacy met by withdrawal + the Items 8/9 regime.
- *Natural disposition — a Bunney-style PARTIAL PRODUCTION ORDER:* overrule the
  objections to the confined items; order production in 14 days; impose the
  confidentiality regime on 8/9; Item 19 in MSH's proposed terms with TQ notice;
  and — *the engine* — a **verification affidavit by an officer with direct
  knowledge** for the non-existence answers (1–2, 3(c), 4, 5, 7, 14, 20). Each
  party its own costs (r 64G(3)).
- *Why the affidavit:* the "do not exist" answers are presently statements in
  correspondence. They bear on the appeal; some (Items 4/5/7) are concessions the
  Appellant will rely on. They should be on oath. This is conventional and
  proportionate — and the non-party can hardly object to verifying its own answers.
- *Caution preserved:* the personal/fraud/reprisal material is NOT engaged by the
  application. Were it pressed, different considerations (collateral purpose) would
  arise. It is not. Note and move on.
- *Likely outcome:* substantially GRANT, in or near the terms of the draft order.
  The Regulator is likely to abide. MSH concedes the core or fights only the
  windows. The draft order is in a form the Commission can adopt with minimal
  amendment — which is itself why it will be.

**One-line bench summary:** *A well-particularised, self-narrowed notice; objections
that are partly concessions, partly privacy (accommodated), partly expense (met by
confinement); records that exist or must be verified; disposition = partial
production order plus verification affidavit, own costs. Grantable as drafted.*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## IV. THE MANAGER'S PRIVACY — how it is cured, and where retribution is foreclosed

The Line Manager is (a) the person whose Items 8/9/3/10 records are sought, AND
(b) the person the PID named. So the Commission is acutely alert to whether the
disclosure is retribution-by-other-means. The application cures it FOUR ways, all
concrete and on the face of the documents:

1. **Field-confinement (the core cure) — draft order ¶4(d):** records produced in
   answer to Items 8/9 are "confined to credential, date and time-stamp fields,
   with non-responsive personal information redacted." → This **de-personalises**
   her record into an objective presence/absence time-series. The application does
   not want anything *private* about her — not content, not reasons, not conduct —
   only "did the credential register, when." Her attendance becomes data points,
   not a dossier.
2. **The protective regime — order ¶4(a)–(c):** Registry-marked "Confidential";
   inspected only by parties/representatives; used only for this proceeding. → No
   publication, no leverage, no life beyond the appeal. The records cannot be
   weaponised against her elsewhere.
3. **Anchoring to a PLEADED FACT, not the person (Annexure B / Section D5):**
   Items 8/9 go ONLY to the pleaded "erratic physical presence" (Stressor 1(a))
   and the "roster was equitable" denial (Form 24 ¶39). The application states
   **"No broader use is made of these Items."** The records measure a SYSTEM fact
   (was the supervisor present) against a contested pleading — not her character,
   integrity, or the fraud suspicion.
4. **The withdrawals (the anti-retribution SIGNAL):** the Appellant does NOT press
   the items that would expose the manager/comparators personally — Item 17
   (comparator payroll), Item 12-balance (comparator leave evidence). A retributive
   applicant presses those hardest; the Appellant drops them.

**Where retribution is foreclosed — the structural proof:**
- The 64G never mentions the fraud, never characterises her conduct, never seeks a
  record to prove she did anything *wrong* personally. It seeks PRESENCE and the
  OPERATIONAL response. The instrument does not pursue her.
- The MINIMALISM is itself the proof: the narrower and more de-personalised the
  request, the more plainly it seeks the fact, not the person. You do not field-
  confine and redact and seal records you intend to use as retribution — you
  field-confine precisely to show you want only the metadata of presence.
- **Critical corollary:** the cure stays robust ONLY because the fraud is kept
  OUT of the 64G. The moment the application touched the fraud/conduct, the
  "retribution-by-disclosure" framing would revive and the privacy cure would look
  pretextual. Discipline rules 1–2 are what make the privacy cure credible.

**Double function:** curing her privacy and proving the Appellant is not
retributive are THE SAME ACT. Field-confinement protects her AND demonstrates the
seeker wants a system fact, not revenge. The cure is the character reference.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## V. THE OBJECTION PATTERN — what MSH resisted vs produced (a TELL, held in reserve)

**The pattern (objective, on the record):**
- **PRODUCED readily:** Items 6, 11, 12(part), 13, 15, 16 — the neutral admin
  records (leave forms, payroll, role description, directives). Nothing adverse.
- **OBJECTED / resisted:** Items 3 (complaints + phrase-lexicon), 10 (directives),
  8 & 9 (manager presence), 19 (Together/union suppression) — i.e. **exactly the
  items that prove the operational dysfunction, the supervisory vacuum, and the
  suppression.** And the "do not exist" answers cluster on the items whose absence
  is itself damaging (3(c) no SOP change; 4/5/7 no FRMS).

So MSH produced the neutral and resisted the probative. The **differential tell**
is the hardest objective evidence: MSH never said "not retained" for 8/9 (the
records exist and are identified), and it objected — rather than denied existence
— on the dysfunction items.

**FACT vs INFERENCE (discipline):**
- FACT: the objections cluster on the probative items; the productions are neutral.
- INFERENCE (Cory): "they resisted because they know what it would show." PLAUSIBLE
  — and consistent with the "ferocity = the unproven fact still feared" tell
  (working-theories §5: how hard Item 9 is fought measures how much the absence is
  feared). BUT it is a motive inference, NOT provable fact. The expense grounds have
  a colourable basis (email-account searches are work). **Do not assert
  concealment** — that revives the conspiracy framing (rule 1) and is discounted
  argument (rule 5).

**How it deploys (reserve only):**
1. Let the Commission DISCOVER the pattern — a party that produces the neutral and
   resists the probative tells the bench where the evidence lies. Discovered, not
   stated.
2. The **verification affidavit (order 6) is the lever:** it forces produce-or-swear
   on exactly the items MSH least wants to produce. They cannot resist on "expense"
   AND maintain "does not exist" — the affidavit collapses the evasion into a sworn
   choice.
3. The resistance pattern CONFIRMS the spine: MSH fights hardest at the vacuum
   (8/9) and the dysfunction (3/10) — which is where the case's strength is. Useful
   confirmation; never an argument.

**Item 19 (union/suppression) caveat:** real, but it sits in the SECONDARY grievance
strand (Stressor 1(g)), not the clean spine. MSH's "proposed narrowing" to 17–18 Mar
is itself content-management (confines the suppression evidence to the keystone
window). Take the production, but do NOT elevate suppression to the spine — it
carries the vexatious-framing risk. The vacuum + dysfunction items are the prize.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
## VI. ITEM 20 EXPOSED — the failure loop it closes (Cory, 13 Jun)

**The two routings (the asymmetry Cory identifies):**
- **Operational complaints went THROUGH the manager** — Item 3: MSH's own answer
  says "all employee complaints relating to Switchboard operational errors are
  made directly to the Line Manager." Her mailbox is the convergence point.
- **The disclosure ABOUT the manager was routed AROUND her** — Item 20 / the
  McGinley chain: when Cory escalated (13–15 May), the response went to ESU / HR /
  the Director, at arm's length from her. Handled as a conduct/HR matter, kept at
  a distance from the manager herself.

**The failure LOOP this closes (the documents interlock):**
1. **Item 3** — complaints flow IN to the manager's mailbox (admitted by MSH).
2. **Item 3(c)** — "no consequential changes" — nothing comes OUT. No SOP change,
   no fix. The manager's mailbox is where complaints went to die.
3. **Items 8/9** — the manager was ABSENT (the vacuum) — which is WHY nothing came
   out: no one was there to act on what came in.
4. **Item 20** — when Cory escalated past the black hole, the response was
   DEFLECTION (routed to HR/ESU as conduct) + REPRISAL (the 48-hour retraction) +
   NO safety assessment. Not a fix — a deflection.

So Item 3 + 3(c) + 8/9 + 20 together prove: **a system fed all its failures into
one absent manager, nothing was done, and when someone escalated, the institution
deflected and reprised rather than fix it.** That is the vacuum, proven end to end.

**What exposing Item 20 BREAKS OPEN:**
- **MSH's "does not exist" collapses** — the McGinley routing (and MSH's OWN July
  2025 production of it) proves the Item 20 response existed. The technical
  reference-number answer is shown false. Credibility hit + verification-affidavit
  exposure (order 6).
- **The institutional-response failure becomes documentary** — a safety-grounded
  disclosure answered by deflection, with no safety assessment. The "every channel
  closed" manner limb, proven.
- **The seam opens** — the McGinley page came via conferencing; the Regulator held
  it; the cross-defendant contradiction is live.
- **It links to the spine** — Item 20 deflection is the institutional mirror of
  the supervisory vacuum: the same absence of functioning management that ignored
  the complaints (Item 3/3(c)) also could not respond to the escalation (Item 20).

**DISCIPLINE (critical):** Item 20 sits in the institutional-response strand —
it supports the MANNER/SEVERITY limb, NOT the spine, and it is FRAUD-ADJACENT (the
PID response). Deploy it as GOVERNANCE/DEAFNESS — "the response to my safety
concern was deflection with no safety assessment." NEVER as
"they protected the fraudster manager and reprised me" (the grievance/conspiracy
frame that revives the vexatious attack). The loop is proven through the
governance lens; the reprisal/fraud stays on the parallel track.

## VII. THE APPEAL OFFICER'S THREE READS OF THE 64G (Matheson — distinct from MSH)

KEY DIFFERENCE FROM MSH: the 64G targets MSH's objection (K-LM26/729). The
Regulator is the RESPONDENT to the appeal but a relative BYSTANDER to the
appellant-v-non-party disclosure dispute. Matheson is NOT the one resisting
production — MSH is. So her reading is structurally different: she can ABIDE.

### READ 1 — the procedural / duty pass (the model-litigant officer)
Notices: filed in time (day 7); proper 64G(1); restrained, particularised,
self-narrowed, concedes items; strikingly professional for a self-rep; **does NOT
attack the Regulator or her conduct** — aimed at MSH records. Assessment:
procedurally proper, grantable; the Regulator's role is to abide/assist the
Commission, not resist (resistance is MSH's). Posture: **ABIDE** (possibly support
— the Regulator benefits from the records on the s 32(5)(a) question too).

### READ 2 — the substantive / merits pass (liability assessor, advised by Willson)
Notices: Schedule A + Annexure B target the governance/fatigue vacuum, manager
presence, dysfunction, institutional response — the STRONG part of the appeal;
production converts assertion → documentary fact; order 6 affidavit forces MSH
onto oath on the non-existence answers (incl. Item 20, which the Regulator's own
disclosure/2025 production contradicts); with Willson's WHS expertise, the fatigue
case is technically valid and the "non-clinical" concession dangerous. Assessment:
**the appeal is strong and STRENGTHENING; liability exposure real and rising.**
Posture: drives the liability assessment UP and toward **SETTLEMENT** (a heard
decision produces adverse findings; settlement avoids them).

### READ 3 — the personal / positional pass (given Issue 4712 + the careful 11 June disclosure)
Notices: the 64G does NOT touch her conduct or the reprisal — it is CLEAN,
disciplined, aimed at MSH operational records (**relief: the appellant kept the WC
track separate from the personal complaint against her**); BUT the order 6
affidavit + trajectory put the seam (the Regulator's held documents, the 11 June
disclosure, the Item 20 contradiction) adjacent; the appellant is FORENSIC
(extracted McGinley in 24h) AND DISCIPLINED (the clean 64G) — capable + restrained;
her own exposure (Issue 4712) is best managed by continued duty-compliant conduct
AND by the matter resolving. Assessment: professionally formidable appellant who
has kept the personal stuff off the WC track — mutually beneficial. Posture:
cooperative-but-careful; **settlement-oriented** (resolution settles the appeal AND
reduces Issue 4712's salience); relieved the 64G is clean.

### COMPOSITE VIEW
Across all three: a STRONG, STRENGTHENING appeal advanced by a forensic-but-
disciplined self-rep, via a procedurally impeccable 64G she should ABIDE not
resist, in a matter heading toward SETTLEMENT — and in which the appellant has,
despite a personal complaint against her, kept the WC track CLEAN, which she reads
as both professional and prudent for everyone.

**STRATEGIC PAYOFF:** this is WHY the clean 64G + the index email work. Matheson
reads the 64G and sees (a) nothing to oppose, (b) a strong appeal, (c) no attack
on her → she abides, rates liability as real, moves toward settlement. The
DISCIPLINE (clean WC track) is precisely what makes her view favourable to
resolution. The reprisal/fraud bleeding in would flip Read 3 from "relief" to
"defend" — and harden the whole posture.

>>> skill/references/case-law-and-directions.md :: text
# Case-Law Integration & Direction Stress-Test — WC/2024/227

**Scope & discipline.** This maps WC/2024/227 onto the governing authorities and
stress-tests each legal direction the case can run. It is **hearing / strategy
material** — the Rule 64G application is deliberately case-law-free (Cory's
instruction) and is **not** affected by anything here. Authorities verified
against public sources 13 Jun 2026; citations not to be asserted as fact in any
filing without pinpoint confirmation against the report itself.

---

## 1. The legal battleground: global (Delaney) vs single-stressor (Mahaffey/Carr)

This is the decisive fork in the appeal, and the Review Decision already chose
the side adverse to Cory.

- **Review Decision 69983 (24 Oct 2024)** applied **Delaney v Q-COMP** — a
  *global* evaluation of management action: it found factors 2–3 reasonable,
  factor 4 (the 17–18 March rostering) **unreasonable**, then reasoned that
  because 2 of 3 causative factors were reasonable, the injury "mainly arose
  out of" reasonable management action → s 32(5) enlivened → claim rejected.
- **The de novo appeal frees Dwyer from that reasoning.** On a hearing de novo
  (*Davis v Blackwood* [2014] ICQ 009) the Commission determines the question
  afresh; the review officer's global approach is not binding.
- **The counter-authorities run the other way:**
  - **Workers' Compensation Regulator v Mahaffey [2016] ICQ 10** (Industrial
    Court — higher authority than a QIRC single member): a **single**
    unreasonable management action can suffice; the s 32(5) exclusion does not
    automatically apply merely because most stressors were reasonable.
  - **Carr v Workers' Compensation Regulator [2022] QIRC 059**: of nine
    nominated stressors only one (excessive workload without support) was
    unreasonable — the appeal **succeeded**. The Commission assessed each
    stressor **individually**, not globally.

**Stress-test of the direction:** Cory's strongest position is that the
**admitted, already-found-unreasonable 7-hour break** (Form 24 ¶1 admitted;
Review Decision found factor 4 unreasonable) is, on *Mahaffey/Carr*, capable of
sustaining the claim by itself. The Regulator's defence depends on *Delaney*
global dilution. **The contest is global-vs-individual, and Cory has Industrial
Court authority (Mahaffey > a QIRC review officer) on the individual side.**
Weakness to shore up: *Mahaffey* still requires the unreasonable stressor to be
a **significant** contributor to the injury — which is a *medical-causation*
question (Hawes/Krishnaiah), so the medical case must tie the injury to the
fatigue/rostering strand, not only to the cumulative conduct.

## 2. Onus — Davis v Blackwood [2014] ICQ 009

Appellant bears the onus on the de novo appeal, including excluding s 32(5)(a).
**Stress-test:** this is a burden, but the 64G converts it into the *necessity*
argument — a party who must disprove reasonableness cannot be denied the records
of the conduct, held solely by its author. The onus is why disclosure is
necessary, not merely useful. (Already the spine of the application's Section D.)

## 3. Disclosure authorities (reserve — NOT cited in the no-case-law 64G)

- **Robson v REB Engineering [1997] 2 Qd R 102** — "directly relevant" = tends
  to prove or disprove an allegation in issue (the narrower standard, not
  train-of-inquiry). The 64G states this as rule-text only.
- **Bunney v Workers' Compensation Regulator [2020] QIRC 210** — applied
  Subdivision 7A to a Form 29 objection; made a **partial-production order**
  within 14 days, upheld privilege only on genuine sub-categories, each party's
  own costs. The model for the order sought. Held in reserve as the template.

**Stress-test:** if the Regulator/MSH cite *Bunney* to argue for narrowing,
that *helps* Cory — Schedule A already self-narrows below the Notice, so a
*Bunney*-style partial order is the floor, not the ceiling, of what's sought.

## 4. Prizeman v Q-Comp [2005] QIC 53 (in repo)

In repo as reference. Confirm its precise holding before any reliance — likely
relevant to the reasonable-management-action characterisation or causation.
**Do not cite from memory.**

---

## 5. The patient-safety / PID strand — a NEW evidentiary direction

**The hypothesis (Cory, 13 Jun):** the 13 May 2024 PID complaint was
**safety-grounded** — its closing line: *"The employee is now making decisions
that directly affect service delivery and patient outcomes."* It alleged the
Line Manager worked unsupervised, was absent, failed to log on/off, and
neglected duties. If, when that disclosure was routed (McGinley email, 16 May),
MSH conducted **no patient-safety assessment and made no safety notes** — i.e.
treated a *patient-safety* disclosure purely as an HR/conduct/PID matter — that
is a distinct institutional-response failure, and may be why Matheson disclosed
the McGinley page.

**What is fact vs inference:**
- FACT: the PID was safety-grounded (patient-outcomes wording, on the form).
- FACT: the McGinley 16 May email routed it through **Human Resources**
  (McGinley = A/Senior Consultant HR) and to ESU — a conduct/HR channel.
- INFERENCE (untested): that **no** patient-safety assessment was done. The
  McGinley email shows HR routing; it does not by itself prove the absence of a
  safety assessment elsewhere.
- SPECULATION (several steps out): that Matheson disclosed *because* it shows
  the absence. Plausible but unprovable on current material.

**Why this matters to the appeal (the real payoff):** it feeds the s 32(1)
causation spine and Stressor 1 (cumulative institutional response). A
patient-safety disclosure answered only as an HR/conduct matter, with no safety
assessment, is exactly the "every channel closed; raising concerns made Cory the
problem" pattern. It also sharpens **Item 20**: the application already seeks
"operational or human-resources action … in response to the disclosures." If
production shows **HR/conduct routing but no patient-safety assessment**, the
absence is itself probative — and the **order 6 verification affidavit** would
force MSH to state what safety assessment (if any) was undertaken.

**Stress-test of this direction:**
- *For Cory:* if no safety assessment exists, it converts his "inadequate
  institutional response" theory from assertion to documentary fact, and ties
  the reprisal/PID strand to a concrete governance failure with patient-safety
  weight (which a WHS-specialist counsel — Willson — will recognise as serious).
- *Against:* (1) the absence of a record is hard to prove except via the
  verification affidavit; (2) the PID's *content* names "fraud" — the
  collateral-purpose grenade — so this strand lives in the PID/reprisal track
  and evidence-in-chief, **never the 64G prose** (discipline rules 1–2); (3)
  causation: a safety-assessment failure must still be tied to *Cory's* injury,
  not only to abstract patient risk.

**Could it be why Renee gave the email?** Honest answer: it's one plausible
strand among the §3 motive set, not a distinct better explanation. The simpler
read remains — she disclosed to discharge her continuing duty / protect her
position before the 64G. But your strand adds a layer: the McGinley page is the
document that shows the *routing* of a safety disclosure into an HR/conduct
channel — and that is adverse to MSH on exactly the point your case needs.
Whether she saw that significance or simply disclosed what conferencing gave her
cannot be resolved from the metadata. **Treat as a lead for the Item 20
production + verification affidavit, not as a finding.**

## 6. Direction stress-test summary — where each runs and where it's weak

| Direction | Authority | Strength | Weakness to shore up |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single admitted unreasonable stressor suffices | Mahaffey (ICQ), Carr (QIRC) | High — ICQ authority, stressor admitted + already found unreasonable | Must show it was a *significant* contributor (medical case) |
| De novo defeats the review officer's Delaney global approach | Davis v Blackwood | High | Regulator re-runs Delaney; needs the individual-assessment framing held firm |
| Records necessary because onus is Cory's | Davis v Blackwood | High (drives the 64G) | none material |
| Partial production proper | Bunney | High | n/a — Schedule A already self-narrows |
| Patient-safety disclosure mishandled (no assessment) | (evidentiary, not yet authority-backed) | Medium, contingent on production | Proof of absence needs the affidavit; keep "fraud" out of WC track |
| Reprisal / s 40–42 PID tort | parallel track | n/a here | Sequenced BEHIND WC settlement (rule 8); already partly fired (Issue 4712) — do not add |

**Bottom line:** the appeal's centre of gravity is **Mahaffey/Carr individual
assessment of the admitted 7-hour break**, fed by a medical case tying that
stressor to the injury, with the patient-safety/PID failure as a corroborating
institutional-response strand surfaced through Item 20 + the verification
affidavit. The 64G is the instrument that produces the records all of this needs.
Nothing here changes the lodged application.

## 7. The "no safety assessment" affidavit scenario — strength + the trap (13 Jun)

**Premise (Cory):** order 6 affidavit confirms no patient-safety assessment / no safety notes were made in response to the 13 May PID; they cannot manufacture a contemporaneous record that does not exist.

**Sound premise — but expect characterisation, not fabrication.** An officer will not swear false; a contemporaneous record cannot be back-dated without detection. BUT the affidavit's WORDING will be chosen as carefully as the 11 June disclosure was. Expect a technically-true reframing, e.g. "the matter was assessed by ESU as a [conduct/PID] complaint" — which converts "no safety assessment" into "assessed through a different channel." The absence is the fact; its CHARACTER is the fight.

**Layered case strength:**
- **Layer 1 (already strong, independent of this):** the admitted 7-hour break, already found unreasonable by the Review Officer, sufficient alone under *Mahaffey*/*Carr*. This is the spine and it does NOT need the safety-assessment finding.
- **Layer 2 (what the finding adds):** corroborates Stressor 1 (cumulative institutional response) — a safety-grounded disclosure handled as conduct-only, no safety assessment = "every channel closed" proven on paper. Makes the *global-reasonableness* defence harder and the *manner/severity* case stronger.
- **Layer 3:** every adverse sworn fact raises the cost of a heard decision (portable findings) vs settlement → leverage.

**What they CAN still do (even unable to manufacture):**
1. Characterise the absence as reasonable ("no formal safety assessment was required; handled appropriately via ESU").
2. Sever relevance — argue the PID-response is the reprisal track, not the s 32(5)(a) reasonableness of the *rostering* action.
3. Contest causation — poor institutional response ≠ significant contributor to the injury vs the admitted stressors.
4. **THE TRAP:** the safety strand is welded to a PID that names "fraud" against Chloe Taylor. Leaning on the PID invites the **collateral-purpose / vexatious framing** — recasting Cory's disclosures as a personal campaign, not protected disclosures. This is the single biggest risk in pulling this thread, and it is why discipline rules 1–2 quarantine "fraud" from the WC track.

**Net:** the case is ALREADY strong on Layer 1 alone (admitted + found-unreasonable single stressor + ICQ authority). The no-safety-assessment finding is a **force multiplier on severity + settlement value, not a silver bullet** — and it must be deployed via the clean institutional-response/governance angle (FRMS/patient-safety), NEVER via the fraud allegation. Strength with the finding: materially raises an already-strong position and pushes settlement value up; does not change that medical causation (injury ↔ the stressors) remains the one element Cory must still prove independently.


---

## 8. THE STRONGEST POINT — the FRMS vacuum is already HALF-CONCEDED in writing (13 Jun)

**MSH's 5 June letter already admits, in writing, that no fatigue-management framework governed the Switchboard before the injury:**
- Items 4 & 7: "Mandatory Fatigue Risk Management System training only applies to health practitioners and clinical assistants. The Logan Hospital Switchboard staff are **non-clinical staff**, and therefore there is no mandatory requirement … to complete [FRMS] training."
- Item 5: "The implementation of fatigue risk management assessment at Switchboard Logan Hospital occurred **after 30 June 2024**."

**Onset was 18 June 2024.** So MSH has conceded on its own letterhead that there was **no FRMS training, assessment, or framework applying to the Switchboard at the time of the admitted 7-hour break** — the assessment was implemented only *after* the injury. This does not need the verification affidavit; it is already documentary. **Order 6(b) is purpose-built to convert it to sworn evidence** ("whether the searches identified any fatigue-management training requirement, assessment process or other requirement applying to Logan Hospital Switchboard staff before 30 June 2024").

**BUT — MSH's escape hatch is the same sentence: "non-clinical."** Their concession is framed as a *defence*: FRMS did not apply because Switchboard is non-clinical, so there was no breach of any framework. **The real contest is not whether a safety assessment was done (it wasn't) — it is whether life-safety emergency-code coordination (Code Blue / MET) should have been INSIDE the fatigue framework.** That is the battleground, and it is where Willson (WHS specialist) will fight. Cory's answer: the *nature of the work* (coordinating clinical emergencies) and the *Neville* governance rationale make the "non-clinical" classification itself the governance failure — you cannot exempt the people who coordinate Code Blues from fatigue management on a clerical label.

**"Does the Form 29 look like the assessment they never did?" — YES, and it is closing-submission gold (contingent on production).** The continuation schedule IS a structured fatigue-risk analysis: the 16h-wakefulness / 4h-commute / 4h-sleep arithmetic, the FRMS control framework, the Neville governance anchor, risk categorisation. The framing for closing: *"The only systematic fatigue-risk assessment ever performed in relation to these shifts is the one the injured worker performed himself, after the injury, for this appeal."* Powerful — but it is rhetoric that lands only once production + the affidavit confirm the absence, and only via the clean FRMS/governance angle, never the fraud allegation.

**Calibration of "the hearing writes itself":** the LIABILITY/unreasonableness limb is close to that strong — admitted stressor + admitted FRMS vacuum + Mahaffey single-stressor authority. But two things never "write themselves": (1) the **non-clinical characterisation** fight, and (2) **medical causation** (injury ↔ stressor), which is Cory's to prove via expert evidence regardless of how damning the governance picture is. Strong, even very strong — but won at hearing through the characterisation argument and the medical case, not by the absence alone.

>>> skill/references/case-theory-synthesis.md :: text
# Case Theory Synthesis — what WC/2024/227 is structurally becoming, and how to plead it

**Status:** hearing/strategy capstone. Pulls together the 9A, the admissions,
the MSH letter, the disclosure, and the metadata. The lodged 64G is unaffected.
Verified facts cited to source; inference flagged.

---

## 1. What MSH gave away by answering item-by-item

MSH addressed all 20 Notice items individually (Items 1–2 together, 3–20 each).
That granularity is a gift: each answer is a fixed position. The load-bearing
ones:
- **Items 4, 5, 7 (CONCEDED in writing):** no mandatory FRMS training applied to
  Switchboard ("non-clinical staff"); FRMS assessment implemented only **after
  30 June 2024**. Onset was 18 June 2024. → **the employer admits it ran the
  Switchboard with no fatigue-management framework at the time of the injury.**
- **Items 1–2:** SPOK records "do not exist" (system upgrade) — but the MET-call
  spreadsheet for 17–18 March is available.
- **Item 20:** "does not exist" on a reference-number technicality — contradicted
  by MSH's OWN July 2025 production (the routing correspondence was already
  disclosed to the Regulator).
- **Items 8, 9:** objected on expense/particularity — the records exist (the
  differential tell).

## 2. The 9A as filed — a three-stressor GRIEVANCE catalogue

The Amended 9A (8 Apr 2026) pleads 13 particulars across 3 stressors:
- **Stressor 1 (hostile course):** (a) Dereliction of Clinical Governance,
  (b) Unilateral Destruction of WHS Records, (c) Refusal to Investigate WHS &
  Fatigue Complaints, (d) Disparate Leave Treatment, **(e) PID**, **(f) Immediate
  Reprisal**, **(g) Suppression of Industrial Representation**.
- **Stressor 2 (remuneration):** (a) Persistent Payroll Failures, (b) Unreasonable Delay.
- **Stressor 3 (fatigue):** (a) Mathematical Reality of the WHS Breach,
  (b) Flagrant Bypass of the Neville Mandate, (c) Unjustified Administrative
  Detriment, (d) Admitted Unreasonableness.
- Plus the legal argument already pleaded: Exclusion Fails Entirely; Global
  Evaluation (Delaney) vs **Single Unreasonable Stressor (Mahaffey)**.

This is how self-reps plead: everything that happened, equally weighted. It is
comprehensive but structurally diffuse.

## 3. What it is STRUCTURALLY TURNING INTO — a governance-vacuum case

The evidence has concentrated the case around a new centre of gravity. The
emerging core proposition:

> *The employer operated a life-safety clinical-coordination function (Code Blue
> / MET) entirely OUTSIDE the fatigue-management framework — by its own
> admission no FRMS applied to the Switchboard until after the injury — rostered
> an admitted, award-breaching, already-found-unreasonable 7-hour break within
> that vacuum, and when the worker raised the safety concern through every
> available channel, closed each one.*

Why this structure is far stronger than the catalogue:
1. **Anchored in admitted + conceded facts** — the 7-hour break (Form 24 ¶1),
   the award minimum (¶3), the Review Officer's unreasonableness finding, and
   the FRMS vacuum (MSH letter Items 4/5/7). Little of the spine needs to be
   *proved*; it is already on the record.
2. **Defeats Delaney dilution** — it is not "nine things, one bad"; it is ONE
   systemic governance failure with manifestations. Global evaluation has
   nothing to dilute against a single coherent failure.
3. **Converts the "non-clinical" defence into the negligence** — you cannot
   exempt the people who coordinate clinical emergencies from fatigue management
   on a clerical label and then call the resulting breach "reasonable."
4. **It is CLEAN** — about systems and classifications, not personalities. No
   villain, no fraud, no reprisal required to win it.

## 4. The structural problem — the case has two personalities

The 9A welds two incompatible cases together:
- **The CLEAN case (wins):** governance vacuum + admitted unreasonable roster +
  the safety concern raised and dismissed. Stressor 3; the fatigue/safety angle
  of 1(a) and 1(c); the manner limb of 2. Pure WHS/governance.
- **The GRIEVANCE/ADVERSARIAL case (vulnerable):** the PID (1(e)), the reprisal
  (1(f)), the suppression (1(g)), the fraud allegation embedded in the PID, the
  "destruction of WHS records" (1(b)). Personal, accusatory — vexatious-framing
  bait.

**The danger is contamination:** the Regulator (via WHS-specialist Willson) uses
the fraud/reprisal material to frame the WHOLE matter as a personal campaign, so
Dwyer discounts even the strong fatigue case. The reprisal complaint against
Matheson (Issue 4712) already handed them this lever once.

## 5. HOW TO PLEAD IT — the structural move (keystone, not catalogue)

Re-weight around the spine. Do not abandon strands — re-rank them:
- **PRIMARY (the spine):** Stressor 3 — the 7-hour break within the FRMS vacuum.
  Admitted + conceded + Mahaffey-sufficient. This wins the appeal by itself.
- **MANNER + SEVERITY (supporting):** the institutional-response strand — pleaded
  as *"every channel through which I raised the SAFETY concern was closed"* —
  WITHOUT the fraud allegation and WITHOUT the reprisal characterisation. This is
  1(a) clinical governance and 1(c) refusal to investigate fatigue, stripped to
  their safety/governance core.
- **HELD BACK (parallel track):** the PID-content (1(e)), reprisal (1(f)),
  suppression (1(g)). Keep them out of the WC pleading's load-bearing structure.
  The fraud word never appears. Issue 4712 runs on its own track behind the WC
  settlement (discipline rules 1, 2, 8).

**Practical reality on amendment:** the 9A is filed (with leave, 8 Apr); pleadings
are closing. The keystone IS already pleaded (Stressor 3 + the Mahaffey argument
are in it). So the RE-WEIGHTING is deployed not by re-pleading but in:
1. **Evidence-in-chief** — lead with the load profile (Code Blue/MET volume) and
   the fatigue arithmetic; establish the work was life-safety-clinical.
2. **The medical case** — the psychiatrist report (commissioned AFTER production)
   structured to tie the injury to the fatigue/governance failure AND the
   dismissive institutional response — cleanly, without the reprisal frame.
3. **Closing** — frame the whole as the governance vacuum, not the grievance
   catalogue. The "the only fatigue assessment ever done is the one the injured
   worker did himself, for this appeal" line lands here.
4. **If production justifies it,** seek leave for a tightened further-amended 9A
   that elevates Stressor 3 — but only if the records materially add; otherwise
   the re-weighting lives in evidence + closing.

## 6. Stress-test of the pleading structure

| Pleading approach | Upside | Risk | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keep catalogue, all stressors equal (current weighting) | preserves everything | Delaney dilution; vexatious framing; strong point spread thin | **Avoid as the hearing posture** |
| Lead with keystone (vacuum + admitted roster), demote grievance to context, excise fraud | concentrates fire on admitted/conceded ground; defeats global dilution; hard to call vexatious when the lead is admitted | requires discipline to NOT lean on the strongest-feeling but most dangerous (reprisal/PID) material | **RECOMMENDED** |
| Drop the grievance strands entirely | maximally clean | loses severity/cumulative evidence that supports causation | Over-correction — keep them as *context*, not spine |

## 7. The one structural tension to resolve — the medical pathway

The strongest LIABILITY structure is the clean fatigue-vacuum. But the medical
evidence so far (Hawes: mechanism = "ongoing breaking of workplace rules by
bosses, victimizing him") points at the **cumulative-victimisation** pathway —
which pulls toward the grievance case. **These must be reconciled in the
psychiatrist report:** the injury should be opined as caused by the fatigue/
governance failure AND the institutional response to raising it — framed as
*systemic failure and dismissal*, not *personal reprisal*. If the medical case
leans only on "victimisation," it imports the grievance frame and its
vulnerability. Commission the report (post-production) on instructed assumptions
that foreground the governance vacuum and the safety-concern dismissal.

**Bottom line:** the case is structurally becoming a **clean governance-vacuum
appeal** — admitted unreasonable roster inside an admitted fatigue-management
vacuum, with a dismissive institutional response as the manner/severity. Plead
it as keystone-not-catalogue; hold the reprisal/fraud on the parallel track;
reconcile the medical pathway to the governance frame. That structure is hard to
dilute, hard to call vexatious, and largely already admitted.


---

## 8. REFRAME (Cory, 13 Jun) — the SUPERVISORY VACUUM is the spine, not the fatigue framework

**Cory's correction (accepted):** the unifying root of the whole case is **the
Line Manager's chronic physical absence and consequent disruption of the
system.** Every other strand — the 7-hour fatigue break, union suppression, the
Director escalation, paging errors, doctor-contact-detail failures, ward
complaints, directives left unassessed — is a **downstream manifestation of one
root: no one was supervising the function.** Each strand alone is small and
individually defensible; UNIFIED by the manager-absence they become a pattern.
Test: remove the other strands and the absence still carries the case; remove
the absence and each strand is defensible in isolation → the absence is the
load-bearing fact. **This supersedes the "fatigue-framework vacuum" as the
primary spine; the two combine (no supervisor + no framework = total vacuum).**

**Why this is the better spine — the s 32(5)(a) FORK (the key insight):**
the defence is "reasonable management *action* taken in a reasonable *way*."
A chronic supervisory absence puts the Regulator on the horns of a dilemma:
- If the absence was a management *choice* → defend its reasonableness →
  impossible: you cannot reasonably leave a life-safety clinical-coordination
  function (Code Blue/MET) unsupervised. The rostering done in that vacuum
  (the admitted 7-hour break, in the Mon–Fri/weekend roster-seam) is then
  unreasonable *action*.
- If the absence was NOT management action ("just absence, neutral") → then
  s 32(5)(a) does not *exclude* an injury arising from the unsupervised,
  dysfunctional system, because that injury did not arise from *management
  action* at all.
**Either fork defeats the exclusion.** The more the Regulator characterises the
absence as "not action," the more it concedes the injury did not arise from
reasonable management action. This is the structural trap.

**The evidentiary spine is Items 8 & 9** (the sign-in / swipe records) — which
is exactly what MSH fights hardest (the differential tell: never "not retained"
for 8–9). The 64G's most-contested items ARE the proof of the spine. The
roster-seam analysis already connects it: manager works Mon–Fri, the 7-hour
break falls in the weekend/night supervisory vacuum.

**THE DISCIPLINE LINE — own the absence, NOT the motive (critical).**
There are two manager-absence stories and only one is safe:
- **OWN (clean, structural):** "the manager was not present to supervise the
  system, and the attendance records prove it" — an operational FACT from Items
  8/9. No villain; a structural supervision failure.
- **NEVER (the trap):** "the manager was committing fraud / stealing / lazy /
  victimising me" — the PID-content, the character attack, vexatious-bait.
The attendance records prove ABSENCE (clean). They do NOT prove fraud or malice.
"Own it" = own the *vacuum*, never the *motive*. The injury pathway is
"unsupervised dysfunctional system + no one to respond when I raised it," NOT
"she victimised me."

**Causation reconciliation (updates §7 of case-law doc):** the psychiatrist
report should tie the injury to *operating a life-safety function in a
supervisory vacuum, and the failure of an absent management structure to respond
when concerns were raised* — framed as systemic/structural, not personal
victimisation. This keeps the Hawes "victimising" mechanism re-anchored to the
clean vacuum frame.

**Net structural verdict:** the case is a **management-vacuum** appeal — a
chronically absent supervisor running a life-safety function with no fatigue
framework, into which fell the admitted unreasonable roster and the operational
failures, and an absent structure that could not respond when concerns were
raised. Plead the VACUUM as the spine (Items 8/9 the proof), run the s 32(5)(a)
fork, own the absence and never the motive, point the medical case at the
structural failure.

## 9. Two clarifications (Cory, 13 Jun) — one strengthens, one is a trap

### 9.1 "Victimisation" = objective differential detriment (STRENGTHENS causation)
Cory clarifies the Hawes "victimising" mechanism is NOT a vague feeling — it is
concrete, documentable detriment: **pay withheld** (the AVAC/payroll delay,
partly admitted at Form 24 ¶38) and **differential treatment** (the COVID leave
obstruction, 1(d) — the disclosure shows the leave form declined twice; the
"Mode A vs Mode B" disparity). This RE-ANCHORS the medical-causation pathway to
**objective facts**, not subjective perception — much stronger. In the
supervisory-vacuum frame these are downstream too: an absent manager who does not
process pay or handle leave correctly. Use as the SEVERITY/cumulative limb,
anchored to the documents (pay records, leave-form declines). Caveat: the
Regulator will characterise the pay delay ("waiting payroll confirmation") and
leave decline ("policy") as reasonable — contestable, so it supports rather than
carries the case. The SPINE stays the supervisory vacuum + admitted roster.

### 9.2 The fraud escalation — why he used it, and why it STILL can't enter the WC track
Cory explains the "fraud" word in the PID was **the strongest language available
because the patient-safety concerns were never heard** — an escalation forced by
institutional deafness, not a vendetta. This is TRUE, HUMAN, and the coherent
causal sequence: safety concern → not heard / no assessment → escalation to
strongest language → differential detriment → injury.

**But the explanation does NOT immunise the word in the WC track — and explaining
it re-arms the grenade:**
- To justify "why I said fraud," you must foreground the fraud allegation again.
- The Regulator's answer to "I escalated to fraud because I was unheard" is still
  "he made a serious unproven criminal allegation against a named colleague" —
  and "I used the strongest word I could" can be spun as deliberate escalation,
  FEEDING the vexatious frame, not defusing it.

**The refinement (important — the explanation has a HOME, just not this one):**
- **DEPLOY in the WC track:** "I raised patient-safety concerns repeatedly and
  they were not heard." The institution's DEAFNESS is the wrong — it is the
  institutional-response failure, the s 32(5)(a) manner limb, the "every channel
  closed" severity. Point at their failure to hear, never at your escalation.
- **DO NOT deploy in the WC track:** "...so I alleged fraud" / "the fraud was
  justified." The escalation is the SYMPTOM; you never defend it here.
- **The fraud-escalation explanation IS valuable — in the PID/reprisal track**,
  where "I escalated a genuine safety concern in good faith because it was
  ignored, then suffered detriment" is protective (good-faith disclosure under
  s 40–42 PID Act). It is an ASSET there, a LIABILITY in the WC appeal.
  Track-specific: save it, do not burn it in the wrong forum.

**Net:** the "safety concerns not heard" sequence is gold for the WC case — it is
the institutional-response failure feeding the cumulative/manner limb. The fraud
escalation that the deafness PROVOKED is the symptom you keep on the reprisal
track. Own the unheard safety concern; never defend the fraud word in this forum.

## 10. Two sharp points (Cory, 13 Jun) — the drafting structure + the outcomes asymmetry

### 10.1 The PID's LANGUAGE structure — hedged fraud, asserted outcomes (good-faith proof)
Verified against the form: Cory **hedged the fraud** — "It **appears** that Chloe
Taylor... is engaging in fraudulent activities"; "I **suspect** she was not
present" — but **asserted the patient impact** — "The employee **is now** making
decisions that directly affect service delivery and patient outcomes." This is
the language of a discloser RAISING A SUSPICION FOR INVESTIGATION, not asserting
guilt — which is exactly the protected-disclosure standard (report a reasonable
suspicion in good faith; you need not prove it). The thing he stated as FACT was
the patient-outcomes effect. **Strong rebuttal to the vexatious framing:** "I did
not assert fraud as fact — I said it *appears* and I *suspect*. What I *asserted*
was the effect on patient outcomes." Caveat (honesty): some conduct
characterisations ("harassment, bullying, dishonesty") are less hedged, and
"thereby stealing from the hospital" is strong even after "appears" — so the
hedge HELPS the good-faith argument but does not make the word safe to
foreground. Hold as rebuttal; do not lead.

### 10.2 The OUTCOMES ASYMMETRY — fraud actioned, safety ignored (powerful)
Cory's point: the **fraud allegation got a response** (ESU referral, PID process —
then the reprisal); the **safety concerns got nothing** — the same roster, still
with the same manager, team triangulated, union + HR unable to mediate, **2 years
later, more errors and complaints, no action, no change**. Two uses:
1. **Institutional-priority asymmetry:** the institution MOVED on the allegation
   that touched the manager personally (and reprised the discloser) but did NOT
   move on the systemic safety failure. That is the institutional-response
   failure made concrete — and it cuts hard against "reasonable management action."
2. **Systemic-reality proof (defeats the "perception" framing):** the conditions
   PERSIST, affect the whole team, independent of Cory, 2 years on. That is not a
   vulnerable worker misperceiving reasonable management — it is documented,
   ongoing, systemic dysfunction. Powerful rebuttal to any "Cory's perception /
   special susceptibility" argument.
**Limits (honesty):** the ongoing/post-injury conditions are CORROBORATIVE (prove
systemic reality, rebut perception) — causation for the injury is about pre-onset
(to 18 Jun 2024) conditions, so post-injury persistence supports rather than
proves causation. And establishing "ongoing" needs Cory's current-employee
evidence + any current records. Deploy as: rebuttal to perception-framing + proof
the failure was systemic, NOT as core causation.

**Combined effect:** the asymmetry (acted on the personal allegation, ignored the
systemic safety one) + the persistence (still unfixed 2 years on) together make
the strongest available answer to BOTH the vexatious framing AND the
reasonable-management-action defence — deployed through the safety/governance
frame, never the fraud frame.

## 11. THE NERVE-CENTRE POINT (Cory, 13 Jun) — why he knows, and why it destroys "non-clinical"

**Cory's point:** he knows about all the complaints/errors because **he IS the
Switchboard** — the convergence node through which every Code Blue, MET call,
doctor-to-doctor, pathology result, ward complaint, paging request and
operational error flows, daily, from every direction. This is structurally the
single most useful fact for several limbs at once:

1. **Destroys the "non-clinical staff" defence (the closing line).** MSH exempted
   from fatigue management the ONE position through which every clinical
   emergency in the hospital is coordinated. *"The person they classified as
   non-clinical is the person the entire clinical-emergency response depends on
   being awake."* You cannot coherently call the Code Blue/MET coordination node
   "non-clinical" — the role IS clinical-emergency infrastructure. This is the
   answer to Items 4/5/7 ("non-clinical, so no FRMS").
2. **Makes Cory a UNIQUELY QUALIFIED WITNESS, not a busybody.** His knowledge of
   systemic dysfunction is not gossip or grievance-collecting — it is **first-hand
   operational data received by virtue of the role.** When the Regulator asks
   "how would a switchboard operator know about complaints across the hospital?"
   the answer is: because the switchboard is where they all converge. He observes
   the dysfunction live.
3. **The daily complaint flow is THREE things at once:**
   - the **cognitive/fatigue LOAD** (he absorbs the operational dysfunction of the
     whole hospital, unmediated) — supports causation;
   - the **manager-absence made concrete** — the complaints landed on HIM because
     no manager was present to triage/escalate them (the supervisory vacuum);
   - the **patient-safety OBSERVATION** — he watches mis-paging, wrong-contact,
     wrong-location clinical events happen in real time, which is WHY his PID said
     "directly affect service delivery and patient outcomes." His safety concern
     is grounded in direct operational observation, not speculation.

**Limit (honesty):** the CONTENT of third-party complaints (a doctor's complaint
about being mis-paged) may be hearsay if used to prove the underlying fact. But
it is admissible to prove (a) Cory's cognitive load/volume, (b) the existence and
density of a dysfunction pattern, and (c) his state of knowledge/stress — which
is what matters for causation and the manner limb. Corroborate the volume with
the call/paging/MET records (the production helps here). Use the flow to prove
LOAD + PATTERN + his grounded knowledge; do not over-claim it to prove each
underlying third-party fact.

**Combined:** the nerve-centre fact ties the spine together — life-safety
criticality (defeats non-clinical) + the load (causation) + the manager-absence
(complaints unmediated because no one was there) + grounded patient-safety
observation. It is Cory's single most powerful piece of his own evidence and the
core of the load-profile witness statement (already flagged in evidence.md).

## 12. THE FORM 29 PHRASE LEXICON = documentary proof of the nerve-centre (Cory, 13 Jun)

The Form 29 Item 3 filter is a **four-category lexicon of how Switchboard failure
is actually reported by clinicians:** Location-error ('wrong ward/patient/
theatre/ED/unit/bay'...), Directive-error ('switchboard sent me to', 'paged to
the wrong', "shouldn't have been paged"...), Clinician-role error ('wrong
doctor/registrar', 'not my patient', 'not on call', 'paged me instead of'...),
and Operational/directory error ('paging error', 'misdirected', 'misrouted',
'on-call list', 'update the directory', 'list is out of date'...). Item 10 adds
the directive sub-sets ('effective immediately'; pathology/doctor-paging/
call-routing). The integration with the nerve-centre point:

1. **The breadth IS the proof of knowledge.** Only the person AT the convergence
   node could compile this exhaustive, precise vocabulary of switchboard
   dysfunction. The lexicon is, in effect, Cory transcribing from memory the
   actual language of the complaints he received daily. It demonstrates
   first-hand operational fluency, not speculation — the documentary counterpart
   to "I know because I AM the Switchboard."

2. **Every phrase is a PATIENT-SAFETY event.** A doctor paged to the "wrong ward"
   or "wrong patient", urgent pathology delayed, the wrong clinician called to an
   emergency — these are clinical near-misses. The lexicon is a CATALOGUE of
   patient-safety failures flowing through the Switchboard. This is the
   documentary grounding of the PID's asserted "directly affect service delivery
   and patient outcomes" — the safety concern was eyewitness, and here is its
   precise vocabulary.

3. **The breadth is also the LEGAL particularity-cure (anti-fishing).** The
   server-side filter bounded by identified phrase-families is "objectively
   bounded" — a structured proxy for the pleaded dysfunction, not a free-text
   trawl. This is the answer to MSH's particularity objection and the r 64E
   pre-emption (the Form 29 says exactly this).

4. **It maps to the spine (Stressor 1(a) / the vacuum).** The Form 29's own
   relevance note: the Line Manager's unilateral directives "bottlenecked
   emergency workflows and directly caused verifiable delays to the communication
   of urgent pathology results to clinical staff." So the causal chain is
   documentary: manager-absence/disruption → switchboard misfires (the lexicon)
   → patient-safety events → Cory witnesses + raises them → unheard → injury. The
   phrase-lists are the documentary spine of that whole chain.

**Net:** the Form 29's breadth of naming is not just a search spec — it is
(a) proof of Cory's nerve-centre knowledge, (b) a catalogue of patient-safety
near-misses grounding the safety case, (c) the particularity-cure for Item 3, and
(d) the documentary manifestation of the supervisory vacuum (the directives that
bottlenecked the workflow). The same forensic fluency as the metadata work,
applied to the operational reality of the role.
