 I make it as a separate document, rather than within my response to the Request for Medical Information of 31 July
 2026, so that there is no question about what it is or when it was received.

 Clause 10.3.2 provides that, in accordance with the Industrial Relations Act 2016, an employee "may ask the employer
 for a change in the way the employee works, including the employee's ordinary hours of work". Section 27(1)(c) of that
 Act provides that the request may be for "a change to the way the employee works, for example, the use of different
 equipment as a result of a disability, illness or injury".

 Clause 10.3.3 requires that the request be in writing, state the change in sufficient detail to allow a decision to be made,
 and state the reasons. Parts 2 and 3 below do each of those things.

 I make the request under two separate limbs of section 27(1), and I ask that they be considered separately.

   (a) ORDINARY HOURS — Part 2.1. This is made under section 27(1)(a), which concerns "the employee's ordinary
      hours of work", and under clause 10.3.2, which is in the same terms. That limb stands on its own. It does not
      depend on illness or injury, and neither section 27, nor section 28, nor clause 10.3 makes medical information a
      precondition to making such a request or to deciding one. My reasons for it are matters of rostering history and are
      set out at Part 3.
   (b) THE WAY I WORK — Parts 2.2 to 2.5. These are made under section 27(1)(c), which concerns "a change to the
      way the employee works, for example, the use of different equipment as a result of a disability, illness or injury".
 I separate them because a decision on one is not a decision on the other, and because the question of my ordinary
 hours does not require, and should not await, information sought for a different purpose. If the Health Service is not in a
 position to decide (b) at present, I ask that it decide (a), and say so.

 approximately six shifts per fortnight", and records that it "is the pattern Mr Shepherd has in fact worked and tolerated
 over the past twelve months without deterioration, and maintaining rather than increasing it best supports recovery while
 minimising risk of exacerbation". The first page records the arrangement as a "continuation of existing arrangement".

 I am not asking for any reduction from the pattern I have been working. I am asking that the existing pattern continue. It
 was set by the Health Service, worked by me, and sustained across twelve months. No concern was raised with me at

 4. THE DECISION, AND WHO SHOULD MAKE IT
 Clause 10.3.4 provides that the Health Service may grant this request, grant it in part or subject to conditions, or refuse
 it. Clause 10.3.5 provides that it may grant it in part or subject to conditions, or refuse it, "only on reasonable grounds".

 5. THE FRAMEWORK THE DECISION SITS IN
 I set this out for one reason only. Clause 10.3.5 permits the Health Service to grant the request in part or subject to
 conditions, or refuse it, "only on reasonable grounds". Grounds are reasonable against the whole of the law that applies,
 not against the agreement alone. If the request is refused in whole or in part, I would like to be able to understand the
 reasons given under clause 10.3.6 by reference to the same framework the Health Service is applying.

 5.1 THE OBLIGATION
 The Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 provides at section 15(1) that a person must not discriminate "in any variation of the
 terms of work", or "by treating a worker unfavourably in any way in connection with work". Section 15(2) provides that
 "dismissing includes ending the particular work of a person by forced retirement, failure to provide work or otherwise".

 Section 11 provides that indirect discrimination happens if a person imposes a term with which a person with an
 attribute does not or is not able to comply, and which is not reasonable. Impairment is a protected attribute under
 section 7.

 5.2 THE EXEMPTIONS, AND WHAT THEY REQUIRE
 Sections 35 and 36 provide that it is not unlawful to discriminate on the basis of impairment where the person would
 require special services or facilities and supplying them would impose unjustifiable hardship, or where the
 circumstances of the impairment would impose unjustifiable hardship.

 Those provisions are exemptions, and each of them turns on unjustifiable hardship. Section 5 provides that whether
 something would impose unjustifiable hardship depends on all the relevant circumstances of the case, including the
 nature of the services or facilities, their cost and the number of people who would benefit or be disadvantaged, the



Cory Lea Shepherd · MSH-INJ-5795 · Request under clause 10.3.2 — decision due within 21 days (cl 10.3.6)                 Page 3

>>> documents/sent-2026-08-03/attachments-as-sent/REQUEST_Change_cl10.3.pdf :: page 4
 financial circumstances of the person, the disruption that supplying them might cause, and the nature of any benefit or
 detriment to all people concerned.

 HR Policy G03 puts the same test in the Health Service's own words, at clause 2: unjustifiable hardship is "tested
 against the whole organisation, not a division or unit within the organisation", and "the onus is on Queensland Health, as
 the employer, to prove an adjustment is unreasonable, not on the person to prove that it is reasonable".

 I would add that the Health Service is a public entity for the purposes of the Human Rights Act 2019, and section 58 of
 that Act requires a public entity to act and make decisions compatibly with human rights and to give proper
 consideration to relevant human rights in doing so.

 5.3 WHY I RAISE IT, AND WHAT I AM NOT DOING
 I have made no complaint under the Anti-Discrimination Act, and this letter is not one. I make no allegation against
 anyone and I ask for no finding to be made about anyone.

 I raise it because the measures at Part 2 are modest ones, and I would like the reasons for any refusal to engage with
 that. On the shifts I attend, the arrangement at 2.2 costs one telephone call. The roster at 2.1 is the roster the Health
 Service already sets. The complaint-handling arrangement at 2.4 is the Health Service's own established process. The
 correspondence routing at 2.5 is what the Employee Capabilities Checklist itself recommends.

 If the Health Service considers that any of the measures would impose unjustifiable hardship, I ask only that it identify
 which measure, and what the hardship is. That is the same thing clause 10.3.6 requires, expressed in the language of
 the Act.

 6. THE TIME FOR THE DECISION
 Clause 10.3.6 provides:

     "The employer must give the employee written notice about its decision within 21 days after receiving the request. If
     the employer decides to grant the request in part or subject to conditions or to refuse the request, the written notice
     about the decision must state the reasons for the decision, outlining the reasonable grounds for granting the request
     in part or subject to conditions or for the refusal."

 Section 28(3) of the Industrial Relations Act 2016 is in the same terms. Section 28(4) provides that a notice granting the
 request in part or subject to conditions, or refusing it, must state the written reasons outlining the reasonable grounds,
 and must state that the Commission has jurisdiction to hear and decide a dispute over the request under chapter 6.
 Section 29 provides that if the written notice is not given within 21 days after the request is received, the employer is
 taken to have decided to refuse the request.

 Twenty-one days from the date of this letter is Monday 24 August 2026.

 I record these provisions because a date has not been available in this matter at any stage. I have asked several times
 to be told when I would know whether I am returning to work, and I have not been given a date. The certified agreement
 provides one, and I would much prefer that the request be dealt with by agreement well before it.

 1.2 THE TEST APPLIED
 The letter to Dr Ma states the purpose of the request:

     "to identify and implement any appropriate workplace controls or reasonable adjustments to support a safe and
     sustainable return to his substantive position."

 Human Resources Policy G03 (QH-POL-210), which the Health Service has cited, sets the limit at clause 3:

     "Reasonable adjustment may need to be supported by medical or rehabilitation information, where necessary, to
     either identify required workplace adjustments and/or assess the suitability of proposed adjustments."

 I have applied that test to each question: is this information necessary to identify a required adjustment, or to assess the
 suitability of a proposed one — and is the person being asked the right person to answer it?

 Applying that test, the nine questions divide four ways. I am not declining to provide information. I am proposing that
 each question be directed to whoever is able to answer it.

 in substance, most of the nine questions.

 logged and redirected to management/the dedicated complaints area, not actioned, resolved or absorbed by Mr

 PART 4 — QUESTIONS FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE
 These four questions ask a doctor to answer matters which the Health Service's own policy and the Work Health and
 Safety Act 2011 place with the Health Service. I ask that the Health Service answer them, after which the properly
 medical component of each can be put to my practitioners.

 4.1 QUESTION 2 — is there a performance or conduct process?
 The question asks whether I can "follow a reasonable and lawful direction issued by [my] supervisor" and "participate in
 discussions in relation to [my] workplace performance and/or conduct."

 These are not questions about capacity to perform the genuine occupational requirements of my role. They concern
 readiness for a management process. Either such a process is on foot concerning me — in which case I am entitled to
 be told of it, given particulars, and afforded procedural fairness — or there is not, in which case the questions do not
 serve the stated purpose of this inquiry.

    → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: please confirm whether any performance or conduct process concerning me
     is on foot or contemplated, and if so provide particulars.
    → THEN, IF APPROPRIATE, FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Does the employee have capacity to participate in
     ordinary workplace meetings and supervision, and are any supports required?"
 The premise of Question 2 is separately incorrect and is addressed at Part 5.

 4.2 QUESTION 3 — is the workplace safe?
 The question asks whether I am "medically fit to return to their substantive role under the existing reporting
 arrangements, including working with and reporting to their current line manager." That asks a treating doctor to certify
 that a workplace arrangement is safe. Under section 19 of the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 that duty rests with the



Cory Lea Shepherd · MSH-INJ-5795 · Response to Request for Medical Information of 31 July 2026                        Page 4

>>> documents/sent-2026-08-03/attachments-as-sent/RFMI_Response_and_Allocation.pdf :: page 5
 Health Service; under the Managing the risk of psychosocial hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 a psychosocial
 hazard is a feature of the work, identified and controlled by the PCBU; and G03 clause 1 requires proper consideration
 of that Code. A doctor can advise on me; a doctor cannot assess the Health Service's reporting arrangements.

 The letter of 7 July 2026 records that the Health Service "does not have sufficient information to understand the nature
 of these matters or assess whether they present any psychosocial hazards or risks". That gap is real, and it is closed by
 the Health Service consulting and assessing — sections 47 to 49 require consultation with workers directly affected, and
 none has occurred since 26 June 2026. For completeness, the matters concern how work in the unit is organised and
 decided: how patient safety concerns raised at the switchboard are escalated; how changes to work and roster have
 been introduced; fatigue and recovery between shifts; and staff input into decisions affecting the work. They are
 workplace matters, which is why the assessment belongs with the Health Service.

    → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: a risk assessment of the Switchboard work environment addressing the
     psychosocial hazards identified. Clause 7.2.1 of the certified agreement provides the mechanism.
    → THEN FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Are any adjustments recommended in relation to supervision
     arrangements, and if so, what are they in functional terms?"

 4.3 QUESTION 6 — what are the genuine occupational requirements?
 The question asks whether I can "fulfill the full inherent requirements of [my] Role ... without restrictions or modifications
 to duties."

 This applies the wrong test. G03 states its purpose as assisting employees "to meet the genuine occupational
 requirements of their role by applying principles of reasonable adjustment," and at clause 3 provides that adjustments
 "should support the employee to undertake the genuine occupational requirements of their role, without risk to their own
 health and safety or that of others in the workplace." Section 34 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 is to the same effect.
 Neither asks whether an employee can perform a role without adjustment.

 A clinician also cannot determine which duties are genuine occupational requirements. That is the employer's
 determination. The Health Service has itself already made part of it: its letter states that "established process for client
 complaints received by Switchboard employees is for immediate escalation and management by the Health Service
 Client Liaison Officer and/or Manager, Switchboard Services," and the Role Description at Attachment 2 contains no
 complaint-handling responsibility.

    → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: identify which duties of the role it says are genuine occupational
     requirements, having regard to the Role Description at Attachment 2.
    → THEN FOR MY PRACTITIONER: "Can the employee perform the genuine occupational requirements of the
     role with the adjustments you have recommended?"

 4.4 QUESTION 9 — can the adjustments be accommodated?
 The question asks: "If we are not able to accommodate the restrictions you have recommended, is Mr Shepherd able to
 safely return to the workplace?"

 This presupposes an inability to accommodate before any accommodation has been assessed. G03 clause 2 provides
 that unjustifiable hardship "is tested against the whole organisation, not a division or unit within the organisation," and
 that "the onus is on Queensland Health, as the employer, to prove an adjustment is unreasonable, not on the person to
 prove that it is reasonable."

 The question therefore asks my doctor to answer the final step first, on a hypothetical the Health Service has
 constructed and not yet tested, and on which the onus is not mine.

    → FOR THE HEALTH SERVICE: assess the recommended adjustments against the whole organisation. If it
     considers any cannot be accommodated, identify which and its reasons.
    → THEN, IF NECESSARY, the question can be put to my practitioner properly.

 PART 6 — DELEGATION AND CONFLICT OF INTEREST
 This is not a personal complaint about any individual. I make no allegation and I ask for no finding about anyone. My
 concern is with how the process is being run — who is deciding, on what material, and under what instrument — and
 with the support and adjustment that ordinarily apply when an employee is certified fit with restrictions. G03 clause 1.1
 provides for temporary adjustments so an employee may "continue work during their recovery"; the Workplace
 rehabilitation standard requires suitable duties to be actively sought and the worker's connection with the workplace
 maintained, for "either a work or non-work-related injury/illness". I obtained the checklist the Health Service required for
 that purpose. It certified me fit with restrictions. What followed was exclusion rather than adjustment.

 Due process is the other half: being told what power is being used and who decides; a fair opportunity to respond before
 a serious employment consequence; consultation on the matters in issue; deadlines that are not one-sided; and
 decisions made by an officer independent of the matters they concern — what the Managing the risk of psychosocial
 hazards at work Code of Practice 2022 calls organisational justice. I do not say any tribunal has found a denial of fair
 process; I say that process has not been applied, and I ask that it be.

 I asked on 28 July 2026 who is making decisions about me and whether any conflict of interest has been identified. I
 have not received a response. Both letters of 31 July 2026 are written in the first person of the decision-maker and
 signed by Mr Hughes, Director, Corporate Services; question 3 asks my doctor about the reporting arrangements within
 that same directorate, and the Manager who gave the advice of 2 July 2026 reports within it. The officer determining my
 return therefore sits within the arrangements in issue. I ask the Health Service to confirm: (a) the source and instrument
 of the delegation; (b) whether any conflict has been identified, declared and managed, and how; and (c) whether the
 decisions of 2 and 3 July 2026 were made with the knowledge or approval of the officer now determining my return.

 6.1 A PROPOSED MANAGEMENT OF THE CONFLICT
 I propose the ordinary separation of functions: the clinical material held exclusively by the Injury Management team on a
 medical-in-confidence basis — which is what the Checklist itself recommends at Additional Comments 4(c); any
 decision concerning my capacity or return made by an officer outside Corporate Services; and implementation —
 rostering, and putting the adjustments in place — retained within Corporate Services. The officer steps out of the
 decision, not out of the workplace. I record, because it bears on the assessment, that on 3 October 2025 I made a
 formal written request for review to the A/Director, HR Business Partnering concerning a process initiated by the officer
 who has signed the letters of 31 July 2026; I do not reopen it here. Code of Conduct clause 1.2 provides that a conflict is
 not wrongdoing in itself — failing to disclose and manage one is likely to be.

FACTS
The 3 July 2026 ECC certifies me fit for modified duties
and reduced hours from 3 July 2026 as a continuation of
the existing arrangement. The doctor viewed the AO3
Switchboard position description (ATT14) and recorded
that usual switchboard duties remain suitable with
stated modifications (including no complaint-handling;
limits on peak weekday day/afternoon shifts;
predictable rostering; minimum 10-hour break). I was
performing work consistent with those limits when I
provided the ECC. The same-day direction not to attend

WHAT HAS BEEN WRONGLY APPLIED


1. "Current QSuper Income Protection claim" → ordinary
pay sits with ART (your 15 July email)


Wrong application.
• An IP file is not ordinary wages for a permanent
employee who is certified fit, ready and available, and
directed by the employer not to attend.

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-28_1739_Cory_to_HR_incorrect_application_EB12_Award_policies.pdf :: page 3
• On the material available to me notified by employee
(myself) May 2025 and February 2026 and now 3rd July
2026 certification of that partial capacity, ART put
benefit payments are not applied from 1 June 2026.
Treating the Fund as presently replacing ordinary pay is
incorrect on that record. Partial capacity and partial
payment does not dislodge this framing.
• IP administration is separate (Mr Zappia). It does not
displace ATT02 EB12 cl 6.1 (employment security) or
ATT02 EB12 cl 7.1.5(g)–(h) (injury management;
management of ill or injured employees).
• Coding "IP no pay" while held out after an ECC is not a
correct application of ATT02 or of ATT12/ATT13 (special
leave).


2. WCRA rehabilitation only if accepted claim; return
purely at "employer discretion" (your 15 July email)


Wrong application.
• Even if WCRA statutory rehab is limited to accepted
claims, that does not exhaust your duties under ATT02
(EB12), ATT03 (HHS Award), ATT10 (QH-POL-210) and
ATT09 (QH-IMP-401-5).
• ATT10 applies to all Queensland Health / HHS
employees and includes temporary reasonable
adjustment for rehabilitation/RTW and for capacity
restriction — not only accepted workers' compensation
claims.
• ATT02 EB12 cl 7.1.5 requires the parties to address
injury management, management of ill or injured
employees, fatigue, psychosocial issues and the Code
of Practice 2022 (ATT05), and security for administrative
staff in frontline positions.
• "Discretion" does not correctly authorise indefinite
exclusion, refusal of interim duties "in any capacity,"
and non-payment without applying ATT09, ATT10 and
ATT02 Parts 6 and 7.


3. Further medical framing me as the psychosocial risk
before return "in any capacity" (your 13–15 July emails)


Wrong application of ATT05 and ATT02.
• ATT05 and ATT02 EB12 cl 7.2 require assessment of
psychosocial hazards in the workplace and work
system (including workplace risk assessments as
requested through an HCF by employer or union).
• The 3 July ECC already identifies workplace stressors
(complaint-handling; blame for others' failures;

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-28_1739_Cory_to_HR_incorrect_application_EB12_Award_policies.pdf :: page 4
rostering/fatigue; unresolved line-management
matters). Those are workplace issues under ATT05 and
ATT02 cl 7.1.5(j) and 7.2.
• Framing psychosocial risk as a personal barrier inside
Injury Management / QSuper misapplies ATT02 cl 7.2
and cl 7.1.11 (feedback when WHS matters are raised).
• Workplace psychosocial issues I have raised over
more than two years are not properly dealt with by
indefinite IM hold-out. That process is not the correct
forum under ATT02 cl 7.2.
• I will cooperate with reasonable medical requests that
are specific and linked to identified job tasks under
ATT14. Open-ended further medical is not a correct
precondition to all duties where ATT14 and the ECC
already define capacity I have been performing.


4. "Unable to facilitate" / no alternative duties (Chloe 2
July; your 13–15 July emails)


Wrong application of ATT09, ATT10 and ATT02.
• Chloe's 2 July email made facilitation conditional on a
completed ECC. I provided that ECC on 3 July while
working. Facilitation was then refused and I was
directed off — the opposite of facilitating return on the
medical basis required.
• The ECC states fit from 3 July as continuation of the
existing arrangement and that usual switchboard duties
remain suitable with modifications against ATT14.
Refusing all duties "in any capacity" does not correctly
apply ATT10, ATT09 or ATT02 cl 7.1.5(f)–(h).
• Correct application requires identifying any specific
duty and restriction said to be incompatible, what
modification was considered, and what was rejected —
not a blanket refusal.


5. Leave coding as sick leave / sick leave no pay / "IP no
pay" while certified fit and directed not to attend


Wrong application of ATT02, ATT12 and ATT13.
• From 3 July 2026 the relevant absence is employer-
directed while I am certified fit and available. That is not
ordinary sick leave for that period.
• "IP no pay" is not the correct industrial answer under
ATT02 when the employer has directed me off after an
ECC.
• ATT02 EB12 cl 9.12 provides that Directive 12/24:
Special Leave (ATT12) applies to employees covered by
the Agreement. ATT13 QH-POL-231 (C7) also applies.

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-28_1739_Cory_to_HR_incorrect_application_EB12_Award_policies.pdf :: page 5
• Special leave under ATT12 and ATT13 must be applied
for employer-directed exclusion while I am ready, willing
and able within the ECC. Where the only barrier is
refusal to facilitate certified duties, special leave on full
pay (or ordinary pay as if at work) must be applied.
Please correct coding and identify the delegate and
instrument for each day from 3 July.

Wrong application of the ECC itself.

reduced hours from 3 July 2026 as a continuation of the
existing arrangement. The doctor viewed the AO3
Switchboard position description (ATT14) and recorded
that usual switchboard duties remain suitable with stated
modifications (including no complaint-handling; limits on
peak weekday day/afternoon shifts; predictable rostering;
minimum 10-hour break). I was performing work
consistent with those limits when I provided the ECC. The
same-day direction not to attend disrupted that work. The
28 August 2026 date on the ECC is a review of restrictions
— not the start of capacity.


WHAT HAS BEEN WRONGLY APPLIED


1. "Current QSuper Income Protection claim" → ordinary
pay sits with ART (your 15 July email)


Wrong application.
• An IP file is not ordinary wages for a permanent
employee who is certified fit, ready and available, and
directed by the employer not to attend.

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-29_1610_MSH_reply_to_28July_letter.pdf :: page 5
• On the material available to me notified by employee
(myself) May 2025 and February 2026 and now 3rd July
2026 certification of that partial capacity, ART put benefit
payments are not applied from 1 June 2026. Treating the
Fund as presently replacing ordinary pay is incorrect on
that record. Partial capacity and partial payment does not
dislodge this framing.
• IP administration is separate (Mr Zappia). It does not
displace ATT02 EB12 cl 6.1 (employment security) or ATT02
EB12 cl 7.1.5(g)–(h) (injury management; management of
ill or injured employees).
• Coding "IP no pay" while held out after an ECC is not a
correct application of ATT02 or of ATT12/ATT13 (special
leave).


2. WCRA rehabilitation only if accepted claim; return
purely at "employer discretion" (your 15 July email)


Wrong application.
• Even if WCRA statutory rehab is limited to accepted
claims, that does not exhaust your duties under ATT02
(EB12), ATT03 (HHS Award), ATT10 (QH-POL-210) and
ATT09 (QH-IMP-401-5).
• ATT10 applies to all Queensland Health / HHS employees
and includes temporary reasonable adjustment for
rehabilitation/RTW and for capacity restriction — not only
accepted workers' compensation claims.
• ATT02 EB12 cl 7.1.5 requires the parties to address injury
management, management of ill or injured employees,
fatigue, psychosocial issues and the Code of Practice 2022
(ATT05), and security for administrative staff in frontline
positions.
• "Discretion" does not correctly authorise indefinite
exclusion, refusal of interim duties "in any capacity," and
non-payment without applying ATT09, ATT10 and ATT02
Parts 6 and 7.


3. Further medical framing me as the psychosocial risk
before return "in any capacity" (your 13–15 July emails)


Wrong application of ATT05 and ATT02.
• ATT05 and ATT02 EB12 cl 7.2 require assessment of
psychosocial hazards in the workplace and work system
(including workplace risk assessments as requested
through an HCF by employer or union).
• The 3 July ECC already identifies workplace stressors
(complaint-handling; blame for others' failures;
rostering/fatigue; unresolved line-management matters).

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-29_1610_MSH_reply_to_28July_letter.pdf :: page 6
Those are workplace issues under ATT05 and ATT02 cl
7.1.5(j) and 7.2.
• Framing psychosocial risk as a personal barrier inside
Injury Management / QSuper misapplies ATT02 cl 7.2 and
cl 7.1.11 (feedback when WHS matters are raised).
• Workplace psychosocial issues I have raised over more
than two years are not properly dealt with by indefinite IM
hold-out. That process is not the correct forum under
ATT02 cl 7.2.
• I will cooperate with reasonable medical requests that
are specific and linked to identified job tasks under ATT14.
Open-ended further medical is not a correct precondition
to all duties where ATT14 and the ECC already define
capacity I have been performing.


4. "Unable to facilitate" / no alternative duties (Chloe 2
July; your 13–15 July emails)


Wrong application of ATT09, ATT10 and ATT02.
• Chloe's 2 July email made facilitation conditional on a
completed ECC. I provided that ECC on 3 July while
working. Facilitation was then refused and I was directed
off — the opposite of facilitating return on the medical
basis required.
• The ECC states fit from 3 July as continuation of the

remain suitable with modifications against ATT14. Refusing
all duties "in any capacity" does not correctly apply ATT10,
ATT09 or ATT02 cl 7.1.5(f)–(h).
• Correct application requires identifying any specific duty
and restriction said to be incompatible, what modification
was considered, and what was rejected — not a blanket
refusal.


5. Leave coding as sick leave / sick leave no pay / "IP no
pay" while certified fit and directed not to attend


Wrong application of ATT02, ATT12 and ATT13.
• From 3 July 2026 the relevant absence is employer-
directed while I am certified fit and available. That is not
ordinary sick leave for that period.
• "IP no pay" is not the correct industrial answer under
ATT02 when the employer has directed me off after an
ECC.
• ATT02 EB12 cl 9.12 provides that Directive 12/24: Special
Leave (ATT12) applies to employees covered by the
Agreement. ATT13 QH-POL-231 (C7) also applies.

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-07-29_1610_MSH_reply_to_28July_letter.pdf :: page 7
• Special leave under ATT12 and ATT13 must be applied for
employer-directed exclusion while I am ready, willing and

facilitate certified duties, special leave on full pay (or
ordinary pay as if at work) must be applied. Please correct
coding and identify the delegate and instrument for each

Wrong application of the ECC itself.

Hi Cory,


Thank you for reaching out.


Yes, we do provide the services aligned with your
outline below.


The most applicable is a Psychosocial Risk
Infrastructure Audit. This include a review of all
internal data as you have outlined in your email
(surveys, reporting systems, claims, rosters, policies),
as well as interviews with stakeholders across the
organisation which generally involves a mix of work,
health and safety, human resources, senior
executives, HSR’s and workers where risk is indicted.


This Audit is comprehensive and provides in-depth
report and briefing with specific recommendations
where the organisation can improve its system of
work for complying with relevant state based
regulations and codes of practice, and the ISO
standards.


Costs for the audit range between $10-30,000
dependant on the size of the review and number of
interviews, a more definitive price can be provided
once the client is available to scope the project.


We also offer psychosocial risk assessments - an
independently run survey hosted and facilitated by
Psychgroup, and may also include qualitative

>>> documents/correspondence-2026/2026-08-05_2053_PsychGroup_Hellwege_indicative_proposal_10-30k.pdf :: page 2
interviews, this screens for all active psychosocial
hazards across an organisation or work area and is
followed by a comprehensive report with
recommendations. Risk assessments are free as part
of any Partner Program, to enable the organisation to
fully implement recommendations across a 12 month
program, brochure attached.


In terms of role related risk assessments, this is
certainly something we can offer as part of a role
related risk assessment and make recommendations
of general controls to mitigate role related risks.
However, for an individual role related psychosocial
risk assessment to inform either fitness for work,
return to work or to guide a medical practitioner, this
would be a separate service and individualised to the
employee.


I hope this helps, please pass these details on to your
relevant contact within the hospital for a more
definitive scoping and costing as required.

 Subject: Important news - COVID-19 update 24 August 2020

 Having trouble viewing this email? View Online

 Dear colleagues,

In response to the recent cluster of COVID-19 cases associated with the Brisbane Youth
Detention
Centre, Metro South Health has been determined to be in a ?Moderate Risk? for the purposes of
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) use.

Moderate risk requires the use of flat surgical masks in most clinical settings for staff,
patients and visitors and immediate steps are to be taken to commence the implementation of the
following PPE requirements.

Continuous surgical mask use is recommended for healthcare workers during periods of moderate
community transmission of COVID-19, to reduce the risk of transmission of COVID-19 between
healthcare workers and patients (who may be asymptomatic but infectious, especially early in
the
course of illness).

This will require healthcare workers who work in clinical areas and common workplaces to
continuously wear a surgical mask during their routine activities throughout the entirety of
their shift.

Healthcare workers who generally work alone in their own office will be required to wear a mask
when outside of their office if physical distancing cannot be maintained.

Recommended PPE escalation according to a moderate risk of unexpected COVID-19 infections in
patients or healthcare workers have been outlined for you below.
 For healthcare workers
 Routine care
 For suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19 patients
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Gown Gloves Aerosol generating procedures
For suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19 patients
 P2/N95 respirator Protective eyewear Gown Gloves Aerosol generating procedures for
non-COVID-19
patients
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Routine care of non-COVID-19 patients (within 1.5 metres)
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Hospital staff during activities other than direct patient
care
 Surgical mask when physical distancing of 1.5 metres cannot be maintained (e.g. ward rounds,
handover meetings)

>>> documents/correspondence-packs/01_CS_Logan_Switch_PACK_103pp_2020-2026.pdf :: page 7
For patients and hospital visitors
 Patients
Suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19
(excluding paediatric patients)
 Surgical mask where tolerated, unless inpatient in own bed Patients
Non-COVID-19 (excluding paediatric patients)
 Surgical mask where tolerated, unless inpatient in own bed Visitors
 Surgical mask OR own mask if adequate (fabric mask with at least 3 layers)
All Metro South Health staff are to adhere to the following Queensland Health mask
recommendations to assist with the management of COVID-19 community transmission:
 Masks should be changed when they become damaged, soiled or wet. Masks should never be
reapplied
after they have been removed. Masks should not be left dangling around the neck. Avoid
touching/adjusting the front of the mask while wearing it. Hand hygiene should be performed
upon
touching or discarding a used mask. Masks need to be removed for eating and drinking and this
is
permitted, if necessary and safe. It is important to limit the duration that the mask is
removed
to help minimise any potential risk of exposure. Staff must practise physical distancing when
on
meal breaks when a mask is not in place. Staff must dispose of used masks in waste receptacles
as
soon as they are removed. It is now more important than ever to maintain appropriate physical
distancing in the workplace and remember to maintain your hand hygiene. If you are a vulnerable
employee or have any concerns, then please discuss this with your manager.

 Remember ? if you are unwell then stay home and if you have any symptoms then get tested.

If you require further clarification on these PPE guidelines, please speak to your relevant
line
manager.

Good Afternoon Everyone,

 Thank you everyone for your time this morning for those of you whom were able to join in our
meeting today and for those of you whom could not attend our meeting today, please see the
attached draft roster for consultation. Attached above is a 10 hour draft roster for your
consideration.

 Please note start and finish times of shifts could potentially be changed based on staff
feedback, as long as they still meet business requirements. In the roster the full-time lines
and
the part-time lines (0.8 FTE and 0.7 FTE) rotate through all lines of that FTE at the end of
the
4 weeks due to all lines for that FTE not having exactly the same penalty rates. For part-time
staff there is one shift per fortnight in each line which is shorter due to 10 hours not evenly
splitting into rostered FTE hours per fortnight.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on draft 10 hour roster above and
the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 24 th March 2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate. I am more than
happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to this business case for change and
can
be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

Subject: Draft LH Switchboard Rosters for Consultation
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Good Afternoon Everyone,

Please see the attached three draft rosters for consultation and feedback.

 Roster 1 : Is an 8 hour roster with RDOs. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating
through first than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so
on. We recognise that this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two
whole
days off? post night duty for full time staff.

 Roster 2 : Is an updated version of the 10 hour draft Switchboard Roster that was previously
presented but with adjusted shift times, given we had the overwhelming feedback that the
midnight
to 10am shift was not popular. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. This
roster
is industrially compliant.

  Roster 3 : Is a 8 hour roster without RDOs. Full-time staff instead have 9 x 8 hour shifts and
1
x 4 hour shift per fortnight. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. The only
lines not to rotate in this roster is the FTE lines 0.6 FTE, O.4 and 0.2 FTE. We recognise that
this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two whole days off? post night
duty for full time staff.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on these draft rosters, including
preference and the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 2 7 th May
2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate.

 I am more than happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to these rosters and
business case for change and can be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

 Kind Regards
 Tammy

 Tammy Reese

 Subject: Draft LH Switchboard Rosters for Consultation

 Good Afternoon Everyone,

Please see the attached three draft rosters for consultation and feedback.

 Roster 1 : Is an 8 hour roster with RDOs. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating
through first than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so
on. We recognise that this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two
whole
days off? post night duty for full time staff.

 Roster 2 : Is an updated version of the 10 hour draft Switchboard Roster that was previously
presented but with adjusted shift times, given we had the overwhelming feedback that the
midnight
to 10am shift was not popular. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. This
roster
is industrially compliant.

  Roster 3 : Is a 8 hour roster without RDOs. Full-time staff instead have 9 x 8 hour shifts and
1
x 4 hour shift per fortnight. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. The only
lines not to rotate in this roster is the FTE lines 0.6 FTE, O.4 and 0.2 FTE. We recognise that
this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two whole days off? post night
duty for full time staff.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on these draft rosters, including
preference and the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 2 7 th May
2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate.

 I am more than happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to these rosters and
business case for change and can be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

>>> documents/correspondence-packs/01_CS_Logan_Switch_PACK_103pp_2020-2026.pdf :: page 53
Please see the attached three draft rosters for consultation and feedback.

 Roster 1 : Is an 8 hour roster with RDOs. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating
through first than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so
on. We recognise that this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two
whole
days off? post night duty for full time staff.

 Roster 2 : Is an updated version of the 10 hour draft Switchboard Roster that was previously
presented but with adjusted shift times, given we had the overwhelming feedback that the
midnight
to 10am shift was not popular. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. This
roster
is industrially compliant.

  Roster 3 : Is a 8 hour roster without RDOs. Full-time staff instead have 9 x 8 hour shifts and
1
x 4 hour shift per fortnight. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. The only
lines not to rotate in this roster is the FTE lines 0.6 FTE, O.4 and 0.2 FTE. We recognise that
this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two whole days off? post night
duty for full time staff.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on these draft rosters, including
preference and the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 2 7 th May
2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate.

 I am more than happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to these rosters and
business case for change and can be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

 Kind Regards
 Tammy

 Having trouble viewing this email? View Online

 Dear colleagues,

In response to the recent cluster of COVID-19 cases associated with the Brisbane Youth
Detention
Centre, Metro South Health has been determined to be in a ?Moderate Risk? for the purposes of
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) use.

Moderate risk requires the use of flat surgical masks in most clinical settings for staff,
patients and visitors and immediate steps are to be taken to commence the implementation of the
following PPE requirements.

Continuous surgical mask use is recommended for healthcare workers during periods of moderate
community transmission of COVID-19, to reduce the risk of transmission of COVID-19 between
healthcare workers and patients (who may be asymptomatic but infectious, especially early in
the
course of illness).

This will require healthcare workers who work in clinical areas and common workplaces to
continuously wear a surgical mask during their routine activities throughout the entirety of
their shift.

Healthcare workers who generally work alone in their own office will be required to wear a mask
when outside of their office if physical distancing cannot be maintained.

Recommended PPE escalation according to a moderate risk of unexpected COVID-19 infections in
patients or healthcare workers have been outlined for you below.
 For healthcare workers
 Routine care
 For suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19 patients
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Gown Gloves Aerosol generating procedures
For suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19 patients
 P2/N95 respirator Protective eyewear Gown Gloves Aerosol generating procedures for
non-COVID-19
patients
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Routine care of non-COVID-19 patients (within 1.5 metres)
 Surgical mask Protective eyewear Hospital staff during activities other than direct patient
care
 Surgical mask when physical distancing of 1.5 metres cannot be maintained (e.g. ward rounds,
handover meetings)

>>> documents/correspondence-packs/02_Chloe_Taylor_PACK_462pp.pdf :: page 12
For patients and hospital visitors
 Patients
Suspected / probable / confirmed COVID-19
(excluding paediatric patients)
 Surgical mask where tolerated, unless inpatient in own bed Patients
Non-COVID-19 (excluding paediatric patients)
 Surgical mask where tolerated, unless inpatient in own bed Visitors
 Surgical mask OR own mask if adequate (fabric mask with at least 3 layers)
All Metro South Health staff are to adhere to the following Queensland Health mask
recommendations to assist with the management of COVID-19 community transmission:
 Masks should be changed when they become damaged, soiled or wet. Masks should never be
reapplied
after they have been removed. Masks should not be left dangling around the neck. Avoid
touching/adjusting the front of the mask while wearing it. Hand hygiene should be performed
upon
touching or discarding a used mask. Masks need to be removed for eating and drinking and this
is
permitted, if necessary and safe. It is important to limit the duration that the mask is
removed
to help minimise any potential risk of exposure. Staff must practise physical distancing when
on
meal breaks when a mask is not in place. Staff must dispose of used masks in waste receptacles
as
soon as they are removed. It is now more important than ever to maintain appropriate physical
distancing in the workplace and remember to maintain your hand hygiene. If you are a vulnerable
employee or have any concerns, then please discuss this with your manager.

 Remember ? if you are unwell then stay home and if you have any symptoms then get tested.

If you require further clarification on these PPE guidelines, please speak to your relevant
line
manager.

 Good Afternoon Everyone,

 Thank you everyone for your time this morning for those of you whom were able to join in our
meeting today and for those of you whom could not attend our meeting today, please see the
attached draft roster for consultation. Attached above is a 10 hour draft roster for your
consideration.

 Please note start and finish times of shifts could potentially be changed based on staff
feedback, as long as they still meet business requirements. In the roster the full-time lines
and
the part-time lines (0.8 FTE and 0.7 FTE) rotate through all lines of that FTE at the end of
the
4 weeks due to all lines for that FTE not having exactly the same penalty rates. For part-time
staff there is one shift per fortnight in each line which is shorter due to 10 hours not evenly
splitting into rostered FTE hours per fortnight.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on draft 10 hour roster above and
the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 24 th March 2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate. I am more than
happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to this business case for change and
can
be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

Subject: Draft LH Switchboard Rosters for Consultation
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Good Afternoon Everyone,

Please see the attached three draft rosters for consultation and feedback.

 Roster 1 : Is an 8 hour roster with RDOs. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating
through first than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so
on. We recognise that this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two
whole
days off? post night duty for full time staff.

 Roster 2 : Is an updated version of the 10 hour draft Switchboard Roster that was previously
presented but with adjusted shift times, given we had the overwhelming feedback that the
midnight
to 10am shift was not popular. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. This
roster
is industrially compliant.

  Roster 3 : Is a 8 hour roster without RDOs. Full-time staff instead have 9 x 8 hour shifts and
1
x 4 hour shift per fortnight. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. The only
lines not to rotate in this roster is the FTE lines 0.6 FTE, O.4 and 0.2 FTE. We recognise that
this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two whole days off? post night
duty for full time staff.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on these draft rosters, including
preference and the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 2 7 th May
2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate.

 I am more than happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to these rosters and
business case for change and can be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

 Kind Regards
 Tammy

 Tammy Reese

 Subject: Draft LH Switchboard Rosters for Consultation

 Good Afternoon Everyone,

Please see the attached three draft rosters for consultation and feedback.

 Roster 1 : Is an 8 hour roster with RDOs. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating
through first than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so
on. We recognise that this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two
whole
days off? post night duty for full time staff.

 Roster 2 : Is an updated version of the 10 hour draft Switchboard Roster that was previously
presented but with adjusted shift times, given we had the overwhelming feedback that the
midnight
to 10am shift was not popular. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. This
roster
is industrially compliant.

  Roster 3 : Is a 8 hour roster without RDOs. Full-time staff instead have 9 x 8 hour shifts and
1
x 4 hour shift per fortnight. This is a rotating roster with each line rotating through first
than second pay period (fortnight) and then dropping down to the next line and so on. The only
lines not to rotate in this roster is the FTE lines 0.6 FTE, O.4 and 0.2 FTE. We recognise that
this roster is not industrially compliant as it does not afford ?two whole days off? post night
duty for full time staff.

 Consequently, we are now inviting feedback from all parties on these draft rosters, including
preference and the consultation period for is now open today and will close on the 2 7 th May
2022 .

 Feedback regarding this draft roster can be sent to myself via email
Tammy.Reese@health.qld.gov.au or to LBH_HR@health.qld.gov.au . Together Queensland Union
members
are more than welcome to provide their feedback to their union/union delegate.

 I am more than happy to answer any questions staff may have in relation to these rosters and
business case for change and can be reached via email or on 3299 8934.

Welcome to your EAP
Feel supported and connected with a confidential
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and innovative
wellbeing resource. Life can be complicated. Get
help with all of life’s questions, issues and concerns
with TELUS Health. Any time, 24/7, 365 days a year.
We offer support for mental, financial, physical and
emotional wellbeing. Whether you have questions
about handling stress at work and home, parenting
and child care, managing money, or health issues,
you can turn to TELUS Health for a confidential

SIS50215 Diploma of Fitness                                 Date this document was generated: 4 September 2015




Qualification Description
This qualification reflects the role of individuals who perform a range of activities and
functions within the fitness industry. These individuals have substantial depth of knowledge
to plan, conduct and evaluate advanced exercise programs using principles of program design,
and progressed anatomy and physiology knowledge to support delivery of functional,
effective and safe exercise programs.

They have specialist skills to independently implement current approaches supported by
evidence, and establish strategies for the prevention of recurrence of injury with guidance
from medical or allied health professionals where appropriate.

The qualification does not provide the skills and knowledge for an individual to provide
advice or exercise instruction to high risk clients, other than to refer the client to an
appropriate medical or allied health professional.

This qualification provides a pathway to work in a diversity of fitness industry businesses
including fitness centres, gyms, aquatic facilities, community facilities and in open spaces,
where risk management (through risk assessment and hazard control processes) does not
already exist.

Individuals who specialise in Fitness Service Coordination develop collaborative programs
across various health and wellness sectors. They have knowledge of relevant local and
national health networks, and the skills to build and maintain stakeholder relationships.

Individuals who specialise in Management manage and support a team of fitness
professionals. This involves mentoring staff on business skills and technical skills. These
individuals have skills and knowledge in marketing and sales; business analysis; time and
financial management; recruiting and retaining personal trainers.

Possible job titles include:
    advanced personal trainer
    fitness services coordinator
    personal training manager.

No occupational licensing, certification or specific legislative requirements apply to this
qualification at the time of publication.

replaced in the Packaging Rules by the unit HLTAID014 - for more information see:
https://asqa.gov.au/news-events/news/reminder-about-superseded-hlt-first-aid-units

Targeted training for operational stream

Human Resources Policy G13 (QH-POL-240)



  Purpose
  To outline the eligibility provisions for operational stream employees to access the targeted
  training all-purpose allowance (the allowance), and the training and development education
  incentive fund (the incentive fund).


  Application
  The following provisions are applicable to Queensland Health, Hospital and Health Services
  (HHS) and Queensland Ambulance Service operational officers at:

  •     classification levels OO2 to OO4 regarding the allowance; and
  •     classification levels OO2 to OO5 regarding the incentive fund.
  OO5 classification level employees are eligible for the incentive fund only.


  Delegation
  The ‘delegate’ is as listed in the relevant Department of Health Human Resource (HR)
  Delegations Manual, or Hospital and Health Services Human Resource (HR) Delegations
  Manual, as amended from time to time.


  Legislative or other authority
  •     Queensland Public Health Sector Certified Agreement (No. 11) 2022 (EB11)


  Related policy or documents
  •     Salary Advancement HR Policy C16 (QH-POL-219)
  •     Targeted training for operational officer (002-005) endorsed qualifications list
  •     Operational Officers’ Employee Training and Development Education Incentive Fund –
        Implementation Guide
  •     Operational Officers’ Employee Training and Development Education Incentive Fund –
        Frequently Asked Questions

Policy
1.           Principles
Queensland Health is committed to recognising the knowledge and skill of public sector
employees through the payment of a targeted training allowance to eligible operational
stream employees who have successfully completed a higher recognised accredited
qualification.
Queensland Health is also committed to encouraging the development of higher skills for
public sector employees through establishing a training fund. This enables 180 eligible
operational stream employees per year for the life of the EB11 agreement to be reimbursed
up to $1,800 per qualification under the fund to study a qualification relevant to their role.

2.           Targeted training allowance
The Queensland Public Health Sector Certified Agreement (No. 4) 2000 (EB4) provided for a
targeted training all-purpose allowance (the allowance) for OO2, OO3 and OO4 employees
who attain appropriate qualifications under the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF).
These provisions are continued in the Queensland Public Health Sector Certified Agreement
(No. 11) 2022 (EB11) for OO2, OO3 and OO4 operational services officers.

2.1          Access to the targeted training allowance
An operational stream employee is entitled to payment of the allowance on condition:

•     the employee has been employed at the top increment of their classification level for 12
      months or more. For the purpose of this policy the top increment is OO2(4), OO3(4) or
      OO4(4) for the relevant classification level. An employee in receipt of the allowance will
      still be eligible to progress to OO2.4E and OO3.4E as per cl13.1 of EB11. This progression
      will not be affected by receiving this allowance, nor will the progression impact an
      employee receiving the allowance.
•     the employee holds an approved AQF qualification and has provided a certified copy or
      satisfactory evidence of the qualification, such as the original, to Human Resources (HR)
      within the department or hospital and health Service (HHS) (refer Attachment One for
      the application of AQF and Attachment Two for the application of the allowance. The
      relevant AQF qualifications for each classification level are as follows:
      −      OO2(4)
             −      Access to low allowance – AQF certificate II or higher
             −      Access to high allowance – AQF certificate III or higher

•     the qualification is directly relevant to their role (refer to the Targeted training for

•     the AQF level of the qualification is appropriate for their classification level (refer clause
      6 of Attachment 2).

3.         Operational employees training and development education
           incentive fund
Eligible operational stream employees at levels OO2 to OO5 may apply for funding
assistance (up to $1,800) to attain an AQF qualification relevant to their role, in accordance
with the following criteria:

•     The employee is a full time or part-time permanent OO2 to OO5 employee.
•     The employee is a temporary employee with greater than 12 months’ continuous service,
      and the Operational Stream Oversight Committee (OSOC) has approved the employee to
      access the incentive fund, on the proviso it will not displace an eligible permanent
      employee.
•     A performance and development process is completed with the employee’s line manager
      and a suitable AQF qualification relevant to the employee’s role has been identified.
•     An expression of interest is completed and forwarded to the Program Officer,
      Cunningham Centre, Darling Downs Hospital and Health Service for approval to access
      funding.
Funding is conditional upon the student providing consent for the Cunningham Centre to be
advised by the training provider of the student’s enrolment status, history of results and any
instances of withdrawal or deferment. For more information please refer to Operational
Officers’ Employee Training and Development Education Incentive Fund – Implementation
Guide.

Attachment 1 – AQF Qualifications
1.      How to recognise Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF)
        qualifications
All vocational education and training qualifications issued under the framework include the
following elements:

•    Name, code and logo of issuing body
•    Name of person receiving the qualification
•    Nomenclature as in the framework, e.g. certificate I, diploma
•    Date issued
•    Authorised signatory.
Additionally, in the vocational education and training sector the following elements are to
be included:

•    Industry descriptor, e.g. engineering
•    Occupational or functional stream, in brackets, e.g. fabrication
•    The words… ‘the qualification certified herein is recognised within the Australian
     Qualifications Framework’
•    When appropriate include the words ‘achieved through new apprenticeship
     arrangements’.
The qualification is also to include the nationally recognised training logo (see example
below).




All Australian university based degree and post graduate qualifications are also to be
accepted as higher qualifications for the purpose of the Operational stream targeted
training allowance.

Attachment 2 – Eligibility and application process
The following information is provided as the minimum mandatory standard practice,
procedure or process to enable satisfactory compliance with this Queensland Health HR
policy.
Local guidelines/procedures may be developed to facilitate implementation of this policy.
Any local guidelines/procedures must be consistent with this policy and attachment and
ensure employee entitlements continue to be met. Updated or new local
guidelines/procedures must be tabled at a relevant Hospital Consultative Forum (HCF).

1.      Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF)
The AQF is the current unified system of national qualifications. Registered training
organisations (RTOs) are accredited to provide training and issue qualifications according to
requirements of the AQF.
All accredited qualification certificates are to display the name and logo of the issuing RTO,
the nationally recognised training logo, and the logo of the relevant state or territory
training authority (refer Attachment One).
For qualifications approved and accepted by Queensland Health for the purposes of
accessing the allowance, refer to the Targeted training for operational stream employees -
endorsed qualifications list.
An employee who possesses qualifications that are not recognised under the AQF may seek
recognition of prior learning (RPL) or recognition of current competencies (RCC) from an RTO.
Costs associated with recognition and award of qualifications by a training provider are the
responsibility of the individual employee unless otherwise agreed between Queensland
Health and the employee.

2.      Appropriateness of qualifications
When it has been determined that an employee holds an AQF qualification, the
department/HHS is to assess whether the qualification is appropriate and directly relevant
to the employee’s current position.
Only qualifications that directly contribute to an employee’s ability to perform their current
role, duties and responsibilities are to be deemed relevant.

3.      Insufficient documentation of qualifications
The department/HHS is to ensure they sight evidence that the employee has been awarded
the full qualification prior to paying either the additional increment or allowance.
Information provided by the employee that demonstrates partial completion or a particular
component of a qualification is not acceptable.
When the department/HHS is unable to make a determination as to the AQF level of a
qualification due to insufficient detail provided, the employee is required to provide a
certified copy of the qualification and any other relevant supporting documentation to the
department/HHS for consideration. It is the employee’s responsibility to liaise directly with
the training provider to determine the AQF level.

Human Resources Policy G13 (QH-POL-240) – Attachment 2
Chief Human Resources Officer – 15 June 2023                                          Page 1 of 5
                                   PRINTED COPIES ARE UNCONTROLLED

>>> documents/correspondence-packs/02_Chloe_Taylor_PACK_462pp.pdf :: page 367
The department/HHS is to forward information to HR Branch for verification only after all
attempts have been made to determine the relevancy of the qualification to the employee’s
position and AQF qualification level. All supporting documentation is to be submitted
including a certified copy of the qualification, details of the qualification’s content and
endorsement of how it is relevant to the role. All qualifications are then to be presented to
the Operational Stream Oversight Committee (OSOC) and a decision is to be forwarded to the
department/HHS.

4.      Statements of attainment/achievement and certificate of
        proficiency
A statement of attainment is not acceptable, as this does not indicate the successful
completion of an entire qualification. Any employee who has only provided the employer
with a statement of attainment is required to produce further documentation to support
their claim for the allowance.
A statement of attainment or statement of achievement from a training course such as an in-
house program, or from organisations not registered as an RTO, are not acceptable and are
not recognised for the purposes of accessing the allowance.
A certificate of proficiency, except those recognised under the AQF (refer Attachment One),
are not recognised for the purpose of the allowance. Refer to Salary Advancement HR policy
C16 for additional information for anaesthetic technicians.

5.      Other qualifications
5.1     Advanced diploma or higher qualification – OO4 employees only
An OO4 employee who possesses a relevant advanced diploma or above (or recognised
overseas equivalent) is deemed to possess a qualification equivalent to a diploma
(certificate V) for the purposes of accessing the allowance.

5.2     Overseas qualifications
When an employee possesses an overseas qualification, it is the responsibility of the
employee to provide a conversion statement and a complete list of the subjects completed.
The employee is to contact their local Department of Employment, Small Business and
Training (DESBT) office to attain such a statement at their own expense. The employee may
also be required to have their qualification assessed by an RTO to determine articulation to
the AQF.

5.3     Trade equivalence/apprenticeships
When an employee presents a certificate of recognition from DESBT or its predecessors that
indicates the employee has obtained trade equivalence, e.g. as a cook, the department/HHS
is to note that most trade equivalent qualifications are recognised at AQF certificate III level.
The department/HHS is to seek further clarification from the original training provider or
DESBT to determine articulation to the AQF, except those outlined in the Targeted training
for operational stream employees -endorsed qualifications list.

7.         Approval date for recognising qualifications
All documentation is to be date stamped upon receipt. Payment is made from the date
documentary evidence of the AQF qualification/s is received by the local HR unit.
The line manager is to endorse the direct relevance of the qualification to the employee’s
role prior to submission at OSOC. If the qualification is referred to OSOC and the
qualification is endorsed, payment of the allowance is from the date the employee provided
documentation to HR.

Chief Human Resources Officer – 15 June 2023                                                 Page 3 of 5

If an employee possesses an AQF qualification that meets the criteria outlined in this policy,
but the employee has not been on the top increment for 12 months or more, documentary
evidence of the qualification is to be placed on the employee’s personnel file. It is the
responsibility of the employee to advise their local HR unit in writing when the 12 months
has elapsed and they are eligible to apply for the allowance.
Once the employee’s qualifications have been assessed, the department/HHS is to contact
the employee directly and advise them in writing whether or not they have been successful.
Such advice is to contain either the details of their new entitlement or reasons why they
were unsuccessful at that point in time. Information provided in this policy is to assist the
department/HHS in communicating the relevant reasons to employees.

8.      At least 12 months service on the maximum paypoint
The department /HHS is to ensure that an employee seeking payment of the allowance has
spent at least 12 months with Queensland Health on the maximum pay point, for example
OO3(4) or OO4(4). An employee is not required to work a minimum number of hours within
the 12 month period to access the allowance.

9.      Continued payment of the allowance
9.1     Cessation of allowance on transfer to another role
An employee who accesses the allowance and subsequently no longer occupies a position
relevant to the AQF qualification is to cease receiving the allowance from the date of
commencement in the new role.
9.2     Disciplinary processes
When an employee is subject to a disciplinary process, the subject of retention of the
allowance is to be addressed in accordance with that process.
9.3     Retention of payment on deployment
When an employee is subject to the deployment process, they are to retain their original
increment and allowance subject to the salary maintenance provisions applicable to surplus
employees.

10.     Higher duties
An employee who is receiving the allowance and relieves in a higher duties position, is to
cease receiving the allowance for the higher duties period. If an employee relieves in higher
duties and has a qualification relevant to the higher position and they fulfil the other
requirements, including being on the highest paypoint for 12 months or more, they are then
able to access the allowance for the higher position.
An employee in receipt of the allowance and relieving in higher duties, and as a result is
receiving less remuneration than they were in their substantive position, is to be
remunerated at the next highest paypoint of the higher level at which they will receive more
remuneration than they receive in their substantive position (including the allowance). This
may be the second or third paypoint of the higher level.




Human Resources Policy G13 (QH-POL-240) – Attachment 2
Chief Human Resources Officer – 15 June 2023                                         Page 4 of 5

>>> documents/correspondence-packs/02_Chloe_Taylor_PACK_462pp.pdf :: page 370
Example
If an OO2(4)E who is receiving the allowance commences higher duties at OO3, the allowance
is to cease. As the fortnightly pay of level of OO3(1) and level OO3(2) is less than OO2(4)E with
the allowance, the employee is to be remunerated at OO3(3).
To receive the allowance in addition to the higher duties, the employee is to be at OO3(4) for
at least 12 months.

Purpose of the role
To provide a highly effective and efficient communication service to the public and staff of the Logan Hospital within
Metro South Hospital and Health Service.
The occupant of this position is required to work continuous shift work over the full 24-hour period, 7 days a week


Your key responsibilities
 ▪    This position reports to the Switchboard Manager, Corporate Services, Logan Hospital.
 ▪    Attend courteously to all telephone enquiries and clients’ requests, displaying tact, diplomacy and
      interpersonal skills of a high standard when dealing with the public and members of staff. Maintain call
      queues to minimum at all times.
 ▪    Collate information and maintain Omnivista database and SharePoint to ensure information held within
      Switchboard Services is accurate and appropriate.
 ▪    Provide a service to support hospital staff in the allocation, coordination, and fault repair of all pager
      units for the hospital. This includes allocating pagers to hospital staff and submitting paging units for
      repair, maintaining database and registers with accurate and current information.
 ▪    Participate in the Emergency Response process by receiving emergency response notifications and
      distributing them to the appropriate response groups, dependent on the category of emergency, as per
      emergency code procedures, strictly adhering to protocols and timeframes.
 ▪    Ability to communicate at all levels and effectively establish and foster networks throughout the hospital
      to maintain accurate and current records for effective switchboard operations.
 ▪    Maintain discretion and exercise judgement where necessary to resolve problems within the scope of
      your role; in situations where precedence have not been set and procedures not defined.
 ▪    Interact in a sensitive, timely, effective, and appropriate manner with members of the general public and
      service providers, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times.
 ▪    The ability to multitask and operate under pressure, particularly where high volume call traffic is
      concerned.
 ▪    Contribute to a cohesive team environment by sharing information, supporting and assisting colleagues
      in a proactive manner.
 ▪    Ability to work effectively as an individual with limited supervision to meet deadlines and establish work
      priorities, and work as a member of a multi-disciplinary team in a changing environment.
 ▪    Ensure patients and other staff are treated fairly and with mutual respect and understanding, regardless
      of cultural, religious, ethnic and linguistic backgrounds, gender, identity, ages or abilities.

We are Metro South Health
We are the major public healthcare provider for Brisbane’s south side, Logan, Redlands and the Scenic Rim. We
operate five major hospitals and a range of community, specialty and state-wide healthcare services. We are
renowned for teaching and research excellence.
We are truly dedicated people who care about our community. We come to work to make a difference. We save
lives, changes lives and make the world a better place. We overcome the many challenges that come our way by
going above and beyond and achieve the best possible outcomes by working together. We are bold, innovative,
collaborative, inspiring.
We are part of and proud of the community we serve. We are better together.

Our values
Our values of Integrity, Compassion, Accountability, Respect, Engagement and Excellence, shape our
culture. Our values guide our day-to-day decision making and are fundamental to what we care about as a health
service, how we behave, how we interact with each other and provide care to the many patients who come through
our doors every day.




Diversity and inclusion
We are the most culturally diverse area of Queensland with 28.5% of the community born overseas and 16% from
non-English speaking countries. Our employees proudly reflect the community in which they work. At Metro South
Health 20.5% of staff identify as coming from non-English speaking backgrounds.
Having a workforce that reflects and understands the needs and expectations of our community is important to
delivering safe, kinder, and more inclusive care.
We recognise our strength comes from the diversity of our people and so we encourage people of all genders,
ethnicities, ages, abilities, languages, sexual orientation and family responsibilities to apply.
We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace for our people and our community.


Flexible working arrangements
Metro South Health supports and encourages work-life balance for the mutual benefit of Metro South Health and its
employees. Work-life balance is about a person’s ability to manage their paid work commitments with their career
goals, personal, community and cultural responsibilities. Through flexible working arrangements such as leave, flex
time accrual or a reduction in working hours, there is an opportunity to match the individual’s requirements with
those of the workplace – delivering quality health services.


Additional information
For further information about this opportunity and the benefits and conditions of working at Metro South Health
please refer to the Information for Applicants document attached with this Smart Jobs advertised vacancy.
